chapters.title: Chapter 29 - 29:Danzo Or The Villagers.
chapters.content:
"The audience should stay in the auditorium and not run around," Zenkichi said coldly, glancing at the Konoha ninjas in the Hokage Rock Shelter with an emotionless expression.
He then turned his attention to the Nine-Tails, noticing that it was currently being suppressed by the Third Hokage and the others.
After all, the Nine-Tails at this point was not in full form. Even a complete Tailed Beast would struggle against so many Kage-level opponents.
"Hokage-sama, have you forgotten something?"
"As your enemy, I'm still here."
Zenkichi's tone was ice cold. His body transformed into light particles and rose into the sky, reconstituting himself in midair.
Eight-Span Magatama!
Golden light particles formed on Zenkichi's fingertips before firing down continuously toward the Third Hokage and the others.
"Earth Style: Earth Wall!"
The Third Hokage created a tall, thick rock barrier to resist the light blasts, but it had limited effectiveness. The beams rained down from above at a steep angle, and the earth wall couldn't block many of them.
Hiruzen and the others had no choice but to dodge in all directions.
With the pressure lifted, the Nine-Tails had a chance to recover. Without hesitation, it gathered chakra and condensed a purple Tailed Beast Bomb in its mouth.
The Tailed Beast Bomb exploded internally before releasing a devastating energy beam. It destroyed large parts of Konoha, and the shockwave reached the Hokage Rock, partially collapsing the shelter.
"Beautiful!" Zenkichi clapped slowly, smiling in satisfaction.
"Roaaar!"
The Nine-Tails howled as the red chakra cloaking it dispersed, revealing the battered figure of Uzumaki Kushina.
"One minute's up!"
"You helped the Nine-Tails and caused massive destruction to Konoha. I'll never forgive you!" Kushina glared at Zenkichi, gritting her teeth.
"Oh? A threat? Harsh words? I'm terrified," Zenkichi said mockingly, his expression unfazed.
"Did you hesitate when you tried to seal me moments ago?"
"We're already at war. Don't speak as if you're still standing on moral high ground."
Zenkichi scanned the battlefield and noticed Tsunade tending to Namikaze Minato's injuries with medical ninjutsu.
"Zenkichi, don't forget what you said!" Kushina stood between him and Minato, her tone serious.
"Relax."
"I'm a man of my word. I won't do anything to Namikaze Minato again."
"Even if he tries to strike again, I won't go all out on him."
Zenkichi spoke casually, allowing the Third Hokage and others to breathe a sigh of relief.The most update n0vels are published on
"But…"
"I only said I'd spare Minato. I never said I'd spare you."
"And those in the shelter behind you… There must be tens of thousands."
"So, tell me—what can you do to protect yourself and them from me?"
Zenkichi's words caused the expressions of the Third Hokage and others to darken.
His body turned into golden light. Countless particles zipped through the air, and in an instant, he appeared next to Shimura Danzo.
"Speed is weight."
"Elder Shimura—"
"Have you ever been kicked at the speed of light?"
Zenkichi's leg shimmered with golden light.
Bang!
A powerful kick shattered Danzo's clone into rubble.
"Substitution technique, huh? How scary," Zenkichi drawled mockingly.
In the next instant, he appeared midair once more, reformed from light.
Below him was the real Shimura Danzo, sent flying from the earlier kick.
"The whole of Konoha is within my surveillance range. Where do you think you're going, 'Konoha's Pot King'?"
Zenkichi raised his hand and fired a laser at the approaching Jiraiya, forcing him to retreat.
"Don't worry."
"Konoha still holds many secrets I've yet to uncover. This battle isn't ending anytime soon."
"I'm quite interested in this so-called 'bond' you all keep preaching. Let's see what it's really worth."
Zenkichi's tone was eerily calm, making the Third Hokage and others feel a chill down their spines.
He moved again, appearing beside Danzo and placing one foot on his chest.
Raising his other foot, golden light crossed his leg, preparing to strike Danzo's head.
"Your turn, Hokage-sama."
"Come now, make your divine choice."
"One: Place Danzo's life above all else. Let hundreds of Konoha villagers die for him. I'll spare Danzo and never target him again."
"Two: Sacrifice your old comrade for Konoha. Danzo is one of your own—let him die for the village. I'll let the villagers go and won't harm them."
Zenkichi glanced toward the shelter nearby, speaking with casual menace.
In canon, the Third Hokage was notoriously lenient toward Shimura Danzo.
Danzo interfered in the Uchiha massacre, instructing Itachi to annihilate the clan; attempted to assassinate the Third Hokage, only stopped by Hatake Kakashi; performed unethical human experiments; stole Hashirama's cells; and may have even been involved in the suicide of the White Fang.
Despite all this, Hiruzen had consistently let Danzo off with nothing more than a slap on the wrist.
Was Danzo the one he valued most?
Zenkichi wanted to know just how deep that relationship ran—and what Hiruzen would choose when forced to weigh his friend against the village.
Zenkichi stared at the Third Hokage lazily, eyes filled with curiosity.
"How deep does your bond go? Let's find out. Choose wisely—it reflects your true heart."
"Stop dreaming!"
"I am the Third Hokage. I won't compromise with you so easily!"
"I'll protect Konoha—and I'll save Danzo!"
Sarutobi Hiruzen shouted and charged toward Zenkichi without hesitation.
"What a pity. Looks like you've been abandoned."
Zenkichi smiled slightly and looked down at Shimura Danzo.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 30 - 30:Please Me, And Maybe I'd Let You Live.
chapters.content:
Danzo Shimura's eyes flickered, his mood a mixture of frustration and disquiet.
To be honest, if he and Sarutobi Hiruzen had switched places, he wouldn't have hesitated to abandon Hiruzen. He might've even been glad—the greatest obstacle standing in the way of his Hokage ambitions, gone.
But people are selfish, after all.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Sarutobi Hiruzen gave up on him in a tactful and roundabout way, and that stung. Deeply.
"Here you go!"
Zenkichi smiled faintly, grabbed Shimura Danzo, and casually hurled him toward Sarutobi Hiruzen.
"Danzo!"
Sarutobi Hiruzen called out in surprise.
Truth be told, he had already prepared himself for the worst. He thought Zenkichi would kill Danzo the moment he got close—he had braced himself for it.
But to his surprise, Zenkichi let Danzo go that easily.
Danzo's expression twisted in conflict as he looked at Hiruzen. Somehow, despite the relief in Hiruzen's face, Danzo could still see the glimmer of disappointment behind it.
"Don't be careless!"
A greasy voice echoed as a golden flash burst forth. A thick golden laser pierced through Danzo's arm.
With his advanced Observation Haki, Zenkichi could sense every meridian, bone, and muscle within Danzo's body.
The laser shattered bone and seared through vessels and nerves with scorching heat.
"Some people are born for certain things."
"Don't underestimate yourself, Danzo."
"If anyone was destined to tear Konoha apart, it's you."
Zenkichi chuckled internally and watched indifferently as Hiruzen dragged Danzo aside.
"Bastard!"
Jiraiya and Uzumaki Kushina leapt into action, sealing jutsu formations flaring to life from both sides.
"It's useless!"
"Failure after failure—how long until you learn?"
Zenkichi spoke lazily, his body dissolving into golden light particles, then soaring into the sky to hover above.
"Hmm~ It seems you don't learn at all. But I can't blame you—after all, you have no means to deal with me."
Zenkichi's gaze swept over Jiraiya and Orochimaru. The intensity of his stare caused their hearts to clench, their stances turning defensive.
Eight-Span Magatama!
Golden light flashed in his hands. Dense clusters of light bullets surged and rained down toward Jiraiya and Orochimaru.
Sarutobi Hiruzen and the others were within range too, but this time, they didn't dodge.
Having been caught off guard before, they had already come up with a strategy to deal with the Eight-Span Magatama.
"Earth Style—Earth Dome Prison!"
The ground trembled. A sturdy rock dome rose up like a fortress, shielding the Third Hokage and others as the light bullets pounded it with roaring force.
"Earth Style? Impressive defense."
Zenkichi commented offhandedly, then unleashed an even greater barrage. The intensified assault shattered the earthen structure below.
The Third Hokage and the others were once again forced to scatter, desperately avoiding the golden bombardment.
"You let your guard down!"
A faint voice whispered near Jiraiya, making his expression freeze.
Suddenly, Zenkichi appeared at his side midair, arms folded. Before Jiraiya could react, Zenkichi spun, sending him flying with a sideways kick.
"You bastard…"
Jiraiya, one hand already forming seals, lunged. But Zenkichi dissolved into light once more and reappeared in the sky above.
He stomped downward, golden light gathering around his heel.
With a sharp kick, he fired a golden energy beam that slammed into the ground next to Jiraiya, triggering a massive explosion. The shockwave blasted Jiraiya off his feet.
"Zenkichi, what are you trying to do?!"
The Third Hokage shouted in fury upon seeing Jiraiya struck down.
"Don't panic. This is only number three."
Zenkichi stood with one foot planted on Jiraiya's back, smirking at the approaching Sarutobi and others.
"You prepared five different assassination strategies to kill me—did I complain?"
"Instead of wasting time being angry, maybe you should focus on solving my multiple-choice questions."
"Hokage-sama, it's your turn for a divine decision."
"To show my respect, I'll help test how strong your bonds really are!"
Zenkichi clasped his hands together. Golden light flared between them.
As he pulled his hands apart, a massive golden sword formed from pure energy.
"Sword of Totsuka!"
The glowing blade shimmered ominously, aimed directly at the fallen Jiraiya.
"Hokage-sama, time for a god-level choice!"
"Option One: Kill Orochimaru. Jiraiya survives, your student bond deepens."
"Option Two: Spare Orochimaru, the genius of Konoha. Let Jiraiya die."
Zenkichi stared down at Sarutobi Hiruzen with a smile. He was ready to unravel the very foundations of Konoha, one bond at a time.
Sarutobi clenched his fists. His voice was low and grim.
"Your request is absurd… You're just mocking us."
Zenkichi scratched his chin and nodded. "You're not wrong. Then how about this—new rule."
"You must attack Orochimaru. One minute."
"With the intent to kill."
"If I sense you've hesitated—or your strike lacks killing intent…"
"Slash!"
Without warning, Zenkichi swung the Totsuka Sword, severing one of Jiraiya's arms in a golden flash.
"You…"
Sarutobi's eyes widened in fury and disbelief.
"Oops. Sorry, my bad."
"Jiraiya looked like he was about to form a hand seal. I had to remind him not to."
Zenkichi's voice was casual as he glanced down at the injured Jiraiya.
"You scum…"
Jiraiya shouted in pain and fury.
"Zenkichi of Kirigakure, if you have the guts—just kill me! Face me in battle! What good is this cheap trickery?!"
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow in mild amusement.
"Battle?"
"To me, this isn't a battle—it's a scheme, an ambush, a stage. But never a true fight."
"Against me, you're helpless. You call this chaos a fight? Don't kid yourself."
"This is penance. This is you paying the price."
"Please me enough… and maybe I'll let you live."
His tone was flat, uncaring.
If he hadn't held back—Konoha would have been erased from the shinobi world that very day.

chapters.title: Chapter 31 - 31:The Fourth Choice.
chapters.content:
Since we reached 100 Powerstones,as promised I'd be dropping 5 Bonus Chapters.
<><><><><><><><><><><>
"You bastard..."
Hearing this, the Third Hokage was both shocked and furious, but he didn't dare to strike again.
Earlier, Zenkichi had captured Danzo and forced him into a god-level choice. He didn't hesitate and mentally prepared himself to sacrifice Danzo.
However, Zenkichi let Danzo go easily, which gave Sarutobi a false sense of hope.
He thought Zenkichi wouldn't actually go through with it—only for Zenkichi to slap him in the face the next moment.
Jiraiya had an arm severed!
For a ninja, losing an arm was the same as losing half their power.
After all, 99% of ninjutsu in the shinobi world required hand seals, and Jiraiya wasn't capable of forming seals with just one hand.
In simple terms, a once-shadow-level powerhouse like Jiraiya had been rendered crippled.
Even if he retained some combat ability, he was no longer the formidable force he once was.
---
"Hokage-sama, do you have any objections to what I said? If you do, speak up!"
"Though you prepared five battle strategies, none of them proved useful."
"You no longer have anything that can threaten me. The entire battlefield is under my control."
"I can leave when I want and stay when I want. If you want to fight, then stay and fight."
Zenkichi looked at the Third Hokage with lidded eyes, his voice calm and unhurried.
The Third Hokage's expression darkened. "But this situation... isn't it because of your betrayal? You tricked us into fighting among ourselves."
To be honest, Sarutobi Hiruzen was starting to feel regret.
Had he known Zenkichi would be this difficult to deal with, he never would've acted so rashly.
He thought the five plans were enough to handle Zenkichi, but they turned out to be completely useless.
If Zenkichi were willing to negotiate, Hiruzen might even agree to cede territory or offer compensation.
At the time, he had simply assumed Zenkichi was a Kirigakure ninja and therefore a future enemy of Konoha.
Rather than let him grow into a threat, it was better to strike first.
But Zenkichi was far more dangerous than anticipated.
---
Looking at Hiruzen, Zenkichi said calmly, "Don't worry, Hokage-sama. I won't make you face endless god-level choices."
"You made five plans for me. I've prepared five multiple-choice questions for you."
"Once you answer all five, I'll leave Konoha. How about that? I think that's quite sincere."
The Third Hokage stared coldly at Zenkichi. "Why should I believe you?"
Zenkichi smiled. "You don't have any other options."
Hiruzen gritted his teeth and looked at Orochimaru nearby. "Orochimaru, you're my most gifted student."
"Of my three disciples, you're the one with the most techniques. Just one minute—surely you can hold on for that long?"
Truthfully, what Hiruzen wanted was another alternative.
Jiraiya was already half-crippled. Sacrificing him for the sake of maximizing gains made sense.
Zenkichi's strength was no joke—if he went all out for a minute, Orochimaru might not survive.
From Konoha's point of view, risking a healthy Orochimaru to protect a nearly-disabled Jiraiya wasn't a wise move.
But...
With so many people watching from nearby, Hiruzen couldn't bring himself to abandon Jiraiya.
Sometimes you know what the right decision is, but you simply can't make it.
---
With no other choice, the Third Hokage attacked Orochimaru.
A cold killing intent burst from him as he moved, wielding the adamantine staff and striking at Orochimaru without hesitation.
Orochimaru, who possessed remarkable ninjutsu talent, had the best chance of inheriting Hiruzen's title as "Professor of Ninjutsu."
His mastery of diverse and complex techniques, along with life-saving abilities, made him Konoha's most tenacious shinobi.
---
"Sarutobi-sensei…"
Orochimaru dodged in panic as he avoided Hiruzen's furious assault.
It was obvious—Hiruzen was going all out.
---
"What a performance," Zenkichi murmured with a smile as he stepped on Jiraiya's back.
Jiraiya struggled to lift his head and opened his eyes, seeing Sarutobi Hiruzen attacking Orochimaru.
"Old man… Orochimaru…"
Jiraiya muttered, then glared angrily at Zenkichi.
But Zenkichi didn't care. He ignored him completely.
Truth be told, Jiraiya, Namikaze Minato, and the others were all characters Zenkichi had liked a lot in his previous life.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
But now? Zenkichi's mind was sharp—he understood one truth:
Children talk about likes and dislikes. Adults only care about gains and losses.
So what if he admired Jiraiya?
When Jiraiya had attacked him earlier, he didn't hold back at all.
So why should Zenkichi show mercy?
Being soft-hearted would only lead to a pathetic end.
At worst, he could emulate ancient emperors—bury those he admired with honor.
And if that wasn't enough…
Zenkichi turned to Tsunade and said casually, "I'll raise her as your wife."
---
"One minute is up."
Sarutobi Hiruzen abruptly halted his attack, glancing coldly at Zenkichi.
"Bravo," Zenkichi said with a smile, clapping slowly. He kicked Jiraiya toward Tsunade, placing him beside Namikaze Minato and Shimura Danzo for healing.
---
"The fourth choice," Zenkichi said, his eyes flashing coldly, "I want Namikaze Minato to kill Uzumaki Kushina."
---
"What?!"
"Impossible!"
The Third Hokage and Hiruzen shouted in unison.
Uzumaki Kushina was the Nine-Tails' Jinchūriki—Konoha's nuclear deterrent.
If there was still any hope of defeating Zenkichi, it lay with Kushina.
Not only that—her mastery of sealing arts was second to none.
---
"Impossible? Then just have Namikaze Minato attack her for one minute."
"A minute of true killing intent. A minute of full power."
"If I even suspect he's holding back…"
Zenkichi smiled and pointed toward Hokage Rock. Golden particles of light gathered into arrows and fired.
Boom!
A loud explosion rang out near the monument.
Zenkichi's voice was lazy yet sharp. "If I catch anyone slacking, I'll kill a Konoha ninja."
"If that's not enough… I'll kill ten thousand villagers to make up the difference. I say it—I do it."
---
Namikaze Minato's face twisted in rage as he stared at Zenkichi.
But Zenkichi simply returned his gaze with a calm smile.
And now, the relationship between Uzumaki Kushina and Konoha would plummet to a freezing point.
In that case, why not drive a wedge between them?
---
After all, when Minato sealed him earlier, he didn't show any mercy.

chapters.title: Chapter 32 - 32:A Hostage?
chapters.content:
The first choice: Uzumaki Kushina releases the Nine-Tails' chakra.
Although the Third Hokage, Sarutobi Hiruzen, approved it, Uzumaki Kushina's hesitation did not go unnoticed by Hiruzen and the others.
This was a very dangerous sign.
As Konoha's "nuclear weapon," the Nine-Tails' Jinchūriki getting personally involved could drag the village into disaster.
After this incident, Hiruzen and the others would undoubtedly increase their surveillance on Uzumaki Kushina.
Even if she was loyal to Konoha—what if someone threatened her like Zenkichi did?
In the second choice, Sarutobi Hiruzen gave silent consent to sacrificing Shimura Danzō.
This would further deteriorate the already strained relationship between the two, reducing their bond to nothing but a formality.
Shimura Danzō, whose arm had been crippled by Zenkichi, would now be more determined than ever to retain power. His desperation would only grow, pushing him to pursue strength by any means.
The Sharingan and Hashirama cells—things Danzō had long coveted—would definitely come into play.
The third option had Sarutobi Hiruzen attacking Orochimaru and simultaneously crippling one of Jiraiya's arms.
Jiraiya, a loyal and powerful shinobi of Konoha, would be weakened, and the trust between Hiruzen and Orochimaru would suffer a devastating blow.
Even though they understood Hiruzen's reasons for attacking Orochimaru, the killing intent was real.
Trust is fragile—once broken, it rarely recovers.
The fourth choice…
Zenkichi looked at Namikaze Minato calmly, a playful smirk tugging at his lips.
He raised his hand, a golden light beginning to shine at his fingertips. His voice was casual, yet chilling:
"Haven't decided yet?"
"The countdown starts now. If you don't choose, I'll kill one Konoha villager every minute. You know my speed—you can't stop me."
"Namikaze Minato, are you really going to put the village—your home—at risk for a woman from the Land of Whirlpools?"
"You said once that you wanted to be Hokage. If so, you need to be prepared."
"To the Hokage, the village must always come first. Even if it means sacrificing your brother, wife, child, or comrade."
"The First Hokage once said this. I'm just reminding you."
"Now choose."
The golden light on his fingertip grew brighter.
"Sorry, Kushina."
"I'm injured. I can't hurt you."
"We've sparred many times—you know my style."
"Hang in there. You can do this."
Minato spoke sincerely after a moment of hesitation, gritting his teeth.
Uzumaki Kushina felt her heart twist. It hurt.
She knew Minato had made the correct decision, but human emotions aren't so easily cast aside.
"Perfect."
Seeing Minato and Kushina begin to fight, a satisfied smile formed on Zenkichi's face.
From the moment Namikaze Minato chose to act, there was no going back. Their relationship would never be the same.
And Minato's earlier hesitation would leave a poor impression on the people of Konoha.
This was not the behavior of a true Hokage.
Compared to the Third Hokage, Minato was lacking.
Hiruzen had been willing to sacrifice his closest friend, Shimura Danzō, without hesitation. He'd let his best friend die for the village.
And Minato? He hesitated to attack Uzumaki Kushina.
Clearly, Minato placed personal feelings above duty.
Even in the original timeline, his behavior wasn't what one would expect from a Hokage.
He didn't have to die—but he chose to.
Don't say it was the Nine-Tails' sneak attack. He willingly used the Reaper Death Seal, sealing the beast inside himself, then dying in the process.
Why?
Because he didn't want Kushina to die alone?
What a joke.
Once you're dead, how do you "go on the road" together?
Unless it was plot armor, he simply couldn't bear the pain—dying out of sorrow and attachment.
If his wife died, he couldn't go on.
And the son? Just an afterthought.
"Uzumaki Kushina's future is going to be difficult."
"If you don't become the next Hokage, her status will drop quickly."
"Jiraiya is injured. His influence will fade too."
"You won't be able to help her."
"And after what you just did… will you two even stay together?"
"I'm really looking forward to the fallout."
Zenkichi murmured, glancing at Tsunade in the distance.
Once he reveals his fifth option, Konoha's countdown begins.
After Sarutobi Hiruzen and the others destroy the last remnants of the First Hokage's legacy and shatter the people's faith in Konoha…
That will be the day he rises, with his ambitions laid bare and the world watching.
A cold light flashed in Zenkichi's eyes.
He may have imitated Kizaru—but he was not Kizaru.
He could be carefree in life, even in battle.
But when it came to his goals, he was anything but passive.
Why time travel, if not to change the world?
"One minute is up."
Namikaze Minato backed away, smiling in relief.
Uzumaki Kushina had easily withstood his attack.
As an assassin-type fighter, Minato's blows didn't cause much damage—he specialized in speed and stealth.
Kushina, using part of the Nine-Tails' chakra and forming a tailed beast cloak, blocked all his attacks.
Minato looked pleased, oblivious to Kushina's complicated expression.
"Fifth choice."
Zenkichi announced lazily, glancing at the Third Hokage and others.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"If you hadn't betrayed me… none of this would be happening."
"Konoha's credit is worthless to me. I need insurance."
"I want a Konoha ninja as a hostage, to make sure you never pull something shameless again."
"The granddaughter of the First Hokage, princess of the Senju clan—Tsunade. She's the perfect hostage."
---

chapters.title: Chapter 33 - 33: Leaving Konoha.
chapters.content:
"Take Tsunade as a hostage?"
The Third Hokage was slightly startled and looked at Tsunade not far away.
Jiraiya immediately shouted, "No! Tsunade is the granddaughter of the First Hokage and the princess of the Senju clan. If she's used as a hostage, Konoha will be utterly disgraced!"
Zenkichi replied casually, "Disgraced? With all due respect, Konoha is already disgraced."
"In front of the strong, the weak never have dignity. Don't you understand that?"
Jiraiya and the others glared at Zenkichi with clenched teeth, anger written all over their faces.
"Ooh, such fierce expressions! Are you planning to kill me with your eyes?"
"Don't be so ungrateful. I've been rather kind to you."
"Don't forget, you attacked me first."
"You tried to kill me, but I spared your lives."
"You should be thanking me, not looking like I owe you something."
"Do I have to willingly die just because you decided to come after me?"
"Or am I supposed to generously forgive you after being ambushed, and even apologize because I didn't go along with your plans?"
"Please. That kind of thinking is absurd."
Zenkichi said lazily, casting a relaxed glance at Jiraiya and the others.
"If you want someone to blame, blame the ones who made the decisions."
"If they hadn't schemed against me, none of this would've happened."
"We're all adults here. We have to bear the consequences of our own mistakes."
His voice rang out clearly, deliberately loud enough for the Konoha villagers near the Hokage Rock to hear.
"Alright!"
"Hokage-sama, make your decision."
"I won't leave Konoha without a hostage."
"Either let me go, or prepare to fight me."The most update n0vels are published on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"The clock's ticking—thirty seconds left."
Zenkichi raised his left hand and started timing.
The Third Hokage hesitated. He was waiting for Tsunade to speak up.
If she volunteered, it would make things easier.
"Enough!"
"Isn't it just being a hostage? I'll go!"
Tsunade stood up suddenly, her voice full of force.
"Tsunade, you don't have to—"
The Third Hokage turned to her, his expression pained.
"No need to say anything. I understand."
Tsunade gave him a cold glance.
The Hokage's earlier hesitation had already told her everything.
She wasn't a child anymore—of course she understood what he was thinking.
He wanted her to stand up. So she did.
"Very good!"
"Tsunade-sama, let's go."
Zenkichi flashed her a grin, then turned to leave Konoha Village.
The Third Hokage let out a long breath of relief.
Tsunade gave Konoha one last glance, then followed.
Jiraiya watched her go, eyes full of reluctance, before collapsing in a faint.
---

While in Konoha, Zenkichi achieved a series of accomplishments.
He dismantled Konoha's five strategic responses, killed numerous shinobi, and severely injured both Jiraiya and Namikaze Minato—forcing Konoha into submission.
Thanks to this string of achievements, his Kizaru template advanced to 41%.
---
"Navy Six Styles…"
Zenkichi frowned slightly. To him, this reward was underwhelming.
For others, perhaps the Navy Six Styles were powerful techniques.
But for Zenkichi? They were nearly useless.
Finger Gun?
He could fire lasers from his fingertips. Far more destructive.
Shave?
He could move at the speed of light. What use was a high-speed step technique?
Tempest Kick?
He already had a light-speed kick that could strike from afar.
Moonwalk?
He could fly and remain airborne via his light-particle form. Why would he need a move that lets you walk on air?
Paper Art?
While it allowed dodging with extreme flexibility, Zenkichi could phase into light, making attacks pass through him entirely.
Iron Body?
It boosted physical defense, but again—his elemental form made him immune to 99% of the attacks in the shinobi world.
Even in the rare event that he needed to take a hit, he'd rather counterattack than defend.
"Totally useless."
Zenkichi muttered to himself.
"Then again… maybe it's not that useless."
"Even if I don't use it, I can pass it on to others."
"Once I return to Kirigakure, I should try to take control of the Ninja Academy."
"If that doesn't work, I'll go straight to the Daimyo of the Land of Water and establish a Naval Academy instead."
"The Land of Water is made up of islands. It's often raided by pirates. A navy would suit them."
Zenkichi began to plan his next steps.
Tsunade, walking behind him, suddenly called out, "Hey! What exactly are you trying to do?"
Zenkichi didn't look back. "I already told you in Konoha. Your village has no credibility. That's why you're coming to Kirigakure as a hostage."
Tsunade scoffed. "You think I'm buying that? With you around, Kiri has nothing to fear from Konoha breaking its word."
Zenkichi replied lazily, "It's not about fear. It's about preparation. What if Konoha does break the agreement?"
"Am I supposed to rush back again? Sorry—I've got better things to do."
"I don't have time to clean up Konoha's mess a second time."
"Punching the clock and getting things done—that's my goal. I don't leave loose ends."
Tsunade looked at him in disbelief. "That's it? Then why let Konoha off so easily?"
Zenkichi turned his head with a grin. "Because Konoha's insignificant."
"What I've done is more than enough to file my report, so I'm done with it."
...Not that anyone would understand that, Zenkichi added silently to himself.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 34 - 34:Konoha's Hokage Circle.
chapters.content:
Naturally, Zenkichi took Tsunade away not just to capture a hostage.
He took her in order to throw the hokage's position into confusion.
Zenkichi had already brought considerable harm to Konoha, and someone needed to be held responsible for it.
Following the principle that those in power must bear responsibility, the position of the Third Hokage would inevitably become unstable.
Had Zenkichi not taken Tsunade, then in the original timeline, she would most likely have become the Fifth Hokage.
At that point, the Third Hokage could step down willingly, accepting responsibility for his mistakes and resigning to atone, which would help stabilize the situation in Konoha significantly.
However, with Tsunade taken away by Zenkichi, there was no one left in Konoha capable of succeeding the title of Hokage.
In the original timeline, the Fourth Hokage, Namikaze Minato, was no longer in the picture.
Whether it was the Third Hokage or other Konoha elders—or even the general public—none would accept someone who had abandoned his duties as Hokage to reclaim the role.
As for Jiraiya, he had lost an arm, and his strength had declined to the point where he was no longer a viable candidate.
Danzo Shimura was in a similar condition—also having lost an arm and now functioning only as Konoha's shadowy backroom manipulator.
Orochimaru had both the strength and the reputation to become the Fourth Hokage, but Hiruzen Sarutobi would never allow it.
Even if Orochimaru claimed to have moved on from Hiruzen's past actions, would the old man dare to believe him?
The once-close bond between master and student had long since fractured.
As for the White Fang of Konoha...
It was nearly impossible for him to become Hokage.
While bloodline isn't a requirement to inherit the Hokage title, a close connection is still necessary.
That connection might come in the form of a direct relationship—such as father and son, teacher and student—or an indirect bond, like grandfather and grandchild or mentor and disciple.
For example, the past Hokage line has always reflected such connections:
The Second Hokage was the younger brother of the First.
The Third was a student of the Second.
The Fourth was a student of the Third.
The Fifth was also a student of the Third.
The Sixth was a student of the Fourth.
The Seventh was the son of the Fourth and the student of the Sixth...
The same applies to other villages.
The Third Tsuchikage was the disciple of the Second Tsuchikage—and the grandfather of the Fourth.
The Fifth Kazekage was the son of the Fourth, who had studied under the Third.
(Officially, Rasa, the Fourth Kazekage, learned Magnet Release from the Third.)
Though the details for earlier Kage successions may be unclear, the pattern of inheritance and strong connections remains consistent.
Whether it's a son succeeding his father, an elder brother stepping in, or a disciple carrying the will of their master—there's always a meaningful bond.Follow current novᴇls on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
But White Fang had no such close connection to any of the Hokage.
How could someone inherit the Will of Fire without that connection?
And how could someone without the Will of Fire serve as the Hokage of Konoha?
White Fang, out!
To be precise, he was never truly in consideration.
The Hokage can only come from a select lineage—the "Hokage circle."
White Fang wasn't part of it.
A pity!
The simple-minded villagers and naïve lower-ranking shinobi in Konoha had no clue.
Because of White Fang's strength and prestige, some might indeed propose him as Hokage.
"But if that happens, wouldn't it spell his end?"
"After all, if White Fang became Hokage, it would essentially mark a change in dynasty for Konoha."
Zenkichi murmured this to himself, looking forward to the chaos it might bring.
Besides the names already mentioned, Mitokado Homura, Koharu Utatane, and Akimichi Torifu—all disciples of the Second Hokage—were technically qualified to become Hokage.
But their strength and capabilities were too mediocre. They lacked the necessary prestige to truly lead Konoha. The difficulty for them to ascend was immense.
---
Kirigakure Forward Base
Terumi Mei sat atop the trunk of a massive tree just outside the Kirigakure base.
She stared in the direction of Konoha, as if waiting for someone.
Elder Genji appeared beside her and said calmly, "There's no point in waiting. He'll come back when the time is right."
Terumi Mei rolled her eyes. "Easy for you to say! That's Konoha—the strongest shinobi village in the entire ninja world!"
Elder Genji chuckled. "Even if it's Konoha, they won't find Zenkichi easy to deal with."
"His abilities are too unique. There aren't many ways to counter him."
"No matter how many ninja Konoha has, it's meaningless if they lack the tools to restrain him."
There was genuine admiration in Elder Genji's voice—he was clearly envious of Zenkichi's special abilities.
Terumi Mei frowned. "Even if Zenkichi-kun is powerful, Konoha isn't a pushover."
"Konoha is filled with strong shinobi and hidden techniques."
"Zenkichi-kun's power isn't absolute. Surely Konoha has a countermeasure."
Elder Genji mused, "True, Konoha may have something up its sleeve..."
"But Zenkichi's strength isn't limited to just his ability. I trust he'll manage."
Terumi Mei asked in frustration, "Can't we send a squad to Konoha to meet up with Zenkichi-kun?"
"He sent a clone to escort us back when we left."
Elder Genji shook his head. "No. The Third Mizukage hasn't declared war. If we act rashly, we'll risk starting a conflict."
"And Zenkichi didn't ask us for assistance. So it's best not to move without his signal."
He looked at her and tried to reassure her. "You don't need to worry. He'll be fine."
"Even if Konoha captures him, we can use diplomacy or even the threat of war to secure his release."
Suddenly, Terumi Mei's expression lit up. "I don't think that's necessary. There he is."
Elder Genji blinked. "Really? Let me see!"
On the road leading to the Kirigakure base, Zenkichi and Tsunade were walking toward them at a relaxed pace.
Elder Genji and Terumi Mei immediately rushed to meet them—both visibly relieved.
Whether it was Terumi Mei or Elder Genji, both placed great value on Zenkichi.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 35 - 35:A Princess Becomes A Maid.
chapters.content:
"Zenkichi-kun, you're finally back!"
"I thought you were in danger in Konoha!"
Terumi Mei appeared in front of Zenkichi using the Body Flicker Technique, her tone excited.
"Why are you here?"
Zenkichi was a bit surprised—he hadn't even entered the base yet.
"Ever since we returned, this girl Mei has been worried about you."
"She's been waiting here the whole time, and now she finally sees you come back."
Elder Genji replied with a smile, explaining their presence outside the base.
"Yeah?"ᴛhis ᴜpdated by NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Worried about my safety? You have so little faith in my strength."
"I thought you'd be more worried about Konoha's safety."
Zenkichi said lazily, pointing at Tsunade beside him.
"Princess Tsunade of Konoha… why is she with you?"
"Seeing how well you two seemed to be getting along, I thought Konoha had sent her to escort you!"
"But that doesn't seem to be the case," said Elder Genji with surprise, glancing at Tsunade.
"Konoha sending someone to escort me? You're overthinking it."
Zenkichi glanced at Elder Genji and replied nonchalantly.
"What's going on, then?"
Seeing Tsunade's cold expression, Elder Genji continued questioning Zenkichi.
"After I left, Konoha attacked me."
"Even though they prepared five plans to counter me, they still failed."
"I gave them a proper lesson and brought Tsunade back as a hostage."
Zenkichi spoke casually, like it was no big deal.
Elder Genji was stunned for a moment, and asked in disbelief, "You mean… Konoha attacked you and you defeated them?"
"Even Tsunade, one of the legendary Sannin, was captured by you?"
Zenkichi nodded calmly. "Of course."
Elder Genji looked at Tsunade and could tell from her expression that Zenkichi wasn't lying.
"…Give me a moment."
"The world's changing too fast—I can't keep up."
Elder Genji exhaled deeply and gave a wry smile.
---
Later, in Elder Genji's office at the Kirigakure base.
Zenkichi sipped his tea calmly as he recounted everything that had happened in Konoha. He didn't hide anything—there was no point. And because of that, both Elder Genji and Terumi Mei were utterly shocked.
"Incredible…"
"If everything you've said is true, I'll report to the Third Mizukage immediately."
"We can't just sit on our hands. We should mobilize and launch an attack on the Land of Fire."
Elder Genji's expression was serious as he spoke.
"Huh?"
Tsunade's expression changed slightly, her eyes narrowing in alertness at Elder Genji.
"Princess Tsunade, you'll stay here for now."
"When we begin peace negotiations with Konoha, they'll likely offer something in exchange for your return," Elder Genji said coldly.
"Are you making that decision on your own?"
Zenkichi shot Elder Genji a lazy glance.
"Attacking Konoha now?"
"You think you can beat Konoha just because I beat them once? Even if we attack with Kirigakure's forces, at best we'll gain some land."
"And if we can't hold it?"
"At worst, we trigger a war we're not prepared to win."
Elder Genji leaned forward, eyes burning with urgency. "Are you serious?"
Zenkichi's expression hardened. "I'm not joking. I won't attack Konoha."
Elder Genji calmed slightly. "Why not?"
Zenkichi smirked. "Because Kirigakure doesn't have the strength to take Konoha."
"Even if we manage to conquer the Land of Fire, we can't hold it securely."
It's easy to seize land with strength, but that's not the point. Conquest isn't the goal—control is.
Konoha had been around for just a few decades, but it was thriving and had the support of its people.
Even if Kirigakure conquered its territory, it wouldn't be able to effectively govern or utilize it.
Suppressing internal rebellion is harder than waging war.
Even if occupation by force were possible, it would require absolute superiority—overwhelming power.
Unfortunately, Zenkichi's method of defeating Konoha wasn't by brute strength—it was strategic.
Had he possessed overwhelming power that crushed resistance and silenced rebellion, maybe he could've ruled by force.
But he didn't.
So instead, he chose to manipulate Konoha's internal policies and sow discontent among the people.
Once their faith in Konoha was broken, and once he had enough power to suppress resistance, only then could he truly rule.
Elder Genji frowned. "These kinds of things are for Lord Mizukage to decide. All we need to do is seize the land."
Zenkichi shook his head. "Sorry. I refuse."
Elder Genji looked frustrated but said nothing further.
Zenkichi's strength gave him the leverage to say no.
"…Fine."
"If that's your decision, so be it."
"You'll return to Kirigakure in a few days. The Mizukage wants to see you."
"Oh, and what about Tsunade?"
Elder Genji turned to Tsunade. "Shall we detain her?"
Zenkichi waved a hand lazily. "No need. She's too strong—you couldn't hold her."
"She'll stay with me. I'll watch her personally."
Tsunade's expression darkened. "What did you just say?"
"I said you'll live with me. Problem?"
"I happen to be short on help. You could play the role of a maid."
"Having a princess work as a maid… sounds amusing."
Tsunade snapped, "You're dreaming!"
Zenkichi shrugged indifferently, then added with a sly grin, "Actually, Kirigakure's medical systems are lacking."
"You, being one of the most renowned medics in Konoha, could really help us improve."
Tsunade scoffed. "As if I'd share something as valuable as medical ninjutsu with enemies."
Zenkichi smiled. "Enemies? You're mistaken."
"Lady Tsunade, Kirigakure is now Konoha's ally!"
"To ensure our alliance holds strong, Konoha even sent you as a gesture of goodwill."
"You must carry your responsibilities and help solidify our alliance by spreading medical ninjutsu—through action."

chapters.title: Chapter 36 - 36: Babysitting Kids?
chapters.content:
"Is this Kirigakure Village? This is my first time here."
"Compared to Konoha, this place is seriously underdeveloped."
Tsunade followed Zenkichi into Kirigakure, glancing around as she spoke.
"Behind, right? It's okay to be behind."
"Besides Konoha, the other villages aren't much better than Kirigakure."
"So, you should understand now, right?"
"Why is it that whenever a war breaks out in the shinobi world, Konoha is always the one that gets dragged into it first?"
Zenkichi looked around Kirigakure casually, his tone calm.
"I don't understand."
Tsunade shot him an annoyed glance.
"You don't get it? You're hopeless!"
"With awareness that low, it's a wonder you're the granddaughter of the First Hokage!"
Zenkichi rolled his eyes lazily.
"Why?"
Tsunade was curious and asked,
"Because the gap between rich and poor is too wide, and economic development is uneven."
"Most importantly, your Konoha, the village that got rich first, refuses to guide the rest of us."
"Not only that, you actively block our future prosperity. What choice do we have but to resist?"
Zenkichi sighed, still in his usual relaxed tone.
"To stop you?"
"As far as I know, Konoha is always the one starting trouble."
"We've always been peace-loving."
Tsunade frowned, not quite understanding.
"Peace-loving?"
"That part's true."
"But it's not because of your kind hearts."
"It's because peace benefits you the most."
"Do you think other villages enjoy war and death?"
"We don't have a choice. Peace is a slow poison for us."
Zenkichi shook his head. Tsunade was still too naïve.
Sure, she was a great doctor and fighter, but her limited perspective held her back from understanding the deeper issue.
"What's going on? Explain it to me properly!"
Tsunade suddenly grew agitated, rushed up to Zenkichi, grabbed his shoulders, and looked him in the eyes.
"You really want to know?"
Zenkichi smiled.
"Obviously!"
Tsunade said bluntly.
"Give me your medical ninjutsu and be my maid for a week. Think of it as tuition."
Zenkichi smiled casually.
"You wish."
Tsunade was stunned for a second, then instantly refused.
"Then that's it. I can't just go around telling people the truth for free."
Zenkichi shook his head regretfully and strolled off toward the Mizukage Building.
---
Inside the Mizukage's Office.
When Zenkichi saw the Third Mizukage, his expression turned serious.
"Zenkichi, long time no see."
"When we first met, I knew you were no ordinary kid."
"Now it seems my instincts were spot-on."
The Third Mizukage smiled and spoke to Zenkichi like a kindly old man.
"Master Genji already told me about your situation. Are you really serious about the Land of Fire?"
After a short exchange, the Third Mizukage's tone turned grave.
"No."
"I have bigger plans for the Land of Fire."
Zenkichi's confident smile returned as he spoke with certainty.
He shared everything he had done in Konoha, outlining his plan to undermine the people's faith in the village. He didn't act like Kizaru this time—no lazy, aloof persona. Instead, he spoke like a true strategist.
He knew when to act like Kizaru, and when to drop the act.
After all, he was just borrowing the image—he wasn't really Kizaru.
He might act lazy sometimes, but he wasn't aimless. He had ambition, and now wasn't the time to slack off.
If he pretended to be Kizaru here and slacked off—
What if the Third Mizukage offered him a job or support, and he blew it by acting like a bum?
Being lazy felt good, sure—but that wasn't his goal.
It's fine to rest occasionally, but doing it all the time? No way.
So now, Zenkichi laid out his plans, showing the Third Mizukage his serious, capable side.
Only if the Third Mizukage acknowledged his abilities would he consider passing down the title.
As Zenkichi spoke, the old man's eyes lit up. His gaze toward Zenkichi grew more satisfied by the minute.
"Zenkichi, your talent is impressive."
"Your original instructor is no longer suitable to guide you."
"If you don't mind, come to me for advice in the future."
The Third Mizukage stroked his beard and looked Zenkichi over with a smile.
"No problem!"
"I do have some questions about ninjutsu and would be honored to learn from you."
Zenkichi smiled, already planning to learn some high-level jutsu.
Even though he had Kizaru's power… it's always good to expand your arsenal.
As for having the Mizukage as an instructor—
It was symbolic, a way of declaring loyalty.
The Third Mizukage chuckled.
"Judging from your analysis, Kirigakure doesn't need to make any major moves for now."
If the Third Mizukage had turned out to be a fool, Zenkichi would've… well, too bad. All the previous inheritors of the Will of Water were dead.
But wait—didn't Terumi Mei become the Fifth Mizukage in the original?
She wasn't even directly connected to the Third Mizukage.
So what gives? If you didn't get approval from the previous Mizukage, you couldn't be one?
If the Third Mizukage hadn't clearly taken his side, Zenkichi would've made backup plans.
Still, the old man accepted him into the fold and even made him his student. That was reassuring.
Having the Mizukage as your instructor meant you were now part of his faction—heir to the Will of Water!
---
"Good. Let the other villages clash for now and drain their strength."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ
"In the meantime, we'll consolidate internally and build up power."
"By the way, don't take on any external missions for now. I've got an easy assignment for you."
"How about being the principal of the ninja academy? It's a simple job—just manage the kids."
Zenkichi blinked.
Principal… of a ninja school?
Babysitting kids?
Me… Arakawa Zenkichi, channeling Kizaru… destined to be a kindergarten principal?
---

chapters.title: Chapter 37 - 37: Elite Squad (1/2)
chapters.content:
The principal of the Ninja Academy is essentially a shadow leader of the village.
The Third Mizukage handing over the position to Zenkichi was a clear sign—he was appointing him as the next Mizukage.
There was no avoiding this.
Zenkichi was powerful and had shown open interest in the Mizukage title.
If he wasn't granted it, could Kirigakure survive the storm he'd bring?
---
Ninja Academy – Principal's Office
A young woman in her mid-twenties, exuding charm and maturity, walked into the office and placed a stack of documents on Zenkichi's desk with a smile.
"Principal, these are the records of all current students at the academy."
Zenkichi glanced at her with a complicated expression before giving a light nod.
Her name was Mizunashi Yukie, the vice principal of the Ninja Academy.
She handled most of the day-to-day affairs.
"You're dismissed for now," Zenkichi said, waving her off.
The Mizunashi clan had excellent genes—even the men were handsome. The women? Stunning.
If she stayed any longer, Zenkichi was worried he might lose his composure.
"Actually…"
"Principal, there's one more… personal matter I wanted to speak to you about."
Yukie hesitated, eyes flickering.
"Personal matter?"
Zenkichi looked intrigued. "Go on."
Could it be that Mizunashi Yukie was… interested in him?
She hesitated again.
"Our clan head would like to invite you to a banquet," she said finally.
"The Mizunashi clan considers you an honored guest. There's something important they wish to discuss."
Zenkichi's expression shifted, but he remained relaxed.
"When?"
"Would tonight be alright?" Yukie asked, looking hopeful.
"Tonight's fine," Zenkichi replied casually.
He could already guess what the Mizunashi clan wanted.
They were preparing for the day he officially took over as Mizukage.
---
Zenkichi turned his attention back to the student files.
"Hoshigaki Kisame… Momochi Zabuza..."
Upon seeing the names of these two exceptional students, Zenkichi smiled. Kirigakure still had talent.
"Make arrangements to evaluate them early," he said.
"From what I can see, they already meet genin-level standards."
"Keeping them in school any longer is just a waste of time. Let them graduate."
Zenkichi stepped out of the office and handed the files of Zabuza and Kisame for processing.
He had plans—he intended to form his own elite squad.
---
That Evening – The Mizunashi Clan Compound
Zenkichi arrived at the Mizunashi compound as scheduled.
The status of the Mizunashi clan in Kirigakure was comparable to the Hyuga clan in Konoha.
The Kaguya, Oniden, and Mizunashi clans were the backbone of Kirigakure—just as the Senju, Uchiha, and Hyuga had been in Konoha.
They were founding clans with deep influence.
"Zenkichi-kun, welcome!"
The Mizunashi clan leader, Mizunashi Yanagi, greeted him warmly.
Despite his middle-aged appearance, the man had a youthful, handsome face.
Zenkichi couldn't help but admire the Mizunashi clan's genetics.
Yanagi hosted Zenkichi graciously, making it clear the clan wished to support his rise to power.
Zenkichi didn't comment. He knew their real reason—
They wanted to ensure that, once he was in power, he wouldn't target them.
Especially now, with tensions rising between bloodline clans and civilian shinobi.
---
"There are two very talented civilian students at the academy," Zenkichi said casually.
"I'm planning to make them my disciples."
"But a shinobi team needs at least three members. I'm still short one."
"If there's a promising talent within the Mizunashi clan, that would be ideal."
Yanagi hesitated briefly, then nodded with resolve.
"My daughter, Mizunashi Yukine. She's very gifted."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. Yanagi's conflicted expression hinted that Yukine wasn't just anyone.
"May I meet her?" Zenkichi asked.
Yanagi waved to his attendants, and soon a young girl with a refined and beautiful face was brought in.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
She looked about twelve or thirteen.
Zenkichi studied her quietly.
Was Yanagi hesitating because he feared Zenkichi would harm her?
No, that didn't seem right.
I mean, I'm handsome enough—am I not worthy of his daughter?
Then again, from a bloodline clan's perspective, handing over a child with a Kekkei Genkai was no small decision.
Take the Kaguya clan, for example.
In the original timeline, the entire clan was nearly wiped out. Only Kimimaro, the last known possessor of the Shikotsumyaku, survived.
Even now, the Kaguya clan had only three members with awakened kekkei genkai out of hundreds.
Unlike the Senju, Hyuga, or Uchiha, most bloodline clans couldn't mass-produce inheritors.
So Yanagi's hesitation wasn't surprising.
Zenkichi turned to Yukine.
"Have you awakened your Ice Release?"
The girl nodded quietly.
"Excellent. You'll be my disciple from today onward," Zenkichi said, clearly pleased.
Yanagi still looked hesitant—but after thinking it through, he smiled. The deal was worth it.
---
With his three disciples identified, Zenkichi requested command of an ANBU team from the Third Mizukage.
He was granted leadership and assigned Terumi Mei, Ao, and Yagura to his squad.
Additionally, the Oniden clan's rising prodigy—Oniden Mangetsu—was transferred to Zenkichi's ANBU unit as well.
Just like that, he had gathered the brightest young talents of Kirigakure under his command.
His squad was a strategic mix of civilians and bloodline shinobi.
This careful balance would ease tensions on both sides.
It was a classic political move—just like when the Second Hokage took Uchiha Kagami as his student.
---
The Second Hokage had been a genius at governance.
He created the Ninja Academy to break the clan monopoly on shinobi power, centralizing control under the village.
ANBU was the next evolution—like a university for elite shinobi.
It served as both a training ground and a tool to divide the clans and consolidate authority.
His ideas were so effective that every major village adopted them.
Ninja Academies, ANBU divisions, Kage leadership structures—they all became standard features across the shinobi world.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 38 - 38: Elite Squad (2/2)
chapters.content:
"I didn't expect that we'd meet again so soon, Kisame-senpai."
Momochi Zabuza appeared on the rooftop of the Ninja Academy, gazing at Kisame Hoshigaki, who had been waiting there.
Kisame looked at Zabuza and said slowly in his distinct voice, "You got the order to come here too? Looks like we're really fated to work together."
Just then, a crisp voice rang out.
"Are you two Kisame Hoshigaki and Momochi Zabuza? You're early."
Minazuki Ao stepped onto the rooftop, eyeing them with a curious expression.
"Who are you?"
Kisame and Zabuza turned their gazes to Minazuki Ao, both unfamiliar with him.
The Ninja Academy trains shinobi, but it's not the only path. A large clan like the Minazuki has its own internal training methods, and Minazuki Ao had never attended the public academy. He was trained strictly within his family.
Compared to the academy's training, the clan's was more intensive and personalized—better in both targeted instruction and the strength of the teachers.
"The water is clear without the moon," Ao said cryptically.
"Just like you, I was chosen by Master Arakawa."
"Lord Arakawa?"
"The principal of the academy?"
"The famous Arakawa-sama?"
"Come to think of it, he did say something about early graduation."
Kisame and Zabuza exchanged surprised looks, their expressions growing excited.
Just then, a flash of golden light erupted in the sky—radiant like a second sun. The brilliance faded, revealing Arakawa Zenkichi standing atop the rooftop.
"Yo~ everyone's here early."
Zenkichi gave a lazy wave, standing casually before them.
"Lord Arakawa!"
Minazuki Ao spoke with respect, and both Kisame and Zabuza bowed their heads in greeting.
"No need for formalities."
"As usual—let's start with introductions."
"Name, hobbies, dreams, pet peeves—that's the drill."
Zenkichi waved his hand casually.
"I'll go first."
"My name is Momochi Zabuza. My dream is to become the Mizukage."
"I don't particularly like anything. I hate troublesome stuff."
"And even though we're teammates, don't drag me down—"
"Or I'll kill you."
Zabuza stepped forward with an indifferent expression.
"Wants to be Mizukage? Ambitious."
"Kill your teammates? Cold-blooded."
"Momochi Zabuza, that mindset is dangerous."
Zenkichi gave his measured opinion.
In the original timeline, Zabuza had always been ambitious. After failing to assassinate the Mizukage, he became a rogue ninja bent on upheaval.
If Zenkichi hadn't stepped in, Zabuza would likely have killed every student in the graduation exam, just as the records showed.
"...Tch."
Zabuza scowled slightly, feeling like punching someone.
"No matter."
"I'll fix your attitude in due time."
"Next—who's up?"
Zenkichi tilted his head toward Minazuki Ao and Kisame.
"I'll go."
"My name is Mizunashi Yukine. I want to become the Mizukage and restore my clan."
"I like sweet things and hate anything bitter."
Ao paused thoughtfully before finishing.
"Likes and dislikes don't have to be just about food," Zenkichi said with a smirk, "but whatever."Follow current novels on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
He turned to Kisame.
"Your turn, Kisame Hoshigaki."
"My name is Kisame Hoshigaki. I want to become a great shinobi."
"I don't particularly like or dislike anything."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "That's it?"
Kisame nodded. "That's it."
Zenkichi clicked his tongue.
"You've even discarded your likes and dislikes?"
Kisame replied solemnly, "Personal attachments are liabilities on missions."
Zenkichi shook his head.
"A ninja that self-aware at your age? That's terrifying."
Kisame Hoshigaki…
He was a true shinobi—one who wouldn't hesitate to kill comrades or even himself for the mission. His mental discipline was downright chilling.
In the Akatsuki, where most were driven by their own chaos, Kisame was one of the few with unshakable conviction.
And his talent matched his will.
Not only did he have an enormous chakra reserve, but he also managed to tame Samehada—the infamously uncooperative blade.
"Not bad."
"Come with me. I'll show you how mission intake works."
"Starting today, you'll begin with entry-level missions."
Zenkichi tucked his hands into his pockets and walked downstairs in a relaxed stride.
---
Half an Hour Later
Outside Kirigakure, by the riverbank, Kisame and Zabuza were fishing.
Zabuza and Kisame were casting nets by the water's edge, while Mizunashi Yukine was walking atop the river, casting nets with precise chakra control.
Her efficiency was clearly superior.
"I already taught you how to walk on water. Use it!" Zenkichi lounged beneath a sun umbrella, reclining on a deck chair and sipping tea from a small table he had set up.
"Lord Arakawa, this isn't fair!"
"There's no way she learned that water-walking from you. She clearly knew it already!"
Zabuza shouted, annoyed.
"Of course she did."
"That was taught by her clan elders. So what?"
"Once you learn something, it's yours. Doesn't matter where it came from."
"Or do you expect enemies to give you a fair fight on the battlefield?"
Zenkichi responded casually while pouring himself another cup.
Zabuza went silent.
Zenkichi glanced at him lazily.
"Still upset? The one who should be upset is Mizunashi Yukine."
"You're all learning new skills, but she's just repeating something she already mastered."
Zabuza froze, then silently turned back to fishing.
He couldn't argue with that.
Zenkichi was right.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 39 - 39: Marine Six Styles.
chapters.content:
"Teacher Zenkichi, my mission is complete."
Mizunashi Yukine had caught enough fish and ran up to Zenkichi to report.
Zenkichi nodded. "You can go to the Mizukage Building to report the rest. The timing is up to you."
Yukine left, only to return not long after.
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow in surprise. "Why are you back so soon?"
Yukine stared at him. "Teacher Zenkichi, shouldn't you teach me some real techniques now?"
"You've already taught the others useful abilities, but not me. That's not fair."
Zenkichi chuckled and said casually, "What a cunning little girl."
"So, what do you want to learn? Water Release, Fire Release, Lightning Release, Earth Release, Wind Release—any of those?"
Yukine looked at him, eyes burning with determination. "Can I really learn any of those?"
Zenkichi smiled mysteriously and replied with pride, "I basically don't know any of them."
Yukine: "..."
Seeing her stunned expression, Zenkichi said proudly, "Surprised?"
"Don't be. You have to understand—I was just a civilian to begin with."
"How could someone like me have access to advanced ninjutsu?"
"My strength comes from unique abilities that can't be passed on."
Yukine looked visibly discouraged after hearing that.
"As the daughter of the Mizunashi clan head, I think you should understand."
"Ninjas from clans like yours should focus on mastering the jutsu passed down through your bloodline."
"After all, your family has hundreds of years of inherited techniques—you already have everything you need."
"So instead of coming to me, you should be honing those at home."
Zenkichi sipped from his teacup as he spoke.
In both bloodline clans and secret technique clans, members typically specialize in their family's jutsu.
Take the Ino-Shika-Cho trio, for example—even though their instructor was Sarutobi Asuma, they all trained in their respective clan techniques.
Or Yuhi Kurenai's team: Hinata Hyuga, Kiba Inuzuka, and Shino Aburame. All from prominent clans, yet none learned Kurenai's genjutsu.
Yukine understood the logic, but Zenkichi's power still tempted her. Being taught by someone as strong as him was appealing.
Seeing her disappointment, Zenkichi sighed. "If you really want to learn ninjutsu… tell me what kind."
"Even if I don't have powerful Release-style jutsu, I've still got connections. I can ask the Mizukage to get something for you."
"But I don't think you need it. Since you've awakened Ice Release, what you should focus on is mastering that bloodline technique."
Yukine's eyes lit up, and she nodded firmly. "You're right, Teacher Zenkichi. I should focus on Ice Release. There's no need to bother Mizukage-sama."
"I wanted to learn from you because of your strength—not for random techniques."
"I figured someone as powerful as you must have amazing skills. That's why I came to ask."
Zenkichi shrugged lazily. "I can't teach you my strongest techniques. But what about… taijutsu?"
Yukine perked up. "Taijutsu?"
No matter what type of ninja you are, taijutsu is a core requirement.
You don't need to be on Might Guy's level, but you should at least be able to fight in close combat.
Zenkichi nodded. "Exactly. I've got a powerful taijutsu system—six main techniques."New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"If you can master and integrate them, you could dominate the ninja world. Almost no one would be able to stop you."
Yukine's eyes gleamed. "That strong? I want to learn!"
Zenkichi smirked slyly. "This taijutsu style still needs some refining. I'll teach it to you later."
The Six Forms—a physical style requiring high-level fitness—originated from another world. According to its source, it's meant to surpass normal human limits.
But unlike that world, Naruto's world has chakra. Chakra can bridge the gap.
So even without inhuman physical strength, you can use the Six Forms by supplementing them with chakra.
Tsunade is the perfect example. Her natural strength isn't immense, but her chakra-enhanced strikes make her one of the strongest taijutsu users in the world.
In short: she makes up for lacking raw strength by amplifying it with chakra.
Even Might Guy, who pushed his physical limits through years of training, only surpassed human norms when he opened the Eight Gates.
So while ordinary people in the Naruto world can't break human limits just by working out, chakra provides a workaround.
"Go ask Tsunade," Zenkichi muttered, then pulled a book from a sealed scroll and began reading.
---
Later that evening, at Zenkichi's home.
Thanks to his rising status, his humble residence had become a luxurious villa.
Inside, a blonde woman was drinking. When she saw Zenkichi walk in, she angrily tossed a newspaper at him.
"Take me back!" Tsunade barked with a scowl.
"Reason?" Zenkichi asked calmly as he caught the paper.
Tsunade huffed. "Read it yourself! Your Kirigakure launched an attack on one of the Fire Country's allies."
Zenkichi scanned the article. Sure enough, it was about Kirigakure striking a Fire Country ally.
"Well… that's unexpected."
It wasn't an ideal time for Kirigakure to act. So why had they?
Maybe the lower-ranking ninjas were restless, and holding them back would cause more harm than good.
Or maybe there was internal tension—clan ninjas and civilian ninjas clashing within the ranks, with war used as a distraction.
Zenkichi mulled it over and smiled faintly. "Whatever. It doesn't affect me much either way."
---

chapters.title: Chapter 40 - 40: Nintaijutsu.
chapters.content:
"First of all, Kirigakure did not attack Konoha. Even if Kirigakure and Konoha are allies, my ally's ally is not necessarily my ally."
Zenkichi sat down slowly in front of Tsunade and said casually.
"Secondly, there is no formal alliance treaty between Kirigakure and Konoha. When we signed our agreement, you attacked me."
"After that, I made a scene and left Konoha with you. In other words, there was no real alliance treaty at all. Kirigakure already showed a great deal of restraint by not retaliating against Konoha."
Zenkichi continued with a lazy expression,
"Finally, you stayed as a hostage to prevent Konoha from stirring up trouble. This is a one-sided restriction. Do you understand?"
"Only Konoha is bound by this arrangement. Kirigakure isn't restricted at all. That's the price of your sneak attack—try to understand that."
Tsunade glared at Zenkichi angrily, but he returned her gaze with indifference.
She sighed in frustration, her expression conflicted. "What exactly do you want?"
Zenkichi replied flatly, "What I want has nothing to do with you. Just do your job."
"I told you to share your medical ninjutsu with Kirigakure, yet you haven't done it."
"And since you've been in my home, you've done nothing but slack off and ignore your duties as a maid."
"If this continues, I'll consider making you repay your debt with your life. Are we clear?"
Tsunade slammed the table, furious. "How dare you!"
Zenkichi's face turned serious as he stared her down in silence.
Feeling the pressure, Tsunade's tone softened. "If you let me go, I'll consider handing over the medical ninjutsu."
Zenkichi smiled. "Don't worry. Once things stabilize in Konoha, I'll let you return."
"Until then, you're not only going to share your medical ninjutsu with Kirigakure—you're also going to help me perfect a new technique."
Due to the unique physical limits in the shinobi world, the Rokushiki (Six Styles) cannot function purely as taijutsu.
Unless someone opens the Eight Gates to surpass their physical limits, it's nearly impossible to perform the techniques in their original form.
But if they are transformed into a form of nintaijutsu, they can become far more accessible.
Tsunade's monstrous strength technique is an example of instant application—like taijutsu, but powered by chakra.
She looked at Zenkichi suspiciously. "You're not joking?"
Zenkichi met her gaze seriously. "This is no joke."
Once Konoha stabilizes, the Fourth Hokage will be chosen.
If Tsunade returns at that point, her position will be awkward.
It would be like a prince who was captured and released after the second prince has taken the throne.
Even if she isn't targeted, the leadership in Konoha—already manipulated by Zenkichi—will likely continue fighting among themselves.
Eventually, Tsunade will grow disillusioned with Konoha, just like in the original timeline, and leave.
By then, Zenkichi would have a real chance to recruit her, further paving the way for Kirigakure's influence over Konoha.The source of this content ɪs NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
If even the granddaughter of the First Hokage no longer believes in the village, will the other shinobi still be willing to fight for it?
(*Clarification: The protagonist doesn't want to destroy Konoha outright.
His goal is to unify and reform the shinobi world—not become another unstoppable villain who slaughters the Five Great Villages.
Public support is key. It defines whether he's seen as a tyrant or a savior.*)
Tsunade thought for a while before sighing. "Fine. I accept. I'll hand over the medical ninjutsu I've mastered to Kirigakure."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "No hesitation this time?"
Tsunade replied coldly, "Hmph. As if I had a choice. If I want to leave, I have to trust you."
Zenkichi offered a half-hearted compliment. "Wise choice, young Lady Tsunade. You'll thank yourself later."
Tsunade got to work creating scrolls to record her medical ninjutsu techniques.
She also began writing manuals that documented her medical knowledge.
As Tsunade busied herself, Zenkichi remained as relaxed as ever.
His main daily task was taking his three apprentices fishing and drinking tea under an umbrella.
Momochi Zabuza complained, "We've already mastered the Water-Walking Technique. Why are we doing this boring work?"
Zenkichi answered casually, "You think I'm just training your skills? Wrong. I'm training your mindset too."
"Momochi Zabuza, your attitude is a mess. You're impulsive and short-tempered. How can a ninja complete missions like that?"
"If you don't fix this flaw, I'll throw you out of the team. I won't let you disgrace me."
Zabuza, caught off guard, quickly apologized. "I'm sorry, Sensei Zenkichi. I was wrong—I won't do it again."
Seeing that Zabuza was genuinely remorseful, Zenkichi nodded with satisfaction. At least this guy's still salvageable.
"Zenkichi-sensei, about that taijutsu you mentioned…"
Mizunashi Yukine approached Zenkichi with a hopeful look.
"We're still preparing for that," Zenkichi said calmly. "Learn other things first. Don't worry—it won't be long."
That night, Zenkichi drafted the Six Styles Nintaijutsu Training Method and handed it to Tsunade.
She took the scroll and asked, "What's this?"
"Read it first," Zenkichi said lightly. "Then we'll talk."
After reading for a bit, Tsunade frowned. "This is taijutsu? It seems too idealistic…"
"It's not feasible. No ordinary human could physically pull this off."
Zenkichi smiled. "What about turning it into nintaijutsu? Use chakra to boost your physical limits."
"I'll use taijutsu, you use ninjutsu. Combine them into nintaijutsu—it becomes ours. That was the deal. You agreed to help me perfect it."
Tsunade hesitated.
If this technique truly came to fruition, it would be a powerful weapon.
For Kirigakure to gain something like this…
"You still want to leave, don't you?"
Zenkichi picked up a nearby glass of water and spoke calmly.
The words instantly made Tsunade falter.
"You're so cruel…" she muttered, glaring bitterly at him.

chapters.title: Chapter 41 - 41: Fourth Hokage.
chapters.content:
After several days of training, Kisame Kisaki and Zabuza Momochi—already very talented—had successfully mastered the art of water walking. They spent several more days repeatedly training while also completing their fish-catching assignments.
Once they completed their water-walking task, Zenkichi guided them in learning how to climb trees and taught them the basic control of chakra.
Later, he took them into the mountains and forests near Kirigakure to suppress bandits, allowing them to experience real combat, see bloodshed, and harden their resolve.
It had to be said—these three were exceptionally gifted.
Moreover, coming from Kirigakure, a village known for its cold and brutal methods, they were naturally tough-minded and not the least bit shaken by bloodshed.
"To have such outstanding performance at such a young age… you're monsters in the making," Zenkichi said lazily, glancing at the three of them with a hint of pride.
"I'm satisfied with your progress. Next, I'll teach you a set of ninjutsu."
"This set consists of six techniques: single-point attack, area-of-effect attack, teleportation, full defense, agile evasion, and mid-air mobility."
"If you can master, integrate, and coordinate all six, there's almost nothing in this world you won't be able to handle."
Zenkichi said this with a rare glint of passion in his voice. This Six-Style Ninjutsu had been developed through his collaboration with Tsunade.
Mizunashi Yukine lit up. "Really?! Zenkichi-sensei, are you finally going to teach us that Nintaijutsu you've been talking about?"
Zabuza licked his lips and grinned. "So it's finally time to learn the good stuff. I've been waiting for this."
Kisame didn't say anything, but his excitement was clear on his face.
"The Water Clone Jutsu," Zenkichi said, forming hand seals. Three identical clones appeared beside him.
"My clones will train each of you individually. They hold all of my knowledge and experience, so they're perfectly capable of teaching you everything you need."
Zenkichi flopped back into his rocking chair and lazily sipped a cup of tea.
The three of them—Zabuza, Kisame, and Yukine—were momentarily speechless.
This old man really knew how to enjoy himself.
Still, seeing the clones, they couldn't complain. Individual instruction would definitely be more efficient than the three of them crowding around one teacher.
Just then, an ANBU ninja in a mask appeared beside Zenkichi and knelt slightly. "Captain, the Mizukage has summoned you."
Zenkichi groaned as he left the comfort of his chair and set his book and teacup aside. "Alright, let's go."
He walked alongside the masked ANBU toward the Mizukage's office.
As they made their way through the village, Zenkichi glanced at the ANBU and asked, "So, how's life in ANBU treating you?"
"It's alright," came the resigned voice of a woman beneath the mask. "We've only recently joined, so we're still undergoing training. Nothing too intense yet."
Zenkichi arched an eyebrow. "Huh. I figured they'd be throwing you into the fire already. I mean, you're not exactly average."
The woman removed her mask slightly, revealing her face—it was Terumi Mei.
She gave him a look of mild annoyance. "Speaking of which, Captain, you've barely shown up for our training. You've been slacking off."
Zenkichi yawned. "Well, I don't really need ANBU training."
Terumi Mei rolled her eyes. "You're just lazy. Like a salted fish with no dreams. If you weren't so absurdly strong, the Mizukage never would've picked you as his successor."
Zenkichi grinned. "That's nonsense. You're still too young to understand my ultimate secret—my unique bloodline ability: 'The more I slack, the stronger I become!'"
"When I fully awaken this power, I'll surpass everyone. There's wisdom in conserving energy. Don't be so hasty."
Terumi Mei sighed. "Fine. Whatever makes you happy. But seriously, when will our ANBU training end? There's a war going on, and we're still stuck here."
Zenkichi looked at her curiously. "You want to go to the battlefield that badly?"
She nodded. "It's not just me. Everyone under your command is itching to move. This is war. Who isn't eager to prove themselves?"
Zenkichi nodded thoughtfully. "I see. But it's not really up to you. None of you are strong enough to be decisive factors yet."
Even Momochi Zabuza and Kisame had expressed the same desire—to fight. They'd shouted multiple times about wanting to head to the front lines.
When Zabuza and Kisame graduated early, it was largely because the village believed they were urgently needed.
But in truth, Kirigakure hadn't made any large-scale war moves yet. The desire to fight was real, but the orders hadn't come.
Before long, Zenkichi arrived at the Mizukage's office.
The Third Mizukage handed him a classified document. "Read this."
Zenkichi scanned it. The intel came from Konoha.
"Akimichi Torifu has become the Fourth Hokage? So it ended up being Akimichi Torifu, huh?"
He smirked slightly, amusement in his eyes.
Akimichi Torifu had been a disciple of the Second Hokage. He had inherited the Will of Fire and was technically qualified to be Hokage.
Otherwise, how could someone like him—once a disciple of the Second—fail to even become part of the Konoha Council?
But Akimichi Torifu lacked power—not just in battle, but also in leadership and political acumen.
He now sat at the Hokage's desk, overwhelmed by paperwork, scratching his head in frustration.
In Konoha, within the Hokage's office, Hiruzen Sarutobi had stepped down but retained the position of Hokage's assistant, continuing to influence the village.
With limited power and zero ambition, Akimichi Torifu was easy to control. That's why the Third Hokage had chosen him.
His weak presence in the original events wasn't just due to lack of strength, but also his lack of ambition.
Torifu's rise to Hokage was a political compromise by the village elders.
"Let me help you with that," Sarutobi Hiruzen said, walking over with a kind smile.
"Hiruzen, you're just in time!" Akimichi Torifu smiled in relief and immediately passed him the workload.
Though Sarutobi Hiruzen had resigned, Torifu didn't blame him for the past and fully trusted his capability and character.
Which was exactly what Hiruzen wanted.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Even without the Hokage title, his influence remained. Had the Fourth Hokage been Danzo, Homura, Koharu, or even Orochimaru, he wouldn't have had any presence left.
But Akimichi Torifu? He was never one to fight for power.
