chapters.title: Chapter 55 - 55: Zenkichi, A Threat.
chapters.content:
Zenkichi was stunned. He hadn't expected Madara Uchiha to say that.
He looked at Madara in astonishment, then smirked and replied jokingly:
"Old man Madara!"
"You've got quite the imagination—and a sharp mind to match."
"What if your guess is right? What would you do then?"
Madara stared coldly at Zenkichi and said, "Even though this is a world ruled by chakra, that doesn't mean other forms of power don't exist."
"Kid… maybe you've encountered a power different from the chakra system, but this world is still governed by chakra in the end."
"Do you know the origin of chakra? Do you understand the truth behind the shinobi world? How much do you really know about this world filled with despair?"
Zenkichi casually raised his hand, and a golden, cross-shaped light spun on his fingertips.
"Battlefield sage now, are we? Going to drop some life advice?"
"How scary."
"Has the Shura of the shinobi world stopped being a butcher and become a life coach?"
With a smirk, he fired a golden laser from his fingertip.
"It's useless."
"Maybe I can't hurt you, but you're not defeating me either."
"Susanoo combines offense and defense into one—it's an absolute defense that withstands all attacks."
Madara looked calmly at the laser exploding outside of Susanoo.
"Is that so?"
Zenkichi replied lazily as his body transformed into countless light particles, rising into the sky and reassembling mid-air.
"Yasakani no Magatama!"
Golden energy bullets formed in Zenkichi's hands, pouring down like a tidal wave upon Madara below.
Madara snorted coldly, his Susanoo solidifying further. The powerful defense resisted the bombardment of golden bullets. They only caused ripples across its surface—insufficient to destroy it.
Meanwhile, Tobi phased into the ground and brought Black Zetsu and Nagato to Madara's side. Thanks to Susanoo shielding them from above, their location was secure.
"I told you… it's useless."
Seeing Zenkichi descend after the barrage, Madara sneered.
"You really are something, Madara. Strong as a monster."
"And Susanoo—what a terrifying defense."
"If I want to defeat you, I'll have to wait until you exhaust your remaining life force."
"Judging by your age, you're nearly at the end, aren't you?"
"You must've paid a heavy price to return to a youthful state."
Zenkichi stood opposite Madara, completely unbothered by the circumstances.
"Was that intentional?"
Konan watched from a distance, puzzled. Zenkichi's Yasakani no Magatama had destroyed all the forest conjured by Madara's Wood Release.
Even the vines they'd been hanging from were obliterated.
"Enough chatter, we have to go—now!"
Jiraiya urged in a low voice, his expression tense.
Madara noticed them trying to escape but didn't bother reacting. To him, they were mere ants—insignificant.
"I'll seal you long before my life force runs dry."
Madara clapped his hands together, chakra surging between his palms. Then, he opened his hands and launched a jet-black sphere directly at Zenkichi.
"Chibaku Tensei!"
The Rinnegan's sealing technique unleashed powerful gravitational force. The black sphere sucked in debris and broken wood as it flew toward Zenkichi, attempting to trap him in an artificial satellite.
"Chibaku Tensei? Good technique."
"But all ninjutsu has a flaw."
"Unfortunately for you—I know this one's weakness."
Zenkichi casually opened his mouth and fired a concentrated laser beam directly at the sphere.
The sphere shattered under the fierce impact, and the gravitational pull vanished. Debris that had been midair crashed to the ground.
But then—
Slash!
In the next instant, Zenkichi's body was split in two.
As if struck by an invisible blade.
"Huh?"
Zenkichi's eyes widened—but he quickly understood what had happened.
The shadow from Limbo: Border Jail.
A unique Rinnegan ability, usable only by Madara.
Limbo clones existed in a parallel dimension, invisible and untouchable to those without Six Paths chakra or the Rinnegan.
"What a close call…"
Zenkichi muttered, as his bisected body dispersed into light particles and reformed whole in front of Madara.
"You sensed my Limbo clone?"
Madara raised an eyebrow, though his tone remained calm.
Limbo: Border Jail was an extraordinary ability. That's why Madara believed it would work—to strike Zenkichi when he wasn't in light form.
After all, the light state couldn't be maintained indefinitely without drawbacks.
(Yeah, Uses Stamina)
Madara understood well how concealed Limbo clones were.
Unless someone had the Rinnegan or Six Paths powers, detection was impossible.
"Sense them? Not exactly."
Zenkichi shook his head. "I just reacted."
"My body instinctively transformed into light when I was attacked. Like a reflex."
"A reflex?"
Madara frowned. He didn't fully believe Zenkichi.
Once again, his four Limbo clones moved in.
They suddenly attacked—shattering Zenkichi's body again.
Countless light particles floated up into the air and reassembled, Zenkichi now hovering above.
"You didn't sense them?"
Madara narrowed his eyes with suspicion.
"I told you. It's instinct."
"My body just reacts to danger—it's not that I saw or sensed them."
Zenkichi hovered mid-air, answering casually.
Madara's eyes flashed. The Rinnegan pulsed with power—he unleashed a genjutsu instantly.
Zenkichi stiffened for a second—but then recovered almost immediately.
Madara stomped the ground, launching himself into the sky toward Zenkichi.
He reached out, grabbing at Zenkichi's body with surging ocular power.
"The Human Path…?"
"A soul-extracting ability? Not today."
Zenkichi smirked and split into light particles, evading instantly.
The Human Path could be fatal—but fortunately, Limbo clones couldn't use Rinnegan abilities. Otherwise, Zenkichi would've been in real danger.
Madara attacked repeatedly, trying to catch Zenkichi with the Human Path.
But Zenkichi was too nimble—slipping through his grasp like a monkey.
"Madara-sama… perhaps we should retreat for now?"
Black Zetsu sent a mental message from his hiding spot. He and Madara shared a form of telepathic communication.
In the original history, Black Zetsu had done the same after being halved by Terumi Mei.
"No."
"I'm running out of time. I must eliminate Zenkichi before I die."
Madara's tone was unwavering.
His life was already nearing its end—and only the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path had kept him alive this long, by flooding him with chakra.
If Madara's body was a teacup, the vitality was tea.
Time had cracked the teacup, causing the tea to leak out. The statue kept refilling it—but more cracks formed each time.The most update n0vels are published on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Now, Madara had poured in too much chakra. The cup was shattering.
Once all the tea was gone, the cup would be beyond repair.
No amount of refilling could save it.
"Black Zetsu, get out of here."
"Kumogakure, Iwagakure, Sunagakure, and Konoha's forces are all nearby. Lure them here."
"They all possess strong sealing capabilities. If they clash with Zenkichi, maybe—they can seal him."
Madara paused, forming a backup plan in his mind.
No matter what, Zenkichi had to be removed before the end.
Zenkichi knew too many secrets. He could derail everything.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 56 - 56: White Zetsu
chapters.content:
The Country of Rain, the Frontline Base of Konoha Village
In the commander-in-chief's camp, Tsunade stood in front of the map, frowning in thought.
After being released by Zenkichi, Tsunade returned to Konoha.
However, what she encountered there left her disappointed and disheartened with the entire village.
Uzumaki Kushina was under surveillance by Konoha's Anbu and even had her personal freedom restricted.
With Kushina's fiery personality, how could she possibly accept such conditions?
She had a major quarrel with the village, but in the end, it amounted to nothing.
Sarutobi Hiruzen, who had once been lenient toward her, was now firm in his decision to keep her under watch.
After returning, Tsunade personally asked Hiruzen and the others for an explanation.
After all, her grandmother was Uzumaki Mito, and she'd had a close relationship with Kushina since childhood.
Yet, the Konoha higher-ups, including Hiruzen, were adamant that Kushina needed to be monitored.
Even though they were her grandfather's disciples, they showed no compassion.
Hiruzen bluntly told her that Kushina was an unstable risk.
If her lover were to betray Konoha, they couldn't allow such a possibility to go unchecked.
Though Hiruzen's explanation made logical sense, it left Tsunade cold.
What chilled her even more was the death of Konoha's White Fang under suspicious circumstances.
A top-tier combat force had vanished, and Tsunade had her suspicions.
After everything she'd witnessed, she had already begun to consider leaving Konoha.
The village was no longer what her grandfather had built. It had become a playground for schemers.Follow current novels on No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
But still—it was the home of her childhood, the legacy of her grandfather.
As much as she was disappointed, Tsunade couldn't stand by and watch it fall apart.
So, she decided to stay—at least until the war ended.
---
"Tsunade-sama, I have an urgent report!"
Suddenly, a voice called from outside the tent.
"Come in," Tsunade replied, taking a seat.
The Konoha ninja entered with a strange look on his face.
"Tsunade-sama! According to the intelligence we've gathered, Uchiha Madara and Zenkichi have both appeared in the Land of Rain. They're fighting!"
"Uchiha Madara? Zenkichi?" Tsunade echoed in disbelief.
"Yes!" the ninja affirmed. "Our spies confirm it was the Uchiha Madara—known as the Demon of the Battlefield, thought to have been killed by the First Hokage in the Valley of the End."
"As for Zenkichi… it's the same one we know from Kirigakure."
Tsunade narrowed her eyes. "That's nonsense. Even if Zenkichi appearing makes sense, how could Madara Uchiha be in the Land of Rain?"
The Konoha ninja gave a bitter smile. "That's what we thought, too. But the spy said the man looked exactly like the figure carved on the Valley of the End monument."
Tsunade let out a dry laugh. "Even if Madara were alive, he wouldn't still look like the young man on that statue."
"If he's alive, he should be an old man by now."
Boom!
At that moment, a massive surge of chakra erupted in the distance.
The chakra was overwhelming—on par with a Tailed Beast.
"How can one person have that much chakra?" Tsunade exclaimed, her eyes narrowing as she looked toward the horizon.
The ninja beside her looked grim. "That direction… is exactly where Zenkichi and Uchiha Madara were said to be fighting."
Tsunade stood immediately and barked orders. "Ninjas from the Yamanaka clan and the Sealing Corps, come with me! Everyone else, stay behind!"
This kind of overwhelming battle—Tsunade couldn't ignore it.
After all, both Madara and Zenkichi were enemies of Konoha.
Two monsters fighting each other? This was the perfect time to act.
If she could reap the benefits—or even subdue either of them—it would be a major gain.
Of course, she wasn't only thinking of gaining an advantage.
Zenkichi and Uchiha Madara had left deep impressions on her. Both were essentially invincible.
If she didn't seize this chance to act, she would regret it for the rest of her life.
---
Not far from Konoha's frontline base was Sunagakure's own base.
The Konoha ninja who had just spoken to Tsunade? He was actually a White Zetsu. After absorbing chakra, White Zetsu could perfectly mimic others.
In the original timeline, only Uzumaki Naruto, with his unique sensory abilities, could distinguish White Zetsu clones.
Given the urgency of the current situation, Tsunade and her forces had no reason to doubt the imposter.
While feeding Tsunade misinformation, White Zetsu also delivered the same to Chiyo, Sunagakure's commanding officer.
---
"Uchiha Madara… is it really him?"
Chiyo narrowed her eyes, deep in thought.
"Sister, we should go check it out," Ebizo said beside her.
"You're right," Chiyo nodded. "If it really is Madara, we need to know."
"Back in the day, the only one who could match him was Senju Hashirama. He was the embodiment of Shura in the ninja world."
"But we still don't know if it really is Madara. And if he's still young…"
Chiyo paused there, her face darkening. Then she called for the Sealing Corps to assemble.
They'd also gathered some intel on Zenkichi.
Although Chiyo was skeptical about Zenkichi's strength, now wasn't the time to take chances.
She gave the order. "The Sealing Corps and a few sensory-type shinobi will come with me. The rest will stay here with Ebizo."
One of the senior officers voiced another idea.
"If we received this intel, Konoha must have as well. And since Uchiha Madara was once a Konoha shinobi—who later turned on them and even fought the First Hokage—they'll take this more seriously than we do."
"I suggest we use this chance to strike Konoha and gain the upper hand in the war."
Chiyo went silent for a moment, then shook her head.
"No. Sunagakure is in peace talks with Konoha. We can't afford to act recklessly."
"Konoha's sincerity this time is real. We must support the village's diplomatic stance. Remember—winning the war isn't the ultimate goal."
A faint smile crossed her face.
Konoha was serious this time.
They had even sacrificed the one responsible for her son and daughter-in-law's deaths: Konoha's White Fang.
How had he died?
Much like how Sunagakure's own hero, Pakura, had been sacrificed in the original timeline.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 57 - 57: Battlefield Rose
chapters.content:
"Old Uchiha Madara!"
"Are you at your wits' end?"
Countless light particles formed Zenkichi's body in mid-air. Looking down at Uchiha Madara below, he said casually,
"Kid."
"With your strength, you're not ready to dance yet."
Uchiha Madara looked up and stared at Zenkichi floating in the sky. The Limbo clone was already close to Zenkichi.
Using the ability of his Limbo: Border Jail, Madara switched positions with his invisible clone and appeared directly beside Zenkichi, his palm imbued with the power of the Rinnegan reaching for him.
"It's useless."
Zenkichi spoke lazily, his body shattering into countless particles of light as he instantly retreated from Madara's reach.
"No matter how hard you try, you can't do anything against my speed."
"Even if you appear within arm's reach, the moment you do…"
"I become light."
"Human abilities are powerless in the face of light-speed."
Zenkichi's body reassembled in the distance. He looked at Uchiha Madara and spoke calmly,
"Rats who can only dodge…"
"You rely entirely on unique abilities. This way, you'll never become truly strong."
(Yeah just like Kizaru, the skill is broken tho. Ngl)
Uchiha Madara's face darkened as he snarled at Zenkichi,
"Oh~"
"Ah, Ban is really strict."
"But I think my ability is more than enough…"
"Right, Madara-san?"
Zenkichi raised his hand and casually pointed at Madara. A beam of golden light spurted from his fingertip, condensing into a sharp arrow that launched toward his opponent.
Susano'o!
A light blue Susano'o manifested around Madara, blocking Zenkichi's attack. The golden laser struck Susanoo's hand, scattering radiant sparks across the battlefield.
Susanoo's massive hand shielded Madara, deflecting the light particles in all directions. The highly concentrated energy exploded violently upon impact—
Boom boom boom!
"Mere fireworks. They're nothing compared to me!"
"Little devil, do you want to dance?"
Madara roared in fury and drove Susanoo into the sky, charging at Zenkichi.
"I'd be honored to dance with the Battlefield Rose!"
Zenkichi responded lazily, golden light bullets appearing in his hands before raining down like a golden storm.
Yasakani no Magatama!
The dense barrage of golden light pelted Susanoo, forcing Madara to constantly burn through his eye power to maintain his defense.
As they clashed at close range, Madara swung his sword at Zenkichi, but once again, Zenkichi transformed into light and teleported away.
"Is that all you can do? Repeat the same move over and over?"
Madara glared at Zenkichi with disdain.
"How scary," Zenkichi replied, unfazed by Madara's killing intent.
"Sure, I only have a few tricks, but you still can't touch me."
"A great man once said…"
'Three strikes that win the world—any more is a waste.'
"Light-based attacks, light-speed movement, and turning into light. These three are enough."
"There are only a handful of people in the world who can block these moves."
'And the best part—they're simple. Direct. They perfectly match Kizaru's sleazy personality.'
Zenkichi smiled, unbothered by Madara's escalating rage.
"You'll never be convincing if all you rely on are cheap tricks!"
"A truly strong person must possess the power to overwhelm everything!"
Madara's fury was growing.
"How scary…"ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Zenkichi shrugged, his expression that of total indifference—which only made Madara's blood boil further.
"Old man Madara!"
"Your rage only proves how powerless you are."
"You can't do anything about my abilities."
"You're resorting to low-grade provocations just to get me to fight you head-on."
"But what a shame."
"The character I'm playing now… is a cowardly bastard."
"So you're doomed to be disappointed. I won't fight you head-on."
Zenkichi said casually, further enraging Madara.
"How scary…"
"The Battlefield Rose of the past is already withered—now he can only stand there, helpless and angry."
"Time spares no one."
Zenkichi spoke with mock sympathy.
To be fair, even Zenkichi agreed with some of Madara's ideology.
Right now, his powers were enough to inspire awe and fear throughout the ninja world.
But convincing people to believe in him? That was different.
He didn't have the overwhelming power to crush all enemies, nor the durability to tank massive attacks on behalf of others.
Such a leader doesn't inspire confidence.
But…
Zenkichi stared at Madara with a faint grin. He hadn't yet achieved overwhelming strength—
—but once he kills Madara, everything will change.
Who is Uchiha Madara?
One of the two strongest shinobi of his era—the Battlefield Rose, the Asura of the Ninja World.
Especially now, at the height of his power, Madara could easily dominate all nine tailed beasts.
With a pair of Rinnegan in hand, even if Hashirama Senju were resurrected, defeating Madara would be no simple task.
But if Zenkichi could kill this Madara…
Then the rewards would be tremendous.
He would unlock more of the Kizaru template and gain the power to dominate the entire ninja world.
Zenkichi raised a finger.
Golden light flared from his fingertip, forming a spinning cross of energy.
"Battlefield Rose, let me send you off with this attack."
Zenkichi said lazily, launching the golden laser toward Madara's Susanoo.
"Pointless tricks!"
Madara resisted the laser with Susanoo's reinforced arms and growled,
"What's with that nickname you keep using—Battlefield Rose?"
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow and chuckled.
"Battlefield Rose? I meant you, of course!"
"Who else would deserve that name?"
"The rose who danced in the heart of every battlefield."
Madara's expression twisted—he was absolutely livid. The nickname was far too feminine!
"Bastard!"
"If I weren't focused on sealing you, I'd make you regret that!"
Madara snarled as his powerful ocular chakra surged, further solidifying Susanoo.
Suddenly, Zenkichi's expression changed.
While still firing golden lasers, he felt something.
Using Observation Haki, he sensed the presence of an unfamiliar ninja approaching.
---

"Old Uchiha Madara!"

Zenkichi replied lazily, eyeing Madara with a smirk.
Uchiha Madara said calmly, "Victory and death don't have to contradict each other. Sometimes, they arrive together."
As he spoke, strange black markings crawled across his face—the sign of a powerful curse seal.
The markings converged into his eyes.
"What is that?" Zenkichi asked, genuinely curious.

What caught Madara off guard, however, was that Zenkichi didn't show the slightest interest in the Rinnegan.

"You know far too much. That White Zetsu shouldn't have had access to all this intel."

chapters.title: Chapter 59 - 59: Alliance Against Zenkichi.
chapters.content:
"The battle is over!"
"Who's winning?"
"It should be Zenkichi from Kirigakure!"
"It's him?"
"Yes! From what I can sense, he has the smaller chakra reserves between the two.
Although the other one had much more chakra earlier, it suddenly plummeted.
That must've been because Uchiha Madara used some kind of forbidden technique to restore his youth and strength. But after the technique wore off, everything reverted."
"Chiyo-sama, should we act now? I don't sense any decrease in Zenkichi's strength.
Actually… it's not just that—his chakra seems to have increased after the battle."
A sensor ninja from Sunagakure reported the findings to Chiyo with a serious expression.
"His chakra increased again? That's absurd!"
"He must be pretending—to scare us off."
"As far as I know, Zenkichi has exceptional sensory perception," Chiyo muttered, frowning with disdain.
Though doubtful, she couldn't afford to hesitate.
Even Uchiha Madara had been defeated by Zenkichi. If they waited any longer, he might recover completely. And if he's on par with Madara, Sunagakure may as well surrender now.
Chiyo made her decision.
She and the Sunagakure ninjas moved quickly toward Zenkichi's location.
At the same time, ninjas from Konoha, Iwagakure, and Kumogakure also entered the battlefield.
Zenkichi stood silently, digesting the swordsmanship he'd just mastered—swordsmanship at the level of a true great swordsman.
Suddenly, he opened his eyes.
The ninja forces of all four major villages had surrounded him.
"Took you long enough."
"Konoha's Tsunade, Sunagakure's Chiyo, Iwagakure's Kitsuchi, Kumogakure's Raikage… Important people from every village, huh?"
Zenkichi scanned the crowd around him with a calm, uninterested gaze.
"Zenkichi… I must admit, you're a genius," the burly Third Raikage said, stepping forward. "If you're allowed to grow further, you might even surpass the First Hokage one day.
For the sake of our villages—and the balance of the ninja world—we have to kill you now."
"How scary."
Zenkichi let out a lazy yawn, clearly unimpressed.
"Don't give me that 'for peace' nonsense. You want to kill me for your village's safety, not for peace."
Kitsuchi, representing Iwagakure, spoke gravely:
"No. Your existence has shattered the balance of power. If left unchecked, you'll drag the world into even greater war."
Zenkichi replied slowly,
"Then it's simple: let me reach my full potential—and surrender to me."
"Once that happens, we'll all be on the same side. As one family, there'll be no more war."
Chiyo scoffed and summoned the ten puppets of Chikamatsu.
"Such arrogant delusions. I see now that your mind hasn't caught up with your talent."
"Regardless, your abilities are undeniable. This is a once-in-a-lifetime chance. We must eliminate you now."
Zenkichi chuckled and shrugged.
"Fine, I get it. What about you, Tsunade?"
Tsunade hesitated, clearly conflicted.
The Third Raikage frowned.
"Princess Tsunade, what are you waiting for? I thought the rift between Konoha and Zenkichi was beyond repair."
Chiyo chimed in:
"After last time, I'm sure Konoha came better prepared. We need your strength."
Tsunade's expression turned uncertain. She knew how dangerous Zenkichi was.
Honestly, she doubted anyone here could stop him.
Zenkichi looked at her with a relaxed smile.
"Princess Tsunade, would you mind just watching from the sidelines? After I clean this up, we'll talk properly."
The Konoha shinobi around her exchanged uncertain glances.
"Tsunade-sama...?"
Tsunade raised her hand, then gave the order.
"Retreat."
Without hesitation, she led the Konoha forces away from the battlefield.
"…She left?"
Chiyo stood stunned.
"Coward!" the Third Raikage barked in anger.
"Useless woman!"
Kitsuchi remained calm.
"Well now, maybe the old saying about big breasts and small brains isn't absolute. At least Tsunade knows when to bow out."
"But unfortunately…" He pointed at the others.
"You're not going anywhere."
"You showed up to challenge me, didn't you?" Zenkichi said, coldly. "So you should've been ready to die."
"Perfect timing, actually. I just picked up a new technique."
"Let's see what it can do."
Zenkichi brought his hands together. As he pulled them apart, a massive golden sword of energy appeared in his grip.
Totsuka-no-Tsurugi!
With the gleaming lightsaber in hand, Zenkichi swung effortlessly.
A roaring wave of golden energy slashed through the air—headed straight for Chiyo.

"He's become stronger!"

"Earth Release: Mountain and Earth Technique!"
Seeing this, Kitsuchi immediately took action, forming hand seals to release an Earth Release jutsu. The ground on either side of Zenkichi roared and rumbled.
Two enormous boulders rose from the earth, closing in on Zenkichi like giant, moving mountains.
"Boring."
Zenkichi swung the longsword in his hand, and a golden light blade tore through the air. The sword energy surged out like a tsunami.
Before the twin mountain-like formations could reach him, they were split cleanly in half by Zenkichi's blade.
"Hell Stab: Three-Finger Spearhand!"
The Third Raikage roared, lightning erupting across his body as he charged toward Zenkichi like a living thunder tank.
Zenkichi's previous attack hadn't caused him much damage.
The Third Raikage was known to have the toughest physique among all shinobi—excluding non-human Six Paths beings.
With nearly unbreakable defense and the power of his Lightning Release Armor, he was the ultimate tank in the ninja world.
The Third Raikage in the original timeline had fought 10,000 enemy shinobi over three days and nights.
He wasn't killed in that battle; he died from sheer exhaustion after his own chakra reserves were depleted.
"What incredible speed!"
Zenkichi watched as the Raikage closed in. In an instant, his body scattered into countless golden lights, and he appeared mid-air—right above the Raikage's head.
A cross-shaped golden light bloomed under Zenkichi's feet as he kicked downward with a blinding volley, sending the Raikage flying.
"Speed is weight."
"The Third Raikage... You understand this better than anyone, right?"
Zenkichi said coolly. Their fighting styles were similar. Zenkichi relied on light-speed kicks and acceleration. The Third Raikage's power was also heavily based on the speed of his Lightning Release Chakra Mode.
In the original manga, the Fourth Raikage once clashed with Tsunade and managed to overpower her monstrous strength through speed-enhanced blows.
"So speed equals power?"
The Third Raikage stood up from the rubble, a storm of lightning raging around him.
"Then let's find out whose speed is stronger—yours or mine!"
The moment he finished speaking, his body turned into a blur of pure blue lightning.
He extended two fingers and pointed them at Zenkichi, dashing at him like a bolt of vengeance.
To the average eye, the Third Raikage looked like real lightning.
But to Zenkichi, he was still too slow.
Just like in One Piece, where CP9 agents using Soru moved too fast for normal people—but still not fast enough to match someone like Luffy in Second Gear.
And even Luffy in Second Gear struggled to match the speed of Kizaru.
"Hell Stab: Two-Finger Spearhand!"
"Laser."
As the Raikage charged with two fingers raised, Zenkichi casually lifted his own finger, golden light radiating from the tip.
A focused laser beam shot from his fingertip, colliding head-on with the Raikage's attack.
Golden energy and blue lightning clashed, canceling each other out. The Raikage's fierce offensive was completely blocked.
"Now's our chance!"
Chiyo's eyes gleamed as she gave orders to the sealing corps around her.
While Zenkichi was occupied with the Raikage, Chiyo planned to have him sealed.
Multiple seal-wielding shinobi from Sunagakure acted in unison, dark tendrils spreading from the ground toward Zenkichi.
"Annoying old crone."
Zenkichi shot a cold glare at Chiyo. Golden light burst from his body, scattering into shimmering particles that danced through the air before reassembling above.
"Sunagakure shinobi... Let me send you off properly."
He sneered, his form erupting in radiant gold. The blinding brilliance forced several people to hastily don sunglasses.
These sealing and sensory-nin had limited combat power. As Zenkichi dashed into their ranks, they crumbled like paper under the onslaught.
His tsunami-like sword aura tore through them. They couldn't stop him.
With a swift motion, he unsheathed the golden sword Ama no Congyun and waved it. A massive surge of sword energy roared forth.
Before anyone could react, Zenkichi's golden silhouette exploded into the crowd of Sunagakure nin.
"Damn it!"
Chiyo growled. These shinobi were vital to Sunagakure's forces.
"Zenkichi... I swear you'll die without a grave!"
Zenkichi shrugged at her words.
"How scary."
"If you're going to kill me, I might as well send you off first."
Seeing Chiyo activate the Ten Puppets of Chikamatsu, Zenkichi smirked and slashed with his lightsaber without hesitation.
"Earth Release: Earth Flow Rampart!"
Kitsuchi once again intervened, erecting a thick wall of stone to shield Chiyo.
But Zenkichi's blade shattered the rampart instantly, its sword energy crashing into the Chikamatsu puppets, forcing them back.
Chiyo relied on the ten puppets to absorb the rest of the impact, breathing a sigh of relief...
Until golden light shimmered above her.
The Chikamatsu puppets were obliterated.
Dense light bullets rained down like a storm, ripping through their defenses.
They struck Chiyo directly, ending her life in an instant.
Puppet masters are weak in direct combat. They rely on deception and poison. But even high-grade puppets made from rare materials couldn't withstand Zenkichi's Yasakani no Magatama.
The overwhelming light bullets shredded them into pieces in seconds.
Yasakani no Magatama!
"Goodbye, Chiyo."
Zenkichi descended from above, his eyes cold and voice like steel.

chapters.title: Chapter 61 - 61: Third Raikage Flees.
chapters.content:
"Sand Hidden Village Chiyo..."
Tsunade, who was watching the battle from a distance, was stunned and sighed with a complicated expression.
Although she and Chiyo were not from the same generation, they had been old enemies who clashed for many years.
Chiyo was Sunagakure's greatest puppet master and its most skilled poison expert. The poisons she crafted had brought immense suffering to Konohagakure.
And the one person Konoha could rely on to counter Chiyo's poisons was their finest medical ninja—Tsunade.
The reason Tsunade had been stationed in the Land of Rain this time was precisely to face Chiyo in battle.
But just now, her longtime opponent—Chiyo—was killed before her eyes by Zenkichi.
"Chiyo..."
The Third Raikage and Kitsuchi also wore complicated expressions.
As the enemy, Sunagakure had lost a Kage-level powerhouse—something that, under normal circumstances, would be a cause for celebration.
But in the current situation, Chiyo's death wasn't something they could feel pleased about.
—they might be next.
The Third Raikage's eyes sharpened, and murderous intent flared. Only the index finger of his left hand remained extended.
"Hell Stab—One-Fingered Assault!"
The Third Raikage roared as he launched his most powerful thrust, charging at Zenkichi like a bolt of lightning.
"Piercing Strike!"
"Kenjutsu Thrust!"
A golden lightsaber formed in Zenkichi's hand. He met the Third Raikage head-on with full power, unleashing terrifying force.
Invisible shockwaves shattered the surrounding terrain, sending massive chunks of earth skyward.
The devastating impact spread outward, forcing weaker ninja to retreat.
"Ahhh!"
The Third Raikage bellowed in frustration as he was knocked back.
Zenkichi's raw power had completely surpassed him.
"Sealing Corps, move!"
Kitsuchi gritted his teeth and ordered the sealing team into action.
It was Chiyo's provocation that had triggered Zenkichi's wrath in the first place. But now, Kitsuchi had no choice. If he didn't act, he would have to kneel and beg before Zenkichi.
"Trying again? Pointless."
Zenkichi's voice was calm as his body turned into golden light particles, instantly appearing behind Kitsuchi.
"Speed is weight."
"Have you ever been kicked at the speed of light?"
A lazy voice rang out behind Kitsuchi, sending a chill down his spine.
Zenkichi's foot glowed with a golden cross as he kicked forward. His strike landed squarely on Kitsuchi.
Kitsuchi's body flew through the air and shattered into stones mid-flight.
"Earth Clone? Nicely executed."
Zenkichi casually raised a hand and fired golden lasers at a boulder in the distance.
Boom!
The ground trembled. A rock wall rose to intercept the golden beams.
Boom!
The impact rocked the wall with a fierce explosion. A figure dashed from the smoke and flame.
"You're skilled at Earth Style."
Golden light shimmered as Zenkichi reappeared behind Kitsuchi. Without hesitation, he brought his sword down and severed one of Kitsuchi's arms with ease.
Kitsuchi screamed and fell back in panic.
Missing an arm, he was now useless—his Earth Release techniques required both hands. One-handed or seal-less Earth techniques were ineffective in comparison.
"Huh?"
After neutralizing Kitsuchi, Zenkichi frowned and looked toward the Third Raikage.
To his surprise, the Raikage had chosen to flee, taking the Kumogakure shinobi with him.
"Running away?"
Zenkichi was slightly taken aback. This was the Third Raikage—the man who once held off an army alone.
But thinking deeper, Zenkichi understood.
Given Zenkichi's current level of power, defeating him seemed impossible. In that case, escape was the wisest move.
In the original timeline, the Third Raikage died holding off enemy forces to protect Kumogakure's army.
But now, there was no army here—no reason to sacrifice himself for other villages.
Not for foreign ninja. Not even for the handful of Kumogakure soldiers.
The leaders of the great villages had to weigh cost against gain. No one with sense would risk everything for a few low-level soldiers.
Just like how the Second Hokage, in the original story, only chose to stay behind because he was protecting future leaders like Sarutobi Hiruzen. If it were just nameless Anbu, would he have made the same choice?
The Third Raikage might be headstrong, but he wasn't stupid.
"You won't escape. Too slow."
Zenkichi's body shone with golden light, transforming into countless particles as he flew toward the fleeing Kumo-nin.
In a flash, he appeared above the Third Raikage and his men. Light orbs formed in his palms.
"Yasakani no Magatama!"
A hailstorm of glowing projectiles rained down on the group below.
The Third Raikage and his elite struggled to withstand the bombardment.
Moments later, only the Raikage remained standing—his iron defense having saved him.
The rest of the Kumogakure shinobi were completely annihilated by Zenkichi's overwhelming attack.
"You bastard!"
Furious, the Third Raikage lunged at Zenkichi again, his index finger aimed to deliver another Hell Stab.
"Farewell, Third Raikage."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Zenkichi's expression was flat as he watched his opponent charge.
He raised a leg glowing with golden light, and his body vanished in a flash.
In the next instant, Zenkichi reappeared at the Raikage's side and delivered a blindingly fast kick.
His strike connected with the Raikage's wrist, redirecting the lethal thrust.
The Raikage's Hell Stab pierced his own chest—blood gushed from the wound.
"Left-handed?"
"Or did you adjust your strike to avoid hitting the heart?"
Zenkichi materialized before him, watching with curiosity.
The Raikage yanked out his hand. Lightning surged in his chest as he tried to cauterize the wound.
"Pointless struggle."
"You can't beat me."
Watching the gasping Raikage prepare for another desperate clash, Zenkichi shook his head and formed a blade of divine light—the Totsuka-no-Tsurugi.
"Let me end this."
He drove the sword forward, closing the chapter on the Third Raikage.

chapters.title: Chapter 62 - 62: Storytellers.
chapters.content:
"It is said that the Third Raikage has the strongest spear and the strongest shield. Now it seems that his spear is more powerful."
"He has the most powerful attack—Hell's Thrust. Zenkichi's hand pierced through the strongest shield the Raikage was so proud of. Neither the Lightning Armor nor his body could block it!"
Tsunade stood on the hillside in the distance, watching the fate of the Third Raikage with emotion.
The Third Raikage had been caught by Zenkichi, and after being pierced by his own Hell Thrust, the Thunder Armor was shattered and his life was already counting down.
The devastating power of the Hell Thrust not only broke through his armor and physical defenses—it also destroyed his internal organs.
Although the Third Raikage was left-handed, he couldn't pierce the heart on the left side of his chest using his right hand. Knowing he wouldn't escape, the Raikage smiled heroically and launched one final all-out attack, coating his index finger in Lightning Release chakra.
Zenkichi didn't move unnecessarily. Calm and direct, he formed a golden lightsaber and thrust it forward—sending the Third Raikage to his death.
Any other time, the wound might not have been fatal. But under Zenkichi's Observation Haki, even a slight injury to vital organs meant a rapid decline in combat effectiveness.
And unfortunately for the Raikage, the chest wound from his own strike had ruptured crucial organs.
"This is the final thrust from hell…"
The Third Raikage roared.
"Go to hell and stab!"
Zenkichi replied indifferently. The tip of his golden lightsaber clashed with the Raikage's finger, completely overpowering it.
"Are you going to run too?"
After killing the Third Raikage, Zenkichi turned his gaze to the distance, where no one remained in sight.
Everyone in that direction had used Earth Release—Iwagakure's Jutsu—to escape underground.
But hiding beneath the earth was useless against Zenkichi's Observation Haki.
His body turned into golden light, soaring into the sky. Then, countless golden light orbs rained down.
Yasakani no Magatama!
The sky filled with deafening roars as the densely packed golden orbs bombarded the earth.
They pierced through the soil, killing many Iwagakure ninjas and burying them underground forever.
Others were driven out by the pressure of the golden barrage, forced back to the surface.
A moment later—
Kitsuchi, who had lost an arm, stood before Zenkichi with a group of defeated Iwagakure ninjas.
"Why do you insist on running? I don't want to kill you."
Zenkichi stood before them, shaking his head with pity.
Kitsuchi glared at him coldly, eyes filled with disbelief.
Zenkichi shrugged helplessly. "You're being unfair. Just because you attacked me and tried to take my life—does that mean I have to kill you?"
"After all, you're so weak. Even if you want to kill me, it wouldn't make a difference."
Zenkichi sighed. His words made Kitsuchi's face flush red with shame—he nearly spat blood from the insult.
"So, you're safe."
"I've decided to spare your lives. You can go."
Zenkichi smiled and waved his hand, allowing them to leave.
Kitsuchi and the other Iwagakure ninjas exchanged confused glances, unsure what Zenkichi was planning.
"Zenkichi, what are you playing at? Just say it!"
After a moment of hesitation, Kitsuchi spoke coldly.
"There's really nothing."
"You saw it yourself—powerful figures like Chiyo and the Third Raikage were killed by me."
"Wouldn't it be a waste if no one spread word of such a glorious event?"
"So…you're lucky enough to be chosen as my storytellers. That's why I let you go."
Zenkichi explained lazily, causing the group's expressions to darken.
That's why they were spared…
Although it felt humiliating, none of them were foolish enough to take their own lives.
"Can't they be storytellers?"
Kitsuchi glanced at Tsunade and the others in the distance, sneering as he spoke to Zenkichi.
He didn't believe for a second that Zenkichi hadn't noticed them.
"I noticed."
"But having them alone as witnesses isn't enough."
"Humans are short-sighted. They might not believe I have this kind of strength."
"Your village might even blame Konoha for your deaths."
"So…"
Zenkichi looked at Loess and the others and explained lazily.
"I got it."
Kitsuchi gave Zenkichi a deep look, then turned toward Tsunade and the others. A flicker of hatred flashed in his eyes.
It was unfair. It wasn't just loss—it was imbalance.
They all came for the same reason, with the same goals.
So why was Konoha safe and sound while everyone else suffered and died?
Noticing Kitsuchi's envious stare, Zenkichi smiled faintly and instantly appeared before Tsunade with a flicker of movement.
"What do you want?"
Tsunade exhaled and asked him as calmly as she could.
"Nothing."
"I just wanted to tell you that you're free to tell others exactly what happened today."
"I'm curious to see how the major ninja villages will react."Google seaʀᴄh ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Zenkichi gave a light smile and spoke casually.
"All those things you did back in Konoha—there were hidden motives, weren't there?"
"Don't deny it. I've figured it out."
Tsunade stared at him and spoke firmly.
"Tsunade, do you remember the question I once asked you?"
"Well, I have the answer now."
"The reason the great villages attack Konoha is because they're all in competition."
"If you think of the ninja villages as shopping malls, then Konoha is the one with the best layout."
"People go to Konoha to show off, and most of the customers are pulled in by Konoha's allure."
"If the competition continues peacefully, Konoha will eventually crush all the others and leave them behind."
"So the other villages start wars to drag everyone down—buying themselves time."
"That's the truth of the Shinobi World War: the village leaders—the shopping mall owners—starting conflict to protect their interests."
"When you tried to kill me just now, it wasn't to uphold peace. It was to protect your own assets."
"If we want true peace, the selfish ones need to step aside."
Zenkichi narrowed his eyes, speaking with resolve.

chapters.title: Chapter 63 - 63: Child Of Prophecy.
chapters.content:
Tsunade let out a breath and said with a somewhat complicated expression, "Sure enough! So, the current situation in Konoha is all caused by you."
Zenkichi shook his head. "No. The current state of Konoha was inevitable. I merely accelerated the process and pulled off its fig leaf."
"Without me, Konoha would appear prosperous on the surface—but its decay is rooted deep within. No matter how well you dress it up, it's still rotting."
"Unless someone overwhelmingly powerful appears, Konoha will collapse eventually. Too many corrupt roots were buried long ago."
"To be honest, your grandfather Senju Hashirama made a huge mistake. He should have united the shinobi world while he had the chance. That was the best opportunity for peace."
"The First Hokage was too naive. He believed everyone wanted peace as he did—but that was impossible. This world has never lacked evil."
"The village system was meant to bring peace."
"But now the cart has come before the horse."
"To protect the village, people are willing to start wars."
"If the five great shinobi villages were to merge, war would disappear from the world."
"But is that possible?"
"Would the leaders of the five villages be willing to give up their power? Absolutely not."
"They're obsessed with their own interests—their vision is far too narrow."
"If the world is to know true peace, it must be unified."
"This world needs a single will and a strict teacher."The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"I will bring unity to this world—and no one can stop me."
Zenkichi's voice grew passionate as he stared at Tsunade, eyes filled with unwavering determination.
Tsunade turned her head, avoiding his gaze. "Even so… Aren't you afraid I'll tell others?"
Zenkichi smirked. "Tsunade, what makes you think I'm ashamed of my beliefs?"
"Even if the leaders of the five great villages stood before me, I'd say the same thing to their faces."
"Because compared to me, their power is insignificant."
Tsunade's expression stiffened, at a loss for words.
"Goodbye."
"I'm sure we'll meet again soon."
Zenkichi waved to Tsunade, then, with a flicker, appeared on the devastated battlefield. He began collecting the bodies of key figures—Uchiha Madara, the Third Raikage, and Chiyo.
If possible, Tsunade truly didn't want to face Zenkichi again. After a moment of silence, she said slowly, "Whether what he said is true or not… you'll have to decide for yourself."
Yahiko was quiet for a moment. He looked up at her. "Is what he said true?"
Jiraiya gave a bitter smile but said nothing.
Tsunade looked off into the distance, her back to them. "No need to hide. He already knows you're here."
After Zenkichi departed, Jiraiya led Yahiko and Konan out of the woods nearby.
The corpses of powerful shinobi are valuable sources of intelligence. Zenkichi sealed them into scrolls, intending to send them to Kirigakure for analysis.
"The reason he told me all that was probably for your ears as well," Tsunade said.
"I've heard about the Akatsuki you founded. Your intent to regulate war is admirable."
"But this world isn't as simple as you think. The causes of war are complex."
"A village isn't a person. It makes decisions based on logic, not emotion. Emotional wars are rare."
"So your idea of regulating war isn't realistic. You can't offer the villages what they seek when they go to war."
"Ninety percent of wars are for profit. And sadly, your Akatsuki can't give them what they want."
"Zenkichi said the other villages attacked Konoha because they feared its rapid growth."
"One major reason may be to seize Konoha's resources for their own benefit."
"That's their goal. Can Akatsuki stop such wars?"
"Even though your organization has had some success, I'll be blunt—"
"Those results weren't because of Akatsuki. It was because those villages were already ready to negotiate and just used you as a convenient tool."
Perhaps spurred on by Zenkichi's words, Tsunade explained things to Yahiko with a complicated look.
When Tsunade originally left Konoha, she had clearly seen its darkness and decay.
Even so, she returned and became the Fifth Hokage—proof enough that she wasn't lacking in intelligence or foresight.
While her style appears direct and rough, even reckless…
Don't forget—Tsunade is the greatest medical-nin in the shinobi world.
Someone who deals with life and death on a daily basis cannot be careless.
She has a subtle, sharp mind.
Yahiko was silent for a moment. He looked at Jiraiya and asked, "Master Jiraiya, what happened to the child of prophecy you mentioned before?"
Jiraiya responded with a somber tone, "The creature I signed a summoning contract with is from Mount Myōboku—one of the three great sage regions. The Great Toad Sage has the ability to foresee the future."
"He prophesied that I would train a disciple who would either bring destruction to or save the shinobi world. Because Nagato possessed the Rinnegan, I believed he was that child."
Yahiko smiled, though his expression was complicated. "Since you believed Nagato could lead the world to salvation or ruin, why did you neglect him for so long?"
"If he truly could shape the future of the world, shouldn't he have mattered more to you? Why did you stay away for so long? If we were just ordinary apprentices, fine—but shouldn't the fate of the world have changed your priorities?"
"Jiraiya-sensei… Can you tell me why?"
"Don't lie. I'll find out the truth later."
Yahiko's tone was calm, but distant—and it left Jiraiya silent.
After a long pause, Jiraiya sighed. "Because I found another possible child of prophecy."
Yahiko's voice dropped. "Who?"
Jiraiya answered, "He's the Yellow Flash of Konoha. You've heard of him, right?"
Yahiko chuckled bitterly. "I see. Rather than Nagato—who carries the burdens of the Rain Country—you'd rather place your hopes in Namikaze Minato, who was born and raised in Konoha?"
---

chapters.title: Chapter 64 - 64: Explanation from 3 Villages.
chapters.content:
"Our origins make you doubtful, but Namikaze Minato's background can reassure you."
"In other words, you're unwilling to let Nagato lead the ninja world from the bottom of your heart, because it might endanger Konoha's interests."
"I didn't expect even you, Jiraiya-sensei, to be so narrow-minded. It's understandable for others, but… you're the one who trained the Child of Prophecy!"
"Isn't the child of prophecy meant to lead the entire ninja world? Why must he remain fixated on Konoha?"
"You raised him with that mindset—do you want him to reshape the ninja world into one dominated by Konoha?"
Yahiko looked at Jiraiya with disappointment in his eyes.
Looking back, Jiraiya truly hadn't been a responsible teacher. He had failed the role of mentor to the child of prophecy.
In the original story, the reason he took in Nagato and the others was because of Nagato's Rinnegan. He believed Nagato might be the child of prophecy, so he taught all three—but it was really Nagato he cared about. Yahiko and Konan were just along for the ride.
Yet after training them, he left. Not once, but several times, abandoning them for years. If Pain hadn't emerged, Jiraiya might never have remembered them again.
If their relationship was just that of teacher and student, it wouldn't have been so bad. Letting the students grow on their own makes sense.
But considering Nagato had the Rinnegan—and was possibly the child of prophecy, the one destined to change the ninja world—Jiraiya's neglect was irresponsible.
And what about Namikaze Minato, another disciple Jiraiya valued and believed could be the child of prophecy?
What did Jiraiya do?
After Minato became the Fourth Hokage, Jiraiya left the village to wander the world. If he had been in Konoha when Uchiha Obito attacked, maybe things would've turned out differently.
If he had stood beside Minato when Obito made his move, or been there when others tried to influence Nagato, maybe Nagato wouldn't have lost his way.
As the supposed guide of the child of prophecy, Jiraiya failed that role.
When you really think about it, Jiraiya acted like he was casting a wide net—constantly searching for whoever might be "the one." Like a womanizer chasing prospects, once he was done, he moved on to the next. And those he left behind? Forgotten.
If they died, that only meant they weren't the chosen one.
Yahiko spoke slowly, voice filled with bitterness: "Nagato was captured by those two strange individuals. We… we don't have the power to save him."
This kind of thinking was dangerous. No wonder even Tsunade looked down on him.
---
"The Akatsuki we founded together now feels like a joke. I've decided to leave the Land of Rain for a while."
Jiraiya frowned. "Where are you planning to go?"
"I'm heading to Kirigakure to find Zenkichi. What he said earlier truly inspired me. Maybe he holds the key to realizing my dream."
Jiraiya fell silent, clearly unwilling to let his student seek out a former enemy.
But seeing the growing rift between himself and Yahiko, he could only sigh and nod.
---
Kirigakure Village
Ever since Zenkichi subdued the Kaguya Clan, Kirigakure had grown far more stable and peaceful.
Upon his return, Zenkichi headed straight for the Mizukage's office and tossed a scroll onto his desk.
"Inside are the bodies of Uchiha Madara, the Third Raikage, and Chiyo from Sunagakure. Have them examined."
"The corpse of a powerful shinobi is a treasure trove of secrets. See what you can learn from them."
The Third Mizukage caught the scroll midair, puzzled. Just as he was about to ask what it contained, Zenkichi spoke—and the words made his hand tremble.
"Whose bodies are you talking about?"
"The legend of the shinobi world, the Shura—Uchiha Madara."
"The commander of Kumogakure—The Third Raikage."
"And the greatest puppet master and poison expert of Sunagakure—Chiyo."
Zenkichi's tone was calm, but the names struck the Mizukage like thunderclaps.
With shaking hands, the Mizukage unsealed the scroll. Three corpses appeared in his office, their faces unmistakably familiar. His eyes twitched.
"Is this… frail old man really Uchiha Madara?"
"If we're going by age, it makes sense he'd look like this."
"But how did you confirm his identity? Age spots don't prove anything."
"I didn't find him," Zenkichi replied coolly. "He found me. He used a forbidden jutsu to restore his youth."
"Unfortunately for him, even in his prime, he couldn't defeat me."
"As for the Third Raikage and Chiyo…"
"They sensed the battle between me and Madara and tried to interfere, hoping we'd weaken each other."
"But they misjudged my strength. I killed them both."
Zenkichi's tone remained casual. The Third Mizukage could only let out a bitter smile.
"The Third Raikage and Chiyo… those two were giants in the shinobi world."
"If you killed them, those villages won't let this go."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
He wasn't wrong—but neither was he overly concerned.
With Zenkichi in Kirigakure, they had nothing to fear.
"So what if they don't let it go?"
"I already defeated Konoha. Why would I be afraid of them?"
"If anything, I'm the one who should be demanding answers."
"They tried to take advantage of the situation. I was only defending myself."
"Send a message to Kumogakure, Iwagakure, and Sunagakure!"
"They owe us an explanation."
Zenkichi sneered. He clearly didn't take the threat of those villages seriously.
"Iwagakure?" the Mizukage asked. "What does this have to do with them?"
"Oh, right. Ōnoki's son, Kitsuchi, also showed up and tried to interfere. I didn't kill him, though. Just broke one of his arms and sent him back."
Zenkichi spoke like it was nothing, as if describing a sparring match.
"You really are…"
The Mizukage sighed, helpless.
"No more chatter. Send their bodies to the Interrogation Division. See if we can extract any valuable intel."
"As for reparations or consequences—we can handle that discussion later."
Zenkichi scoffed and cast a glance at the corpses.

chapters.title: Chapter 65 - 65: Sunagakure.
chapters.content:
"Really!"
"I knew the death of Konoha's White Fang wasn't that simple… using his head to appease Chiyo of Sunagakure?"
"That move eliminates internal threats and pacifies external enemies. A masterstroke."
"It's a shame something like this can't be brought to light. If the Konoha shinobi ever find out…"
Zenkichi looked at the report in his hand, a playful smile tugging at his lips. He was already considering the terms he'd offer Sunagakure.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
"Send a message to Sunagakure."
"Send me the so-called hero of the Hidden Sand, the Burning Release kunoichi—Pakura"
"Tell them we want to burn her alive."
"This is the price Chiyo should pay for trying to use me."
"If they refuse, I'll pay Sunagakure a visit myself."
Zenkichi smiled faintly, speaking as though it was of no consequence.
The Third Mizukage thought: The Burning Release user Pakura of the Hidden Sand? She's a rising star in Sunagakure… Would they really give her up?
Zenkichi responded with certainty, "They'll agree."
"Tell them they don't need to get their hands dirty."
"Just use a confidential mission as a pretext to lure her out."
"They were involved in the White Fang's death—they know this method well."
"Besides…"
"The Fourth Kazekage, Rasa, will help us."
A sneer curled on Zenkichi's lips, his tone laced with mockery.
Pakura wasn't part of the Kazekage bloodline, yet her strength and prestige rivaled it.
Could someone like Rasa truly tolerate her presence?
This had already been hinted at in the original events.
Zenkichi thought to himself: Kumogakure and Iwagakure… these two villages are relatively united. Typical methods of sowing discord won't work.
Forget it. Just request some supplies from them.
The Third Mizukage asked, "Sunagakure's terms are set. What about the other three major shinobi villages?"
To them, Zenkichi's proposal was a generous offer—it gave Sunagakure a way out and a reason to get rid of Pakura.
In other words, the top brass of Sunagakure feared the power of the Burning Release and sought to eliminate her.
Their public justification simply didn't hold water.
These were villages that had clashed to the point of killing each other's leaders.
How deep was that hatred?
Even in history, the Second Mizukage and Second Tsuchikage died in battle with each other.
If these villages were truly separated by vast distances, how did such battles even happen?
If distance were a true barrier, then Kirigakure and Iwagakure wouldn't have clashed in previous wars.
In reality, the Land of Water and the Land of Earth are separated by sea, but are geographically closer than the Land of Water and the Land of Wind.
Even though a continent lies between Kirigakure and Iwagakure, this is a globe—the world of Naruto is round.
A look at the ninja world map reveals that even a sneak attack from Kirigakure could reach Iwagakure.
The excuse given by Sunagakure was that they feared a surprise attack from Kirigakure while fighting Iwagakure.
And so, Pakura was betrayed by her own superiors, sent to Kirigakure under false pretenses—and executed.
"Sunagakure is so poor they'd rather sacrifice a shinobi than pay for resources. That's unlike Iwagakure and Kumogakure—both wealthy villages."
In the chaotic world of shinobi, those two villages stood out—relatively stable, with little internal conflict.
That very stability allowed them to grow and eventually rival Konoha.
Throughout the Naruto series, Kumogakure never produced a major missing-nin. No other village can claim that.
While Iwagakure gave rise to Deidara, he didn't defect willingly—he was coerced by the Akatsuki.
Initially, like Roshi , he simply left the village. Neither had scratched-out headbands at the time.
Still, it didn't mean these villages had no problems—they were just harder to exploit.
And Zenkichi didn't yet have the leverage to do so.
---
The Land of Rain — Sunagakure's Forward Base
Ebizo, overseeing operations here, received word of Chiyo's death at the hands of Zenkichi.
His expression darkened.
"Sister…"
"Zenkichi—I'll kill you for this!"
He gritted his teeth, killing intent surging from his body.
His bond with Chiyo ran deep—not just siblings by blood, but comrades in arms for decades.
Upon hearing she had been killed by Zenkichi, Ebizo flew into a rage.
In contrast, Rasa—the newly appointed Fourth Kazekage—reacted quite differently.
Though now the leader of the village, real power remained with Chiyo and Ebizo. That had long infuriated him.
Despite acknowledging Chiyo's combat prowess, Rasa couldn't help but feel relief at her demise.
He bore the same ruthless confidence as Danzo.
He believed that consolidating power in his own hands would be best for the village.
---
"You want me to hand over Pakura to die?"
Rasa looked at the message from Kirigakure, a smile tugging at the corners of his lips.
Two birds, one stone.
He was tempted to send Kirigakure a thank-you gift.
Yes, the village would lose two shinobi of Kage-level strength. But Rasa didn't think it was a major loss.
Powerful shinobi were important—but a unified village that obeyed him? Far more valuable.
Sunagakure's barren terrain meant few dared to invade. External enemies weren't the real danger—internal division was.
If Chiyo and Pakura weren't dealt with carefully, the result could be civil war.
That risk was far greater than the loss of two elite shinobi.
Kage-level power could be cultivated again. But a village torn apart might never recover.
After all, a strong fortress often crumbles from within.
---
"Zenkichi of Kirigakure… I won't forget you."
"If the seal could destroy you…"
A cold sneer curved on Rasa's face.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 66 - 66: Old Relic.
chapters.content:
Cloud Hidden Village – Kumogakure
After receiving news that the Third Raikage had been killed in battle, a storm of curses broke out across Kumogakure. Soon after, the Fourth Raikage was appointed.
Unlike the chaos that typically plagued other villages during succession, the next Raikage had been decided long ago.
When the Fourth Raikage fought side by side with Killer Bee, he had already made up his mind—he would be the next to wear the mantle of Raikage.
Raikage's Office
The Fourth Raikage glared at a letter from Kirigakure, then slammed his palm onto the desk, shattering it in fury.
"Damn it!"
Sparks of lightning crackled across his body as he roared. His eyes were locked on the letter.
"Kirigakure is going too far!"
"They killed my father, and now they have the nerve to demand compensation from us? This is outrageous!"
His voice echoed through the room.
"Lord Raikage, please calm down."
A calm voice came from a man with oil paint streaked across the right side of his face. He was Blue B—the current Eight-Tails Jinchūriki and the Raikage's cousin.
Strong, disciplined, and capable of suppressing the power of the Eight-Tails, Blue B was one of the strongest shinobi in Kumogakure. Because of both his power and lineage, he served as the Raikage's right hand.
In the original timeline, he had fallen to a trap by Orochimaru—poisoned by genjutsu-inducing drugs and devoured after the Eight-Tails was forcibly extracted from him.
But now...
Thanks to the interference of Zenkichi, Orochimaru had yet to target him. Blue B still lived.
Blue B advised, "Zenkichi of Kirigakure is not someone to be taken lightly. If we reject their terms outright, we may put the entire village in jeopardy."
The Fourth Raikage growled, "So we're supposed to just roll over and let Kirigakure push us around?"
Blue B shook his head, offering a faint smile. "Of course not. Zenkichi is powerful, and Kirigakure is getting arrogant."
"They've provoked not just us, but Konoha, Sunagakure, and Iwagakure too. Four of the Five Great Shinobi Nations have grievances with them."
"I suggest we bide our time—send them some supplies to lull them into a false sense of peace, and when the time is right, we strike together with the others."
The Fourth Raikage's eyes lit up with understanding. "Yes… this is a solid plan. Why should we alone take the lead? Let the other villages pull their weight."Googlᴇ search No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
"If we act now, we'll only wear ourselves down and give Konoha and the others a chance to swoop in and benefit. We can't let those snakes outmaneuver us."
He cursed the other hidden villages with disdain.
After a moment, the Raikage added, "Fine. If they want supplies, they'll get them. But they'd better return my father's body."
Blue B nodded. "We should issue that demand jointly with Sunagakure. They're still missing Chiyo's remains—Kirigakure is holding them too."
---
Iwagakure
"Uchiha Madara is still alive? Are you sure?"
The Third Tsuchikage, Ōnoki, stared seriously at his son, Kitsuchi.
Ōnoki carried a deep grudge toward Uchiha Madara. As a young shinobi, he had once faced Madara in his prime and had been crushed.
Madara had long since forgotten that battle. But Ōnoki never did. The memory haunted him.
Kitsuchi spoke cautiously, "From what our scouts observed, it seems Madara really was alive—though very old."
"Most likely, he used some forbidden method to temporarily regain his peak strength."
"But that power didn't last. He was eventually overwhelmed and killed by Zenkichi."
"One of our sensory ninja reported that Madara's chakra suddenly collapsed at one point—it fits."
Ōnoki let out a long breath. "So he finally died…"
"I can't believe Madara lived all the way from the Warring States Era to now. He's like some ancient relic that refused to disappear."
"Has there ever been anyone more stubborn?"
Ōnoki muttered bitterly, a look of complex emotion on his face.
"Father, what should we do about the letter from Kirigakure?" Kitsuchi asked once his father had calmed.
"Kirigakure again…"
"Ever since Zenkichi appeared, they've become insufferable."
"They crippled my son, and now they want compensation from me?"
Ōnoki scoffed, killing intent in his voice.
"Father, don't act rashly," Kitsuchi warned. "I've fought Zenkichi before—he's not a normal shinobi."
"His abilities are bizarre. He shrugs off all attacks."
"Just like the rumors say, only high-level sealing techniques affect him… but those are too slow. He's far too fast."
"In short, we still don't have an effective counter."
Ōnoki snorted. "Don't worry. I won't rush in blindly."
"We've got allies. When the time comes, we move together."
Kitsuchi furrowed his brow. "Allies? I have to remind you, Father… when we last tried to take out Zenkichi, Tsunade from Konoha stood by and watched."
"We all coordinated the assault. But after a few words from Zenkichi, she did nothing."
"That shows we can't trust Konoha too much. They may backstab us."
"Maybe Zenkichi did something in Konoha that shook their spirit. Now they don't even dare confront him."
Ōnoki nodded slowly. "That's a good point. Then we'll reach out to Kumogakure and Sunagakure first."
"They've both lost high-ranking shinobi to Zenkichi. They won't let it slide."
"As for those hotheads in Kumogakure… there's no doubt they'll want revenge."
"I hear the new Raikage is the son of the last one?"
"Hmph. Like father, like son. If the father was a reckless brute, the son can't be much better."
Ōnoki sneered coldly.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 67 - 67: Pakura.
chapters.content:
I changed the fanfiction name, since it'd be more than just Kizaru's template in the future.
__
The Kingdom of Water, in a canyon.
Amidst the mist, a woman in smart clothing walked slowly from the distance.
"Pakura of the Hidden Sand Village?"
A deep voice rang out, and Zenkichi slowly stepped forward toward the well-dressed woman.
"It's me! Zenkichi from the Hidden Mist Village?"
Pakura looked at Zenkichi with a hint of curiosity and wariness in her eyes.
Zenkichi's strength made her uneasy; her mission made her defensive.
"By order of the Fourth Kazekage, I've come to negotiate with your Hidden Mist Village. Please rest assured—I have the full authority to speak on behalf of Sunagakure."
Pakura's voice was calm. The Fourth Kazekage had ordered her to secretly negotiate with Kirigakure.
"Negotiate? That guy Rasa really sent someone for this nonsense? You're naive. Don't you think this task is ridiculous?"
"What right does Sunagakure have to negotiate with Kirigakure right now? He sent you here to die!"
Zenkichi shook his head and chuckled, then said casually.
"Nonsense!"
Pakura's expression changed, and several fireballs suddenly materialized around her.
The fireballs radiated a blazing orange light, their high temperatures warping the air.
"Scorch Release fireballs? Interesting."
Zenkichi commented indifferently. A faint golden glow enveloped his body—the elemental form ignored the extreme heat.
Pakura didn't attack immediately, instead stepping backward. The burning orbs orbited around her like vigilant guards.
"Scared? Trying to run?"
Zenkichi gave a lazy smile, his right index finger glowing with a brilliant golden light.
"Fireball!"
Pakura's eyes flickered as the Scorch Release fireball surged toward Zenkichi.
"Scorch Release—Steaming Kill!"
This technique could evaporate water within a human body—a deadly Kekkei Genkai.
But Zenkichi didn't move. He stood firm, letting the fireball strike his body.
The fireball hissed and flared, engulfing him in blistering heat—but it had no effect.
"It's useless."
"I am light. Light can't be burned."
"And light contains no moisture."
Zenkichi stated calmly, raising one hand and firing a laser from his finger. The golden beam shot toward Pakura.
Pakura reacted quickly, displaying impressive physical agility as she narrowly dodged the laser.
Boom!
Zenkichi's laser struck the cliff behind her, blasting rock into the canyon and blocking her escape.
"Do you really intend to kill me?"
"You agreed to negotiate and now want to break your promise?"
"You'd tarnish Kirigakure's name just to eliminate me? Is my life that valuable?"
Pakura's voice was cold and composed now, her anger contained.
"Do you think this is about a broken promise? Naive."
"Your fate was sealed the moment the negotiation was proposed."
"Sunagakure abandoned you. They sent you here to die—so I could vent my rage. Understand?"
Zenkichi's words darkened Pakura's expression.
"Are you joking?"
Pakura asked, keeping her tone steady.
"What do you think?"
Zenkichi replied lazily, studying her with amusement.
Pakura fell silent.
Zenkichi laughed. "So you're starting to believe me. Did Rasa show his hand too early? What a joke."
Pakura answered coldly, "Whether you're telling the truth or not, I'll confirm it myself."
"For now, killing you is all that matters."
Zenkichi smirked. "Kill me? How terrifying. Female shinobi from Sunagakure sure are bold—brash, even. I like it."
Pakura snorted and drew a long scroll from her body, flicking it open with a snap. The scroll lunged toward Zenkichi like a serpent.
"This is… a sealing technique?"
Zenkichi recognized it instantly.
It was a type of ninja tool reinforced with sealing arts—similar to what the Shinobi Alliance used to suppress reanimated foes with red talismans during the Fourth Great Ninja War.
"Pakura, you really did your homework."
"Sealing techniques do work on me, but…"
"Your attack speed isn't enough. I move at the speed of light."
With a casual sigh, Zenkichi's body scattered into particles of light and reformed behind Pakura, his hand gently landing on her shoulder.
"Don't panic."
"I'm not here to kill you. I believe we can still talk."
He spoke slowly, his palm holding her in place without hostility, though she didn't dare move.
"What are you trying to do?"
Pakura asked coldly, a trace of panic in her voice.
"You still think there's a chance, right?"
"You believe I'm lying and that Sunagakure didn't betray you."
"Then how about I give you a chance to find out?"
"Just disappear. Don't take action. Just watch."
"I'm betting—soon enough, Sunagakure will publicly declare you dead."
"They won't need a body. All they'll need is Kirigakure's confirmation."Thɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Think about it."
Zenkichi's eyes gleamed as he looked at her with a mischievous edge.
Pakura's tone hardened. "What kind of confirmation?"
Zenkichi grinned. "Only three words… 'Everything goes well.'"
"Sunagakure will announce your death, but they'll never mention you died in the Land of Water."
"After all, this was a covert mission. No one knows where you went—except for you and the higher-ups."
Pakura's face turned pale.
After a long pause, she murmured, "None of what you said is confirmed. Everything could be a lie."
Zenkichi answered evenly, "Could be. Then wait and see."
"But in the meantime, come back to Kirigakure with me. Use a transformation jutsu—don't show your real face."
"And don't try anything foolish. If you do, I'll kill you myself. Believe me… you can't beat me."
Zenkichi's words were calm, but left no room for doubt.
Pakura nodded silently, signaling her compliance.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 68: Four Kage Summit.
chapters.content:
Half a month later.
In a town in the Land of Wind, Zenkichi and Pakura sat across from each other.
At this time, both were using the Transformation Jutsu to disguise their appearances. In the nearby alley, a Sunagakure shinobi was on patrol.
"You should be worried now, right?"
Zenkichi raised his teacup and said casually.
"I really didn't expect it..."
"But thinking back, there were actually many clues in the past."
"It's funny how I was too naive at the time to notice the signs, let alone the danger hidden within them."
Pakura sighed, her expression tinged with complexity.
"Now I have a question. Why did you help me?"
"Don't tell me you saved me without any reason."
"For Kirigakure, killing me—a Suna shinobi—would've been the safest move, right?"
"Or… do you think you can recruit me?"
Pakura looked at Zenkichi with intrigue.
"To recruit you? Yeah, that was the idea."
"How about it—work with me?"
Zenkichi smiled, completely unashamed.
Pakura pondered. "What's your goal?"
Zenkichi said, "The First Hokage created the one-country-one-village system. After decades of practice, it's clear that it's a failure."
"The wars and disasters caused by decaying villages aren't much different from the chaos of the Warring States era."
"If anything, the only difference is the age of the soldiers."
"Back then, kids as young as four or five were sent to war. Now, they're at least six or seven."
"I've decided to change the current ninja world and reshape it according to my own ideals."
"I've imagined these changes countless times—now I finally have the chance to make them real."
A light flashed in Zenkichi's eyes, and a bright smile crossed his face.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Pakura asked thoughtfully, "According to your ideals? What kind of world are you trying to create?"
Zenkichi smiled. "At the very least, a world where someone like you—an upright fool—won't be discarded so easily."
Pakura smiled faintly. "Alright. I'm in. What do you want me to do?"
Zenkichi mused, "Originally, I thought of having you return to Sunagakure and wrestle for power with Rasa. But the more I think about it, the less necessary that seems."
Pakura sighed. "You sure think big. Rasa is the Fourth Kazekage. I'm just a jōnin with a bit of fame."
"Even if people call me a hero of Sunagakure, I'm still far beneath him in status and influence."
"Fight him for power? That's just not realistic."
Zenkichi scoffed. "Really? I don't think it's that hard. Rasa's thinking is… unorthodox, to put it nicely. Beating him wouldn't be that difficult."
'Just look at his ridiculous decisions in the original timeline!'
'Before Gaara was born, Rasa sealed Shukaku inside him. His wife died giving birth. All because of Rasa.'
'And to test the seal's effectiveness, he even had his brother-in-law try to assassinate Gaara.'
'Gaara killed him. Rasa couldn't stop him. And that only pushed Gaara further into darkness.'
'And that's not all. Rasa tried multiple times to kill his own son. His logic is twisted beyond saving.'
'So why not find the right moment to form a special unit? Someone like Pakura, whose strength and reputation rival Rasa's, could very well rise to the top.'
'For now, looking at the reactions from the other major villages, we probably don't have to wait long.'
'But thinking about it again—it might be too troublesome and time-consuming. Maybe it's not worth it.'
'His strange policies will ruin his reputation on their own. With the way his mind works, getting played into a corner is inevitable. It'll be hilarious.'
'A man like Rasa should just step down.'
'Even after he was reincarnated by the Edo Tensei, he was a disgrace. Gaara sealed him with no resistance.'
'He was the only one among the three Kage-level shinobi who couldn't break free of the Edo Tensei.'
'And the way he died? Taken down by Gaara and Kimimaro. It was pathetic.'
"Judging from the current situation, it's best to keep the fact that you're still alive under wraps. When I launch my assault on Sunagakure, you'll appear and destroy their morale."
Zenkichi had decided—Pakura's appearance would shatter Sunagakure's fighting spirit.
But this tactic would only work once, so her survival had to remain a secret.
If Sunagakure caught wind of it, they'd spin the narrative and weaken the effect.
Pakura shrugged. "So you're telling me my current mission is… doing nothing? Just hiding?"
Zenkichi replied seriously, "If you're bored, you can wear a mask and act as my personal ANBU."
"Of course, you'll need to avoid using your signature Scorch Release. That won't be a problem, will it?"
Pakura said proudly, "Don't underestimate me. Even without Scorch Release, I'm more than capable of holding my own as an elite jōnin."
"I'm proficient in taijutsu, shurikenjutsu, wind release, and fire release."
Zenkichi nodded approvingly. "In that case, starting today, you're my personal ANBU."
"Your codename will be… 'Y'. What do you think?"
Pakura answered calmly, "No problem. But more importantly—I want to hear your next move."
"If you plan to change the world, you must have a real strategy, right?"
Zenkichi smiled. "Next, we're heading overseas. I'm calling back all of my loyal disciples and subordinates."
"The four major villages are about to act. We need to see what moves they'll make."
"At the very least, they'll definitely unite to face me—the common enemy."
"Maybe we'll even see a Four Kage Summit. Just thinking about it is exciting. When that happens, we'll make our move."
"Even if it doesn't have the prestige of a Five Kage Summit, it's still a rare, high-level gathering."
Under the joint initiative of Iwagakure and Kumogakure, Sunagakure, Iwagakure, and Kumogakure had reached a preliminary agreement.
Now, they were trying to pull Konoha in as well.
They didn't want Konoha standing on the sidelines.
Although Tsunade's previous decisions had left a bitter taste, Konoha's power was too significant to ignore.
---
