chapters.title: Chapter 84 - 84: Leave and return stronger.
chapters.content:
"You want to take the Four-Tails from my body?"
Seeing Zenkichi approaching with the sealing cauldron, Roshi sneered.
Once the Tailed Beast was removed from his body, he would die as a Jinchūriki. But he was already seriously injured and had no strength left to resist.
"In that case…"
A fierce look flashed in Roshi's eyes as he shifted his consciousness into the sealed space within and directly released the beast himself.
Red Tailed Beast Chakra erupted from his body, forming into a giant, red-furred monkey. The Four-Tails, Son Gokū, let out a deafening roar.
"Releasing the Four-Tails?"
"You'd rather die than let me take it easily?"
"How scary~" Zenkichi said lazily, eyes hidden behind his sunglasses as he looked up at the beast.
"Should I split this Tailed Beast up?"
"…Forget it. Let's decide later."
He murmured to himself, then turned his attention to knocking the beast down first.
Son Gokū didn't hesitate. The moment it appeared, it opened its mouth, gathering a massive amount of chakra.
Tailed Beast Bomb.
Knowing Zenkichi's power from within Roshi's body, the Four-Tails wasted no time. It opted for its strongest move to avoid being defeated without using it.
A dense, purple-black sphere began forming between its jaws, pulsating with immense power.
On the sidelines, Tsunade's expression changed dramatically. "We can't let that Tailed Beast Bomb explode here! The entire Konoha will be destroyed!"
Zenkichi smiled. "Don't worry. I won't let it hit Konoha."
He extended both hands toward the Tailed Beast Bomb mid-air. At that moment, Armament Haki surged from his body.
A refined form of force that could impact and deflect—similar to how Silvers Rayleigh once knocked out a giant elephant in the original timeline.
Zenkichi wasn't aiming to harm the Four-Tails with this. His goal was to knock the Tailed Beast Bomb away.
With a powerful blast of Haki, he redirected the sphere into the sky.
Thankfully, the Tailed Beast Bomb wasn't the type to detonate on contact—otherwise, even he might not have dared try that method.
"It's useless!"
"The Tailed Beast Bomb will fall back down eventually. Konoha's still going to get blasted!"
The Four-Tails roared furiously.
"Oh really? How scary~"
Zenkichi raised his hand toward the heavens.
A golden arrow, made of condensed light particles, shot skyward and pierced the sphere—detonating it midair.
The explosion lit up the skies above Konoha with a blinding fireball. A shockwave tore through the village, akin to a level-nine storm, tearing roofs and collapsing walls.
The blazing light, wind, and sound brought the entire battlefield to a standstill.
"So this is the power of a Tailed Beast Bomb… terrifying."
Zenkichi stared into the sky and commented blandly.
Then, turning back to the massive red ape in front of him, he added, "So, do you have anything else up your sleeve?"
The Four-Tails, stunned, began gathering chakra again for another Tailed Beast Bomb.
But Zenkichi didn't give it the chance.
In a flash, he appeared behind the beast.
One-Sword Style — Iai Slash.
In a blink, Son Gokū's fur was cleaved. The beast collapsed from the single sword draw—no longer the Four-Tails… just another fallen monster.
"Now you're just a tailless Super Saiyan monkey. Pretty useless."
Zenkichi turned away from the limp form. Golden light pulsed at the heel of his boot, and he kicked Son Gokū's body aside.
The Sealing Cauldron of Sunagakure activated. Chains formed of golden script shot out, latching onto the beast's body and dragging it into the cauldron.
"These Four-Tails are valuable. Let's store them properly."
He glanced at the now-tailless form and sealed it inside a scroll.
"Now… shall we go finish this war?"
He turned to Tsunade. A softness flashed in his eyes.
"I hope you won't lie to me. Otherwise…"
Tsunade, jaw clenched, looked at him with complicated emotions.
"You better not get your hopes up," she said quietly. "I can't guarantee I can convince Konoha."
"Even if I'm the First Hokage's granddaughter… I'm not the one in charge of Konoha now."
A trace of mockery crept into Zenkichi's expression.
"The ones in charge now?"
"Other than Sarutobi Hiruzen and Akimichi Torifu, who had at least a shred of integrity, the rest were pathetic."
"Mito Kadoe died running away, while Sarutobi and Torifu fell honorably in battle."
"Now only Koharu and Shimura Danzo remain among the elders… and they've already chosen to flee."
---
Underground, beneath Konoha.
Danzo glared at Koharu impatiently.
"I'm seriously injured—I had no choice but to come here for treatment. But you? You're not hurt. Why are you here?"
"The Konoha shinobi out there still need your leadership!"
Koharu remained calm. "My shadow clone is leading them. I came here to protect you."
"We're all that's left of Konoha's leadership. I won't let you die alone."
Danzo stared at her with his one good eye. She met his gaze without fear.
"…Fine. Then stay."
He lifted her onto a makeshift stretcher and carried her toward their next destination.
They found Orochimaru waiting nearby.
Danzo spoke directly: "Zenkichi attacked Konoha, and Kirigakure backed him. Konoha's fall is inevitable."
"But we can't die here."
"We are Konoha. As long as we live, there's still hope. So I've decided—I'm leaving with the Root division. We'll survive. Regroup. Rebuild."
Orochimaru said nothing, but took out a sealing scroll and began packing his experimental tools. His actions were answer enough.
Koharu looked at Danzo in disbelief.
"Danzo… you…"
Danzo's expression didn't change. "If it's for Konoha, I'll endure humiliation. If you disagree, you're free to stay and die here."Follow current novels on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Koharu's expression hardened. After a moment, she clenched her fists and spoke:
"For Konoha's sake, I'll endure."

chapters.title: Chapter 85 - 85: Surrender.
chapters.content:
Inside Konoha Village
Momochi Zabuza and the others stared at the blazing sky for a moment, then turned their attention to the massive Four-Tails in the distance.
Moments later, a golden flash lit up the battlefield, and the enormous beast vanished without a trace.
Zabuza's eyes lit up. "Zenkichi-sama must've defeated the Four-Tails! Let's press forward!"
"Konoha's ANBU—surrender now and we'll show mercy!" he shouted, surging with morale.
The sudden announcement left the ANBU around them speechless and overwhelmed.
"Captured without resistance? What a grand idea."
A cold voice cut through the battlefield. It was Koharu's shadow clone, her tone sharp as she directed Konoha's ANBU to surround Zabuza's group.
Suddenly, Mangetsu Hōzuki stepped forward, using the Water Transformation Technique. His body liquefied, blending into the surrounding moisture and forming a monstrous construct of water.
With a crushing swing, the watery titan slammed into the ANBU without hesitation.
Shuriken and ninjutsu rained down, but the chakra-infused tailed beast coats shielding the Kirigakure shinobi nullified most attacks.
Terumi Mei followed suit, unleashing highly corrosive acid from her mouth. The toxic fluid sizzled as it tore through the environment, forcing ANBU to scatter.
Thanks to the Tailed Beast chakra enhancing them, the strength of Kirigakure's shinobi became overwhelming.
"Water Release – Water Shark Bullet Technique!"
Hidden in the rear, Kisame Hoshigaki stood surrounded by allies. Shielded by layers of Tailed Beast chakra, he transformed into a walking artillery battery.
With chakra stolen from Konoha shinobi, Kisame rapidly launched shark-shaped torrents—waves of condensed water bursting outward with each attack.
Even with superior numbers, Konoha's ANBU couldn't gain the upper hand. Every enemy they faced was powered by tailed beast chakra—pseudo-jinchūriki enhanced far beyond normal levels.
Without Kage-level strength, victory was impossible. The protective coat of a Tailed Beast was no joke.
Even in the original timeline, Naruto's Version 2 cloak left Jiraiya heavily wounded and overwhelmed Orochimaru—without even manifesting all nine tails.
Though Mangetsu and the others lacked the Nine-Tails' chakra, their power was still fearsome.
"Stop this at once!"
"There's no need for more bloodshed. Konoha shinobi—stand down!"
Tsunade appeared in the distance, her voice echoing across the battlefield.
Koharu's shadow clone narrowed her eyes, face darkening. "Tsunade… what is the meaning of this?"
Her voice trembled with anger.
Tsunade remained calm. "Just what I said. Konoha has lost. If we continue to resist, more of our comrades will die. It's time to surrender."
"You… traitor!" Koharu snapped. "You're the First Hokage's granddaughter, yet you'd betray the village like this?!"
She turned to the surrounding shinobi. "Everyone listen up! From now on, Tsunade is considered a traitor to Konoha. You are no longer to follow her orders!"
Shinobi still loyal to the village called out in defiance:
"Tsunade-sama, please reconsider!"
"You're one of the Legendary Sannin! How can you just give in like this?"
"This is disgraceful!"
"Would the First Hokage approve of this?"
Before any of them could shout another word, golden lasers silently flashed—piercing their skulls with chilling precision.
Zenkichi lowered his glowing fingers as he stepped into view, expression casual.
"I think you misunderstood something."
"This isn't about Tsunade begging for your loyalty, or me asking for your submission."
"In truth, Tsunade doesn't want to see you killed. She's asking me to let you live."
"If you'd rather die proving a point—then so be it."
A crushing wave of killing intent poured from Zenkichi. Golden light radiated from his body like a warning sun.Follow current novels on
"Gulp!"
Several Konoha shinobi instinctively took a step back, unable to resist the suffocating pressure.
"Don't falter!"
Koharu's shadow clone barked—but was instantly vaporized by a pinpoint laser from Zenkichi.
Bang!
The clone dispersed in a puff of white smoke.
Gasps rippled through the remaining ANBU. They hadn't even realized the real Koharu had already fled—leaving them behind.
"What a bunch of fools."
"The real Koharu ran long ago. Only you suckers are left."
Zenkichi looked around at the stunned shinobi, his tone lazily amused.
"You have three seconds."
"Either drop your weapons, sit your asses down, and I'll accept your surrender."
"You'll have a place in the new village I'm building."
"Or… keep fighting, and I'll personally put you down."
As he spoke, his right hand gleamed with golden light.
"Three… two… one…"
As if some unseen signal had passed through them, one Konoha shinobi dropped his kunai.
Then another.
Soon the ground was littered with surrendered weapons. The remaining ANBU squatted silently, signaling their surrender.
"Your face is really persuasive," Zenkichi said to Tsunade with a faint smile.
"No. This is because you're powerful."
Tsunade replied, her expression complicated.
Not far away, Terumi Mei stared at the pair, dumbfounded.
What's going on between these two? she wondered.
Did they… get closer?
Damn it!
She suddenly felt an unfamiliar twist in her chest—heartache and frustration tangled together.
Zenkichi exhaled calmly.
"Alright, the fighting's over. Let's check on the situation outside the village."
But as he spoke, his eyes narrowed slightly.
Observation Haki pulsed quietly in his senses.
Danzo and the others… had escaped.
Zenkichi made no move to pursue. A cryptic smile curled at the corner of his lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 86 - 86: Purpose.
chapters.content:
Outside Konoha Village
"Jiraiya-sensei… something's happening in the village."
Minato appeared beside Jiraiya in a flash of the Flying Thunder God Technique, concern clouding his face.
"The Four-Tails' chakra vanished… and the Eight-Tails disappeared too."
"Could it be… Burubi from Kumogakure and Roshi from Iwagakure have both fallen?"
Jiraiya's expression darkened, his body shifting back warily.
But before he could speak further—
"You're getting distracted in battle? That's your mistake!"
Jūzō laughed viciously, swinging his Executioner's Blade as he lunged toward them.
Jiraiya and Minato narrowly dodged.
Jiraiya's eyes swept over the Kirigakure troops encircling them.
"We can't afford to worry about the village right now," he said, his tone serious. "Let the Hokage and the others handle Konoha. Our duty is to stop Kirigakure's advance."
"Minato… we have to trust our comrades."
Minato nodded reluctantly. He knew Jiraiya was right.
As much as he wanted to return and check on the village, his absence here—even for seconds—could cost lives.
The battlefield shifted quickly. If he left and Kirigakure took the chance to kill Jiraiya, Konoha would suffer irreparable damage.
Kirigakure had committed everything to this invasion.
Not only did they deploy Arakawa Zenkichi, their strongest force, but even the legendary Seven Ninja Swordsmen had been sent out.
Though Samehada was mysteriously absent, Kirigakure's strength was still overwhelming.
The Hyūga, Uchiha, and other major Konoha clans were fighting at full strength just to keep them back.
But it was a losing battle.
Zenkichi had already pinned down the high-level forces of Konoha, while Momochi Zabuza and the rest of Kirigakure's elite crushed the ANBU resistance.
Konoha's ordinary shinobi barely held the line.
Then—
BOOM!
A golden light exploded above the battlefield like a second sun, piercing through the night.
All heads turned.
Descending from the sky, surrounded by fading golden radiance, stood a tall, handsome young man.
"Still fighting, are we?" Zenkichi's voice carried across the plain.
"Let me save you the trouble—there's no need to keep going."
"The battle in Konoha is already over."
He smiled faintly.
"And my presence here… should be proof enough."
The field fell silent.
Jiraiya's face twisted with dread.
"Zenkichi! What did you do to the Hokage?!"
Zenkichi shrugged lazily.
"The Third Hokage, Hiruzen Sarutobi… the Fourth Hokage, Akimichi Torifu… and council member Mito Katō—they're all dead."
"As for the remaining top brass… Shimura Danzō and Koharu Utatane fled with their loyalists."Follow current novels on ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
"Suna, Kumo, and Iwa forces have been completely wiped out."
Silence gripped the battlefield.
"But don't worry," Zenkichi continued with a calm smile. "I'm not here to slaughter anyone else."
"If you surrender, you'll still be part of Konoha… only now, it'll be a Konoha under my rule."
Mixed emotions flashed through the Konoha shinobi. Some clenched their fists. Others hesitated.
"You've done enough," Tsunade's voice rang out, stepping forward.
"There's no need for more lives to be lost. I ask you all… stand down."
The Konoha forces wavered, eyes wide.
"Lady Tsunade…?"
The granddaughter of the First Hokage—one of the Legendary Sannin—was asking them to surrender?
"Tsunade…" Jiraiya muttered, his expression pained.
"Do you really understand what you're doing?"
Tsunade met his gaze evenly.
"I do. And so do you."
"Konoha has its flaws, but it's our home!" Jiraiya barked.
Zenkichi's voice cut in coolly.
"So because it's your home, you turn a blind eye to its darkness?"
He stepped forward, his tone firm.
"Konoha is not as pure as you believe."
"It's waged war after war, bringing ruin to weaker nations for its own benefit."
"Internally, it's no better. The Uchiha were cast aside and suppressed for Madara's sins."
"The White Fang, hailed as a hero, was disgraced and driven to death by his own people."
"The Senju gave their lives for Konoha, yet now only Tsunade remains."
Zenkichi looked over the crowd.
"I've come to purge this darkness… to end the cycle of bloodshed."
"If you're willing to walk beside me, I welcome you."
"If not, you're free to go. And if you choose to fight—" his voice darkened, "—I'll meet you head-on."
He raised a hand, golden light building at his fingertips.
"You have three days."
"Enter and leave Konoha as you please. Those who wish to leave, may leave. Those who stay, fight with purpose."
His words held no hesitation—only absolute certainty.
To him, letting go of uncertain allies was better than dragging dead weight forward.
He had no fear of retaliation.
If Orochimaru and Danzo—two of Konoha's deadliest—were allowed to escape, what use were lesser threats?
Let them come.
Zenkichi had plans for them, too.
Those traitors… would serve as his whetstones.
He needed opposition to test and temper his growing army.
There would always be those with ambition, hidden daggers behind false smiles.
When Orochimaru and Danzo returned to reclaim Konoha, they'd unknowingly help Zenkichi cleanse his own ranks.
Because in the end—
Even enemies had their purpose.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 87 - 87: Persuasions.
chapters.content:
"Kushina, come with me!"
"The village is no longer the Konoha it used to be. Let's leave together."
"We might have a chance to return someday… but right now, we need to go."
Namikaze Minato stood before Uzumaki Kushina, trying to persuade her.
But her expression remained calm—cold, even.
"Leave Konoha? Why would I?" she said flatly.
"You want to leave because you're clinging to a memory of the old Konoha."
"But me? I never held such illusions. I feel nothing for it."
Minato faltered. "I know… Konoha has done things lately that disappointed you…"
"But still—this is the village where you grew up. Don't you have any feelings for it?"
Kushina's voice dropped to ice.
"Konoha was never my village."
"My village was Uzushiogakure. But that's gone now."
"And Konoha didn't lift a finger to help when it fell."
Her words cut deep.
"We, the Uzumaki clan, gave Konoha everything. We made enemies for them. We even gave them me—the most talented of our generation—to serve as a Jinchūriki."
"And when our village was wiped out? Konoha gave us nothing."
"I owe them nothing. But they owe us everything."
"So no—I'm not leaving. If anything, I think Zenkichi might give me something Konoha never did: a place to belong."
Minato grew anxious.
"But… you're the Nine-Tails' Jinchūriki! Zenkichi will use you—"
Kushina sneered. "And what were you planning, Minato?"
"If I had gone with you, would others not try to use me too?"
"Could you even protect me from that?"
Her eyes burned now.
"You couldn't even stop Konoha from isolating me. You couldn't do anything back then."
Just then, a chuckle echoed nearby.
"Well said, Uzumaki Kushina. You've become sharper."
A familiar figure walked over and sat beside her.
Arakawa Zenkichi.
He threw Minato a cold glance. "Just because I said people can leave freely doesn't mean you get to force someone to go with you."
Minato had no answer. He turned and left quietly.
Kushina frowned. "What are you doing here?"
Zenkichi smiled. "Since you've decided to stay, you're one of mine now. Of course I care about you."
"I admit—I was surprised you didn't act last night. After all, you are the Nine-Tails' host."
Kushina huffed. "I didn't act because the Nine-Tails wouldn't hurt you… and because I'm done with Konoha."
Zenkichi nodded. "Fair."
Kushina blinked, slightly thrown off by his simple reply.
She suddenly felt awkward. She didn't know why.
Before, she admired him. But now… she wasn't sure what she felt.
Zenkichi stood.
"I came to tell you something important."
"From now on, Jinchūriki will no longer be treated as weapons."
"You are heroes—people who sacrifice for the village, not tools to be feared."
"Also, I've heard there are still Uzumaki orphans scattered across the world."
"Even if only a few remain, I'll find them. I'll reunite your clan."
Kushina stared, stunned.
Then said quietly, "…Thank you."
Zenkichi smiled.
"You won't be alone anymore. No one will spy on you. No one will isolate you."
"Go see Tsunade. She misses you."
"Or… come see me."
He laughed and walked away.
Kushina watched him go, fuming slightly—but then her lips curled into a small smile.
---
Meanwhile…
Minato failed to convince Kushina and next sought out his student: Hatake Kakashi.
But Kakashi met him with a cold stare.
"No, Sensei. I'm no longer a Konoha shinobi."
"My father gave everything to Konoha—and they betrayed him."
"Do you really expect me to fight for that same village?"
His gaze dropped to the White Fang dagger left by his father.
"Hiruzen is dead. But Danzo still breathes. And I'll make him pay."
---
Elsewhere, Jiraiya left the Uchiha Clan compound, face grim.Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
They too had refused to go with him.
"The Uchiha clan never had a future in Konoha," their clan head had said.
"We stayed before because we had no choice. But now—we won't make the same mistake."
Their words echoed in Jiraiya's ears.
Was he wrong all along?
The so-called persuasion mission had failed.
In the end, only a small handful of shinobi left with Jiraiya and Minato.
Notably, the Ino–Shika–Chō clans chose to stay.
They knew the odds.
Zenkichi now held too much power. The chance of defeating him was near zero.
Though they might not rise to power under his regime, the clans could still protect their legacy.
That was enough for them.
Their motto was simple:
"Support whoever's in charge."
The three families had no bloodline limits or elite forces. Yet they had survived since the Warring States Period by staying loyal to the village—any village.
Jiraiya couldn't understand it.
But Zenkichi did.
To him, their loyalty was conditional, not moral. And that made them reliable in their own way.
Even the Akimichi clan, where Akimichi Torifu once stood, refused to leave with him.
Jiraiya walked through Konoha's streets, heart heavy.
He still couldn't believe how little support remained.
But something within him flared.
No. I'm not wrong.
"We'll be back."
His eyes burned with determination.
And then—he saw two figures walking toward the village gates.
He froze.
"Yahiko… Konan?!"
He couldn't believe it.

chapters.title: Chapter 88 - 88: Mizukage.
chapters.content:
After Yahiko and Konan learned that Konoha had been overtaken by Zenkichi, they didn't react with much emotion.
After offering simple condolences to Jiraiya, they continued toward the village.
To them, Konoha was partly responsible for the chaos that consumed the Land of Rain. So its downfall didn't stir much sympathy.
Jiraiya felt a pang of disappointment. His students' indifference stung more than he expected.
He couldn't help but question himself—Had he failed them?
---
When Yahiko and Konan arrived at Konoha, they found the village mid-reconstruction. Several patrolling shinobi approached them, and Yahiko clearly stated his purpose.
They had visited Kirigakure before, but Zenkichi had already gone overseas by then.
Uninterested in staying, they left Kirigakure and planned to search for Zenkichi at a later time.
When they returned, they heard he had taken a team to Konoha for the Chūnin Exams.
Yahiko found it strange. As the former leader of Akatsuki, his instincts told him something was wrong.
Ever since Zenkichi reawakened him, Yahiko's perception and intuition had sharpened significantly.
So, trusting his senses, he brought Konan to Konoha to investigate.
His suspicions were confirmed—Konoha had changed.
---
"Are you here looking for answers?" Zenkichi asked calmly.
"Fine. I'll give them to you—but not now."
"Come to the meeting later. I'll explain everything."
He looked over Yahiko thoughtfully before turning away.
---
Not long after, Terumi Mei entered the Hokage's office and closed the door behind her.
"Is everything in Konoha under control?" she asked.
"I think it's time you inherited the title of Mizukage."
Zenkichi lounged on the sofa, legs crossed, casually trimming his nails.
"In two days," he replied. "I'll assume the role and merge both villages into one unified ninja organization."
---
Soon after, Zenkichi officially became the Mizukage of Kirigakure.
Then, Konoha was merged into Kirigakure, becoming part of the new structure. To respect the identity of the original villagers, the name "Konoha" was retained in title only.
---
Later, Zenkichi addressed the gathering shinobi:
"Decades ago, the Warring States Period plunged the entire ninja world into chaos."
"Take the Land of Fire, for example—the Senju, Uchiha, and Hyūga clans fought endlessly."
"But when the First Hokage founded Konoha, peace came to this land."
"Why? Because a powerful ninja organization arose—one strong enough to prevent senseless conflict."
"None of the other clans or groups could challenge that authority, so they accepted Konoha's order."
"It's clear, then: the reason the world isn't at peace today is that it lacks that kind of centralized power."
"The Five Great Nations are powerful—but they're divided. They prioritize profit and politics over peace."
"The First Hokage had the strength to suppress the entire world and form a unified force. But instead of doing that, he hoped the Five Kage would maintain balance through understanding."
"That dream failed."
"Now, it's time to try something else."
"If words can't unite us, we'll use steel."
"From this day forward, I declare the formation of a new organization—one that will suppress chaos and unite the ninja world!"
---
Zenkichi's proposal wasn't met with resistance.
Both Konoha and Kirigakure had suffered heavily during the past wars. His plan resonated with the weary shinobi.
Even Yahiko, who met with Zenkichi in private, acknowledged the idea's appeal.
"Each village has its own motives," Yahiko said. "But if we allow them to check and balance each other, a stable alliance might be possible."
Zenkichi's tone was casual.
"You want a coalition built on negotiation—where the Five Villages form a single organization to maintain peace?"
Yahiko nodded. "Something like that."
But Zenkichi's eyes narrowed slightly.
"Peace hasn't failed because people didn't try hard enough. It failed because there's no real power to enforce it."
"The so-called 'Ninja Alliance' you speak of is just a fragile collection of self-serving factions."
"Even if they agree for now, who watches the watchers?"
"Who holds the Five Villages accountable when they themselves make up the alliance?"
Yahiko frowned but stayed silent.Googlᴇ search NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Zenkichi continued, more direct now:
"Imagine if there once was a true alliance—one massive organization upholding peace. But slowly, smaller villages formed inside it, each with their own interests."
"Eventually, those factions clashed with the core ideals. Some stayed true, others chased power."
"And when the corruption spread, the alliance broke apart—becoming the fragmented world we know today."
"You see now?"
"Bringing those villages together again under a weak banner will only repeat the past."
"Without absolute authority, a large group will always be torn apart by smaller ones."
"That's why this coming war is necessary."
"To break those groups. To destroy the power they use to divide the world."
---
Peace without strength is an illusion.
Zenkichi would not make the same mistake as the First Hokage.
He would build something stronger—and make it last.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 89 - 89: White Zetsu.
chapters.content:
Sunagakure — Hidden Sand Village
The Fourth Kazekage, Rasa, stared at the report in his hands with a heavy expression.
Pakura—a threat to his position—was dead. Chiyo and Ebizo, who kept him in check, were gone too.
By all accounts, this should have been a time of celebration.
But it wasn't.
His gaze hardened on a single name in the report: Zenkichi.
Everything had gone wrong because of this man.
Rasa gritted his teeth. He wanted to kill Zenkichi with his own hands.
But the man's overwhelming power left him feeling helpless.
Direct confrontation? Out of the question.
Still… any method would do, as long as Zenkichi died.
He'd heard that sealing techniques could restrain Zenkichi. Fortunately, he had already begun training a team specialized in fūinjutsu.
Just then, a voice echoed in the room.
"Fourth Kazekage Rasa…"Thɪs ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
A white humanoid figure rose from the ground beside him.
"What are you?" Rasa demanded, startled but not shaken.
The figure was White Zetsu, sent under Black Zetsu's orders. Though Rasa couldn't fully grasp what the being was, he didn't sense any immediate threat.
And Rasa, despite his flaws, was still a proud Kage.
"I'm an enemy of Zenkichi—just like you. That makes us allies."
"You're troubled, aren't you?" White Zetsu continued. "Both Kirigakure and Konohagakure have fallen under Zenkichi's control. And now, he's set his sights on unifying the ninja world."
"You villages are his next targets. Even if you surrender, there's no guarantee he'll accept it."
"You only have one option—fight him to the end."
Rasa narrowed his eyes, golden sand beginning to float in the air around him.
"Did you come here just to spout nonsense?" he asked coldly.
Seeing the situation getting tense, White Zetsu quickly shifted focus.
"I'm offering something useful," he said quickly. "I can serve as a liaison. I can help you connect with the other major villages."
"Zenkichi's power is overwhelming. One village alone can't stop him. But united, you might have a chance."
Rasa paused, considering the offer.
"I've already begun reaching out to the others," he replied.
"And I can make it easier," Zetsu said. "My clones are linked through a shared consciousness, and my travel speed is unmatched."
Rasa gave a small, calculating smile.
"Fine. I'll give you a chance."
---
Iwagakure — Hidden Stone Village
The Third Tsuchikage, Ōnoki, hovered in the air, eyes heavy with worry.
He might've clashed often with Rōshi, but he couldn't deny the man's importance to Iwa.
Now that Rōshi was dead, his heart carried a weight he didn't show on his face.
"Zenkichi…"
Just thinking of the man who killed Rōshi—and crippled his own son—filled him with bitterness.
"My Dust Release should be able to finish him."
He muttered to himself, clinging to that hope.
Suddenly, a voice rose from below:
"Zenkichi isn't that easy to deal with, Tsuchikage-sama."
White Zetsu emerged from the ground.
"You need help."
Ōnoki turned with narrowed eyes.
"Cooperation? I'm listening."
He was cunning enough to entertain any strategy that offered a chance at victory.
---
Kumogakure — Hidden Cloud Village
The newly appointed Fourth Raikage slammed his fist through yet another desk.
His top subordinate Burui had died in Konoha. The Eight-Tails was gone. The Amber Purification Jar, a national treasure, stolen.
The losses were staggering.
All because of that one man—Zenkichi.
"Lord Raikage, please calm down."
A calm voice drifted up from the ground as White Zetsu emerged.
"Anger won't fix anything. Let's talk about how to eliminate Zenkichi."
"Who the hell are you?"
The Raikage's body flickered. In the blink of an eye, he had White Zetsu by the throat, hoisting him into the air.
"I'm here to help you destroy Zenkichi," Zetsu answered, unbothered.
"You?" the Raikage sneered. "You think you can deal with him?"
"Then how about these eyes?"
A second White Zetsu figure rose from the earth—this one with a single eye, rimmed in black and glowing purple.
The Rinnegan.
The Raikage's face froze.
"That eye… the Rinnegan?"
Even he had heard of its terrifying reputation.
Seeing that the Raikage hesitated, Black Zetsu, hidden within Tobi, let out a silent breath of relief.
He knew the Raikage was a hothead, so he'd brought both Tobi and Nagato to assist in convincing him.
---
Amegakure — Hidden Rain Village
Hanzo the Salamander, the so-called Demigod, sat in silence, eyes cold as a White Zetsu emerged from the ground before him.
The silent entrance put Hanzo on edge.
If such infiltration were used for assassination, even he would be in danger.
"Demigod Hanzo," Zetsu said calmly. "Don't be alarmed. I came to negotiate."
"Your mastery of poison is unmatched. We need your help to defeat Zenkichi."
Hanzo scoffed.
"Why should I fight Zenkichi? I hold no grudge against him."
White Zetsu's grin widened.
"You may not know this yet, but Zenkichi is forming a vast ninja organization to control the entire shinobi world."
"And people like you—those who stand alone—will be his first targets."
"He won't ask. He'll simply remove you to make room for his order."
"Unless, of course, you're willing to swallow your pride… and serve him."
Hanzo went quiet.
There was a time when he might have considered joining Zenkichi to pursue peace.
But power changes people.
Years of ruling the Land of Rain had corroded his ideals.
And Hanzo was no longer the man he used to be.

chapters.title: Chapter 90 - 90: Reanimation Jutsu.
chapters.content:
After Jiraiya left Konoha with a group of ninja, they settled in a smaller village.
Jiraiya had no clear plan for the future, and confusion clouded his mind.
The shinobi under his command felt the same uncertainty. Tensions began to rise among them.
---
"We should establish a new ninja village and prepare to counterattack Konoha when the opportunity comes!"
"And wait until the end of time to strike back? That's way too slow!"
"We should seek help from the other hidden villages. They also suffered losses at the hands of Zenkichi. We have a common enemy."
"Just because we share an enemy doesn't make us allies. Don't forget the deep grudges between Konoha and other villages."
"Exactly! Our strength is too weak right now. What if another village tries to absorb or crush us?"
"I say we abandon this fantasy of reclaiming Konoha."
"We left to escape Zenkichi. We were lucky to survive—why go back to die?"
"You're right. We don't stand a chance against him!"
---
Jiraiya watched the heated argument, exhaustion weighing heavy on his shoulders.
Suddenly, a calm voice echoed through the air:
"If you're struggling to decide... maybe we can help."
Jiraiya turned sharply. His expression darkened the moment he saw the speaker.
A familiar white figure had appeared—the same one that had once controlled Nagato.
"You..." Jiraiya muttered furiously. "How dare you show your face in front of me?"
"Jiraiya, calm yourself."
"You can't touch me right now, and getting angry won't help either," came Black Zetsu's voice from within White Zetsu Tobi ."I'm not here to fight—I came to negotiate."
Jiraiya's chakra flared, and he sneered:
"Negotiate? I've got nothing to say to the likes of you."
"Are you sure?" Black Zetsu replied. "You want to reclaim Konoha, don't you?"
"That's our concern. It has nothing to do with you," Jiraiya snapped. "Your connection to Uchiha Madara makes you impossible to trust."
"I never asked for your trust," Black Zetsu said coldly. "I only came to deliver a message."
"Sunagakure, Kumogakure, and Iwagakure are preparing to join forces against Arakawa Zenkichi. Why not have the remnants of Konoha join them?"
Jiraiya scoffed.
"You, and those other three villages, aren't exactly trustworthy allies either."
"I understand," Black Zetsu replied, his tone patient. "But this isn't the time to be picky."
"Ever since you fled Konoha, your intel network has been in shambles, hasn't it? So let me tell you what you've missed."
"Arakawa Zenkichi has openly declared his plan to create a ninja organization to suppress the entire shinobi world. To make that happen, the other villages must be conquered or eliminated."
"Unless everyone surrenders and accepts his restructuring, they'll all be his targets—Sunagakure, Kumogakure, Iwagakure, and even smaller villages like Amegakure, Takigakure, and Kusagakure."
"But now, they've united to form a ninja coalition—a rare chance to stand against Zenkichi."
"Will you miss this opportunity? Your strength might be the final push needed to defeat him."
"If Zenkichi wins this war, he'll be unstoppable. His new world order will crush any hope of revenge."
"You won't even be allowed to form a village, let alone reclaim Konoha. If you can't defeat him, how do you plan to fight back?"
---
Black Zetsu's voice was low and hoarse, dripping with temptation.
"Jiraiya-sensei…" Namikaze Minato stepped forward, worry etched on his face. "If what he says is true, we have to join the fight."
Another shinobi echoed from the side:
"This could be our last chance. We can't afford to ignore it."
Jiraiya glared at Zetsu with killing intent, then sighed deeply.
"Fine. If everything you say checks out, we'll fight when the time comes."
"It's a deal," Black Zetsu replied. "I'll contact you when the time is right."
With that, White Zetsu Afei sank into the earth and vanished.
---
In the Land of Fire, deep in a hidden forest, Tobi emerged once again—this time beside Orochimaru and Danzo Shimura.
He repeated the same message he had delivered to the others.
A secret base was concealed among the trees, where Orochimaru and Danzo had taken refuge.
---
"You really went to all this trouble to find us," Orochimaru said, yellow eyes gleaming. He stared at the glowing Rinnegan with interest and gave a soft chuckle.
"It's a rare opportunity," Black Zetsu said flatly. "Are you going to let it pass?"
"We'll send some personnel when the time comes," Orochimaru replied, smiling.
"Good. I'll be waiting for your cooperation."
With that, Zetsu departed.
As he vanished, Danzo snorted.
"If that pest didn't know our location and we weren't uncertain of killing him, I wouldn't bother involving my top men in a war like this."
"Orochimaru, we need to focus our efforts on perfecting the Reanimation Jutsu. Put the Hashirama cell research on hold. My limbs still work, it's not urgent."
"Once you've perfected it, we'll control the ninja world with an army of reanimated shinobi. Then we'll have all the time we want for our experiments."
---
Reanimation Jutsu—a powerful forbidden technique.
Danzo, once a high-ranking official in Konoha, had handed this jutsu to Orochimaru, the infamous mad scientist.
Together, they waited in the shadows, working to perfect the technique.Thɪs
The regeneration ability of reanimated shinobi was astonishing. A reanimated ninja could rebuild themselves quickly, although their combat ability had yet to match their living counterparts.
Zenkichi's resilience had been the inspiration.
---
Danzo's conclusion was simple: to defeat a man like Arakawa Zenkichi, they would need an army of undead warriors—resilient, tireless, and endless.

chapters.title: Chapter 91 - 91: How do I revive the Senju clan?
chapters.content:
"Achievement achieved – take over as Mizukage!"
"Template character——Kizaru!"
"Unlock progress: 88%!"
"Achievement achieved – annex Konoha!"
"Template character——Kizaru!"
"Unlock progress: 91%!"
Looking at his system interface, Zenkichi fell into deep thought.
Judging from the rate of progress, it wouldn't be long before he fully unlocked the Kizaru template.
"Once I do... I'll be eligible for my second character template, right?"
Zenkichi muttered to himself, a faint smile tugging at his lips.
"Zenkichi, we've got a situation,"
Tsunade's tone was grave.
"Sunagakure, Iwagakure, and Kumogakure have joined forces. They've formed a ninja alliance and are advancing toward Konoha."
"In addition to the three great villages, Amegakure, Kusagakure, and Takigakure have also sent forces. We're looking at a total army of 80,000 ninja."
Tsunade wore a heavy expression. The sheer scale of the threat weighed on her visibly.
"Just a bunch of stray dogs," Zenkichi scoffed.
"Three major villages? To me, they're nothing but opportunists trying to grab whatever scraps they can."
"..."
Tsunade fell silent, the tension in her expression easing slightly.
Zenkichi seemed unfazed by the news, almost as if he already had a countermeasure.
He patted her shoulder, voice calm but confident.
"Don't worry. I'll handle it."
"Eighty thousand? Even if they brought a hundred thousand, it wouldn't change the outcome."
"You know what true overwhelming force is? You're looking at it."
Tsunade chuckled quietly.
"If that's the case, then I'll stop worrying."
But then her face shifted. A flicker of hesitation passed through her eyes.
She looked at Zenkichi, clearly struggling with what she wanted to say.
"If you've got something on your mind, say it. I'm not going to bite."
After a pause, Tsunade finally spoke.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"According to reports… Jiraiya and some of the Root members that escaped earlier are among the alliance ranks."
Zenkichi yawned.
"Is that so? Well, bad luck for them. I already gave them a chance to walk away."
Tsunade sighed. His stance was crystal clear.
"Alright. I suppose… since you already killed my teacher, losing two more teammates doesn't mean much anymore."
She said it bitterly, a trace of defeat in her voice.
Zenkichi chuckled lightly.
"Sarutobi Hiruzen should've thanked me, honestly. At least he didn't die at the hands of his own student."
"Wait—no, maybe he would've preferred that. Maybe he wanted to be surpassed."
"If so, then yeah, he probably does resent me."
Tsunade narrowed her eyes.
"Are you suggesting I would've been the one to kill Sarutobi-sensei?"
Zenkichi shook his head.
"No. That's not your style. Even if you knew he was behind the fall of the Senju Clan, you'd never raise a hand against your teacher."
Tsunade deflated, her expression falling.
"But Orochimaru? He's a different case. He's methodical—calculating. You've seen it too. The cracks between him and Sarutobi are already there."
"Because of Hiruzen's weakness, Orochimaru will leave Konoha. And when he becomes strong enough… he'll return to kill him."
Zenkichi's voice was resolute. He spoke with the certainty of someone who knew the future.
Tsunade frowned.
"Orochimaru wouldn't go that far… would he?"
Zenkichi shook his head.
"He would. He has to. Killing his teacher is the only way to prove that the one who doubted him was wrong."
Tsunade remained silent. The more she thought about their personalities, the more it made sense.
"So don't lose sleep over Sarutobi's death. If it had been up to you, it might've been your hands, too."
"As for Jiraiya… let it go. Everyone walks their own path."
"If they think they're right, let life and death settle the score."
"And if guilt starts creeping in? Think about Uzumaki Kushina."
"You'll realize that loyalty, even friendship, doesn't mean what you think it does. In their eyes, you're not more important than the village."
"If sacrificing you brought peace, they'd cry for you—but they'd still do it."
"You're emotional, Tsunade. But you're not just a woman. You're a shinobi—and that kind of sentiment will only drag you down."
Zenkichi's words landed hard, silencing her once again.
"Zenkichi-sama!"
At that moment, Nara Shikaku entered the room.
As Konoha's chief strategist, he had been brought fully under Zenkichi's command.
"The coalition forces are approaching Konoha. What are your instructions?"
Zenkichi didn't hesitate.
"No need to see them off. Just crush them."
Though a little taken aback, Shikaku nodded. After all, he had witnessed Zenkichi's power firsthand.
"Alright," he said simply.
"Come on, don't look so glum," Zenkichi said, turning back to Tsunade.
"Once this is over, peace will reign. Your grandfather's dream will come true. Your brother's tragedy—won't happen again."
"The Senju Clan… if you want it restored, I'll help you do it."
Zenkichi looked her in the eye, completely serious.
"Grandfather's dream… Nawaki's regrets…"
Tsunade visibly steadied herself. But confusion remained.
"I'm the last of my clan. How can I possibly revive it?"
Zenkichi smiled slyly—and suddenly pulled her into his arms.
If Terumi Mei could make the first move, then so could he.
"When I return from the battlefield, come to my room that night."
"Then you'll understand exactly how I plan to revive the Senju Clan."
With that, he released the now-blushing Tsunade, laughed, and strode out of the Hokage's office.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 92 - 92: Zenkichi's Plan.
chapters.content:
The mighty ninja coalition was on the move.
The Fourth Kazekage, Rasa, wore a scowl as he turned to the Tsuchikage and Raikage beside him.
"There are so many of us—why are we gathering just to fight Zenkichi?"
"I think we should leverage our numbers. Split up and attack both Konoha and Kirigakure. That'll stretch Zenkichi thin and wear him down."
The Fourth Raikage scoffed.
"Too much trouble. If we all converge, Zenkichi will too. It's better to settle this with one decisive battle and avoid a drawn-out war."
"As for splitting forces and hoping someone else kills Zenkichi... I think that just increases the chance he picks us off one by one."
The Third Tsuchikage gave Rasa a disdainful glance, his tone cold and logical.
"Konoha and Kirigakure aren't our real targets. This war is about one man—Zenkichi."
"If he dies, his forces will collapse. We can handle the rest easily."
"But if Zenkichi survives, it won't matter even if we raze both villages."
"Dividing our forces now would be a mistake. We strike him down first—then we can split up."
---
On the plains before the ninja coalition, Zenkichi arrived, leading the combined armies of Konoha and Kirigakure.
Both sides stopped. They faced one another across the battlefield.
"Kids!"
"Send in the Seven Ninja Swordsmen, the Uchiha Clan, and the Hyuga Clan as the vanguard. Break their formation!"
Zenkichi waved his hand, issuing his orders.
The Seven Ninja Swordsmen were unpredictable. This was a chance to burn off their excess energy—or lose them without consequence.
As for the Uchiha and Hyuga clans, both had recently submitted to him. He wanted to test their loyalty and see if they would truly fight under his command.
Zenkichi's Haki swept across the Konoha forces. With it, he could sense who among them wavered, who hesitated.
He would use this war to purge the rot within.
The troops responded with a roar, charging toward the enemy with fearless resolve.
Zenkichi didn't move immediately. He stood calmly—this time, he would serve as the general, not the vanguard.
Whitebeard wouldn't rush into battle headfirst, and neither would Kizaru—whose power Zenkichi had nearly unlocked.
"Eighty thousand ninja... how terrifying," he muttered with an exaggerated tone.
"Yamanaka-san, assist me in directing the field."
Beside him, Yamanaka Inoichi nodded calmly. He wasn't a frontline fighter, and his mental transmission techniques were invaluable in a battle of this scale.
---
On the frontlines—
The combined charge of the Seven Ninja Swordsmen, Uchiha, and Hyuga clans faltered. They couldn't break the coalition's lines.
The battlefield erupted into chaos—a brutal melee.
"Idiots! Fools!"
"I am Killer Bee, the Eight-Tails Jinchuriki of Kumogakure—come get clapped!"
Killer Bee was spitting awkward rhymes even as he fought.
His opponent: Hozuki Mangetsu, expressionless, bathed in red chakra.
The Tailed Beast cloak shimmered across Mangetsu's body. Six long tails lashed out, striking at Bee.
"Lariat!"
Killer Bee surged forward, slicing through the first cloak with a powerful chop—his signature Thunderclap style.
His raw strength was terrifying, and the Lariat had real bite.
But Mangetsu's liquefying body dissolved the blow with ease.
"A member of the Hozuki Clan…?"
Killer Bee frowned, Lightning Chakra flaring in his hands.
Before it could connect, Mangetsu's chakra erupted—his Tailed Beast power overwhelming Bee.
Boom!
Killer Bee was hurled back violently.
Mangetsu didn't pause. Forming hand signs, he launched pressurized water bullets—each one striking with crushing force.
"Enough!"
Watching his brother get launched, the Fourth Raikage lost his temper.
Lightning exploded around him.
But Kisame Hoshigaki stepped forward, a grin on his face. With one sweep of Samehada, he devoured the Raikage's Lightning Chakra like it was nothing.
Momochi Zabuza and Ao activated their own second-stage cloaks, shielding Kisame and buying him time to drain even more chakra.
"Out of my way!"
The Fourth Raikage roared, his body a blur of blue lightning.
In an instant, he was in front of Mangetsu.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Die!"
With a chop filled with enough force to fell a mountain, he struck.
Mangetsu's eyes flashed. Red chakra surged, and he instantly took on a humanoid Tailed Beast form.
Boom!
The second-stage cloak absorbed the strike, and a brutal clash followed.
---
In the air above, Onoki, the Third Tsuchikage, floated with both hands extended. A blinding white glow appeared between them—the signature of Dust Release.
"Let's see how you like being reduced to molecules."
"Dust Release: Detachment of the Primitive World Technique!"
He fired his deadly jutsu...
But before it could reach its target, a golden laser pierced the sky.
"Aah—!"
Onoki screamed as the beam tore through his arm. The technique dissipated instantly.
"Dust Release... tricky indeed,"
Arakawa Zenkichi lowered his fingers, casually ending the attack before it could start.
He had hoped the coalition would help him clean out traitors—but Dust Release was too dangerous. It threatened too many of his own forces.
---
"Lord Zenkichi!"
Nara Shikaku stepped forward.
"The Raikage and Tsuchikage are too strong. We've already suffered heavy losses."
"More than half of the Seven Ninja Swordsmen are down. We need you to engage the enemy shadows—now."
Shikaku's voice was calm but insistent. He had clearly seen through Zenkichi's earlier plans.

chapters.title: Chapter 93 - 93: Human Path.
chapters.content:
"Let them retreat slowly. I'll handle the rest of the battle."
Zenkichi stared at the chaos below, then gave the order to Yamanaka Inoichi, who stood beside him.
Inoichi closed his eyes, connecting telepathically with every allied ninja through the Yamanaka Clan's secret techniques.
At the same time, Zenkichi's body shimmered, turning into countless particles of light that shot into the battlefield.
His form reappeared midair, both hands glowing with condensed energy.
Yasakani no Magatama.
Countless golden light bullets rained down on the ninja coalition.
Under the precise control of Observation Haki, Zenkichi's devastating barrage created just enough cover for his troops to begin a calculated withdrawal.
"Damn it!"
Ōnoki stared at Zenkichi, wishing he could fire off his Dust Release—but his shoulder, pierced earlier by Zenkichi's laser, made that impossible.
"Magnet Release: Gold Dust Burial!"
Rasa, the Fourth Kazekage, slammed his hands into the ground. Massive waves of golden sand surged upward, shielding the coalition from the light bullets and surging toward Zenkichi.
Dark ink-like seals crawled across the gold dust, and faint red sealing talismans flickered within the sand.
"A sealing technique? Boring."
Zenkichi didn't move—he neither resisted nor dodged.
The gold sand engulfed him, forming a sealed pyramid in midair.
Boom!The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
It crashed down with weighty finality. The pyramid shimmered with binding seals, red talismans pulsing on its surface.
"Did we succeed?"
Gasps rippled through the ninja alliance. Could the seemingly invincible Zenkichi really be sealed so easily?
Ōnoki and a wounded Jiraiya looked stunned. They had experienced Zenkichi's power firsthand. Could it really end like this?
"Was it really that simple?"
Even Zenkichi's own men appeared dazed.
"What now?"
Jūzō, one of the surviving Seven Ninja Swordsmen, looked grim.
Rasa muttered coldly, "If he's really dead, there's no reason to throw our lives away here."
Ōnoki laughed lightly.
"You're all too young. Ninja battles are dangerous. Even the strongest can fall to a single misstep."
Rasa smirked proudly.
"I thought Zenkichi of Kirigakure would be formidable—but this is all he amounted to."
Then—cracks formed on the pyramid.
Golden light burst forth from within.
Boom!
The entire structure exploded in a brilliant flash, obliterating the sealing tags and scattering gold dust everywhere.
A blazing golden figure floated above the shattered pyramid—Zenkichi, completely unharmed.
"Wow... The Fourth Kazekage's seal was impressive."
"I almost couldn't get out."
"Almost."
He said it with a casual smirk, his tone soaked in mockery.
"Damn you...!"
Rasa's expression twisted with fury. More gold dust erupted around him, infused with even more sealing jutsu.
"You think that'll work twice?"
"If I hadn't wanted to experience your little seal firsthand, you never would've touched me."
With a flicker of light, Zenkichi vanished—then reappeared behind the Fourth Kazekage in an instant.
"Too slow."
With a lazy voice, he raised his foot. A golden cross flared on the sole of his boot as he kicked Rasa square in the side, sending him flying.
"Lord Kazekage!"
The Sunagakure shinobi were stunned. Their leader—so easily overwhelmed?
"Bastard!"
The Fourth Raikage erupted in rage, lightning crackling across his body as he dashed toward Zenkichi.
"Another Kage? This might be the most I've killed in one war."
"No, wait—I've already killed two Hokage... even if one was a former one."
Zenkichi raised his guard. Armament Haki surged over his skin, turning it obsidian-black just as Raikage struck with a Lariat-style chop.
Boom!
He blocked it with ease.
"That actually stung a little."
Zenkichi tilted his head, still casual. His right index finger lit up with golden energy.
Boom!
A laser burst from his fingertip, ripping straight through the Raikage's side.
"Compared to your Lightning Armor… mine's just on another level."
The Raikage screamed as he was flung backward, badly wounded.
"Lord Raikage!"
"Storm Release: Laser Circus!"
A Cloud shinobi formed hand seals. White lightning circled his arms, forming powerful laser beams that shot at Zenkichi.
"Storm Release? Sit down."
Zenkichi unleashed a shockwave of Armament Haki, obliterating the incoming lasers.
In a flash, he appeared before the staggering Raikage and formed a golden lightsaber in his palm.
"Protect Lord Raikage!"
A wave of Cloud ninja charged forward to shield their leader.
"Pointless."
With no change in expression, Zenkichi swung the blade.
A massive golden slash ripped across the battlefield, engulfing the defenders and slicing clean through the ranks. The entire section of the alliance army was cut open.
Whoosh!
The ground trembled. A deadly quiet followed.
Gulp.
All around, shinobi swallowed hard, stunned by the sight of so much devastation in a single strike.
---
Suddenly, a pale white hand shot from the ground beneath Zenkichi, grasping his ankle.
"Finally making your move?"
He wasn't surprised.
Zenkichi's body turned into golden light and ascended upward.
Below, he looked down at the emerging form—White Zetsu, reaching out from the earth.
Under the glow of his Observation Haki, Zenkichi saw the full picture: Black Zetsu, Nagato, and White Zetsu—hiding below.
So that was their plan. Wait for the perfect moment and use Nagato's Human Path to rip out his soul.
"Looks like Nagato's presence is fading. Has he been completely suppressed?"
Zenkichi's eyes narrowed as golden energy bloomed once more at his fingertip.

chapters.title: Chapter 94 - 94: Speed Is Power.
chapters.content:
The golden laser bombarded the earth, and the highly concentrated light particles produced an extremely violent explosion upon impact.
A white figure was thrown from the heart of the explosion—White Zetsu Tobi. The shockwave from the blast sent him flying through the air.
Zenkichi's body flickered, transforming into light particles. In a flash, he reappeared beside Tobi and reached out.
His palm, infused with Armament Haki, grasped Tobi and yanked him away with force—like peeling a banana—tearing him from Nagato's body.
With a flick, Zenkichi flung the tattered White Zetsu like a discarded rag.
What remained was Nagato—half his body overtaken by Black Zetsu.
Now that White Zetsu had been removed, Nagato's eyes regained some clarity. He seemed to recover partial control over his own body.
"I didn't expect... even now, I still can't defeat you," rasped Black Zetsu, his voice hoarse but eerily calm.
A cold glint crossed Zenkichi's eyes. Without hesitation, he extended a hand and plucked Nagato's Rinnegan from its socket.
He had initially wanted to observe what other tricks Black Zetsu might use, but now it was clear—he wasn't worth the caution.
There was no reason to leave the Rinnegan in Black Zetsu's hands.
"What a mistake to lose the Rinnegan," Zenkichi muttered.
"That's right... you haven't won yet," Black Zetsu said again, still unhurried, his voice low and grainy.
As he spoke, Black Zetsu's form slipped away from Nagato's body like liquid.
Zenkichi's expression shifted. Instantly, his body dissolved into light particles and reappeared beneath Black Zetsu.
The light particles condensed into a glowing container in his hand, catching the falling black mass.
No consciousness?
Inside the earthen jar formed of light, Black Zetsu slumped into a ball of viscous fluid, seemingly inert.
Zenkichi reached out to catch the falling Nagato and noted that both of the man's eye sockets were now empty.
"When Black Zetsu came this time... he left a portion of himself elsewhere as insurance," Zenkichi concluded.
"When Nagato arrived, he only had one Rinnegan... the other was still with Black Zetsu."
It all clicked. A flicker of understanding lit Zenkichi's eyes.
As expected of the wily old manipulator—Black Zetsu always ensured he had a fallback plan.
"Nagato!" cried Jiraiya, who was within the Allied Shinobi Forces, eyes locked on the man held in Zenkichi's grasp. His expression was complicated, conflicted.
Zenkichi casually tossed Nagato to his subordinates and turned his gaze toward the ninja army. A mad grin split across his face.
"Release the jinchūriki!"
A command echoed through the minds of the Allied Shinobi Forces. Instantly, the jinchūriki of the One, Two, Five, and Seven-Tails were pushed to the front lines.
The transformation began.
Four colossal tailed beasts stood before Zenkichi, their presence radiating terrifying, suffocating power.
"Do you really think five beasts are enough to stop me?" Zenkichi sneered. "Don't overestimate yourselves."
He lunged forward.
The tailed beasts roared as they charged, their immense chakra shaking the battlefield.
As Zenkichi closed in, a golden cross flashed beneath his feet.
Moving at light speed, he appeared beside Shukaku, the One-Tail, and unleashed a devastating kick.
"Speed is weight!"
"Shukaku, have you ever experienced a light-speed kick?"
The words echoed in Shukaku's ears as Zenkichi's shining figure struck him across the face.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
The massive tanuki was flung away—his size offering no protection from Zenkichi's attack.
Before anyone could react, Zenkichi turned into light particles again, evading the incoming claws of the Two-Tails.
He reappeared in front of the fiery blue cat, speaking calmly:
"Matatabi, a light-speed kick should help you think straight."
A golden flash.
The Two-Tails was sent crashing back like a rag doll.
The Five-Tails, a massive horse-like creature, charged forward with his massive horn aimed at Zenkichi's chest.
"Overestimating yourself."
Zenkichi's voice was cold and measured.
Despite the Five-Tails being one of the stronger bijū—strong enough to have seriously injured the Eight-Tails in the past—it meant little before Zenkichi.
Just as Uchiha Madara's clones had once overpowered the tailed beasts, so too could Zenkichi.
With one brutal kick to the head, the Five-Tails was silenced, letting out a pained whine that sent the Seven-Tails, Chōmei, into retreat.
The giant beetle-like beast, capable of flight, took to the sky in a panic.
But Zenkichi, glowing with golden light, burst into the air, blocking Chōmei's escape route—and kicked it downward.
"What a pity."
Zenkichi's hand brushed the sealing scroll on his waist—within it, another Rinnegan.
If he had already transplanted it, this battle would've ended even more swiftly.
His eyes gleamed coldly as he gazed at the disorganized, panicked Allied Shinobi Forces.
He'd gathered them all in one place—why waste the opportunity?
Zenkichi burst into golden light and shot toward the alliance.
Hanzo of the Salamander gritted his teeth, summoning his massive summoning beast—the giant Salamander.
The creature emerged with a roar, unleashing a deadly cloud of purple mist—a potent poison meant to counter Zenkichi.
But Zenkichi, in his light form, soared above the toxic fog with ease, untouched.
Ironically, it was the ninja below who suffered. Many were caught off guard by Hanzo's attack and were poisoned before they could react.
"Vanish from existence!"
Zenkichi hovered in the sky. Energy gathered in his hands, forming brilliant light bombs that rained down upon the Allied Forces.
"Namikaze Minato. Jiraiya. Gengetsu. The Sarutobi Clan. The Shimura Clan. Hanzo…"
He murmured their names like a curse as the torrent of light obliterated the battlefield.
Ōnoki, the Third Tsuchikage, erected a towering stone barrier in a desperate attempt to block the attack.
But under the merciless assault of golden light, the wall was crushed.
Hanzo's summoned salamander was reduced to pulp, riddled with holes.
Even Minato's Flying Thunder God technique couldn't save him from this overwhelming onslaught.
A beam pierced his heart—he died alongside his teacher, Jiraiya, joining their ancestors.
Zenkichi's assault lasted ten minutes.
When the light finally faded, the ground was unrecognizable—only a massive crater remained.

A series of system prompts echoed in his mind. At last, Zenkichi had unlocked the new character template: Aizen. The unlock percentage had already climbed to 23%.
He had destroyed countless ninja villages, eliminated numerous enemies, and even gathered all the tailed beasts.
These feats not only raised his synchronization rate with existing templates but also granted him access to new ones.
Now, he wielded the Zanpakutō — Kyōka Suigetsu. Unfortunately, he hadn't yet mastered its Shikai.
"Zanpakutō…"
Zenkichi looked down at the long blade in his hand, a subtle smirk on his face.
Until now, he'd been wondering how to deal with Black Zetsu.
But now, with a Zanpakutō that could target souls directly, even Black Zetsu was no longer a real threat.
The true problem with Black Zetsu was his incorporeal, consciousness-based form. But Zanpakutō — especially Kyōka Suigetsu — could strike at the soul. Not even he could withstand its power.
"Aizen… now that's a character who aligns with my tastes."
"Ambitious, deceptive, ruthless, composed, and gifted. Honestly… he's basically me."
Zenkichi chuckled to himself with smug confidence. "Though, let's be real—he's not quite on my level. No focus. No real will to evolve."
"He even orchestrated his own defeat just to create a worthy opponent? Please."
"I won't be copying that part."
"Still, Aizen… he's a damn good match for me."
"There's never been a true ruler in the Naruto world," he muttered. "Not Hashirama, not Madara, not even the Sage of Six Paths."
"But I will be the one to break the divide between mortals and shinobi… and rule them both."
Orochimaru's Underground Base
Danzo sat, his face dark with frustration. "My elite forces were wiped out. Every major village has fallen."
"That man… Zenkichi… has dismantled the entire ninja village system. I've heard rumors he wants to unify all shinobi under one organization."
Orochimaru barely looked up from his scroll. "What's it called? The Shinobi Alliance?"
Danzo shook his head. "No. It's called the Ninja Club. Sounds more like a department than a ruling body."
"Absurd, isn't it? The villages are gone, and now he's reducing everything to a single department."
Orochimaru finally paused, thoughtful. "If that's true… then his ambitions extend beyond the shinobi."
Danzo's expression shifted, realization dawning. "You think… he plans to challenge the Daimyo system too?"
"If he does," Orochimaru replied, returning to his work, "there's no one who can stop him now."
"He holds the greatest military power in the world. There's no counterweight left."
Danzo frowned. "The Daimyo system has existed for generations. Can he truly challenge it?"
Orochimaru answered coolly. "The only reason Konoha submits to the Fire Daimyo is because of funding. Military spending."
"Same reason the Wind Daimyo slashed Sunagakure's budget — they had alternatives. Any resistance could be crushed by other villages hired by the Daimyo."
"That's how the Daimyo played them all. But now, Zenkichi has shattered that balance. There are no other villages."
"The move to eliminate him… I suspect it came with Daimyo backing too."
"But it failed. Now that the village system is gone, so is their leverage."
"If he turns his attention to the Daimyo next—no one will be able to stop him."
Land of Fire – Daimyo's Mansion
Tsunade stood before the Fire Daimyo and his ministers, her expression grave.
"Zenkichi has declared the Land of Fire under his direct control, effective immediately."
"You, Daimyo, no longer govern this country. Your ministers now report to him. You are no longer king of this land."
"But don't panic—Zenkichi won't kill you… if you surrender the throne willingly. He promises prosperity for your family in return."
The Daimyo stared at Tsunade in disbelief. "Tsunade… you're royalty in this nation. How can you be so cold?"
Tsunade's face didn't flinch. "Zenkichi says this is the only path to peace in the shinobi world. You weren't exactly a good leader. Your abdication won't make much difference."
"Peace will only come when all nations are united under a common will."
"Resisting him is foolish. Even the Five Great Villages couldn't stand against him. What chance do you have?"
At her words, the Daimyo's courage faltered.
Tsunade was right. He had no hope of resisting.
The ministers hesitated—until one opportunistic official knelt and addressed Zenkichi as ruler. The rest followed.
Land of Iron
Zenkichi stood before the shattered remains of the samurai commander.
"Samurai swordsmanship? Not bad," he said casually. "You really meant to reject me with that attack?"
"If you oppose my control over the Land of Iron, then you die. Simple as that."
He continued speaking in Kizaru's laid-back tone, golden light gleaming at his fingertips.
"Wait!"
The Daimyo and the surviving samurai elite panicked at the sight of that light. "We can negotiate!"
Zenkichi scoffed. "Too late."
Lasers fired from his fingertips, vaporizing the leadership of the Iron Country in an instant.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 96 - 96: Ruler of the Shinobi world.
chapters.content:
Konoha Village – Hokage's Office
Arakawa Zenkichi stood at the window, gazing at the bustling village below, a faint smile tugging at his lips.
Thanks to Zenkichi's influence, the daimyos from all nations had willingly relinquished their positions. Now, there was only one unified nation in the shinobi world, ruled over by Zenkichi. Both civilians and shinobi lived under his governance.
This monumental achievement had pushed his Aizen template to 42% synchronization, and he was even close to unlocking Kyoka Suigetsu.
After consolidating power, Zenkichi restructured the disbanded samurai, turning them into a new police and military force.
Konoha, once a militarized village, had now transformed into a bustling commercial city. While a few shinobi remained stationed here, the majority had been deployed across the world. Becoming a ninja was no longer shrouded in mystery—it was open knowledge.
"Zenkichi,"
Tsunade entered through the door, staring at him with a perplexed look.
"Why are you looking at me like that?" Zenkichi asked, his warm smile still in place.
"Are you okay?" Tsunade frowned. Something about him felt... off.
"You feel like the king of the ninja world now," she muttered. "You've changed—completely. You used to be a little shameless and cold, but you were sharp and ambitious."
Zenkichi chuckled. "And now?"
"You seem fake," she said bluntly. "This gentle demeanor doesn't suit you."
"That's just your assumption," he replied, still smiling. "A lot of people find this side of me quite charming."
"I'm the ruler of the ninja world now. A little kindness doesn't hurt."
Tsunade scoffed. "Hypocrite."
Zenkichi shrugged, unbothered. "Say whatever you want, Tsunade. After all, we know each other better than anyone."
Tsunade's face turned red. She shot him a glare. "I must have lost my mind."Follow current novels on
"Be honest with me—how many women have you charmed? Something's off about Uzumaki Kushina lately."
Zenkichi sighed. "Don't blame me. They come to me willingly. That's the downside of being too attractive—it's exhausting."
Tsunade crossed her arms. "Exhausting? You sound proud."
Zenkichi stepped forward and took her hand. "Alright, alright. No need to rant."
"At least in Konoha, you're the only woman who's ever succeeded."
Meanwhile, Terumi Mei was in the Land of Water, helping its shinobi adapt to their roles as military police. She was a strong woman, driven by the desire to prove herself. After Zenkichi gave her the opportunity, she immediately traveled there to take charge.
Pakura had gone to the Land of Wind, using her own experience to reform what remained of Sunagakure. Though Sunagakure had sent its main force against Zenkichi, many remained behind. With her influence, she exposed the village's dark past and convinced the remaining shinobi to surrender.
Pakura was once a hero of Sunagakure and still held significant prestige there.
"Zenkichi!"
Just as Zenkichi and Tsunade were relaxing, preparing to contribute to the revival of the Senju Clan, Uzumaki Kushina burst into the office.
Zenkichi and Tsunade quickly stood up, putting on a dignified front, though Kushina clearly wasn't impressed.
"What is it?" Zenkichi asked, putting on a gentle smile.
"Nagato's been discharged from the hospital," Kushina said seriously. "I plan to return to the Land of Whirlpools with him. We're the only two left from the Uzumaki clan. I want to rebuild it."
"You and Nagato?" Zenkichi frowned. "That doesn't sound right."
Why Nagato? What happened to Minato? Why him, of all people?
Kushina's face reddened. "What are you imagining?! It's not like that!"
Zenkichi nodded slowly. "Good. That's a relief."
Still, he reminded himself that clinging to outdated notions of morality didn't suit the new world.
"The Land of Whirlpools has been in ruins for years," Kushina said. "But I still think it's worth rebuilding. That's why I need your approval."
Zenkichi replied calmly, "Why return there? The environment isn't the best. You could consider the Land of Grass. I believe there's another Uzumaki there—a woman. Maybe she and Nagato would be a better match."
Kushina blinked in surprise. "Really? That's great news!"
Zenkichi sighed. At the start of this new era, there were so many tasks to handle. Fortunately, he didn't need to train anymore—otherwise, he'd be overwhelmed.
A short while later, Yahiko and Konan arrived to speak with him.
Yahiko came to say goodbye and informed Zenkichi that he planned to return to the Land of Rain.
He'd remained in Konoha only because Nagato hadn't fully recovered. But now that Nagato had adapted to the ordinary eyes Zenkichi had transplanted into him, Yahiko was ready to leave.
"The work in Amegakure isn't really suited for Konan," Yahiko added. "Could you arrange something safe for her?"
Zenkichi thought for a moment. "Hmm... I still need a secretary. Let her stay here."
Yahiko nodded. "Thanks. I appreciate it."
The ninja world, newly unified under Zenkichi, was still in chaos. Rogue shinobi weren't tolerated, and disturbances continued to arise.
But Zenkichi knew—he would bring order to it all.
His life, at the moment, was stable.
No... not stable.
Boring. Predictable. Dull.
"What about Black Zetsu? Orochimaru?"
"Where's the plan to make the world feel pain?"
"We were supposed to dance together…"
Zenkichi found himself missing those two troublemakers.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 97 - 97: Sasori & Kakuzu.
chapters.content:
"The Scorpion of Red Sand—It Is Indeed You!"
"You've been attacking the shinobi from the Ninja Association repeatedly lately. Are you trying to avenge the destruction of Sunagakure?"
"I didn't expect that you, a former rogue ninja of the Sand, would act like this."
Pakura stood firmly before the Red Sand Scorpion, her voice cold and unyielding.
"Pakura… I never imagined that even you—once the pride of Sunagakure—would become Zenkichi's lapdog."
The Red Sand Scorpion maneuvered within Sasori, its long tail twitching ominously behind it.
"This is the peace shinobi have waited for," Pakura said, closing her eyes briefly, then reopening them with icy calm. "I won't let you two disrupt it."
"This peace you speak of? It's not the kind I've been waiting for," Kakuzu sneered. "Where do you expect me to earn money once peace spreads across the nations?"
"Zenkichi destroyed my income. He destroyed everything I trusted."
"I heard you're one of Zenkichi's women. It must hurt him to see you killed!"
Suddenly, a deep voice echoed in the clearing. Horned and heavily cloaked, Kakuzu stepped out beside the Scorpion.
Pakura's expression didn't change. "So, two destroyers join forces. How predictable."
Kakuzu scoffed. "It took considerable effort to lure you out. Against two shinobi of our caliber, you have no escape."
Pakura curled her lip. "Even Kage-level shinobi can appear pitiful in the face of an entire Ninja Village. Do you know why?"
"Because a shinobi's strength isn't only in battle power—it's in intelligence gathering, strategy, and resources."
"You think I didn't know what the two of you were planning?"
At that moment, three figures emerged from the shadows—Momochi Zabuza, Hoshigaki Kisame, and Mizunashi Yukine—once disciples of Arakawa Zenkichi. They flanked Kakuzu and Sasori from all directions.
Kakuzu glanced around and scoffed arrogantly. "So it's just the four of you? That's not nearly enough."
"Kill me? Even the so-called 'God of Shinobi'—Senju Hashirama—couldn't do that. And you think you can?"
He smirked, clearly proud of the tale he'd been repeating for decades.
"What about me?"
A familiar voice cut in sharply.
Kakuzu and Sasori expressions shifted as they turned to see Zenkichi standing calmly atop a tree branch, his presence overwhelming.
"Zenkichi…"
Their faces darkened. His reputation wasn't mere talk—it was built atop the corpses of countless powerful shinobi.
"Sasori of the Red Sand," Zenkichi called gently. "Would you consider submitting to me? I can spare your life."
Sasori was silent for a moment before responding, "I may despise that old hag Chiyo, but she didn't deserve to die at your hands."
Zenkichi's tone remained neutral. "Interesting. So it was for Chiyo's sake… That actually makes sense."
"After all, you killed the Third Kazekage with your own hands. You've never had any real loyalty to Sunagakure."
Pakura's eyes widened. "You… killed the Third Kazekage?"
Just how old had the Scorpion been when that happened? Only a puppet master could have pulled off something so treacherous.
"Since Sasori refuses to surrender, what about you, Kakuzu?"
Zenkichi turned his attention to him.
"I have to admit, I'm impressed that you survived a battle with the First Hokage. Wouldn't you prefer to work for me instead?"
"Tired of running around murdering people for cash? Come work under me—you'll find it much easier."
Kakuzu raised an eyebrow. "Are you serious?"Thɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Zenkichi smiled. "Of course not. You've killed too many of my people. Surrender was only an option if you'd taken it from the beginning. Now? Death is your only path."
Kakuzu snarled. "You're underestimating me! I'll kill you where you stand!"
Zenkichi laughed. "Kill me? You've developed a sense of humor in your old age."
"But I suggest you stop bluffing. It only makes your fear more obvious."
Pakura gritted her teeth. "Let's stop wasting time with words. Let's end them!"
In an instant, Pakura moved—Shunshin no Jutsu (Body Flicker Technique).
She reappeared in front of Sasori and launched her attack.
"Scorch Release—Twin Fireballs!"
Two searing orange fireballs ignited in her palms and smashed into Sasori. The wooden shell quickly burned and crumbled under the intense heat.
A young man with crimson hair leaped from the wreckage—the true form of the Red Sand Scorpion.
In a swift motion, he fired a barrage of hidden senbon needles at Pakura.
"Iron Body!"
Pakura hardened her body using one of the six styles that Zenkichi taught them, the needles bouncing harmlessly off her skin.
Puppet techniques were weak without toxins. Against hardened defense, they were meaningless.
But the Scorpion wasn't done. He unfurled a scroll and summoned his prized puppet—the Third Kazekage.
The puppet still retained the magnetic chakra of the original. Sand gathered in mid-air.
"Third Kazekage…" Pakura muttered, slipping a golden glove onto her hand.
Six faintly glowing gems shimmered on its surface—a weapon of an ancient civilization, forged from Grayl Stone, found in the Wind Country territory she oversaw.
Just as the puppet attacked, Pakura surged forward. One punch—boosted by the gauntlet—sent the Kazekage puppet flying.
Elsewhere, Kakuzu was under siege.
Mizunashi Yukine, now a master of Ice Release, provided long-range bombardment—a shooter.
Momochi Zabuza, wielding the Executioner's Blade, used brute force—the bruiser.
Hoshigaki Kisame, fused with Samehada, absorbed chakra—the main attacker.
The three pseudo-jinchūriki activated their Tailed Beast Chakra Cloaks, surrounding Kakuzu.
Though Sasori had fallen, Kakuzu held out. With five hearts, he was the ultimate tank.
But with Zenkichi's presence looming, even immortality had its limits.
And Pakura—her golden glove shining—stood tall, unstoppable.
---
