chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 126: You two, become my daughters.
chapters.content:
After resolving matters in the two Naruto worlds, Arakawa Zenkichi activated the system's world-hopping function.
In an instant, he found himself standing amidst a bustling modern city street.
Using Observation Haki, Zenkichi scanned the entire area and quickly grasped where he had landed.
"Fuyuki City... the Holy Grail War?"
He narrowed his eyes in thought, immediately recognizing the world he had arrived in.
(Fate/Stay Series, Do note: i haven't watched it yet. There might be errors so I'm just about to stream it now so as to understand who characters are and to avoid translation errors.)
His Haki continued to probe the city, and soon he sensed several distinct auras—clearly not those of ordinary people.
With a slight movement, Zenkichi vanished from sight, reappearing at the gates of a luxurious villa.
At that moment, two men and three women were slowly exiting the building.
One of the men wore a finely tailored suit, exuding the grace of a noble gentleman. The other, an elderly man, radiated a gloomy and oppressive aura.
They were Tohsaka Tokiomi, the current head of the Tohsaka family, and Matou Zouken, head of the Matou family. With them were Tokiomi's wife, Aoi, and their daughters—Rin, the elder, and Sakura, the younger.
Matou Zouken turned to Sakura and said, "From today, you are the adopted daughter of the Matou family."
Tohsaka Tokiomi added, "From now on, you are no longer Tohsaka Sakura. You are Matou Sakura."
Sakura's eyes were dull. She nodded woodenly, like a puppet. She didn't understand why her father was giving her away. But as a child, she had no say in the matter.
"I don't agree with this deal!"
A clear, commanding voice cut through the air.
A young man walked over with heavy steps and sharp eyes, glaring at Tokiomi.
"Family is the most precious treasure. And you're just handing her away? Bastard!"
Tokiomi frowned. "Who are you? The affairs of the Tohsaka family are none of your concern."
Zenkichi laughed. "Gu ra ra ra!"
(Oh nooo, that was totally unexpected, even for me...)
With a sweep of his hand, a massive naginata materialized—Whitebeard's famed weapon, the supreme-grade blade Murakumogiri.
"Magic?" Both Tokiomi and Zouken perked up, their eyes lighting up with curiosity. Could this man be a mage?
But their expressions quickly changed when Zenkichi swung his naginata and unleashed a surge of sword energy that split the ground—and the distant Tohsaka villa—in two.
Boom!
Tokiomi: "..."
Zouken: "..."
This man was clearly not a magician.
Zenkichi turned to them with a calm smile. "I'm taking these two little girls with me. Anyone opposed?"
Neither man dared to speak.
"Gu ra ra ra! Excellent. You two... are now my daughters!"
"From today, you'll carry the name of Whitebeard and roam this world with pride!"
Zenkichi beamed at Rin and Sakura.
Tohsaka Rin snapped, "Sakura and I don't want to be your daughters, you weirdo!"
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "You don't get to choose. Your parents already agreed."
Rin looked at her parents, saw the fear in their eyes, and growled. She charged at Zenkichi.
"You jerk!"
With a brief pause, Zenkichi lightly bonked her on the head—a gentle but firm "iron fist of love." Rin yelped and held her head, tears welling up.
"That's enough. Now call me daddy," Zenkichi said flatly.
Neither girl responded.
They were clearly frightened, but Zenkichi didn't care. They'd come around eventually.
Whitebeard had converted people with far rougher methods—Zenkichi was confident his charm would do the job faster.
"You two... how about becoming my sons instead?" he joked, smirking. "I think some strict re-education will do you good."
Turning to Tokiomi and Zouken, he mused aloud, "Should I adopt you two too?"
"Absolutely not!" Tokiomi said firmly. "A magician's pride is worth more than life itself."
Zenkichi waved it off. "Relax, I'm just kidding. I'm not into pot-luck parenting."
No need to gather useless baggage. Tokiomi was nothing more than another Danzo-type figure, and Zenkichi had no desire to become a second Scheming King.
"Let's go."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Without waiting for permission, Zenkichi grabbed Rin and Sakura by the hands and led them away.
"His blade...?" Tokiomi and Zouken stared at Murakumogiri in shock.
Zouken hesitated, then flicked a bug toward Zenkichi—a signature Matou technique.
But before it could get close, a laser shot from behind Zenkichi's head and vaporized it.
Zouken screamed and transformed into a swarm of insects to flee, but a barrage of high-temperature lasers incinerated him midair.
"Let's move. Don't look back," Zenkichi said as if nothing had happened, leading the girls away.
Rin's curiosity couldn't be contained. "Did your hair just shoot a laser? What kind of magic is that?"
"You'll find out later," Zenkichi replied casually.
Rin pouted. "You're the worst. Where are you even taking us?"
Zenkichi stopped, deep in thought. "Now that's a good question. I've only just arrived in this world, and there's no ship that can carry me..."
"So, we'll need a place to settle down. Know anyone rich and corrupt in Fuyuki City? No? Never mind. I'll handle it."
He gave up on questioning the girls and turned his sights on Matou's estate.
He'd just wiped out Matou Zouken—it was time to collect his loot.
The Matou family was known for their wealth and magical resources. It'd be more than enough to keep him comfortable.
And if Zouken's ancient relic of a grandson tried to resist... well, Zenkichi wouldn't mind gaining another "son."
If the kid proved hopeless, he could always send him off to meet his ancestors.
With that thought, Arakawa Zenkichi led the two girls to the Matou residence.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 127: Perverted Lunatic?
chapters.content:
Matou Kariya stared at the two little girls who had suddenly appeared in his home and asked with confusion, "Rin, Sakura, why are you two here?"
Zenkichi didn't flinch. His tone was casual, almost indifferent.
"From today onward, the three of us will be living here."
He paused, then added calmly, "Also, I should inform you—your ancestor has been eliminated by me."
Matou Kariya's brows furrowed. "What do you mean by that? Rin, Sakura, what is going on?"
Tohsaka Rin's face was full of irritation.
"This bastard just appeared at my doorstep and took the two of us!"Googlᴇ search Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"And by the way he's acting now, it looks like your house is going to be his next target."
Hearing that, Kariya's expression twisted in anger. He turned to Zenkichi. "Is what Rin said true?"
Zenkichi shrugged. "Of course it's true. That bastard Tokiomi Tohsaka..."
His words were suddenly interrupted when he glanced down and saw Rin glaring up at him. Without warning, he gave her a light flick to the forehead.
"Why are you looking at me like that, little girl?"
"Anyway, back to what I was saying. Tokiomi Tohsaka made a deal with your ancestor, Matou Zouken."
"Yes, Matou Zouken is the patriarch of the Matou family. You don't have to act so surprised."
"That disgusting old man relies on insects to survive. He should've been put down a long time ago. I was simply correcting a mistake."
"If Sakura had really been handed over to him, her fate would have been miserable."
"Matou Kariya can confirm that. Isn't that right? The Matou family's magecraft is practiced through parasitic bugs."
As Zenkichi explained, both Rin and Sakura turned toward Kariya, their eyes filled with disbelief. The reality of the Matou magecraft was far worse than anything they had been taught.
Kariya could only sigh.
"Yes... everything he said is true. Honestly, I'm grateful he stopped it. If not, I wouldn't be able to face Aoi."
Zenkichi's gaze shifted.
"Who's that?"
He raised his hand, and with a snap, a golden beam of light shot out—piercing the wall and striking a boy hidden outside.
"That was Matou Shinji, my nephew!" Kariya exclaimed, stunned. "You... you killed him?!"
Zenkichi looked unimpressed. "That brat? It was a mercy."
He turned back to the girls. "Come with me, Rin, Sakura. We live here now."
Then, glancing at Kariya, he added, "As for you... well, I'm a kind person. I won't kick you out."
Matou Kariya blinked.
"Wait a second. Isn't this my house?"
Zenkichi gave him a deadpan stare. "What's with that look? Listen here—I'm Whitebeard, more dangerous than any demon."
"You know what I do? I'm a pirate. Robbing people is literally part of the job description."
"This place? It's mine now. Respect the hustle."
There was a strange energy to Zenkichi, like he was here not to win anything, but just to enjoy himself. Maybe collect a few godchildren, unlock a few new titles. That kind of vibe.
As he looked at Rin and Sakura, he shook his head a little.
"Too early for goddaughters..."
Tohsaka Sakura suddenly spoke up quietly. "Your name is Whitebeard?"
Zenkichi replied without missing a beat.
"No. That's just one of the many nicknames I've earned from those trembling in awe across the seas."
"I go by many names, but my birth name is Arakawa Zenkichi."
Kariya was watching him closely. "You're not a Servant, are you? No human can use abilities like that."
Zenkichi nodded with conviction.
"Don't underestimate humanity. Of all the races on the sea, humans still rule the top."
Kariya sighed.
"I feel like we're not on the same wavelength here... this conversation is exhausting."
Then he spoke cautiously. "Still... you should be prepared. Tokiomi won't let this go. He'll find you, and it won't end peacefully."
Zenkichi waved him off. "So what? I'm not afraid of him. You're not thinking of sending these two back to Tohsaka Aoi, are you?"
Kariya hesitated.
"Aoi will be heartbroken if she can't see her daughters."
Zenkichi's voice turned firm.
"If she wants to see them, she can come here. But they're not going back. That's non-negotiable."
Kariya lowered his head. He knew he didn't have the power to argue.
Zenkichi turned toward Rin and Sakura.
"From now on, Tohsaka Rin and Sakura Matouare the daughters of Whitebeard."
"In life or death, they are my people. They won't be handed back to Tokiomi under any circumstance."
"And don't even talk to me about that scumbag raising them. He didn't even manage his own marriage properly."
"Just look at what he did to Aoi. He handed her to hell and didn't blink. That's the kind of man he is."
Zenkichi smirked slightly.
"When you see Aoi, tell her she can come here anytime. I wouldn't mind having another daughter."
"Yeah, let her come. I'll fix her broken heart and bring her back to the light."
Rin immediately snapped.
"You perverted lunatic!"
Kariya winced. He was starting to seriously question the wisdom of letting these girls stay with this madman.
Was it really safe?
He fell into deep thought.
Though frankly, it wasn't going to make much of a difference.
Zenkichi had already decided—and no one was changing his mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 129 - 129: Lancelot.
chapters.content:
Time passed swiftly as Arakawa Zenkichi continued training the Tohsaka sisters. Before anyone realized it, the day of the Fourth Holy Grail War had arrived.
Matou Kariya stared down at the three Command Seals etched on his hand. Without hesitation, he pulled out the summoning catalyst—an artifact tied to Lancelot du Lac.
He carefully drew the summoning circle and began to chant in a low, focused tone:
"Let thy body be under my command, thy fate under my control. If thou accedes to this will and reason, then answer me…
Heed me in the name of our covenant. I summon thee, forth from the eternal cycle of death and rebirth!"
A blinding light erupted from the summoning circle. From its center emerged a towering knight, clad in dark armor, his aura soaked in madness and fury.
The Servant: Berserker. Lancelot of the Lake.
In order to amplify his combat strength, Kariya had deliberately invoked the Madness Enhancement when summoning him. The result: a near-mindless warrior consumed by rage.
"...Perfect."
Kariya looked at the knight he had summoned and nodded in grim satisfaction. The time had come to confront Zenkichi.
It had been nearly a year, and throughout that time, Arakawa Zenkichi hadn't slackened in his "education" of the Tohsaka sisters. By now, both Rin and Sakura had grudgingly accepted the codenames he gave them and no longer resisted him as much.
Despite their initial misgivings, they'd come to understand that Zenkichi wasn't truly malicious—aside from refusing to let them go home. Even when Rin mouthed off, the worst she got was a flick to the head. They could still visit their mother freely, something a true kidnapper would never allow.
---
Now, Kariya appeared before Zenkichi with Lancelot at his side.
"Zenkichi," Kariya demanded, "release the Tohsaka sisters."
Zenkichi raised a brow as his eyes settled on the armored knight. "So that's your Servant? Lancelot? And you think he's enough to challenge me?"
He chuckled, amused. "You might want to gather a few allies before coming at me. You'd stand a better chance."
"I'm not here for games," Kariya said coldly. "You've held them long enough. Let them go."
His tone was resolute. He knew his time was short—his body, warped by magic experiments, wouldn't last another three months. But he intended to use the time he had left to do what truly mattered:
First, protect the daughters of the woman he loved—Tohsaka Aoi.
Second, defeat Tohsaka Tokiomi in the Holy Grail War and prove he was the better man.
"Overestimating yourself," Zenkichi sighed and gestured lazily. "Come on then."
Kariya didn't hesitate. With a command, Lancelot charged forward, sword raised high.
Zenkichi drew his naginata, a replica of Whitebeard's weapon, and met the attack head-on.
With a single powerful swing, he sent Lancelot flying.
The Berserker landed heavily, growling under his breath, temporarily stunned.
Zenkichi had already stacked Kizaru's speed with his own immense strength—pure physical combat alone was enough to overwhelm most Servants.
"Matou Kariya, it seems your Servant isn't enough," Zenkichi said with a smile. "Tell you what—I'll make you a deal. Hand Lancelot over to me."
"What?" Kariya snapped.
"I'm serious. Without a Servant, I can't officially join the Grail War. You give me Lancelot, and in return, I'll defeat Tokiomi for you."
"You've seen what I can do. Crushing him would be effortless."
"Impossible," Kariya replied, voice hard. "Defeating Tokiomi is something I must do myself."
"That's admirable," Zenkichi said, then smirked. "But I'm telling you now—you can't beat him."
"His Servant is leagues above yours."
Kariya narrowed his eyes. "Who did he summon?"
"The King of Heroes. Gilgamesh. Class: Archer. Probably the most dangerous Servant in this war."
Kariya's face darkened. That name… it was a nightmare.
"I'll give Lancelot to you," he said slowly. "But only if you promise to defeat Gilgamesh in my place."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "You think Lancelot can beat him? Don't kid yourself. Even with your Command Spells, he'd stand no chance."
"When the time comes, I'll handle Gilgamesh personally."
"I'll beat that golden bastard into the ground."
Kariya blinked. "…Actually, that's not a bad idea."
After seeing how easily Zenkichi overwhelmed Berserker, maybe—just maybe—it was possible.
"You don't want to get humiliated by Tokiomi again, do you?" Zenkichi continued. "You already lost Aoi to him. Are you going to lose everything else too?"
"But if you agree to my terms, I promise I'll rescue Tohsaka Aoi myself. I'll pull her out of the fire that is the Tohsaka family."
Kariya hesitated. "You don't… have any weird thoughts about Aoi, do you?"
Zenkichi raised a brow. "With a body like yours, what does it matter? You can't protect her, but I can. Isn't that enough?"
Kariya clenched his fists.
In the end, he had no choice.
"I'll transfer the Command Spells to you."
With a bitter smile, Kariya passed the magical crest to Zenkichi.
Power surged into Zenkichi's body as the Command Seals etched themselves into his skin. It was an unfamiliar yet exhilarating sensation.
No surprise there. With the templates of Aizen and Kizaru integrated into him, mastering this world's magic was child's play.
Now, as Lancelot's new Master, Zenkichi's powerful energy began to stabilize the Berserker's mind.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
The madness was suppressed, if only slightly, and the knight finally looked at him with clear eyes.
"…Are you my new Master?"
"I am," Zenkichi replied with a grin. "Welcome aboard."

chapters.title: Chapter 130 - 130: King of heroes.
chapters.content:
"It's such powerful magic… It helped purge the effects of the Madness Curse."
Lancelot sighed, overwhelmed by the sheer force of the energy flowing through Arakawa Zenkichi. He hadn't expected such power.
Zenkichi curled his lips, unfazed. "Of course it is."
With Kizaru and Aizen's influence, and the constant evolution fueled by Hōgyoku, Zenkichi's strength had climbed to a terrifying level.
He felt that, with the magical energy he had now—especially enhanced by Lancelot's presence—he might just be able to flip the earth itself.
Lancelot's power was absurd. His magical grip alone could subdue almost anything with ease.
That's what earned him the title of one of the "Four Walking Kings." His ability was so broken, so overwhelming… it was even jokingly referred to as the "Hand of NTR."
"Zenkichi-sama, shall we begin hunting the other contestants?"
Lancelot's tone was eager. The magical reinforcement from Zenkichi left him more empowered than ever.
Zenkichi glanced at him. "Before that, there's something you should know."
He paused a beat before continuing, his tone serious.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the
"Your former king, Artoria… she's also a participant in this Holy Grail War. Are you prepared to face her?"
"…The King?"
Lancelot froze. The image of golden hair and determined eyes flashed in his mind, and bitterness crept onto his face.
"One of the reasons I joined the Holy Grail War was to atone. I wanted to face the King again… to be judged."
"If she's my opponent, I may not be able to guarantee your victory, Zenkichi-sama."
His words carried the burden of a knight's pride and regret, tangled with loyalty and guilt.
"I see. Then answer a few questions for me," Zenkichi said, examining the Command Seal glowing faintly on his hand, "and I'll allow you to act freely."
Lancelot's eyes brightened. "You have my word!"
"Tell me, Lancelot… Is it true that you seduced King Arthur's wife?"
Lancelot's expression stiffened. He laughed awkwardly. "That's purely a rumor, Zenkichi-sama. The relationship between the Queen and me was… entirely innocent."
"Of course, once rumors began to spread, they created misunderstandings. Those whispers eventually led to disaster for the realm."
Zenkichi raised a brow. "Really? Hard to believe. It's said that King Arthur's wife was incredibly beautiful."
Lancelot shifted uncomfortably. "Even so… please don't doubt my discipline as a knight. My devotion—our devotion—was always to King Arthur above all."
His last words trailed into a whisper, but Zenkichi caught them.
"So it's true after all," Zenkichi said, nodding knowingly.
With Artoria's looks, how could the Round Table knights not be tempted?
A pity, really—Queen Guinevere had no say in her fate. Married to a king, yet lacking the charisma to hold a man's gaze.
"You've endured a lot, Lancelot," Zenkichi said. "Tell you what. Why not become mine?"
Lancelot stared. "…"
What kind of twisted logic was that?
He looked visibly awkward. Still, Zenkichi pressed on.
"Besides, your monarch isn't an easy woman. When I meet her, I'll make her my daughter."
"That way, you two can reconcile as family."
To make your former love your sister… Zenkichi grinned. That was poetic in its own way.
He shrugged. "It's pointless to explain further. You'll understand when the time comes."
Lancelot lowered his head. "Please, Zenkichi-sama, do not insult my King's dignity."
May all lovers in the world become siblings, Zenkichi mused, still amused at his own plan.
"Come with me. I'll introduce you to two little girls. From now on, your job is to protect them."
Zenkichi brought Lancelot before Tohsaka Rin and Tohsaka Sakura, casually gesturing between them.
Sakura observed Lancelot with wide, curious eyes. She stood quietly, reserved.
Rin, on the other hand, darted toward him and boldly poked his armor, her curiosity uncontained.
Lancelot smiled politely. As the Flower of Knights, his demeanor remained noble and refined.
"Zenkichi-sama, do you not need me to fight for you to achieve victory?" he asked, clearly longing for the battlefield.
Babysitting wasn't exactly a knight's dream.
If he could meet Artoria in combat… that would be enough. To fall to her blade, he would have no regrets.
"No need," Zenkichi replied casually.
"The Heroic Spirits this time are no pushovers. You may not be able to beat them…"
He paused, flashing a confident grin.
"But I could make them call me 'dad' by the end."
Lancelot chuckled. That arrogance felt oddly reassuring.
"I look forward to the day you win," said Matou Kariya, his voice hoarse from illness as he stifled a dry cough.
"You're not looking so great," Zenkichi noted. "Ever consider switching lifeforms? Maybe become a spirit, or a Hollow?"
"I'm fine…" Kariya muttered. "It's not necessary."
His only drive was the downfall of Tokiomi Tohsaka. Nothing else mattered.
Zenkichi activated his Observation Haki, sweeping through Fuyuki City with a grin.
"Heroic Spirits were summoned today. Everyone's holding back, playing it safe…"
He smirked.
"In that case, I'll stir the pot a little. Let's see who takes the bait."
With a casual step, Zenkichi vanished, reappearing on the outskirts of Fuyuki City. The pressure he released surged through the region like a shockwave.
This wasn't just provocation—it was an invitation.
---
Tohsaka Residence.
The King of Heroes, Gilgamesh, lounged on the couch like he owned the place. No trace of a Servant's humility in sight.
Meanwhile, Tokiomi Tohsaka practically waited on him hand and foot, more retainer than Master.
"Tokiomi, what are you still hesitating for?"
"With my strength, I could annihilate those pests with ease."
"What's the point of sitting around?"
Gilgamesh was irritated. He had long grown bored and wanted to test himself against the other Heroic Spirits.
He didn't regard any of them as threats.
"Please, King, be patient."
"If we want to win, this isn't the right time to act," Tokiomi said carefully, suppressing his own desire to go rescue his daughters.
And yet he told Gilgamesh to restrain himself.
At that moment, a tremendous aura swept across Fuyuki City.
It originated from the city's outskirts—unmistakably powerful, and clearly challenging others.
"…Arrogant, aren't they?" Gilgamesh scoffed.
"But with power like that, they've earned the right to be."
Without another word, the King of Heroes rose and vanished in a flash of golden light.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 131 - 131: Call Me Father.
chapters.content:
Zenkichi's overwhelming aura surged across Fuyuki City, a tidal wave of intent radiating in every direction. His presence alone bent the wills of lesser beings, while Heroic Spirits and Masters alike found themselves caught in the web of his Haki-infused perception.
He wasn't hiding. On the contrary, he stood tall and proud—challenging all who dared approach.
The first to accept the provocation was none other than the Lancer-class Servant, Diarmuid Ua Duibhne. This generation's Lancer was unique, possessing a captivating black mole beneath one eye—a mark that would be charming on a woman, but somehow made him even more striking as a man.
Zenkichi studied him briefly, eyes narrowing.
That mole… it really does have some power over women. Not bad.
"Lancer—Diarmuid. Step forward and fight."
Lancer's expression hardened as he leveled his crimson spear, Gáe Dearg, toward Zenkichi.
"I fight by the code of chivalry," he said solemnly. "I will face you with honor."
Zenkichi tilted his head with a grin.
"Just you? Hah, don't be in such a rush."
"If I defeat you now, you might cling to the illusion that the gap between us isn't insurmountable."
"I'll wait until the rest arrive. Seven Heroic Spirits. One me."
"I want to crush all your confidence in a single strike."
Lancer's brows furrowed in disbelief.
"You're that arrogant? I assumed you were a man of principle. Turns out you're just full of yourself."
Zenkichi chuckled.
"Oh? So you feel insulted already? Let's make it interesting."
"If I beat all of you together—one against six—how about you start calling me 'Father'?"
He leaned on his naginata, grinning wildly. The aura he exuded now was something beyond even the greatest warriors—a kingly force.
"Your arrogance will be your downfall!" Lancer roared, no longer able to restrain himself.
He charged forward and thrust his demonic spear directly at Zenkichi's forehead—an attack that would normally pierce even magical defenses.
But Zenkichi moved, fluid and controlled. With a single flick of his Haki-coated naginata, he knocked the spear aside like it was a child's toy.
Lancer skidded back, eyes wide with disbelief.
"That... that power...!"
From the shadows, a soft gleam emerged. Blonde hair and emerald eyes. Artoria Pendragon had arrived—the so-called King of Knights, often mistaken for a man in history. Her sword, Excalibur, hung ready at her side.
She had been hoping to follow Emiya Kiritsugu's strategic lead, keeping herself hidden until the right moment. But Zenkichi's overt challenge had disrupted everything.
War had already been declared, and to her, fighting from the shadows felt like cowardice.
"You've drawn more attention, huh?" Zenkichi smirked, turning to her.
"Two? Not enough," he continued, arms crossed. "How about I fight ten?"
"Young King Arthur, if you lose, how about becoming my daughter?"Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Artoria narrowed her eyes. "The dignity of a king cannot be mocked."
"Well said!" came a booming voice, cutting through the atmosphere.
A thunderous chariot blazed onto the scene, pulled by divine bulls. The mighty King of Conquerors had arrived—Iskandar himself. His Noble Phantasm, the Gordius Wheel, tore across the field as lightning crackled around its wheels.
"Ha!" Zenkichi let out a bellowing laugh. "That's just an ox cart. I'm the kind of man who can stop a warship with one hand!"
He raised his palm calmly and met the divine bulls head-on.
The moment his hand touched the chariot's front, a shockwave exploded outward. The bulls staggered and halted as if they'd slammed into an invisible mountain. Zenkichi roared, and with sheer brute strength, flipped the chariot skyward.
The King of Conquerors stared in disbelief.
"That was no trick… That strength is real…"
A moment of silence passed—until Zenkichi lifted his head again.
"Only three of you? No, I count four."
He looked into a nearby shadow where a presence lurked. "Hassan. You won't act unless provoked, huh?"
No answer. Only the cold gaze of the assassin lingered.
Then a voice echoed from above.
"To think you'd cause this much chaos with just your mouth."
Standing atop a streetlamp was the King of Heroes—Gilgamesh. Clad in golden armor, his eyes shone with disdain.
Zenkichi grinned.
"King of Heroes, you've got some nerve. Tell you what—be my son. I'll raise you properly."
Gilgamesh's face contorted with rage.
"You dare…"
Behind him shimmered a ripple, like the surface of a disturbed pond. From it, a barrage of treasures burst forth—swords, spears, and ancient relics—all launched from the Gate of Babylon.
Zenkichi's right hand clenched.
A faint white glow enveloped his fist—the power of the Tremor-Tremor Fruit.
"Air Shock."
He punched the space before him, and the very air cracked like glass. The vibration created a mirrored barrier that shattered the incoming Noble Phantasms before they could touch him.
The King of Heroes faltered, his face darkening.
"What… is this strange power?"
Zenkichi turned his gaze calmly and spoke with a booming laugh.
"I am Edward Zenkichi, the man who'll shake this world!"
"Why not save yourselves the trouble? Call me father now—sons and daughters alike."
"But if you insist, I'll beat the entire lot of you into the ground."

chapters.title: Chapter 132 - 132: Conqueror's Will
chapters.content:
"One Piece? A name I've never heard before."
"Edward Zenkichi? That name doesn't seem popular either."
Several Heroic Spirits across the battlefield were visibly confused. Servants summoned by the Holy Grail should be legendary figures—widely known, respected, or feared.
"King, that man isn't a Heroic Spirit," Tokiomi Tohsaka said with certainty, speaking to the King of Heroes. "He arrived in this world a year before the Holy Grail War began. Don't be deceived."
Gilgamesh narrowed his eyes, his golden pupils locking onto the white-haired warrior standing boldly before them.
"You're not a Heroic Spirit?" the King of Heroes asked, skeptical.
Zenkichi smirked.
"Is that so strange? You're not the only ones who can reach the peak."
"There are powerful men in every age. I, Zenkichi, will shake the very earth beneath your feet."
Zenkichi spoke without hesitation, without hiding his identity or his overwhelming aura.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Lancer's eyes sparkled with excitement. "To think such strength still exists in this era."
"Come then! Even if you're human, I won't show mercy!"
Zenkichi spun his naginata with ease, laughing heartily. "I don't want your mercy. I want everything you've got—fight me at full power!"
Gilgamesh gritted his teeth, insulted that anyone else dared speak with such arrogance. His fury boiled over.
"You impudent fool! I'll make you pay dearly!"
The golden Gate of Babylon flared to life behind him. Waves of ancient Noble Phantasms emerged from the portal, glittering with lethal energy.
With a calm breath, Zenkichi clenched his fist. The power of the Tremor-Tremor Fruit surged through him.
He slammed his fist into the air.
Crack—
The sky fractured like glass. A wall of vibrations rippled through the battlefield, distorting space itself. The wave of incoming weapons shattered instantly, thrown back in a chaotic spray of broken treasure.
At the same time, Lancer made his move—coming from behind in perfect sync with the chaos. His crimson spear aimed for Zenkichi's back.
"Well done!" Zenkichi shouted with admiration.
He turned mid-swing, his naginata glowing with Haki, and clashed violently with the spear. Sparks exploded as the force of the blow knocked Lancer backward.
"What… martial skill like that…!" Lancer gasped. Zenkichi's blade work wasn't just strong—it was far superior.
"I'm coming too!"
Artoria Pendragon—King Arthur—moved swiftly. She no longer cared for restraint. Excalibur lit up in her hand, a radiant force of divine power.
It was the strongest single-target Noble Phantasm of any Heroic Spirit.
She unleashed it without hesitation, hoping to break through Zenkichi's formidable defenses. From her perspective, his shockwave technique was a wide-area ability—spread too thin to block a focused attack.
She charged forward, golden energy surrounding her blade.
This attack will pierce him, she thought. It has to!
But Zenkichi raised his hand again and cracked the air. Another mirror-like burst of seismic force rippled outward, and when her strike met the barrier, the light of Excalibur was stopped cold.
She gritted her teeth. It didn't work… the gap is too wide…
Zenkichi smiled, shaking his head.
"King Arthur, your attack won't cut it."
"You're no match for me. Why don't you consider my offer?"
"Be my daughter."
His tone was light-hearted, almost playful—but his power left no room for jest.
"What a terrifying man…" Artoria whispered.
"Zenkichi," came a laugh from the side, "you're the bravest warrior I've ever seen."
It was Iskandar, the King of Conquerors.
"Will you join me? Be my right hand."
Zenkichi cast him a glance. "I serve no one. Save your breath."
"What a shame," Iskandar replied with a grin. "Then allow me to entertain you with everything I have!"
A surge of magical power exploded from his body. The land itself began to shift and warp—reality bending to the might of a true King's Noble Phantasm.
In seconds, the city outskirts vanished, replaced by a boundless desert.
An army appeared, stretching across the horizon.
"This is my invincible army—Ionioi Hetairoi."
"My brave men who followed me in life now fight beside me in death!"
He raised his hand, and the entire army let out a unified war cry.
"Charge!!"
A tidal wave of men and horses stormed toward Zenkichi, the ground rumbling beneath their charge.
From a nearby rooftop, Hassan of the Cursed Arm observed the overwhelming display. His usually calm demeanor cracked.
"This… this isn't something I can fight…"
Even Gilgamesh looked intrigued now. Perhaps this human… truly is worthy of standing among kings…
Artoria tensed beside him. "A king fights alone… but against an army like this… even I would hesitate."
Zenkichi, however, only smiled.
"For me, the number of enemies makes no difference."
Then, with a single step forward, an invisible wave exploded from his body—Conqueror's Haki.
The very air quaked.
The front lines of Iskandar's army staggered mid-charge. Then, one by one, they collapsed. Soldiers dropped like flies, unconscious or paralyzed by the sheer force of his will.
It was as if a mountain had crashed down on them.
"This… this pressure…" Gilgamesh muttered in disbelief.
Artoria's hand trembled slightly. "Such dominance… I've never seen anything like it."
Iskandar's grin faltered. "Even I… don't possess that level of kingly resolve…"
Zenkichi didn't stop there. He poured more power into his Conqueror's Haki, and in seconds, over 80% of the King's Army fell.
No defense. No resistance. Just collapse.
His presence alone was too much.
The strength of Iskandar's army lay in its numbers—but against a man who could mow down legions with willpower alone, numbers meant nothing.
"I'll take care of the rest myself!"
Zenkichi shouted, and in the next moment, his body dissolved into glowing particles.
He shot into the sky.
Then—light.
A downpour of golden projectiles rained from above.
Yasakani no Magatama
The attack struck the ground in a divine barrage, vaporizing the last remnants of the army.
Silence fell.
Smoke and dust cleared. None stood to oppose him.
Only the trembling of the earth remained.

chapters.title: Chapter 133 - 133: Retreat, The Fall of the Conqueror King!
chapters.content:
Dense light bullets rained down upon the King's Army. Under the overwhelming barrage, the army quickly fell into disarray and was crushed.
The King, however, laughed heartily at the sight. There was no fear or anger in his expression—only boundless heroism.
He grabbed his Master, Waver, and said, "Remember the valor and deeds of the Conqueror King. Pass them down forever, my Master."
Waver's voice trembled. "Why do you sound like you're saying goodbye? This... it sounds like a farewell speech."
The Conqueror King gazed at the figure glowing in the sky. "I must seek justice for my soldiers. I will challenge that man."
"You're kidding, right? There's no way you can beat him!" Waver said, visibly shaken.
The King's voice was firm. "Even if I can't, I will not run. A Conqueror never flees from battle."
"My Master, use your Command Spells. This is the last charge of the Conqueror King."
Waver's expression turned solemn. He took a deep breath and clenched his fists.
"Conqueror King, don't lose!"
"You are the strongest!"
"You must claim victory for us!"
Without hesitation, Waver used all three of his Command Seals.
With the activation of the Command Spells, the Conqueror King charged into the sky, his chariot tearing through the heavens with unwavering conviction.
Zenkichi stopped the bombardment and looked at the charging figure.
"You still want to charge me? Why go that far?"
He gave a half-smile. "Become my son, Conqueror. I'll spare your life and restore your human form."
The Conqueror King laughed boldly. "A true king never surrenders. Don't be delusional."
Zenkichi shook his head. "Is that so? What a pity."
He summoned Whitebeard's naginata, the entire blade enveloped in Armament Haki.
"Since you want to go out with pride, I'll grant you an honorable death. One-on-one."
Zenkichi shot down from the sky like a comet.
The moment passed in a flash. The naginata shimmered in his hand and cut cleanly through the air.
The Conqueror King was struck down in one blow. His body dissolved into particles of light and returned to the Throne of Heroes.
"He's dead?"
Both the Lancer and King Arthur were shaken. The Conqueror, a warrior whose strength rivaled their own, had been dispatched so effortlessly.
Hassan's expression eased. He had the worst matchup against the Conqueror King, who overwhelmed with numbers.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
"Now that the Conqueror is gone, the rest are easier to deal with," he muttered.
Zenkichi slowly turned his gaze to the remaining combatants, expression calm and unreadable.
"The Conqueror is gone. Who's next?"
With the fall of the Conqueror, his territory—the Reality Marble—began to fade.
"You're strong enough to be my opponent. Let's finish this," said the King of Heroes, stepping forward with immense presence.
Zenkichi looked at him indifferently as golden light gathered once more.
The King of Heroes scoffed and summoned his treasure—the golden vessel resembling a divine craft—and leapt atop it.
Behind him, the Gate of Babylon shimmered, and a barrage of Noble Phantasms erupted forth once again.
Zenkichi didn't flinch.
"You already tried this. It doesn't work."
A glowing halo formed around his fist as he punched forward. The air shattered like glass, and the mirror-like shockwave blocked the torrent of incoming weapons.
The King of Heroes raised the golden key and turned it. Red circuit lines surged across the sky, exuding overwhelming magical energy.
It was the key to the Gate of Babylon.
Still unfazed, Zenkichi narrowed his eyes.
"The star that split heaven and earth…"
The King of Heroes' strongest weapon—the Sword of Rupture, Ea—emerged. A blade said to rend the world itself.
The laws of the world warped around it. Even the fabric of reality seemed to tremble in response.
Zenkichi calmly drew his Zanpakutō.
"Trying your strongest move? Let's see if it lives up to the legend."
Flowers in the mirror, moon in the water.
He prepared to clash with the otherworldly blade.
Suddenly, magical energy surged uncontrollably from the King of Heroes.
"Tokiomi!" he roared, rage twisting his face.
"You dare interrupt me mid-battle?"
His voice echoed violently in Tohsaka Tokiomi's mind.
Tokiomi sighed bitterly. Despite summoning one of the strongest heroic spirits, he had also summoned the most arrogant and uncontrollable one.
While most Heroic Spirits respected their Masters, the King of Heroes treated his as a mere servant.
Still, Tokiomi had chosen him—and even now, he didn't regret it. He had summoned a true king.
"King, this isn't the time to fight him," Tokiomi pleaded. "If you both go down, someone else will just pick up the prize. We should regroup."
But the King of Heroes sneered.
"Minister, your words cannot sway the will of a king."
"This human will not withstand my blade."
"No one here can."
The King's arrogance radiated as he prepared to unleash Ea, but—
Tokiomi activated his Command Spell, forcibly recalling his Heroic Spirit.
"I loathe this!"
The King of Heroes was furious, but bound by the Command Spell, he vanished in a flash of golden light.
"King Arthur, return as well!" ordered Emiya Kiritsugu.
Without hesitation, King Arthur was summoned back to her Master's side.
Hassan, the Assassin-class Servant, also vanished in response to a recall by his Master.
The Lancer vanished next.
Only the Conqueror King had truly fallen.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 134 - 134: Alliance & Warnings.
chapters.content:
The Servants had retreated to their respective Masters.
Through his Observation Haki, Arakawa Zenkichi could clearly sense their positions.
But he didn't pursue them immediately. These Heroic Spirits might still offer unexpected surprises later.
Zenkichi's Observation Haki enveloped all of Fuyuki City, bringing everything under his awareness.
To him, the squabbles among the Heroic Spirits were just an amusing distraction.
---
Tōsaka Residence
The King of Heroes stormed in furiously, shouting at Tōsaka Tokiomi, "Tokiomi, what the hell are you doing? I was about to crush those pests, and you get in my way now?!"
The Hero King's sharp words tested Tokiomi's patience.
He was willing to show deference to the King of Heroes—as long as the King obeyed his plans.
But seeing the King of Heroes so unmanageable, Tokiomi's tone turned cold.
His voice was firm. "King of Heroes, as a Servant, your duty is to obey your Master's commands. If you follow my instructions, we can seize the Holy Grail and fulfill our wishes."
The King of Heroes looked incensed, but Tokiomi raised his Command Seals as a warning.
"I recognize you as a King, and I honor that. But without me, you're nothing. You're my Servant. I am your Master."
"Obey me. Don't forget your place."
Zenkichi's overwhelming power had left Tokiomi disillusioned with the King of Heroes.
If the King wasn't invincible, then there was no need to treat him like a god.
"You… fine!" The King of Heroes clenched his teeth, clearly furious, but with the threat of a Command Seal looming, he begrudgingly swallowed his pride.
Just then, Kotomine Kirei, Tokiomi's disciple, arrived.
He too was a participant in the Holy Grail War. His summoned Servant was Hassan of the Cursed Arm.
Kotomine Kirei and Tokiomi had formed an alliance from the beginning, intending to cooperate. But the appearance of Arakawa Zenkichi had shattered all of their plans.
Kirei came to discuss a new battle strategy.
The King of Heroes glanced at Kirei with intrigue. There was a glint of understanding in his eyes.
Tokiomi... you think you can command me?
---
Elsewhere
Emiya Kiritsugu studied the intelligence in front of him with a somber expression, strategizing his next move.
Artoria sat nearby, clearly displeased. Her relationship with her Master was strained at best.
Fortunately, Kiritsugu's wife had a close bond with Artoria, who respected and liked her.
Because of that, Artoria had been willing to overlook Kiritsugu's many shortcomings.
At this moment, the King of Knights sat quietly beside Kiritsugu's wife, holding a pure white lily bud.
"No," she said, breaking the silence. "That man is too powerful. We should work together to take him down. If we don't, the Holy Grail War may end with all Servants being eliminated."
Kiritsugu considered her words carefully. She wasn't wrong.
He made his decision. "Tokiomi... I need to speak with him."
---
Matō Residence
Zenkichi continued to use his Observation Haki to monitor all of Fuyuki. No Master or Servant could escape his watchful gaze.
Noticing his opponents' movements, a mocking smile crossed his lips.
"How ridiculous," he muttered. "Weren't they going to eliminate each other first? Looks like they failed. Too much bravado, not enough substance."
Rin approached, arms crossed, smirking. "Oh? Big talk from someone hiding in the shadows."
"Talk?" Zenkichi looked at her flatly. "Girl, you don't understand the difference in power."
"If I wanted to, I could end the Holy Grail War right now."
"But if I did, they'd just blame their loss on bad luck. That wouldn't satisfy me."
"They need to struggle—to realize how truly weak they are. Only then will they kneel, willingly."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
"Kneel?" Rin raised an eyebrow. "What are you planning, you pervert?"
"I'm not a pervert," Zenkichi replied sharply. "I'm Whitebeard, not some creep like Akizuki Kōzō. I want Artoria as my daughter, purely because she's an honorable fool."
Rin rolled her eyes. "Please. Just don't drag my mom into your fantasies."
Zenkichi sighed. "Not like that. I need to speak with your mother about something important."
"Oh yeah?" Rin narrowed her eyes. "Tell me. I'll pass it on."
"Fine." Zenkichi nodded. "I've got a special ability. I can monitor all of Fuyuki."
"Your father is planning to ally with the other Masters to eliminate me. But he's underestimating the situation."
"All Masters are potential enemies. That kind of alliance is destined to fall apart."
"Warn your father. If he's not careful, the enemy might backstab him... and he'll die."
There was a glint in Zenkichi's eye as he said this. He deliberately withheld anything about Kotomine Kirei. No one would believe him anyway. What reason did he have to help them?
The only reason he warned Rin was to avoid unnecessary conflict down the line.
Rin frowned, unsure whether to believe him.
"You're just trying to scare us, huh?"
"Believe what you want," Zenkichi shrugged. "I've said my part."
Rin hesitated, but decided to report the information to her mother, Tōsaka Aoi.
---
Meanwhile
The King of Heroes had begun speaking to Kotomine Kirei.
Looking at Kirei, the King of Heroes gave a wicked, knowing smile.
"Tell me, Kirei... do you want to know what true pleasure is?"
Kirei was caught off guard. His eyes flickered with emotion. "True pleasure?"
Kotomine Kirei was broken.
He couldn't appreciate beauty, only depravity. He was emotionally stunted and incapable of love.
Even after his wife died trying to save him, he felt nothing.
Now, the King of Heroes' words stirred something within him—a darkness long dormant.
It felt like a door to another world had just creaked open.

chapters.title: Chapter 135 - 135: Goddaughters.
chapters.content:
"Rin, Kotomine Kirei and the King of Heroes have allied. According to the intel I found, they plan to turn against your father."
In the Matou residence, Zenkichi spoke seriously to Tohsaka Rin.
"Are you kidding me? That's impossible!" Rin's eyes widened with disbelief.
"Kotomine Kirei is my father's disciple, and the King of Heroes is his summoned Servant. Why would they betray him?"
"You're free to believe what you want. I've said what needs to be said." Zenkichi's expression remained calm, offering no further explanation.
Rin bit her lip. As unbelievable as it sounded, she couldn't afford to ignore the possibility. If it turned out to be true, it would be disastrous.
She quickly called her mother, Tohsaka Aoi, and relayed the information.
Tohsaka Aoi was stunned. "The Hero King and Kotomine Kirei… plotting against him?"
"Where did you hear this?" asked Tohsaka Tokiomi, his expression turning grim.
"Rin told me the man named Zenkichi was the one who said it," Aoi responded.
"Hmph." Tokiomi scoffed, visibly relaxing. "If it came from him, it's not credible. Kotomine Kirei and the King of Heroes are my most trusted allies. Zenkichi is just trying to sow discord."
He dismissed it confidently, sure of his own cleverness. But Zenkichi had anticipated that reaction.
Given Tokiomi's position, trusting Zenkichi without proof was impossible.
However, not long after, Tokiomi began preparing to deal with Zenkichi—only to be ambushed by the very allies he trusted.
Just before the betrayal unfolded, Zenkichi summoned Tohsaka Rin and Tohsaka Sakura, his expression grim.
"Kotomine Kirei and the King of Heroes are about to strike. Looks like Tokiomi didn't believe my warning."
Rin's face turned pale. "You're serious?"
"I wouldn't joke about something like this. Do you want to see for yourself?" Zenkichi asked.
Rin hesitated for only a second before nodding.
Zenkichi led the Tohsaka sisters to the location—just in time to witness Kotomine Kirei standing triumphantly beside Tokiomi's lifeless body.
"Dad!" Rin screamed, fury burning in her eyes as she stared at Kirei and the Hero King.
"Rin?" Kirei raised a brow at her sudden appearance, but showed no emotional reaction.

chapters.title: Chapter 136 - 136: Give me your wife.
chapters.content:
In a luxurious villa, Emiya Kiritsugu sat with his secretary, calmly discussing their next move.
Though several Masters had agreed to cooperate, no specific plan had yet been finalized. The common goal remained clear: defeat Zenkichi. However, none of them dared to underestimate his power. Even working together, they needed a flawless strategy.
Meanwhile, King Arthur sat nearby with Irisviel, sharing a quiet moment. Their bond was as strong as ever, their pure affection growing like a delicate blossom amidst the tension of war.
Suddenly, Irisviel's expression shifted. A strange redness spread across her skin, and King Arthur noticed immediately.
"Irisviel, what's wrong?" she asked, concerned.
Irisviel frowned. "The Lesser Holy Grail within me... It just received two Heroic Spirit souls—Gilgamesh and Hassan."
"What?!" Kiritsugu stood up in disbelief. "You must be joking."
Gilgamesh was considered the strongest among the Servants—aside from Zenkichi—and a critical part of their plan. Even though Hassan lacked raw power, his assassination skills made him a key piece of their anti-Zenkichi strategy.
With both gone, their odds had just plummeted.
As Kiritsugu tried to process the situation, Irisviel's expression changed again. "No—another one. The Caster's soul just entered as well."
The Caster of this war had been a deranged killer. But after Zenkichi eliminated the King of Heroes and Hassan, he apparently finished Caster and his Master off with a precise long-range laser blast.
Out of the seven Servants summoned for this Holy Grail War, Zenkichi had now eliminated four.
Worse, with the deaths of Gilgamesh and Iskandar—the King of Heroes and the King of Conquerors—the very fabric of the world had been disturbed. Their deaths tore small holes in the dimensional barrier, allowing chaotic energy from beyond to pour into the Great Grail.
Deep below, where the Greater Grail was sealed, the ancient altar began to glow. Symbols carved into the stone shimmered, reacting to the surge of power.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
The Greater Holy Grail was awakening.
Zenkichi stood before the altar, a faint smile on his face. His real body was present to welcome the Grail's emergence—his clones were already handling the rest.
In another villa, one of Zenkichi's clones had just defeated Lancer with ease.
Despite his Master burning through all three Command Seals to boost his power, it wasn't enough. Lancer was slain without resistance.
The Lancer's particular charm—his infamous "mole of love"—had caused chaos in his life. Even his Master's fiancée had been drawn to him, complicating their relationship.
But now, as he died, Lancer's Master looked on with an oddly satisfied expression.
"This Grail War… is one where humanity wins," he said softly.
The Grail War, originally meant for Heroic Spirits, had turned into a slaughter—by a human.
Lancer's soul was absorbed into the Lesser Grail. The moment the fifth spirit entered, it overloaded and exploded.
Then something extraordinary happened.
The Greater Holy Grail responded. It began to recognize Zenkichi as the victor.
King Arthur and Lancelot, who had not yet been defeated, felt their existence waver as the Grail's judgment activated.
That's when another clone of Zenkichi appeared before them.
He raised his hand, and a surge of energy drawn from the Hogyoku and deathly power stabilized their fading forms.
"What are you doing, Zenkichi?" King Arthur demanded, standing protectively in front of Irisviel.
"Relax. I'm not here to fight. I came to save her," Zenkichi replied calmly. Then he turned to face Kiritsugu.
"Emiya Kiritsugu," he said, "let's make a deal."
Kiritsugu narrowed his eyes. "What kind of deal?"
"Give me your wife," Zenkichi stated plainly, "and I'll give you the opportunity to make a wish with the Holy Grail."
King Arthur's face twisted with fury. "Zenkichi, you've gone too far!"
But Zenkichi ignored her, his gaze fixed on Kiritsugu.
Kiritsugu's jaw clenched. After a long pause, he finally asked, "You're serious?"
"I don't lie," Zenkichi answered.
Defeated and weary, Kiritsugu lowered his head. "Fine. I accept."
King Arthur stepped back in disbelief. "You're… giving her away?"
Irisviel's expression was conflicted, but she said nothing.
With a faint, bitter smile, she turned to King Arthur and said, "I was created as the Lesser Holy Grail by my family. I was always meant to die after the war."
Zenkichi chuckled. "What if I told you I can save you?"
He looked back at Kiritsugu. "Still want to give her to me?"
Kiritsugu remained silent for a long moment, then nodded.
Zenkichi sighed, shaking his head slightly. "A man like you… admirable, but dangerous."
Then, without warning, he raised his hand. Massive spiritual pressure surged forth, and he pulled Irisviel's soul from her body.
Her soul began to transform, infused with Reaper power.
The soulless body that remained turned into a vessel—the Lesser Holy Grail.
Zenkichi looked at King Arthur. "Someone's been waiting to see you. Go to him."
With a wave of his hand, a powerful force enveloped King Arthur, teleporting her to Lancelot's location.
When she appeared, Lancelot dropped to his knees immediately.
"My King! After all these years… I've waited for this moment."
"I've longed for your judgment," he said, his face full of remorse.
He had never forgiven himself for what happened between him and the queen—an affair that contributed to the fall of Britain.
He had entered this war not to win, but to seek punishment from his King.
"And now," he said, "please… give me the justice I deserve."
---

chapters.title: Chapter 137 - 137: Going back to the Naruto World.
chapters.content:
After King Arthur and Lancelot reunited, the two stood silently in front of each other, their exchange filled with unspoken emotions.
Lancelot: "Please… kill me."
King Arthur: "I can't."
Lancelot: "It's my atonement."
King Arthur: "You are not at fault."
Lancelot: "I beg you, my King!"
King Arthur: "No. I refuse."
Their standoff continued, emotional and unresolved.
From a distance, one of Zenkichi's clones watched, visibly frustrated. He communicated with his true body and activated a Command Spell.
Under the spell's influence, Lancelot charged toward King Arthur, sword drawn, despite the horror in his eyes.
"No!" Lancelot shouted internally. He never entered the Holy Grail War to fight the King he once served.
"You've taken the initiative, haven't you?" King Arthur said calmly, raising Excalibur to defend herself.
"Yes," Lancelot replied bitterly, "I never thought he'd do something like this."
King Arthur frowned. "He's powerful, but this… this is beneath him."
From afar, Zenkichi's clone frowned. He activated the second and third Command Spells.
Lancelot, now fully overwhelmed by magical compulsion, roared as an enormous surge of magical energy burst from his body.
"No!" he screamed, powerless to resist.
King Arthur responded with her full strength, unleashing a radiant wave of power that split the sky.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ
Lancelot, finally at peace, charged toward her without hesitation. Her counterattack consumed his technique—and his body.
"Thank you, Master…" Lancelot whispered with a smile before disintegrating into light.
---
Meanwhile, at the Tohsaka residence…
Zenkichi held Tohsaka Aoi in his arms as she trembled from grief. He sighed and said, "When the Greater Holy Grail is summoned, I'll let you make a wish. Whether or not it brings Tokiomi back will depend on your luck."
Aoi's eyes widened. "You're serious?"
"Of course," Zenkichi replied. "But if I give you this chance, I expect something in return."
Rin immediately grew suspicious. "You pervert! What are you planning?"
Zenkichi chuckled . "Relax, I'm not after your mom. I just want you both to be my goddaughters."
Tohsaka Aoi hesitated, then slowly nodded. She couldn't find a reason to refuse.
Rin stood by, fuming in silence. She glared at Zenkichi, but he paid her no mind.
He led them to the Great Holy Grail's chamber, where King Arthur stood solemnly beside a blood-eyed Emiya Kiritsugu.
"Disappointed?" Zenkichi asked King Arthur with a slight grin.
"I entered this war hoping to redeem my former comrades," she replied, glancing at Zenkichi.
He tapped his chin thoughtfully. "If you recognize me as your godfather, I could bring them back."
"Don't even dream of it!" she snapped. "A king's dignity is not for sale!"
Zenkichi smirked. "Is that so? I have other ways of resurrecting them."
"The Holy Grail War will return in 60 years," King Arthur said firmly. "You won't be around to interfere. I'll use the next one to make my wish."
Zenkichi said nothing, only smiling cryptically.
Just then, the light of the Grail twisted with a dark hue. The evil of the world began seeping from its core.
"What is this…?" Kiritsugu muttered in horror. The Holy Grail he had entrusted with his hope for peace—now radiated darkness.
"It's been corrupted," King Arthur said gravely.
"I don't care," Kiritsugu insisted. "It can still grant my wish!"
Zenkichi stared at the Black Holy Grail. "Maybe. But at what cost?"
"World peace!" Kiritsugu declared, and the Grail responded to his desire.
A surge of twisted light erupted from the Grail, forming a great flame that swallowed the surroundings.
The corrupted Grail, in its twisted logic, fulfilled Kiritsugu's wish in the worst way possible—by interpreting peace as the eradication of all conflict through global annihilation.
"No you don't," Zenkichi growled.
He released a crushing wave of spiritual pressure that forced everyone back. Then, channeling his power, he blocked the Grail's destructive surge.
In his hand, the Hōgyoku pulsed with strange hunger.
It resonated with the tainted Grail—drawn to it like a predator sensing prey.
"So… you want it?" Zenkichi muttered, surprised.
Without hesitation, he allowed it.
A massive vortex of energy erupted from the Hōgyoku, pulling the Black Grail into its core.
The evil flames were consumed, devoured completely by the crystal's limitless hunger.
"It's over…" Zenkichi whispered, surveying the room.
He glanced at his system panel—Whitebeard's template was only 62% unlocked. There was still work to be done.
---
The Holy Grail War ended.
Emiya Kiritsugu, broken and defeated, withdrew into isolation. His dream of saving the world had betrayed him.
Zenkichi, however, left with several new "goddaughters" in tow.
But now, he faced a new dilemma—none of them were usable.
After spending over a year in the Fate universe without romance, his loneliness had reached its limit.
Unfortunately, Tohsaka Aoi and Irisviel had only just lost their husbands, making it inappropriate to make a move.
King Arthur, though tempted by his persistent offerings of good food, still held firm to her morals.
Tohsaka Rin and Tohsaka Sakura were too young—clearly off-limits.
With a sigh, Zenkichi checked his system and selected to return to the Naruto World.
"I wonder how much has changed since I left…"
---
Back in the Naruto world, now designated World No. 1...
Zenkichi sat leisurely on Tsunade's lap, flipping through reports from across the Five Great Nations. Everything that had happened during his absence was there in front of him.
"Seems my plan worked," Zenkichi said with a satisfied grin. "Unifying the shinobi world really did bring peace."

chapters.title: Chapter 139 - 139: Princess of the white eye..
chapters.content:
The Hyuga clan was one of the wealthiest and most powerful families in Konoha—an elite bloodline with deep roots in the village's history.
In front of the grand gates of the Hyuga estate, a small, pouty girl stood with her arms crossed, clearly annoyed.
This girl was none other than Hinata Hanabi, the younger sister of Hyuga Hinata. Her frustration was aimed entirely at Uzumaki Naruto.
Hanabi had known for years that her sister had long harbored feelings for Naruto. As a self-declared protector of her sister, she used to follow Hinata, who in turn secretly followed Naruto. It had become a silly little chain of shadowing back then.
But yesterday, everything changed.
Hanabi had witnessed something that shook her to her core—Naruto and Uchiha Sasuke, holding hands and walking together through the village as a couple.
Two men. Together.
She was still in disbelief.
Outraged on her sister's behalf, Hanabi had been wondering how best to console Hinata when, to her surprise, she spotted Hinata walking toward her with a soft smile on her face.
Beside her was someone even more unexpected: Arakawa Zenkichi, the man who had once saved Konoha.
"Sis!"
Hanabi ran up cheerfully and threw herself into her sister's arms, her curious eyes darting toward the tall figure next to her.
"So, this is your younger sister—Hinata Hanabi, right? What a lovely girl," Zenkichi said with a smile, playfully ruffling Hanabi's hair.
"Z-Zenkichi-sama..." Hanabi blushed, her usual attitude dissolving into a flustered daze.
"I'll leave you two to catch up," Zenkichi said with a grin, giving a polite nod before walking away.
"Aww~ Onee-sama is amazing. You're actually close with Zenkichi-sama now," Hanabi whispered, clinging to Hinata's arm like a playful octopus.
"Hanabi..." Hinata's cheeks turned pink, slightly embarrassed by her sister's teasing.
—
Not long after parting ways with Hinata and Hanabi, Zenkichi bumped into Konan from the First Ninja World. She seemed distant, her aura shrouded in quiet sorrow.
"You don't look too happy," Zenkichi said gently as he appeared beside her.
"I was just talking to the version of me from this world," Konan replied softly. "There's so much tragedy in this timeline... more than I expected."
Zenkichi nodded, his voice calm. "That may be true, but your fate has already changed. You're not bound by what happened here."
"You're right." She turned toward him, her gaze softening. "If I hadn't met you, I might have ended up like her... lost."
She looked at him with something deeper—admiration, perhaps longing. "There's no one like you in this world. That's why everything fell apart."
Zenkichi held her gaze, offering a quiet smile.
With a steady breath, Konan leaned forward, resting her forehead against his. Then, without another word, she kissed him.
Some time later, Zenkichi lifted her gently into his arms and walked toward a nearby hotel.
When fate delivers something to your door, sometimes it's best not to refuse.
Watching from afar, the Konan of this world—Konan No. 2—turned red as she witnessed the scene. Flustered, she quickly spun around and fled.
—

Back at home, Hinata Hinata was lost in thought.
What would she do if Zenkichi came to see her again?
Should she act reserved? Was she reading too much into it?

chapters.title: Chapter 140 - 140: Ōtsutsuki Clan.
chapters.content:
"Who are you?"
Hinata Hanabi stared at the boy standing before her, eyes wide with fear. He had no visible pupils, yet the pressure he gave off made her instincts scream danger.
"What a pure Byakugan... it will be enough to help me evolve the Tenseigan," the stranger muttered. His voice was flat, emotionless.
It was Ōtsutsuki Toneri.
Hanabi stepped back, trying to keep her composure. "Someone—anyone—help!"
"It's useless," Toneri said calmly, raising his hand.
A chakra barrier flared around the room, cutting it off from the outside world. "No one will hear you now."
Hanabi found herself frozen in place as powerful chakra pinned her down. She couldn't move, couldn't even resist.
"My eyes," Toneri said coldly, stepping forward, his pale hand reaching toward her face.
Just as his fingers were about to touch her, a hand gripped his wrist tightly.
"You know," a relaxed voice said, "breaking into someone's home is already a crime."
Arakawa Zenkichi stood behind Toneri, smiling lightly.
"But trying to harm a minor?" Zenkichi's expression darkened slightly. "That's a crime punishable by death in the new ninja laws I wrote myself."
Toneri turned his head slightly. "Are you the so-called visitor?"
"In your world, how fares the Ōtsutsuki clan?"
Zenkichi shrugged, his tone light. "Haven't dealt with them yet, but don't worry—I will soon."
"I see," Toneri replied, then swung his free arm toward Zenkichi. "Good luck. The Ōtsutsuki clan doesn't go down easily."
Boom!
Zenkichi squeezed Toneri's wrist. The puppet body shattered into pieces, vanishing in a burst of chakra fragments.
"Zenkichi-sama!"
Hanabi ran to him, clinging to his leg with wide, terrified eyes.
Zenkichi patted her head . "It's alright. He's gone."
With the puppet destroyed, the barrier broke. Moments later, several Hyuga clan members arrived, alerted by the earlier shout.
"Zenkichi-sama?" one of the guards stammered, confused to see the strongest man in the world casually standing in Hanabi's room.
Soon, the Hyuga elders assembled, including Hyuga Hiashi, Hinata, and other senior clan members.
"I sensed foreign chakra inside the Hyuga compound," Zenkichi explained calmly. "When I investigated, I found a puppet with Ōtsutsuki chakra attempting to take Hanabi's eyes. I destroyed it. That's when you all arrived."
Everyone turned to Hanabi for confirmation.
She knelt respectfully beside Zenkichi and nodded. "It's true. He said he was from the Ōtsutsuki clan. He wanted my Byakugan."
The room fell silent. Even the elders paled slightly.
"Ōtsutsuki...?"
Zenkichi glanced over the gathered Hyuga members. "So, you have heard of them. You seem to know more than you're letting on."
Hiashi straightened and answered solemnly. "Our clan's ancient scrolls speak of three bloodlines: the Hyuga, the Kaguya, and the Ōtsutsuki. While relations with the Kaguya were always strained, we dismissed the Ōtsutsuki as myth. We never expected them to truly exist—let alone target us."
"That puppet got into your estate undetected," Zenkichi said. "That speaks volumes about their power."
"We can't handle something like this alone," Hiashi said, bowing his head slightly. "We'd like your assistance, Zenkichi-sama."
Zenkichi gave a nod. "I'll handle it. Leave the Ōtsutsuki to me."
Relief spread across the room.
"Next," Zenkichi continued, "I'm heading to the Ōtsutsuki stronghold. Anyone willing to come with me?"
Hiashi exchanged glances with the others, then said, "Let Hinata and Hanabi go with you."
"They're young. It's time they witness the true dangers of this world."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow, then shrugged. "Alright."
In the next instant, he teleported away, bringing Hinata and Hanabi with him.
They soared through dimensions via chakra channel, space twisting around them.
Hanabi grinned, her eyes lit up with excitement. "This is amazing!"

chapters.title: Chapter 141 - 141: Clash on the Moon.
chapters.content:
Looking at Hanabi's extremely excited expression, Zenkichi shook his head helplessly.
Not long ago, you were almost blindsided… Why is your heart so big?
After glancing at Hinata, Zenkichi noticed her expression was also a little excited and couldn't help but feel surprised.
Do these sisters really like speed so much?
Before long, Zenkichi brought the Hyuga sisters to a space node connecting the Earth and the Moon and located the hidden spatial passage.
Leading them through, the maze-like traps within the passage posed no challenge to Zenkichi whatsoever.
He swiftly brought Hinata and Hanabi to the Moon, where the Otsutsuki clan resided.
In the Otsutsuki residence, Otsutsuki Toneri sat before the Eternal Tenseigan, monitoring both the Moon and Earth with its immense power.
"Is he coming?"
Sensing the approach of Zenkichi and the Hyuga sisters, a sneer crept onto Toneri's face.
Zenkichi… I should thank you. Soon, I'll destroy the entire shinobi world and create a new, peaceful world without war. All I need now is to kill you, take the Byakugan Princess, and complete the evolution of my Byakugan into the Tenseigan.
Not only had Zenkichi brought him the Byakugan he needed, but also the princess herself.
Toneri didn't attack immediately, choosing instead to remain seated before the Eternal Tenseigan. A powerful protective barrier formed around the massive eye, shielding it from harm.
Toneri intended to battle Zenkichi in front of the Tenseigan while ensuring its safety.
Before long, Zenkichi arrived at the Eternal Tenseigan's chamber with Hinata and Hanabi.
Toneri sneered.
"Zenkichi, you've done well," he mocked.
"You've brought me both the Byakugan and my future wife. How should I repay you?"
He grinned darkly.
"Perhaps by granting you a swift death!"
Zenkichi sighed softly, his tone almost pitying.
"My child… you've lost your way."
"I can still set you right — be my son."
For a brief moment, Toneri was stunned. His face contorted with fury, and he bellowed,
"You bastard! How dare you humiliate me like this?! Die!"
With a roar, Toneri unleashed a blazing beam of ocular energy from the Eternal Tenseigan, aiming it directly at Zenkichi.
But Zenkichi remained calm. He raised a single palm, and a laser-like beam shot from his fingertip, neutralizing the attack mid-air.
"Your strength is decent, and with the Eternal Tenseigan's power, you could easily defeat a Kage-level shinobi," Zenkichi remarked evenly.
"But the man standing before you is no mere Kage."
"Even if you gathered several more Eternal Tenseigans, you'd still be powerless against me."
Toneri's rage boiled over. The Eternal Tenseigan's light blazed, sending out a destructive wave of energy.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Sky Shock!
Zenkichi raised his fist, white energy encircling it as he punched forward. The devastating force of the blow shattered the very air, cracks spreading through space like fractures in glass.
A massive shockwave exploded outward, crashing into both Toneri and the Eternal Tenseigan.
"Reincarnation Defense!"
Toneri hastily channeled the Eternal Tenseigan's power into a dense protective shield.
But under Zenkichi's mighty strike, the barrier was obliterated. The shock force hurled Toneri backward.
"Don't you want to be my son?" Zenkichi remarked dispassionately.
"In that case, I'll send you to meet your death."
With a flicker, Zenkichi appeared beside Toneri in an instant. Kyoka Suigetsu materialized in his grip, its blade flashing down in a single stroke.
The sword cleaved through, ending Toneri's life.
"You really killed him?" Hanabi asked, frowning slightly.
"Didn't you say you wanted to adopt him as your son?"
"I was just making conversation," Zenkichi replied calmly.
"He refused."
Without waiting for a response, he stepped toward the Eternal Tenseigan.
Turning to Hinata and Hanabi, he explained,
"This thing is called the Eternal Tenseigan — a powerful tool created from the fusion of countless Byakugan."
"It rivals even the Rinnegan in power. It evolved from the Byakugan. I figure your Hyuga clan might be able to make use of it."
He studied the Hyuga sisters for a moment, then added,
"The Otsutsuki clan should have a method hidden somewhere for controlling the Eternal Tenseigan. You two should try and locate it."
The Eternal Tenseigan was a treasure of immense power — too valuable to simply destroy.
Some might fear its strength and argue that it should be shattered like the Rinnegan.
But to Zenkichi, there was no need for such dramatics. Power was meant to be put to good use.
Before long, Hinata and Hanabi managed to find a technique allowing them to control the Eternal Tenseigan.
To their surprise, it wasn't especially difficult to wield.
"Zenkichi-sama, you should try it too," Hinata suggested gently.
"This was yours to begin with."
"I'm not interested," Zenkichi replied flatly.
"If you want it, take it."
To him, the Eternal Tenseigan held little value.
"Alright — things here are settled," he said casually, casting a glance around the desolate Moon.
"We're leaving."
