chapters.title: Chapter 142 - 142: The Eternal Eye and the Weight of Power.
chapters.content:
The Hyuga Clan Compound
When the senior members of the Hyuga clan laid eyes on the Eternal Tenseigan brought back by the Hyuga sisters, their joy was unmistakable.
"A treasure like the Eternal Tenseigan is no less than the legendary Six Paths Ninja Tools."
"In fact, the Eternal Tenseigan may surpass even those relics in power."
"The destructive potential of this eye far exceeds what any of the Six Paths Tools can offer. From what I've heard, the tools held by Kumogakure are relatively weak."
"Legend has it the Sage of Six Paths left behind five tools. Only the Amber Purifying Pot is still retained by the Hidden Cloud."
"The function of the Amber Purifying Pot is far too simple. Compared to the Sealing Pot of the Hidden Sand, it's not impressive."
"Three of the four tools once held by the Hidden Cloud require one another to be effective. On their own, they're virtually useless."
"The Bashōsen fan can unleash all five chakra natures, but the chakra cost is enormous."
"The Eternal Tenseigan, on the other hand, doesn't just consume no chakra—it grants its wielder additional power."
The elders surrounded the eye, marveling at its brilliance and power.
One elder turned to Hinata with a serious look. "Hinata, did Arakawa Zenkichi sama truly give you this Eternal Tenseigan?"
Hinata nodded. "Yes. Zenkichi sama entrusted it to us."
Another elder looked between Hinata and Hanabi with a look of satisfaction. He chuckled. "The clan head had great foresight, allowing Hinata and Hanabi to follow Zenkichi sama. It was the right decision."
Hiashi smiled warmly at his daughters. "Hinata, Hanabi, what do you think of Zenkichi sama?"
Hanabi blinked. "What do you mean, Father? Zenkichi sama is very kind!"
Hinata's face turned red, but she nodded gently. "Zenkichi san… is truly a remarkable person."
Hiashi laughed softly. "I see. That's good to hear."
---
Hokage's Office
Tsunade (the second version) frowned, glaring at Zenkichi. "Something as dangerous as the Eternal Tenseigan should've been destroyed. Why did you give it to the Hyuga clan?"
The first Tsunade raised an eyebrow and smirked. "Do we even need to ask? Clearly, it's because of Hinata and Hanabi."
Zenkichi replied seriously, "Don't twist things. My relationship with them is completely pure."
Tsunade No. 1 teased, "Oh? And what about your relationship with us?"
Zenkichi paused, thinking for a moment. "...A mutually beneficial arrangement?"
Crack!
Tsunade No. 2 crushed a teacup in her hand and glared at him. "Care to rephrase that?"
He chuckled nervously. "Just kidding. Of course, our relationship is completely proper and respectful."
Both Tsunades nodded with satisfaction, and Zenkichi quietly exhaled in relief. Somehow, balancing both of them hadn't backfired—yet.
Tsunade No. 2 cleared her throat. "Back to the point. Why give the Tenseigan to the Hyuga clan?"
Zenkichi replied calmly, "Because it was created from countless Byakugan. It belongs with them. And don't worry—there won't be any chaos in the ninja world, because I'm here."
"As long as I'm alive, there will be peace. If I fall, then everything falls. But not while I'm still breathing."
Both Tsunades fell silent.
Because Zenkichi had a point—and right now, his power exceeded even that of the First Hokage. Even someone like Hashirama Senju would hesitate to face him.
He had declared there would be peace—and peace followed.
"Speaking of which, why hasn't this version of the Shinobi World been unified yet?" Zenkichi turned to Tsunade No. 2. "You need to pick up the pace."
Tsunade scoffed. "You think it's that easy? I'm not about to start breaking heads like you do."
Zenkichi smirked. "No need for direct violence. Just a little pressure."
"The Hidden Sand and Hidden Cloud were devastated by Akatsuki's attacks. They no longer have the strength to oppose Konoha."
"As for the smaller villages, they're barely worth mentioning. They can't resist us either."
"Kiri isn't a problem either. The Fifth Mizukage, Terumi Mei, already sees things my way."
Tsunade No. 1 snorted, crossing her arms. "Sees things your way? You mean she slept her way into your camp."
Zenkichi rolled his eyes. "Same result either way. Let's not sweat the details."
"In the end, only Iwagakure remains a problem. But even that isn't much."
"Ōnoki may be stubborn, but he's not stupid. With Konoha this strong, he wouldn't dare start a direct confrontation."
"And if push comes to shove, we let the Hyuga deploy the Eternal Tenseigan. That'll make Iwagakure reconsider."
After a moment of thought, Tsunade agreed. She ordered a formal ultimatum to be sent to the weaker villages first.
---
Later…
"Oh, by the way," Zenkichi said thoughtfully. "Any news on Orochimaru?"
He'd nearly forgotten about the elusive Sannin.
Tsunade No. 2 sighed. "Orochimaru No. 2 was captured. But the original one is still at large."
"Konoha's ANBU has been tracking his movements, but he's proven difficult to catch."
"First, he's cunning. Second... he's actually useful."ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "Orochimaru? Working for Konoha?"
She nodded. "Both versions of Orochimaru are scientific geniuses. Their research could shape the future."
Zenkichi looked genuinely surprised. "So, you've come to see the value of science?"
Tsunade glared at him. "Of course I do. My granduncle was a scientific genius."
"If not for his forbidden techniques and creations, Konoha wouldn't be where it is today. I understand perfectly well how powerful science can be."
---

chapters.title: Chapter 143 - 143: The Hyuga’s Challenge.
chapters.content:
It was rare for Tsunade to acknowledge the truth that technology was the primary productive force, so Zenkichi saw no reason to press the issue.
Killing Orochimaru would be a waste. After all, The snake still controlled much of Konoha's core forbidden knowledge and technology.
Not long after, Tsunade's formal invitation for the unification of the Ninja World was dispatched to all major shinobi villages.
The small and medium-sized villages were filled with unease upon receiving this. Naturally, their leaders were reluctant to relinquish their authority and positions, but they lacked the courage to resist Konoha, knowing full well what fate awaited them should they oppose.
Thus, they chose to lay low and await the decisions of the other Five Great Nations. If any of the other major villages showed a willingness to resist Konoha, they would lend their support. Otherwise, they'd remain silent.
The remnants of Sunagakure and Kumogakure could only sigh upon receiving the invitation. In their prime, they might have scoffed at such a thing — but now, after suffering devastating losses, they understood Konoha held the power to erase them completely.
"Let's wait and see what Iwagakure and Kirigakure decide," the top officials of both villages agreed reluctantly. The matter was no longer in their hands.
As for Kirigakure, Fifth Mizukage Terumi Mei encountered no resistance. She had learned about the circumstances in the parallel ninja world from Arakawa Zenkichi himself and understood that unifying the ninja world was one of the surest paths toward lasting peace. She had no interest in clinging to the title of Mizukage if it stood in the way.
More importantly, Terumi Mei's biggest obsession now was to marry Arakawa Zenkichi. Their relationship was no longer a secret, and after growing truly close, she believed in him completely.
With Kirigakure aligned, only Iwagakure Village remained resistant.
Third Tsuchikage Ōnoki scowled darkly as he spoke, "As if I would give up Iwagakure so easily! Not a chance!"
Though he was painfully aware of Konoha's current overwhelming might — especially with a monster like Arakawa Zenkichi at its helm — Ōnoki refused to surrender without testing Konoha's resolve.
He sent a formal reply, challenging Konoha to a battle before any agreements would be made.
Tsunade wasn't the least bit concerned. She knew Ōnoki's nature and chose to dispatch the Hyuga clan to deal with him. It was time to let the other villages witness that even without Arakawa Zenkichi's intervention, Konoha remained a force that could suppress the entire world.
The Hyuga clan, having recently obtained their new treasure — the Eternal Tenseigan — was more than eager for a worthy opponent.
Outside Iwagakure Village
Ōnoki stood before his forces, a scowl plastered across his aging face. "Is the Leaf Village mocking us? Only sending one clan to face Iwagakure?"
His son, Kitsuchi, spoke carefully. "Father, the Hyuga clan is one of Konoha's most powerful families. We can't underestimate them."
"Tch," Ōnoki snorted disdainfully. "Powerful? A rich family in a village without tigers, so the monkeys became kings. If the Senju and Uchiha clans were still around, the Hyuga would never have climbed so high."
He spat to the side. "Konoha sent them here to insult us. And probably hopes we'll destroy the Hyuga for them."
Kitsuchi hesitated, considering the idea seriously. "If that's the case… Konoha never planned to negotiate in the first place."
Kurotsuchi, Ōnoki's granddaughter, crossed her arms. "It's too soon to jump to conclusions. Let's see what the Hyuga can do first. It's possible their strength skyrocketed after receiving aid from that otherworldly visitor. Maybe you're underestimating them."
"Ha!" Ōnoki scoffed. "A single ninja clan against a Hidden Village? Impossible. Even the Senju and Uchiha, at their peak, didn't have that kind of power — unless you counted Senju Hashirama and Uchiha Madara themselves."
While they spoke, the Hyuga forces approached, the Eternal Tenseigan gleaming ominously.
At their head stood Hiashi Hyuga, calm and proud. "Third Tsuchikage Ōnoki, we're here under Hokage-sama's orders to challenge you."
Ōnoki sneered. "All this fuss for one clan. Are you sure you can afford the loss if your whole family dies here?"
Hiashi remained composed. "That's not your concern, Tsuchikage-sama. What you should worry about is whether your village can survive."
Enraged by the arrogance, Ōnoki wasted no time.
"Dust Release: Detachment of the Primitive World Technique!"
A blinding white light erupted from his hands, the destructive technique capable of disintegrating anything to its base molecules.
But before it could strike, the Eternal Tenseigan activated. Both Hinata and Hanabi Hyuga formed seals, and the attack was effortlessly absorbed by the eye's power.
"Impossible!" Ōnoki's jaw clenched. In his mind, nothing should have been able to counter Dust Release. "What kind of ninja tool is that?! The Hyuga never possessed anything like this!"
Floating midair, he glared at the Hyuga sisters.
"Don't worry, Tsuchikage-sama," Hinata said softly, a hint of amusement in her tone. "After we defeat you, we'll explain everything."
With seals formed again, Hinata's eyes glowed a radiant green. A powerful wave of chakra surged from the Eternal Tenseigan, unleashing an overwhelming attack upon the stunned Iwagakure forces.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 144 - 144: 144: The Fall of Iwagakure and a New World Awaits.
chapters.content:
"What?"
The Third Tsuchikage, Ōnoki, didn't dare be careless. He hastily avoided the barrage of green chakra light spheres surging toward him.
Yet, these dense, overwhelming waves of chakra left him nowhere to dodge. The sky above Iwagakure was blanketed by the relentless onslaught.
On the ground, the shinobi of Iwagakure desperately raised Earth Release barriers for defense, but the green chakra spheres easily bypassed them, rendering their efforts meaningless.
Striking the shinobi one after another, the chakra spheres didn't take their lives. Instead, they forcibly expelled the chakra from their bodies. One by one, the Iwagakure ninjas lost consciousness and collapsed.
"Lord Hokage once said — it's best not to kill when you can avoid it," Hiashi Hyuga remarked, watching the scene unfold with a composed, yet satisfied expression, a hint of excitement glinting in his eyes as he tried to maintain his dignity.
Ōnoki, seeing his entire army fall, was struck by a green chakra sphere as well. In an instant, the chakra within his body was expelled, leaving him powerless. His body plummeted from the sky, only to be caught by members of the Hyuga clan.
"…Defeated."
Ōnoki sighed, accepting the reality of his loss. He never imagined the battle would end like this.
Konoha hadn't even deployed their foreign ally, Arakawa Zenkichi. They had merely sent the Hyuga clan — and still, they had crushed Iwagakure with ease.
He could no longer justify resisting. The unification of the ninja world was inevitable.
In the following days, both Iwagakure and Kirigakure formally declared their support for the ninja world's unification. The remaining major and minor villages quickly abandoned any thoughts of rebellion.
Konoha's overwhelming power had made it clear — their opinions no longer held any weight.
---

Tsunade groaned, clutching her head as she looked at the towering stack of documents on her desk.
"This ninja world unification… is a bigger nightmare than I expected. Why did the workload multiply like this overnight?!"
Tsunade's clone, sitting nearby, sighed. "That's because the unification isn't complete yet. The reorganization and redistribution of shinobi forces haven't been finalized."
"Relax. Once that's done, your workload will lighten."
Tsunade grumbled, clearly unconvinced. "You sound far too pleased about this. You're just sitting there watching me drown in paperwork."
"We're the same person," the clone reminded smugly. "You should split the work with me."
"Fat chance," the original Tsunade retorted. "If you're so free, you can go gamble in the village for me."
With a grin, the clone dispelled itself, leaving Tsunade glaring at the empty space.
"Ugh, damn it."
At that moment, Zenkichi appeared beside her, a casual look on his face. "Why not just use shadow clones? This isn't even a real workload."
Tsunade scowled at him. "You know full well that the exhaustion returns to the original when a shadow clone dispels."
Zenkichi shrugged. "Better short-term pain than long-term suffering."
Tsunade crossed her arms. "Then help me out."
She gave him a pointed look, making it clear she wasn't taking no for an answer.
"Alright, alright," Zenkichi relented. "This is child's play."
With a simple hand sign, he created three shadow clones, instructing them to help process the documents.
Then, leaving Tsunade to her paperwork, Zenkichi made his way toward his next priority — developing his relationships with the two Konans.
Konan No. 1 was already nearing the final stages of courtship, while Konan No. 2 was still being carefully pursued. Zenkichi figured a little more effort would soon bring double the reward.
Things were progressing smoothly with the Hyuga sisters as well. After witnessing the Eternal Tenseigan's terrifying might, the entire Hyuga clan was practically worshipping him.
"Naruto World really is a good place to unwind," Zenkichi mused. "Too bad raising my character template unlock progress is so difficult here."
He decided that after some well-earned relaxation, it would be time to move to another world in search of new opportunities.
---
A Month Later
Zenkichi stepped into the new world.
After completing the dimensional transfer, he found himself standing amidst a dense, ancient forest.
Releasing his Observation Haki, he quickly identified his surroundings — and within moments, he appeared in front of three young boys.
"Who are you?" one of them demanded, instantly on guard.
Zenkichi studied them with interest. "You must be Ace, Sabo, and Luffy."
At the mention of their names, the boys' expressions changed.
Ace stepped forward warily. "How do you know our names?"
Sabo raised his iron pipe in alarm. "Who are you?"
Meanwhile, Luffy's face twisted into panic. "Oh no, it's over! Someone's found out about the trouble we caused — he's probably here for revenge!"
Ace turned and smacked Luffy on the head. "Shut up, idiot! Keep running your mouth and I'll leave you here."
Luffy quickly slapped his hands over his mouth, eyes wide with guilt.
His foolish expression made Ace both angry and amused. No matter how many beatings he dished out, this stubborn idiot never learned.
Zenkichi watched the three of them, a faint smile tugging at his lips.
"Who am I?" he said calmly. "I'm Zenkichi."
His gaze sharpened. "And you three — how about becoming my sons?"
Luffy blinked blankly. "Don't want to."
Sabo snorted. "Like hell we would, you lunatic."
Ace spat. "Are you messing with us?"
Zenkichi's smile didn't waver. "So, you're refusing? Do you know what happens to those who turn me down?"
The air shifted.
Without warning, a powerful wave of murderous intent surged from Zenkichi's body, suffocating the three boys under its oppressive weight.
Their faces paled as cold sweat broke out.
This killing intent was monstrous.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 145 - 145: 145: Godsons.
chapters.content:
Orochimaru could easily terrify Uzumaki Naruto and Uchiha Sasuke with his murderous intent, even though they were already at Chunin-level strength. So, for Arakawa Zenkichi to intimidate these three brats who had never even seen the wider world was no challenge at all.
Under the oppressive weight of Zenkichi's killing intent, the bodies of Luffy, Ace, and Sabo stiffened. No matter how hard they tried to move, their limbs refused to obey.
"What a terrifying presence…"
"It's over… we're going to die here."
"Are we… going to have to surrender?"
These thoughts raced through their minds, though none of them could even manage to look at each other.
After a brief moment, the overwhelming bloodlust around Zenkichi suddenly vanished. He grinned at the three children and spoke calmly.
"Well? I'll give you another chance to decide."
"Become my sons, and I'll make you men of terrifying strength."
"I'll protect you, make you the freest people on the seas."
"Whether you want to become marines or pirates, I'll back you up."The source of this content ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
"Anyone who tries to stop you — I'll crush them."
"And thanks to me, the entire world will remember your names."
One enticing offer after another poured from Zenkichi's mouth.
Luffy and the others stared in silence, each lost in thought.
"I wanna be a pirate. I'm gonna be the Pirate King." Luffy finally blurted, picking his nose as he eyed Zenkichi skeptically. "But my gramps won't ever let me. Can you really help me with that?"
"Yeah," Ace chimed in, folding his arms. "Saying you'll let us do what we want, make us famous, and protect us — sounds too good to be true."
Sabo tightened his grip on his iron pipe, nodding in agreement.
Zenkichi chuckled. "Not convinced? Then watch this."
He pointed a finger at a distant hill, and in an instant, a brilliant golden laser shot from his fingertip, slamming into the hillside. The explosion lit up the sky as fire and shockwaves surged outward.
"That's…!"
"No way…"
"It can't be…"
Luffy, Ace, and Sabo stared at the explosion, feeling the waves of hot air brush past them.
"Is that… the legendary…"
"Light Wave!"
"Unbelievable!"
Their wide eyes sparkled with awe.
Zenkichi sighed inwardly. He hadn't expected something so simple to impress these brats this much.
"Yeah, that's the legendary Light Wave." He grinned. "So, what do you say? Want a godfather who can shoot light beams?"
Luffy broke into a huge grin. "Alright! I'm in! From today, I'm your son!"
Ace and Sabo, while more reserved, exchanged glances before giving small nods of agreement.
Zenkichi raised a brow. "I didn't hear you two properly. Say it out loud."
After a long hesitation, Sabo spoke up. "Godfather… can you teach us how to get stronger?"
He'd always thought the three of them were pretty tough for their age, but after witnessing that display of power, he realized just how far behind they truly were.
Seeing the two lower their heads, Zenkichi nodded in satisfaction.
Then, as if suddenly remembering something, he straightened up and said seriously, "Let's get one thing clear. I'm your godfather, not your relative. I've got nothing to do with the rest of your family."
This wasn't because Zenkichi disliked kids — it was because Garp was a shameless old man who, in Zenkichi's view, had a bad habit of meddling. The fact that Garp was raising the Pirate King's son as his own grandson felt a little too convenient to Zenkichi.
No way was he giving Garp a chance to leech off him.
With a destiny-fated protagonist and two pivotal characters now calling him godfather, Zenkichi felt the progression of his Whitebeard template unlocking once again. Though, to be honest, it didn't bring much tangible improvement yet.
Unless he unlocked the complete Whitebeard, he wasn't getting excited.
"Good." Zenkichi smiled. "From now on, I'll train you personally."
---
Time flew by. In the blink of an eye, a month had passed.
Luffy now stood on the surface of a river, beaming with excitement. He'd successfully fused his physical and mental energy into chakra and could finally tread water.
"Godfather, doesn't it feel like these abilities aren't helping us get stronger?" Sabo asked as he hopped along tree branches nearby.
Zenkichi lay comfortably in a hammock strung between two trees. Without opening his eyes, he replied lazily, "This is just your chakra control training."
"Once you master chakra, I'll teach you combat techniques. Right now, you're building your foundation. Without that, you'll collapse at the first hurdle."
Luffy grinned, scratching his head. "Well, I think walking on water's super useful already. At least now I don't have to be afraid of drowning."
Zenkichi chuckled. "That's right. For Devil Fruit users like you, being able to tread water's a lifesaver."
"Climbing trees and walking on water teaches you how to control chakra through your feet, letting you move smoothly across difficult terrain. It might not be flashy, but it boosts your survival skills. That's part of strength too."
The boys nodded in agreement, their eyes shining with determination.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 146 - 146: 146: Path Of Power.
chapters.content:
Sabo looked expectantly at Zenkichi and asked, "Godfather, when will you teach us some real combat techniques?"
Arakawa Zenkichi chuckled lazily, waving his hand. "Don't rush it. Once you've mastered the basics, I'll show you combat skills worth your time."
Zenkichi possessed countless training methods: taijutsu, ninjutsu, chakra control, and even soul techniques. After Luffy and the others had a basic grasp of chakra, he laid three paths before them.
"A ninja? Someone who can unleash ninjutsu and spit fire and water? I wanna be a ninja!" Luffy declared eagerly the moment he heard the description.
"A Shinigami, huh? That sounds interesting. Maybe I can become the God of Death," Ace mused thoughtfully.
"Taijutsu and swordsmanship sound more up my alley," Sabo said after a pause. "I think I've got a knack for close combat. I'll focus on taijutsu."
"Good," Zenkichi nodded. "But remember, even though you've picked your path, there are skills all of you need to master. Some things are too important to ignore."
For instance, the Clone Technique was a must in the ninja system, whether it was a basic clone, shadow clone, or water clone. Techniques like walking on water or climbing trees with chakra were already mandatory. Beyond that, mastering Water Release ninjutsu was crucial. In a world covered by seas, where seawater nullified Devil Fruit abilities, being able to manipulate water with chakra gave one a significant edge.
Then there was Haki — the Pirate World's essential power. The three colors of Haki were non-negotiable in terms of survival and strength. Zenkichi understood this better than anyone; his own Pika Pika no Mi (Glint-Glint Fruit) made him keenly aware of the threats from other Logia users.
He spent hours instructing Luffy, Ace, and Sabo, offering specific methods tailored to their chosen disciplines. And he didn't skimp — Eight Gates Released Formation alone was a priceless inheritance.
In the world of Naruto, the Eight Gates were a forbidden, body-destroying technique. But in the Pirate World, where natural physical resilience far outstripped that of ordinary humans, the drawbacks were less crippling. Pirates possessed monstrous physiques that broke the limits of what ordinary humans could achieve. Where chakra-enhanced taijutsu practitioners still hit a ceiling, pirates with their raw bodies often surpassed human limitations naturally.
Two months passed in the blink of an eye.
After instilling the three with foundational training methods, Zenkichi parted ways with them.
"Training isn't something you finish overnight. Stay diligent," he told them, hands in his pockets. "When you make it to the seas, you'll hear my name echoing across every ocean."

chapters.title: Chapter 147 - 147: 147: Clash of Wills.
chapters.content:
Garp had returned to Windmill Village a few days ago and quickly found Luffy and the others in the midst of their training.
However, what surprised him most was the rapid improvement in Luffy's strength.
After learning that these changes were due to Arakawa Zenkichi, Garp's heart grew heavy.
What troubled him most was that he couldn't accurately gauge Zenkichi's strength.
Even as one of the peak combatants in the pirate world, Garp wasn't confident he could face Zenkichi head-on.
Although there was no proof that he would lose, years of life-and-death battles had sharpened his intuition — and it screamed danger.
As a result, Garp kept a low profile these days, pretending to be absent while quietly observing Zenkichi's movements.
When he saw Zenkichi preparing to leave, a small sense of relief rose in his heart, and he silently followed.
Now, without Luffy and the others around, Garp felt it was time to confront this man and probe his true intentions.
But rather than heading straight for the sea, Zenkichi made his way into the tavern in Windmill Village, calling out Garp's presence the moment he arrived.
"Makino, step outside for a moment," Garp ordered in a low, serious tone.
Zenkichi glanced lazily at him and spoke with calm indifference, "No need. Let her stay. I've no intention of fighting you."
He leaned back, his expression relaxed and unbothered. "Even if I did, I could suppress you without so much as disturbing her."
A faint grin crossed his face. "But there's no need for things to escalate. After all, Luffy and the others are my godsons now."
"Still, I'll give you a word of advice — don't think you can use them to get to me."
His tone was measured, but the underlying confidence was unmistakable.
"Suppress me, without affecting her?"
Garp's eyes narrowed slightly, caught between shock and rising anger.
For all his tolerance, Garp would never stand for someone belittling his strength.
"You can mock my wits, but not my dignity," Garp growled, his voice low and threatening.
He took a step forward, his presence oppressive. "Come on, then. Let's see if you can really back those words up."
Zenkichi let out a small sigh, his expression unchanged, and before Garp could react — he vanished.
In the blink of an eye, he appeared behind Garp, his sword Kyōka Suigetsu resting coldly on Garp's shoulder, a sharp, invisible pressure radiating from the blade.
Garp's throat tightened as a chill ran down his spine.
For the first time in years, he felt genuine, visceral fear.
"What… monstrous strength…" he thought, swallowing hard.
The sensation wasn't just in his mind; his instincts screamed that one wrong move here meant death.
Zenkichi's disappointment was evident as he withdrew the sword.
"That's enough," he said flatly, as if bored.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
To him, Garp posed no real interest.
Even if recruiting someone like Garp could boost his system's unlock progress, the man was simply too old for it to be worth the effort.
And thanks to the brief encounter, Zenkichi's system had already acknowledged his superiority — counting it as a victory since Garp hadn't even been able to respond.
Without another word, Zenkichi left the tavern, leaving both Garp and Makino stunned.
By the time they regained their senses, there was nothing left of him except a gold coin sitting atop the counter.
Even when Garp unleashed his Haki, scouring the island, he couldn't sense Zenkichi's presence anywhere.
---
Meanwhile — Cocosia Village
Far from Windmill Village, Zenkichi arrived in Cocosia Village.
As he strolled through the streets, he spotted a small, orange-haired girl stumbling along.
She was undeniably cute — a younger Nami, though she had no idea what sort of man, fate had just put in her path.
At that moment, she had just stormed out of Bellemere's house, furious over a petty argument and determined to run away from home.
She barely made it out of the village before crossing paths with Zenkichi.
"Well, aren't you a cute little thing," Zenkichi said, crouching down with an easy smile.
"Little girl, how about coming home with me?"
Nami froze, wide-eyed with fear, and instinctively took a step back.
"W-Who are you?" she stammered.
The teasing grin on Zenkichi's face widened.
"You can call me daddy, if you like."
At those words, little Nami let out a high-pitched shriek and bolted, her tiny legs pumping furiously as she sprinted toward Bellemere's house.
Zenkichi simply laughed, watching her scramble away, then casually followed at a leisurely pace.
"Bellemere! There's a pervert out here who told me to call him daddy!" Nami wailed as she charged through the yard.
Hearing the panicked cries, Bellemere burst from the house, a rifle already in hand and fury etched into her features.
Despite having scolded Nami earlier, the woman's protective instinct was fierce.
She had even prepared a hearty meal for Nami's return, eager to make up after their spat.
"Who the hell are you?!" Bellemere demanded, her weapon trained on Zenkichi.
"Easy, no need to get worked up," Zenkichi said calmly, raising his hands in mock surrender.
"I've got no bad intentions. I just think this little one's adorable."
Bellemere kept her guard up.
"You're not from around here, are you? I've never seen you in Cocosia Village."
"You're right," Zenkichi admitted without hesitation. "I just arrived today."
A grin crept back onto his face. "Actually, I don't have a place to stay. How about you put me up for the night?"
Bellemere blinked, momentarily dumbfounded by the man's nerve.
"Are you insane? We can barely afford to eat as it is, and you expect us to host some drifter?!" Nami snapped, hands on her hips.
Zenkichi chuckled and reached into his sleeve, producing a dazzling, fist-sized diamond that gleamed in the sunlight.
"How about this, then?"
The instant Bellemere and the girls laid eyes on it, their jaws nearly hit the floor.
It was more wealth than they'd ever seen in their lives.

chapters.title: Chapter 148 - 148: 148: Cocoyashi Village.

"Guests from far away, come inside and have some water!"

Earlier that day, Nami had headed to the market in the village center. But just as she arrived, she saw an enormous ship approaching from the distance.

"Of course! We're a superior species. Even the weakest among us is ten times stronger than a human."
The Fishman Pirates jeered as they argued, thrilled at the chance to terrorize weaklings. Having suffered discrimination on the Grand Line for years, the chance to become oppressors here in the East Blue twisted them further, mixing their long-held inferiority complex with arrogance and sadism.

A handsome, dark-eyed young man stepped out casually.

"Screw this—run for it!"
Someone among the fishmen shouted in panic, and the rest immediately scrambled to flee.

"Zenkichi-san, you're amazing!" Nami exclaimed, while Nojiko nodded eagerly in agreement.
"You two want to be strong like me?" Zenkichi smiled teasingly.

Zenkichi's tone softened.
"Really? I want to learn!" Nami declared without hesitation, her desire for strength shining in her gaze.
"I want to learn too!" Nojiko quickly added, refusing to be left behind.
"You both want to learn, huh? But why should I teach you?"
Zenkichi chuckled, giving them a sly look, like an uncle teasing his nieces.
"Um… what do you want in return?"
Nami asked, sidling up to him with a mischievous grin, leaning in close.
"I can repay you," she whispered slyly. "Repay with my body."
The corner of Zenkichi's mouth twitched, a dark line appearing on his face.
If Nami had said that when she was older, he would've been very interested — and gladly accepted her reward, giving her a run for her money. But now, she was still just a cheeky little girl spouting lines she picked up from her delinquent foster mother.
"Cut it out."
"If you want to learn, then call me godfather."
Zenkichi grinned and wagged a finger at them.
"Godfather?" the girls blinked, then grinned mischievously.
"Do you like Bellemere-san?" they teased in unison.
"Where are you getting this nonsense?" Zenkichi snorted. Bellemere wasn't far and could definitely hear them, so he decided to sidestep the question.
"All right, enough talk. You want to learn, call me godfather now or it's too late."
The two girls exchanged glances and then, without hesitation, shouted together.
"Godfather!"

chapters.title: Chapter 150 - 150: 150: Price of Defiance.
chapters.content:
The arrival of Zenkichi brought enormous financial relief to the Bellmere family, quickly elevating them from a struggling household to the wealthiest in Cocoyashi Village.
Afterward, Zenkichi took it upon himself to teach Nami and Nojiko how to train, fulfilling his new role as their godfather. Having already trained Luffy and the others in the past, he was well-versed in guiding new disciples. It didn't take long before Nami and Nojiko began to show noticeable progress.
Around this time, the Navy finally arrived — long after being summoned by Genzo.
"Is the Navy always this slow?" Zenkichi remarked dryly as he watched the warships approach from the port, glancing sideways at Bellmere.
Bellmere's face darkened. "The Navy wasn't always this bad. But lately, it's been nothing but disappointment after disappointment."
Under the gaze of Zenkichi and Bellmere, a naval officer appeared — a man with long, sinister eyebrows and beady eyes. He marched up flanked by his men and declared officiously, "I am Captain Nezumi of the Navy. I understand you've captured the Fish-Man Pirates?"
Bellmere met his gaze evenly. "Arlong and his men are here. There should be a hefty bounty on them, right?"
Captain Nezumi's eyes gleamed. "You've made a grave mistake. Do you realize what you've done, capturing the Fish-Man Pirates? Their captain, Jinbei, has already allied with the World Government as one of the Seven Warlords of the Sea. Arlong and his crew were under his protection. By attacking them, you've violated the Government's accords."
Zenkichi chuckled coldly. "Nezumi, was it? Do you ever use that head of yours for anything besides scheming? Do you think someone capable of defeating Arlong's entire crew would be intimidated by a coward like you? Don't insult me."
His calm voice carried a deadly undertone, and Nezumi instinctively recoiled a step.
"W-What are you planning? I'm a Navy captain!" Nezumi stammered, sweat beading on his brow.
"A Navy captain? Impressive title," Zenkichi mocked. "But don't fool yourself. In this lawless age of pirates, Navy captains are killed like flies. Especially spineless, corrupt officers like you."
In the original events of this world, Nezumi had been a known collaborator with Arlong. But now, with Arlong dead, Zenkichi saw no reason to spare the man who would have oppressed this village.
By the time anyone noticed, Nezumi had already ducked behind his soldiers. A few moments later, Zenkichi's figure blurred and reappeared, this time holding Nezumi's limp, lifeless body.
He turned his gaze toward the remaining naval soldiers still aboard the warship. Raising a hand, invisible pressure radiated from him — an oppressive, formless force. The naval soldiers clutched at their heads, some collapsing on the spot as his immense spiritual pressure crushed their will to resist.
"You really chose poorly," Zenkichi murmured, his voice like a blade across the deck.
The soldiers, panicking, aimed their rifles at him. One desperate soul shouted, "Fire! Kill him!"
Their leader's bravado had emboldened them, but without Nezumi, their morale was brittle. And then, Zenkichi spoke again.
"Your captain's corpse is here. Take him, and tell your superiors exactly what happened — that he tried to steal my rightful bounty, and paid for it with his life. Deliver that message, or I promise you'll regret it."
The remaining soldiers, having witnessed the fate of their comrades and realizing this was a foe far beyond their power, wisely chose to comply. Gathering Nezumi's body, they fled aboard their ship, leaving the village behind in shamed retreat.
Zenkichi watched them go without a flicker of emotion. Sensing Bellmere approaching, he spoke without turning.
"Looks like handing those Fish-Man corpses over to the Navy isn't an option. We'll deal with them ourselves."
Bellmere's face was grave. "The Fish-Man Pirates are the least of our problems now. What about the Navy corpses you left behind? Killing their men — even scum like Nezumi — won't go unnoticed. The World Government won't let this slide. You should leave while you can. The Navy isn't weak. They have the Admirals, Marshal Sengoku, even the Hero Garp."
She said this, not to frighten him, but out of genuine concern. Her years in the service had taught her to fear the might of the Navy's upper echelons.
Zenkichi smiled faintly. "The Navy, the World Government — none of it matters to me. But you're right, it's time I left."
He turned to her, a rare softness in his gaze. "I enjoyed our time together, Bellmere."
With that, Zenkichi vanished, leaving Bellmere standing alone.
As the sea breeze stirred her hair, Bellmere let out a long sigh. Over these past days, she'd grown attached to this enigmatic young man. Handsome, powerful, and kind in his own odd way, Zenkichi was everything she could have wished for. The fact that he was now godfather to Nami and Nojiko only made him all the more irreplaceable.
But he was gone, leaving her with nothing but memories.

chapters.title: Chapter 151 - 151: 151: Godson & Daughter
chapters.content:
Zenkichi left Cocoyasi Village and soon arrived at a small settlement known as Shimotsuki Village.
Atop a hill on the village's outskirts, a boy with moss-green hair was training diligently.
A rope was tied to his hand, connected to a heavy stone dragging behind him as he continuously practiced his sword swings.
This boy was none other than Roronoa Zoro—the one who aspired to become the world's greatest swordsman.
"Hey, kid. Training hard, huh?"
Zenkichi appeared in front of Zoro, smiling casually.
"Who are you?"
Zoro narrowed his eyes at the man and asked, puzzled.
"Who am I?"
Zenkichi thought for a moment, then grinned. "Just a lost traveler. Like you, I can't seem to find my way home."
"No road sense at all!"
Zoro snapped, looking irritated. "What are you even talking about? I just can't find the way back!"
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow, half-smiling. "How can someone like you, a hopeless case when it comes to directions, remember the way home anyway?"
Zoro huffed, clearly annoyed. "That's none of your business! Let's talk about you! Who are you really?"
"I don't recall seeing anyone like you in the village. Are you a pirate or something?"
Zenkichi shook his head. "I'm not a pirate. And that's not something you should worry about."
He paused, then added, "Tell me something—do you really want to become the world's greatest swordsman? I can give you a chance."
Zoro looked at him warily. "What kind of chance are you talking about?"
Zenkichi smirked. "I can teach you how to become strong. But, there's one condition—you'll have to become my godson."
Zoro scoffed. "I'll become the world's greatest swordsman on my own. I don't need help from anyone."
Zenkichi chuckled. "Really? That's some serious confidence."
"But don't be so quick to dismiss it. Are you sure you won't change your mind?"
As he spoke, Kyōka Suigetsu appeared in his hand. With a calm motion, Zenkichi pointed the blade toward the distant sea.
A moment later, the vast ocean split cleanly in two.
"...Whoa…"
Zoro stared, stunned, his eyes wide with disbelief. His young heart was deeply shaken.
Was this really what swordsmanship could do?
Could a single swing of a blade slice the sea?
Zenkichi watched Zoro's reaction with a knowing smile. "So? Does my offer sound more appealing now?"
"If you become my godson, I'll teach you all of this. With my guidance, you'll become the world's greatest swordsman in no time."
Zoro was silent.
The offer was far too tempting.
To wield swordsmanship powerful enough to split the sea and shake the heavens… surely that would make him the strongest.
Finally, Zoro moved. After a brief pause, he threw himself forward and hugged Zenkichi's leg.
"Godfather!"
Zenkichi smiled with satisfaction, nodding. "Very good. From today, I'll teach you the way of the sword."
He possessed the sword skills of Aizen, Kizaru, and even Whitebeard. While none of those men were pure swordsmen, their abilities placed them well above most.
Teaching a beginner like Zoro was no problem.
And so, Zoro's training under Zenkichi began.
His improvement was rapid—and Kuina, who often sparred with Zoro, quickly noticed the difference. Curious and suspicious, she decided to follow him in secret.
One day, she found Zenkichi instructing Zoro in the clearing.
"Zoro! So this is where you've been sneaking off to?" Kuina stepped out from her hiding spot, eyes narrowed.
"Kuina! What are you doing here?" Zoro's face was filled with surprise.
Kuina crossed her arms with authority. "You've been improving way too fast lately. Something was up, so I followed you."
Zenkichi turned to Kuina, a smile on his face. She was a mysterious figure—even in the original timeline, her fate remained uncertain. But one thing was clear: her swordsmanship far surpassed Zoro's at this point.
"You've got a lot of talent, little lady," Zenkichi said calmly. "Want to be my daughter? I'll help you become the greatest swordsman in the world."
"You've already seen how fast Zoro's progressed. That's all thanks to me."
Kuina blinked. "Your daughter?"
She was stunned. That was the last thing she expected.
"Godfather! You said I'd be the one to become the world's greatest swordsman!" Zoro protested loudly, clearly unhappy with the idea of competition.
Zenkichi laughed. "It all depends on your abilities. I'll teach both of you everything I know—swordsmanship, chakra, Haki—and guide you according to your strengths."Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
"But whether or not you become the best, that's up to your own effort."
Kuina looked at Zenkichi, eyes glowing with resolve. "Alright. Godfather!"
To Zenkichi's surprise, she didn't hesitate.
Unlike her real father, Shimotsuki Koushirou—who believed girls couldn't become the strongest swordsman—Zenkichi recognized her potential.
And that was all she needed to hear.
"Excellent!"
With that, Zenkichi looked at his rapidly growing potential, ready to pass down his knowledge of swordsmanship, chakra, and all three forms of Haki.
Training had only just begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 152 - 152: 152: His Name Is Zenkichi.
chapters.content:
Zoro and Kuina continued their training in the clearing, clashing swords with intensity and focus.
Meanwhile, Zenkichi had created a shadow clone, which quietly slipped away into the nearby forest.
There, a middle-aged man dressed in loose training robes stood beneath a tree, observing Zoro and Kuina with a calm, gentle expression.
"You must be Koushirou, Kuina's father," Zenkichi's clone said, suddenly appearing behind him. "Why are you hiding out here?"
Startled by the sudden voice, Koushirou turned sharply, but quickly composed himself.
"It's strange, isn't it? Why would a man of your strength show up just to train two children in swordsmanship?" Koushirou asked, his tone wary, eyes scanning Zenkichi carefully.
"And what if I don't want to answer that?" Zenkichi replied, his interest piqued. He could sense Koushirou's strength—it wasn't weak—but compared to him, it wasn't anything worth worrying about.
Koushirou gave a small nod, relaxing. "That was rude of me. If you don't want to say, then forget I asked."
Zenkichi raised an eyebrow. "You trust me that easily?"
"I trust my eyes," Koushirou said plainly. "I can tell you mean no harm to Zoro or Kuina."
"As long as your intentions toward them are good, I don't see a reason to pry."
Zenkichi chuckled. "You're more open-minded than I expected. How about we spar? I'm curious to see what you're capable of."
Koushirou's gaze sharpened. After a brief pause, he smiled faintly. "Very well."
"But not here. This isn't the place for a serious match."
Zenkichi nodded in agreement. "Lead the way."
A short time later, the two appeared on a mountain ridge far from Shimotsuki Village.
Koushiro had returned home first to retrieve his personal weapons. Now, standing tall on the mountain peak, he drew two gleaming swords.
"I'm a master of the two-sword style. Please, grant me your guidance."
As he readied his blades, his aura shifted—quiet and composed, yet radiating precision and force.
"I understand," Zenkichi said softly, Kyōka Suigetsu materializing in his hand. He stood at ease, spinning the blade lightly in his fingers, refusing to make the first move.
Without warning, Koushiro surged forward, his twin swords cutting through the air in a powerful arc toward Zenkichi.
But Zenkichi moved only slightly, raising Kyōka Suigetsu with practiced ease. A single sweep deflected the entire strike.
"Not bad," Zenkichi said calmly.
Koushiro's eyes gleamed. "You're strong," he admitted. "It's rare to find a true opponent at my level."
With a fierce expression, Koushiro unleashed a flurry of sword strikes, his two blades moving so fast they became a blur. Sword energy streaked across the field in sharp, crisscrossing lines.
But Zenkichi merely stepped forward and waved Kyōka Suigetsu once more.
A shockwave of pressure erupted from his blade, scattering the sword energy like mist in the wind.
"It's over."
A heartbeat later, Zenkichi was behind Koushiro, Kyōka Suigetsu resting calmly against the back of his neck.
"…Yes," Koushiro said with a quiet laugh. "It's over."
"I lost. I didn't expect your strength to be this overwhelming."
"You're impressive," he said, turning to face Zenkichi with sincere respect.
Just then, Zenkichi's expression shifted. His Haki had picked up something from the distance. "Someone's coming."
His eyes focused toward the horizon. "A group of powerful signatures is approaching Shimotsuki Village. They're probably here for me."
A moment passed before Koushiro nodded. "I'll go see."
With a flicker of movement, he vanished from the mountaintop.
Moments later, Koushiro appeared before a group making their way toward the village—led by none other than Monkey D. Dragon.
Dragon was about to rally his comrades when he spotted Koushiro walking toward them, his clothes slightly rumpled from his recent fight.
"Koushiro? What happened to you?" Dragon asked with a curious frown.
"Nothing much," Koushiro replied casually. "Just had a little spar."
"You came at the right time, though. We were just about to go looking for you."Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
Dragon wasted no time, stepping forward. "Do you remember the promise we made when we were younger?"
"I've found a way to change the world. I need your help."
Koushiro's smile faded slightly. He closed his eyes for a moment before answering.
"Dragon, I'm not the man I used to be."
"Back then, I had no attachments. I was willing to risk everything with you."
"But now, I have a dojo, disciples, and a family. I can't leave that behind."

However, Koushiro added thoughtfully, "If you're looking for someone strong—someone who might actually help you—there is someone I can recommend."

chapters.content:
Arakawa Zenkichi inserted a coin into the News Bird's pouch and retrieved a fresh newspaper. Tucked between the pages were several bounty posters.
One, in particular, caught his eye — his own.
The face printed on the paper was one he recognized immediately. It was taken back when he'd been in Cocoyasi Village. Captain Nezumi's men had photographed him using a Den Den Mushi. Zenkichi had noticed but didn't stop them.
After all, he had expected to be targeted by the World Government eventually. If they were going to place a bounty on him, he preferred they use a photo that captured his best angle. So, he'd posed confidently, allowing the shot.
Printed clearly beneath the photo: 20 million Berries.
Zenkichi's face darkened.
"Twenty million?" he muttered with a half-smirk, half-scowl. "That's a slap in the face."
The World Government dared to insult him like this?
He had explained everything to the marines — the corruption that led him to eliminate Captain Nezumi. Those sailors should have relayed that truth to their superiors. Yet, instead of recognizing justice, the Navy slapped a petty bounty on his head. A bounty so low, it was insulting.
"I expected you to clean up your own mess," Zenkichi said aloud, his voice simmering with suppressed fury. "Your own officers were the problem. You should have apologized."
"But I see now… I gave you too much credit."
His gaze sharpened.
"If you're going to oppose me, fine. But to offer this pathetic bounty?"
He clenched the bounty poster in his fist, and a cruel smile crept onto his lips.
"Very well. Since you think I'm worth so little… I'll show you just how wrong you are."
He remembered — the Celestial Dragons would be arriving soon.
A spark flickered in his golden eyes.
"If you're going to put me at the bottom of the barrel, I'll make sure to burn the whole thing down."
Even the destruction of an island wouldn't concern the World Government. But harming the Celestial Dragons? That was another matter.
To the World Government, these bloated nobles — the so-called "descendants of the Creator" — were untouchable. Even the Five Elders, the regime's top decision-makers, were Celestial Dragons themselves.
They were the face of the World Government.
Hurt them, and the Admirals would come.
Kill one, and the heavens themselves would tremble.

Arakawa Zenkichi left without looking back. After killing the Celestial Dragon, he vanished.
Chaos erupted aboard the warship. Naval soldiers and Celestial Dragon guards were in complete disarray, as if the sky had collapsed.

Pass the blame.

Mariejois, Holy Land of the Celestial Dragons.
The heart of the World Government.
The Five Elders—the highest authority—sat in conference, grim-faced as they discussed the recent killing of a Celestial Dragon.
"How many years has it been… and now someone dares attack the Celestial Dragons again?"
"They're world nobles—symbols of our rule. This incident must be dealt with severely."
"The World Government exists to serve the Celestial Dragons. The world needs to see our response."
"No matter how strong he is, the one who did this—Arakawa Zenkichi—must pay."
The Five Elders' stance was unanimous. Zenkichi's actions had crossed a line, and they would not let it slide.
After all, they were gods. There was no way they'd let someone challenge their own caste and live.
"Have the Navy issue a new bounty."
"How high?"
"Based on the guards' and soldiers' reports, Zenkichi was frighteningly powerful. Saint Germaco's personal guard may not be elite, but to take them out so easily, he must be stronger than an average Vice Admiral."
"They also said he used Conqueror's Haki."
"Then it's settled. Set his bounty at 500 million berries."
"Done."
And just like that, the bounty was finalized. Arakawa Zenkichi became a major threat in the eyes of the world.
But the meeting didn't end there.
"These are turbulent times. The situation is worsening."
"The Four Emperors dominate the New World. The Government has all but lost control over the second half of the Grand Line."
"Luckily, the combined strength of the Navy and the Seven Warlords of the Sea still holds a fragile balance."
"Why can't those idiotic Celestial Dragons stop bringing trouble to us?"
"Because they have the privilege to be stupid. Their status allows it."
"If they didn't share our divine bloodline, I'd have the Holy Land Guard wipe them out."
The Five Elders let out sighs of frustration. Their true concern was the world order—ordinary people's suffering didn't matter to them.
They ruled to serve the Celestial Dragons, not the masses.
Still, now that a Celestial Dragon was dead because of naval corruption, the Five Elders were ready to clean house.
"What about those who failed to protect Saint Germaco?"
"Have them kill themselves. It'll erase further accountability."
"And the officer who set Zenkichi's bounty?"
"No need to investigate. We all know what happened."
"Probably a base officer trying to hide navy corruption."
"Have Sengoku conduct a full investigation. It's time to purge the rot."
The Five Elders had long known of corruption within the Navy but ignored it—so long as it didn't interfere with maintaining order.

The office was quiet as Sengoku adjusted his glasses and spoke with a firm tone. "The Navy will begin internal purges immediately. But for now, let's focus on something more pressing."

Just mentioning those two Devil Fruits made Sengoku's eyes narrow.
"Both of those are among the most powerful abilities in the world. Either one alone qualifies someone to become an Admiral-level threat."
Sengoku furrowed his brows. "The Pika Pika no Mi is still with Kizaru, and the Gura Gura no Mi belongs to Whitebeard. Are you saying Zenkichi somehow copied them?"
Garp nodded. "It's possible he's not a Devil Fruit user at all. The reports suggest he's unaffected by seastone."

He sighed heavily. "In my opinion, the best course of action for both the Navy and the World Government would be to negotiate peace with Zenkichi. But... after killing a Celestial Dragon, that bridge has burned."
Sengoku stayed silent, then contacted the Five Elders. He relayed everything Garp had told him.
After a tense silence, the Five Elders responded. They hadn't anticipated that even Garp was no match for Zenkichi. Realizing the danger too late, they agreed to raise the bounty.

And with practice, he'd one day unlock the same abilities Kaguya Ōtsutsuki had demonstrated—abilities tied to the ultimate eye.
Hearing his decision to leave, both Zoro and Kuina looked devastated. They tried to speak, to ask him to stay.

Something about that stillness sent a chill down his spine.

chapters.title: Chapter 160 - 160: 160: A New Era Rises – Zenkichi's Name Echoes.
chapters.content:
"A supernova is born, and a super-criminal with a bounty of 2 billion Berries has emerged!"
"After killing a Celestial Dragon and attacking a former admiral, Arakawa Zenkichi's crimes are unforgivable!"
"Has he surpassed Whitebeard with his overwhelming strength?"
"Whitebeard's throne as the world's strongest man is being challenged. Can he hold back the tide of the new era?"
---
Zenkichi chuckled as he read the latest newspaper, delivered by a News Coo.
With his sharp mind, he could easily see through the World Government's ploy.
They had deliberately released provocative headlines to incite conflict between him and Whitebeard.
After all, Zenkichi's growing strength had already instilled fear in both the Navy and the World Government.
They couldn't track his movements nor confront him directly—so they turned to another monstrous figure: Whitebeard.
The greatest threat to a pirate wasn't always the government—it was often other pirates.
As Zenkichi laughed quietly at the headlines, the rest of the world took notice. The rise of a new "supernova" had shaken the seas.
Although he was still new to the pirate world, his power made him anything but a rookie.
---
Marine Headquarters – Navy HQ
The three admirals of the Navy had all received intelligence regarding Zenkichi. Their reactions, however, varied.
Admiral Aokiji stared solemnly at Zenkichi's file, the laziness usually on his face wiped away.
"It's one thing for Teacher Zephyr to lose… but even Garp San couldn't beat him?"
Aokiji had once followed Garp, and knew firsthand the man's monstrous power.
Even as an admiral himself, Aokiji knew that going toe-to-toe with Garp would end badly for him.
He exhaled softly.
"Looks like we've got another headache on our hands."
The emergence of a figure like Zenkichi in the already chaotic Great Pirate Era would definitely shake the balance of power—and that wasn't good for anyone on their side.
Meanwhile, Admiral Akainu sat silently, holding Zenkichi's wanted poster in his hand. His eyes burned with fury.
Suddenly, magma rippled along his arm. The paper combusted in a burst of heat, turning to ash in seconds.
He growled, voice hoarse and low,
"To be defeated by a rookie… Zephyr has disgraced the Navy—and dishonored justice itself."
"Arakawa Zenkichi… I will find you, and crush you in the name of absolute justice."
As the embodiment of ruthless justice, Akainu never showed mercy toward enemies of the World Government. To him, Zenkichi's existence was unacceptable.
---
By contrast, Admiral Kizaru remained unfazed.
He lounged comfortably in his office, legs crossed, trimming his nails with his usual indifference.
"Hmm… even Zephyr San and Garp San weren't enough? That Zenkichi guy is terrifying."
He sighed lazily.
"I just hope they don't send me to deal with him. I really prefer a life of just clocking in and clocking out…"
Despite his tremendous power, Kizaru had long leaned into his carefree, 'salt-fish' lifestyle, avoiding conflict when possible.
Among the doves and hawks of the Navy, Kizaru stood alone—a powerful yet uninterested middle ground.
---
Moby Dick – Whitebeard Pirates' Main Ship
The man known as the strongest in the world sat calmly on the deck, gazing out at the sea.
Edward Newgate, Whitebeard, was not yet sixty. He wasn't the sickly, weakened man from the Paramount War. Though slightly past his prime, his presence still radiated immense power.
He glanced down at the newspaper in his massive hand and let out a deep, hearty laugh.
"Gurararara! So a brat like this is shaking the sea now… It's a pity he's not a pirate."
There was amusement in his voice, not hostility.
Marco, the First Division Commander, walked over and smiled.
"Pops, do you want to put him in his place? A newcomer challenging your title like that can't be left unchecked."
Whitebeard waved dismissively.
"What's the point? Is the title of 'the world's strongest man' really so important?"
"There've always been people trying to take my head. Every year, another rookie dares to challenge me."
He smirked, shaking his head.
"Don't be fooled, Marco. This is just the World Government's game. They're trying to use me to get rid of that boy."
"Zenkichi has become a thorn in their side, and they're hoping I'll do their dirty work."
Marco frowned slightly.
"But this kind of propaganda might damage your reputation, Pops. People who don't know the full story could think you're afraid of him."
Whitebeard burst into laughter again.
"Gurararara! Do I need anyone's approval for my strength, Marco?"
"They can think what they like."
Whitebeard was unlike other pirates who pursued fame, riches, or power. What he desired most was a family.
That was why he'd taken in so many as his "sons"—to fulfill his dream of building a true family.
His grounded outlook made the World Government's manipulation ineffective.
Still, even if they failed to turn Whitebeard against Zenkichi, the impact wasn't small.
The world now knew his name.
---
Whole Cake Island – Big Mom Pirates
In her vast palace, Charlotte Linlin read the newspaper, her massive frame shaking as she laughed.
"Well, well, well! Who would've thought such a promising young man would appear out of nowhere!"
She cackled with delight, the paper fluttering in her hands as her children looked on in silence.

In the grand halls of Totto Land, the Fourth Emperor's mother—Big Mom—grinned as she scanned the latest issue of the World Economic Times. Her grin stretched wider than any sane face should allow, thick lips curling like a delighted child who had just claimed an entire candy store.

His tone was steady but doubtful. He didn't believe someone with that much power could be swayed so easily. Pride was a defining trait of the strong.

Why would someone like that ever submit?
Big Mom waved off his concerns with a laugh. "Just do as I say. I have plans of my own."
Left with no choice, Katakuri nodded and left to fulfill her command. He may be second in command of the Big Mom Pirates, but in her domain, Charlotte Linlin was absolute.
---
Far across the seas, in the den of the Beast Pirates, Kaido—the strongest creature in the world—sat cross-legged with a giant sake gourd resting against his shoulder.
Drunk again.

He waved a hand lazily. "Go. Dig up everything on this man. If you find out where he is, tell me immediately."
"I want to see what makes this brat think he can challenge Whitebeard's legacy."
---

"This era's getting wild," Shanks said, taking another swig. "Even guys like this Zenkichi are showing up."

Across the world, the name Zenkichi was spreading like wildfire—praised, feared, debated.

Out at sea, Zenkichi walked calmly across the surface of the Grand Line, each step light and deliberate.
He had no interest in ships.
He preferred walking—step by step, alone with the rhythm of the ocean.
Not far away, a golden-crowned pirate ship carved with a crocodile's head cut through the waves.

"Cruel. Cold. Calculated. You didn't come here just to talk, did you?"

"The Admirals are the strongest force under the World Government. They're monsters, walking natural disasters. Defeating one isn't simple."
He sighed, visibly frustrated.
He had once dreamed of toppling legends too. But Crocodile was self-aware enough to recognize the limits of his own strength. Despite his efforts, he had hit a plateau. His potential felt spent, and no amount of ambition could change that.
"Zenkichi," he said slowly, "what if we worked together?"
"You may be powerful, but you're still a newcomer."
"As they say, two fists can't beat four. You alone cannot take on the World Government."

"The World Government isn't the only power either. The Yonko, warlords, and rogue ninja of the New World—all have monsters of their own."

"I have networks, hidden supporters, and ways to expand. If you and I combined our strengths, there wouldn't be a force that could stop us."
For a moment, he looked hopeful.
But Zenkichi let out a quiet, almost dismissive laugh.
"Cooperation?" he echoed. "That implies equality. Do you really think we're equals?"
"If you're looking to serve under me, I'll consider it. But a partnership?"

Erosion Cycle.

Water Release—Hidden Mist Technique.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 - 163: 163: You're not a Marine, Are you?
chapters.content:
"Water Style – Great Exploding Water Wave!"
Zenkichi, who once held the position of Mizukage, had long since mastered countless Water Style techniques.
Being near the ocean only enhanced his power. Drawing from the nearby sea, he channeled chakra, stirring the waves.
The once calm surface of the ocean began to churn violently. A massive swell formed, surging high before crashing toward the shore like a roaring beast.
Seeing the enormous wave bearing down, Crocodile's expression turned grim.
The Suna Suna no Mi, his Devil Fruit, wasn't considered top-tier among the Logia-type abilities. Aside from its shortcomings in destructive force and flexibility, it harbored a unique and glaring weakness.
Unlike other Devil Fruits, where users remained functional even when wet—as long as they weren't submerged—Crocodile's sand-based powers were entirely nullified by water. Even a splash could disrupt his ability to transform.
It was a crippling flaw.
And now, faced with a crushing wall of seawater, Crocodile didn't hesitate. His body burst into a gust of sand, whipping away from the incoming tide.
If he were caught in that wave, it would be over.
The ocean slammed into the beach where Crocodile had stood, saturating the terrain in a blanket of water.
Zenkichi, standing tall on the soaked island, formed seals again with precision. Drawing even more seawater, he unleashed another wave of Water Style jutsu.
From the sea, water began to swirl and rise once more. This time, it formed an immense sphere that hovered ominously over the island like a living dome—a mobile water prison technique, similar to the one used by Hoshigaki Kisame during his battles.
Inside this water prison, Zenkichi could control the battlefield entirely.
"I give up," Crocodile declared, his voice carrying no hint of resistance.
Zenkichi's water jutsu countered him too perfectly.
"It's rare to see someone who can even control the sea," Crocodile muttered, a rare glint of respect—and envy—in his eyes.
"With that kind of power, you're practically invincible out here."
Zenkichi adjusted the hem of his cloak with a cool expression. "Even without it, I still have no equals at sea."
With nothing more to say, he turned and began walking toward the shore.
Crocodile stared after him, watching as the massive water sphere finally burst and collapsed.
His fists clenched tightly.
"My strength is reaching its limits. I can't improve further by ordinary means."
"To become King of the Pirates… I'll need more than just brute force."
"Power… all my underlings are either weaklings or traitors."
"If strength and loyalty won't bring me to the top… I'll need something else."
"The ancient weapons—those world-shattering tools of legend—they're the only way."
"If I can find one… I'll take a country for myself, raise an army, and seize the world!"
Crocodile's resolve hardened.
---
After leaving Crocodile behind, Zenkichi resumed his solitary journey.
He moved across the sea at his own pace, taking time to enjoy the islands he encountered, blending into the local scenes, living like an ordinary traveler.
Until one day…
"Robin! How dare you betray me?!"
On a quiet island street, a voice cracked the air—furious, violent.
Zenkichi turned toward the noise just in time to see a young woman sprinting his way, panic in her eyes.
Behind her, a mob of grizzled pirates closed in fast.
"You there, brat! Stop that woman!"
"You hear us?! If you don't, we'll kill you!"
The leader's threats were loud and clear.
Zenkichi raised a hand lazily, adjusting his new sunglasses—an item he'd just picked up from a market stall. They covered most of his face, and the pirates didn't recognize him.
"How scary," he said softly, mimicking Kizaru's tone with playful mockery.
"You're threatening me? Ever felt a kick at the speed of light?"
Golden light burst from his body.
In a blink, Zenkichi vanished, reappearing instantly before the mob. With a radiant glow shining from his heel, he unleashed a blinding kick, striking the lead pirate with devastating force.
"Wait a minute—!"
"That's the Glint-Glint Fruit!"
"Admiral Kizaru?!"
The panic was instant. Recognition spread like wildfire.
One of them threw his sword. Another tossed away his rifle.Thɪs
"We surrender!"
All at once, the pirates raised their hands in surrender, looking like children caught stealing candy.
Zenkichi stared at them in silence.
"Pathetic," he said finally. "Calling yourselves pirates, yet surrendering without a fight?"
"I'll give you ten seconds to run."
"If you're still here after that, I'll open fire."
"I'm not dragging you to prison. Whether you live or die… that's up to you."
For a second, the pirates hesitated, unsure if he was bluffing.
But then he started counting.
And they bolted.
As they ran, Zenkichi sighed. "Impressive escape skills… for cowards."
Then came the lasers—swift and precise. In moments, most of the pirates were downed. Only a few escaped with their lives.
Zenkichi turned toward the girl.
She hadn't moved an inch.
"Why didn't you run?" he asked, eyeing her with mild curiosity.
"You're not a Marine, are you?" she said, sharp-eyed.
It wasn't a question. It was a statement.
Zenkichi smiled slightly, the golden light fading from his body.

chapters.title: Chapter 165 - 165: 165: Moria, A Warlord.
chapters.content:
The Devil's Triangle.
Zenkichi and Robin drifted into the eerie sea region aboard a small boat. A thick fog blanketed the surroundings, muting all sound but the soft lap of water against the hull.
Robin narrowed her eyes. "Where are we? I can't see a thing in this mist."
Zenkichi answered calmly, "This is the Devil's Triangle. It's a peculiar region—shrouded in fog all year. Some call it a ghost sea, but that's just talk."
Robin's gaze swept across the quiet sea. Dozens of derelict pirate ships floated eerily nearby. "There are so many abandoned ships here," she murmured. "It does feel haunted."
Zenkichi scoffed. "That's not because of nature. Most of this… was engineered."
Robin turned to him, surprised. "You mean someone made it this way?"
"Partially," he replied. "A man with a shattered spine—metaphorically and literally. Just a broken fool trying to hide in fear."
As Zenkichi looked ahead, the fog parted slightly, revealing a massive silhouette looming in the distance.
An island-ship—one that drifted here from the West Blue and eventually merged into the Grand Line.
It was more than a ship. It was a floating island.
And it belonged to one of the Shichibukai—Gecko Moria.
Once heralded as a pirate hero, Moria had dared to challenge one of the Four Emperors. His ambition was fierce; he'd dreamed of standing above even Kaido of the Beasts.
But that dream was shattered—literally. Kaido's brutal strength had demolished his crew and crushed Moria's will. Since then, like Crocodile, Moria had abandoned the pursuit of strength and turned to darker, stranger means.
While Crocodile chased the power of ancient weapons, Moria chose to rely on corpses and shadows—building an army of the undead.Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"You stay here," Zenkichi said to Robin, stepping off the boat. "I'll take a look."
In a flash, he vanished and landed on the drifting island.
As soon as his feet touched the ground, the soil rippled unnaturally. Hands shot up from the earth—decaying arms stretching toward him—followed by entire bodies.
Zombies.
Animated corpses stitched crudely together, each powered by a stolen shadow through the power of the Shadow-Shadow Fruit.
Zenkichi didn't even blink.
"Pathetic," he muttered as the undead rushed him.
Golden light glowed on his fingertip—laser energy condensed with deadly precision.
Zenkichi raised his palm lazily and fired.
Beams of searing light exploded through the charging zombies, tearing them apart.
From the castle at the island's center, a swarm of black bats emerged, fluttering toward him like a living tide.
He recognized the trick.
These weren't ordinary creatures—they were shadows, twisted and weaponized by Moria's Devil Fruit.
Still, he walked forward, unfazed, each step deliberate.
As the bats swarmed him, water from the sea swelled violently. A colossal water dragon, forged from seawater, rose and crashed down.
Water Release – Water Dragon Bullet Technique.
The wave crashed down upon the zombies, saturating their corpses. Saltwater neutralized the shadow-bound abilities. The creatures dropped, lifeless once more.
Zenkichi made his way through the crumbling mob, eventually reaching the towering castle at the center of the island.
From within the shadows, a voice rang out.
"Zenkichi…?"
Gecko Moria emerged, his expression a mix of confusion and hostility.
"What are you doing on my ship?"
Zenkichi regarded him coolly. "I heard you once challenged Kaido. I was passing by, so I figured I'd take a look at what's left of you."
He paused. "I recently met someone who tried to fight Whitebeard. He turned out to be garbage."
"So now I'm curious about you."
"Don't—" Moria's face contorted with rage. "Don't say that name!"
Kaido.
The one who'd ruined him.
Moria had lost everything—his crew, his pride—and the wound was still fresh. Zenkichi's words dug straight into that scar.
"You've lost your spirit, haven't you?" Zenkichi said coldly. "Instead of fighting for your dream, you now hide behind shadows and corpses."
"You think an army of undead will make you Pirate King? They aren't even your power."
"No matter how strong they get, it won't be you doing anything. You're just a coward pulling strings in the dark."
"A rat, pretending to be a lion."
Zenkichi's disgust was plain.
"Your slogans… your ambition… it's all a joke."
Moria's fury exploded. "Die!"
He lunged forward without hesitation.
Despite the strength he still retained—this was not the withered Moria of the future—he was no match for Zenkichi.
Moria had been in decline for only a few months, not yet the pale figure seen years later. His skills weren't gone. His Haki wasn't forgotten.
But even at near-peak, he was still nothing in front of Zenkichi.
The battle was over before it truly began.

chapters.title: Chapter 166 - 166: 166: The Admiral's Arrival.
chapters.content:
Moria condensed his shadow into armor, layering it over himself as he lunged into close combat with Zenkichi.
Unfortunately, Zenkichi's hand-to-hand abilities far surpassed Moria's. Within seconds, he was overwhelmed and sent flying.
Still, Moria wasn't discouraged. Regaining his footing, he condensed his shadow into a humanoid figure—an exact replica of himself—and charged forward once more.
This shadow warrior had properties similar to Logia-type Devil Fruits, allowing it to shift between a tangible and intangible form. Even when physically struck, it could disperse into shadow and reconstitute itself. It could also launch powerful physical attacks, despite being formed of shadow.
Even Haki and Seastone couldn't truly destroy it. This ability made Moria's shadow warrior incredibly difficult to handle, especially in prolonged battles.
The shadow copy was torn apart by Zenkichi's blows repeatedly, only to regenerate effortlessly each time.
This was Moria's preferred tactic—using his nigh-indestructible body double to wear down stronger opponents. As long as their strength didn't vastly outmatch his own, this strategy usually turned the tide in his favor.
Unfortunately for Moria, the difference between his power and Zenkichi's was too great.
And unlike most powerhouses in the pirate world, Zenkichi possessed methods that specifically countered abilities like Moria's.
As the shadow warrior rushed forward again, Zenkichi calmly raised his hand. A white aura shimmered around his palm.
He tightened his fist, then launched a punch into the air. The very space before him fractured like glass, spiderwebbing with cracks.
The shockwave from his punch shattered the shadow warrior completely, dispersing it into fragments of darkness.
In the next instant, Zenkichi vanished—and reappeared behind Moria, his hand tightening around the warlord's throat.
Moria didn't panic. He had already prepared for this and activated his spatial technique, swapping places with his shadow clone to escape Zenkichi's grasp.
"I knew you'd try that," Zenkichi muttered, smirking.
Dark sealing lines spiraled across his palm, forming a chakra-based fūinjutsu from the shinobi world. He slammed his hand into the shadow clone—sealing it away instantly.
"What?!"
Moria's face twisted in shock. He could no longer sense his shadow.
As a wielder of the Shadow Shadow Fruit, his shadow was the core of all his power. Without it, he was helpless.
"You should've known," Zenkichi said, his tone calm. "This is where it ends."
He appeared before Moria again, his fist wrapped in that radiant white aura—and drove it into Moria's skull, extinguishing his life in one final, crushing blow.
Moria was dead.
With his demise, all the shadows he had stolen were released. The zombies under his control crumbled, and the stolen shadows returned to their rightful owners.
A tall, bony figure stepped forward from the ruins and bowed deeply to Zenkichi.
"Thank you so much, sir!"
It was Brook—the skeletal musician and swordsman—restored now that his shadow had returned.
Brook was a user of the Yomi Yomi no Mi, the Revive-Revive Fruit. After dying, he was brought back to life, though by the time his soul found his body, only his skeleton remained.
Even so, in this bizarre world, Brook still functioned. He could walk, speak, eat, and even... use the bathroom, somehow.
"I'm still missing a musician on my ship," Zenkichi said, eyeing him thoughtfully. "Want to join us for a while?"Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
He had no plans to keep Brook permanently—but for now, he was curious to hear the famed Soul King's music.
Brook hesitated only a moment before nodding enthusiastically.
"It would be my greatest honor!"
With Moria gone and the Devil's Triangle descending into chaos, Brook had no better prospects. Sticking with Zenkichi was clearly the smartest move.
"Good," Zenkichi said simply.
They didn't linger. Not long after, they set sail—and left the Devil's Triangle behind.
But just as they did, a massive warship appeared ahead, blocking their path.
At its bow stood a tall man in a yellow-striped suit, hands in his pockets, expression unreadable.
"Why'd you have to come this way?" Admiral Kizaru asked lazily, his voice half-hearted.
"Seems like this is going to end in a fight after all."
He sighed, clearly annoyed.
Kizaru hadn't wanted this mission. Sengoku had insisted.
Originally, Kizaru had planned to "accidentally" miss Zenkichi, to avoid confrontation altogether. But fate had other plans.
Now that they'd crossed paths, there was no going back.
With a resigned shrug, Kizaru stepped forward to the edge of the warship.
He might have preferred to avoid trouble, but he was still an admiral of the Navy—one of the world's strongest.
"Admiral Kizaru?" Zenkichi said, curiosity flashing in his eyes. "Didn't expect to see you here."
A confrontation with a Navy admiral was unexpected—but welcome.
Kizaru's laid-back expression didn't change. He spoke in a flat, matter-of-fact tone.
"You've caught the Navy's attention, Zenkichi. You're a threat to world stability."
"So today, I'm here to arrest you—to prevent you from making things worse."
He paused, then added, "Of course, if you'd rather resist... I can always execute you on the spot."
"To be honest, I prefer that. Arresting people's a hassle—I don't like wasting time."
Kizaru stared down at Zenkichi and sighed again, clearly irritated by the whole situation.

Brook had always held a deep reverence for the Admirals.

The absurdity of the scene shook his belief. Were the Admirals truly as powerful as the legends claimed?
"Think the Admiral's not all he's cracked up to be?" Zenkichi said with a smirk, catching Brooke's expression.
"If you do, I suggest you take it up with him. He's right over there—go ahead, give it a try."

Brooke laughed nervously, waving his skeletal hands in protest. "No, no, I'll pass! I didn't have to fight him to know I'd lose. Just the pressure from that Yasakani No Magatama attack nearly shattered my spine—and I don't even have one!"
When Kizaru unleashed that blinding storm of golden light bullets, Brook had been sure that even his bones would be reduced to dust. He knew his limits.
