chapters.title: Chapter 169 - 169: 169: The Navy's Fleet.
chapters.content:
Admiral Akainu spoke with a grim tone. "I believe we must act against Zenkichi now. He's become a massive destabilizing force."
"If he enters the New World and his strength continues to grow, he'll become a threat on the level of a Yonko. By then, eliminating him might be nearly impossible."
While trimming his nails, Admiral Kizaru replied nonchalantly, "Isn't that kind of development beneficial? If Zenkichi rises to become a force like the Four Emperors, he could disrupt the current balance."
"He might clash with the existing Yonko. And whether it's injuries or deaths, any weakening of their power benefits the Navy."
Admiral Aokiji, leaning back lazily, frowned slightly. "If we let these pirate factions fight unchecked, civilians in the New World will be caught in the crossfire."
Aokiji, a known pacifist among the admirals, was clearly uneasy with that idea.
Fleet Admiral Sengoku's voice carried weight as he replied, "It's true that turning Zenkichi against the Yonko is a strategic move, but I'm concerned things might spiral out of control."
"Our goal is to weaken them through infighting, not let one rise above the rest and become even more dangerous."
"If Zenkichi defeats and absorbs other pirate crews, he might emerge stronger than any of them."
Vice Admiral Tsuru, the calm and calculating staff officer, asked, "Then what's the course of action?"
Sengoku paused to think before speaking slowly. "Zenkichi appeared out of nowhere. His power may surpass even our expectations."
"I believe we should first test his strength—gauge the level of threat before deciding how to engage him."
Akainu's expression darkened. "In that case, let me be the one to test him."
Sengoku shook his head. "Zenkichi isn't someone a single admiral can handle. His power already rival that of the Pirate Emperors."
"I propose we send all three admirals—and I will personally lead the operation."
His declaration sent a wave of shock through the naval high command. Even the Four Emperors weren't usually met with such overwhelming force.
Sengoku looked around at the stunned officers and continued. "Do not underestimate Zenkichi. His strength is far more terrifying than you imagine."
"He knocked Kizaru away with a single punch. He can breathe fire, control seawater—he's shown power that rivals the strongest in the world."
"To fight someone like that, it will take two admirals just to hold him, three to suppress him, and four to ensure his elimination."
"Our goal this time is simple: eliminate Zenkichi. And for that, we require overwhelming power."
Once the decision was made, the Navy acted swiftly. Within hours, a warship carrying Sengoku and the three admirals—Akainu, Kizaru, and Aokiji—left Marineford.
---
Sabaody Archipelago
Zenkichi and Robin strolled leisurely through the bustling streets of the Sabaody Archipelago. The exotic scenery and flavorful food made the island a rare joy during their journey through the world of pirates.
"If you're going to visit the One Piece world, might as well enjoy it a little," Zenkichi said with a smirk as he watched Robin examine a street vendor's wares.
Robin smiled faintly. "I never expected you to be the type who enjoys sightseeing."
Zenkichi looked ahead thoughtfully. "I know someone here who may interest you—a man who knows more about the Poneglyphs than anyone alive. If you're serious about uncovering history, I can introduce you."
Robin arched an eyebrow. "Someone who knows everything about the Poneglyphs? You must be joking."
"I'm not," Zenkichi replied flatly. "I'm talking about Silvers Rayleigh."
Robin blinked, stunned. "Pluton Rayleigh… the Pirate King's right hand?"
Zenkichi nodded. "He's retired, lives quietly now, but if anyone can guide you, it's him."
Though skeptical, Robin's curiosity was piqued. Zenkichi didn't plan to lead her to Raftel, and Robin wasn't prepared for that journey yet either. For now, Rayleigh was her best shot at answers.
Soon, Zenkichi led her to a small, inconspicuous tavern. Inside, an old man sat alone at the bar, drinking casually. His scruffy appearance made him look like just another retired sailor.
Robin leaned in toward Zenkichi. "Are you sure that's him? He's… not quite what I imagined."
Zenkichi chuckled. "Don't let appearances fool you. Veterans may look rough, but their strength and wisdom remain."
He approached the man. "Care to step outside for a talk? My companion has a few questions for you."
Rayleigh glanced over, then grinned. "So the famous rookie wants a word with me? That's interesting."

Zenkichi smirked. "Let's just call it a special insight. I can't really share the details."

Turning to Robin, he added, "If you want answers, let's find a better place to talk. This alley isn't exactly a lecture hall."

chapters.title: Chapter 170 - 170: 170: The Battle Begins.
chapters.content:
"History is like a little girl anyone can dress up—just look away."
Zenkichi spoke calmly, trying to soothe Robin, whose emotions had grown unsteady after learning the truth.
Robin had just heard the full account of the Void Century from Silvers Rayleigh, the former right-hand of the Pirate King. She now knew the secrets buried for 800 years, the truths the World Government tried so desperately to erase.
For Zenkichi, however, these revelations held little weight.
With the power to reshape the seas, to rewrite the course of history itself, he saw no need to dwell on the past. What mattered was the world he was carving through strength.
Suddenly, Rayleigh's expression shifted, sharp and alert. He turned his gaze toward Zenkichi.
"The old man from the Sengoku era brought three admirals with him. I assume they're after you, not me. I've long since retired."
Zenkichi gave a small nod, unfazed. "Yeah. They're here for me. Take Robin and go. I'll handle them."
He had already sensed the presence of the Navy's top brass. But he had no intention of dragging Rayleigh into the confrontation. This was his battle.
Rayleigh understood. Without argument, he turned to Robin. "Let's move."
Robin hesitated, her eyes lingering on Zenkichi with concern and conflict.
"Do you want to stay and fight beside me?" Zenkichi asked with a faint smile. "This isn't your battle, Robin."
She sighed. She knew he was right. Staying would only complicate matters.
"Come on," Rayleigh said gently, and she followed him, casting one last look over her shoulder.
Zenkichi began walking toward the coastline, his pace steady. He wanted an open field—somewhere the battle wouldn't spill over onto civilians.
Out at sea near the Sabaody Archipelago, a colossal Marine warship hovered ominously.
Sengoku stood aboard with a scowl. "I didn't expect Zenkichi to be connected to that relic, Rayleigh. This complicates things."
"Rayleigh's supposed to be retired. Why can't the old man stay out of pirate business?"
Sengoku felt a twinge of uncertainty. Rayleigh wasn't someone to be taken lightly. If he and Zenkichi teamed up, the mission would be in jeopardy.
Akainu stood nearby, his face grim. "When it comes to pirates, we must show no mercy. Just because he 'retired' doesn't make him innocent."Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
His tone carried more than contempt—it carried resentment. The Navy had tolerated Rayleigh for too long.
Sengoku shot Akainu a sharp look. "You think we haven't wanted to deal with him? He's no ordinary pirate. It'd take several admirals to bring him down."
Even with overwhelming force, Rayleigh would likely escape. Worse, if backed into a corner, he could take an admiral with him.
The World Government had chosen to leave him alone only because he had vanished from the world stage. But if he fought today alongside Zenkichi, everything would change.
Just then, Kizaru narrowed his eyes, sensing something unusual. "Hm? Seems like they've separated. That's good. Maybe Rayleigh doesn't want to get involved."
Sengoku, also sensing the situation with his Haki, shook his head. "No… It's not that he didn't sense us. He did."

"Zenkichi's arrogant," he added. "Or perhaps, just confident enough to take on all of us alone."
Footsteps echoed from the forest near the coast.
Zenkichi walked calmly toward the warship, his eyes locked on the four powerful figures waiting atop the deck.
"Fleet Admiral Sengoku, Admiral Akainu, Admiral Kizaru, Admiral Aokiji…"
He gave a mock laugh.
"Quite the welcoming party. You brought the entire top brass just for me? I'm flattered."
"The World Government's strongest assets… dispatched for a single so-called pirate. Doesn't that make you look a little desperate?"

Akainu stepped forward, face like stone. "Justice doesn't need pride. A criminal like you will be eliminated—no matter the cost."
Without another word, molten magma began bubbling at his fists. Heat radiated outward, distorting the air.
Zenkichi's face didn't flinch. "Admiral Akainu… always quick to anger. No heart, only fists."

Water Release: Tranquil Depths.

chapters.title: Chapter 171 - 171: 171: Four Against One.
chapters.content:
A massive surge of seawater rose and slammed into Akainu with unstoppable force.
"Ice Age!"
Without hesitation, Aokiji unleashed his ultimate move. A surge of intense cold exploded from his body, freezing the incoming sea wave into massive crystalline ice.
From afar, Zenkichi watched the scene unfold with calm eyes.
"Freezing seawater, huh? That's quite the power…"
His tone was neutral, but his gaze lingered on Aokiji's handiwork.
"Indeed," he added, "this kind of ability really is a headache for Devil Fruit users."
"But as long as we have Devil Fruit users who can control the sea itself, even that edge becomes meaningless."
Sengoku stepped forward, voice firm and arrogant.
Zenkichi let out a small laugh and glanced at Sengoku, his tone playful.
"Marshal Sengoku, are you serious right now?"
"You honestly believe my biggest trump card is manipulating seawater? I don't know whether to be amused or insulted."
Sengoku's face hardened.
"If not that, then what is your greatest advantage?"
Zenkichi's smirk grew.
"Were the other powers I've shown so far really that forgettable to you?"
Sengoku remained composed.
"Your physical prowess and your Haki are indeed impressive—but they aren't enough to face the four of us together."
"Even Whitebeard, the man known as the strongest in the world, and Kaido, the so-called strongest creature, couldn't withstand a combined assault. Alone, you stand no chance."
Zenkichi raised a brow, then chuckled.
"If you're so curious, then let me show you."
The moment the words left his mouth, a suffocating wave of spiritual pressure burst from his body. It surged across the battlefield like a collapsing sky, bearing down on everyone with an invisible weight.
Sengoku, Aokiji, Akainu, and Kizaru staggered slightly—struggling to breathe as if mountains had fallen on their shoulders. Their eyes widened in disbelief.
"What… what is this power!?"
Even before the fight began, they felt crushed. Their instincts screamed at them: the man standing before them was not someone they could defeat.
"Heh… strong mental suppression," Sengoku muttered. "Is this your Devil Fruit power? Or maybe… Conqueror's Haki, with a unique application?"
Despite the pressure, Sengoku steadied himself. A powerful wave of Conqueror's Haki erupted from him as he stood tall.
"You have it too, don't you?" Zenkichi asked, eyes gleaming. "But it's still not enough."
"I'm not here to bluff," he added coldly. "That was just the surface of what I can do."
Gritting his teeth, Aokiji suddenly shouted:
"Ice Age!"
Once again, freezing air exploded from his body, covering everything in ice. It spread rapidly toward Zenkichi, and in seconds, he was encased in a massive ice sculpture.
Akainu didn't hesitate. Thick magma surged from his arm, forming a massive molten fist.
"Great Eruption!"
With a roar, Akainu hurled his blazing punch at the frozen figure. The magma exploded upon contact—shattering and vaporizing the ice in a burst of steam and heat.
But as the smoke cleared, Zenkichi stood there—untouched.
A transparent barrier shimmered in front of him, the magma halted mid-strike.
"That attack—was that your best move? Disappointing," Zenkichi said mockingly.
"Is this really the strength of the Navy's top admirals? It's no wonder the seas are in chaos."
Up above, Kizaru leapt into the air.
"Yasakani no Magatama!"
Dozens of glowing golden light bullets rained down toward Zenkichi.
But once again, the shimmering spiritual pressure barrier above him twisted and blocked the attack. Sparks danced across the shield, but none of the light bullets broke through.
"All at once!" Sengoku roared. His body gleamed with golden light as he activated his Devil Fruit.
In a blinding flash, Sengoku transformed into a towering golden Buddha.
Mythical Zoan—Human-Human Fruit, Model: Daibutsu.
With a thunderous boom, he thrust his palm forward. A massive shockwave exploded from his hand and crashed toward Zenkichi.
But the barrier held.
"Impossible!"
Aokiji's eyes widened. His body moved on instinct, punching at the barrier with a Haki-infused fist.
Still nothing.
The shockwave dispersed harmlessly, and Zenkichi remained still, arms crossed.
The others stared in disbelief.
"Three admiral-class attacks… and he didn't flinch," Aokiji murmured.
The sinking feeling in their hearts grew.
Was Zenkichi truly this powerful?
Sengoku forced a chuckle, trying to mask his unease.
"You're quite good at defense, Zenkichi."
He tried to rationalize it, assuming the barrier was Zenkichi's Devil Fruit ability—an advanced defensive skill.
But in truth… they all knew the truth: this wasn't just an ability. This was a crushing, overwhelming power that bent the rules around it.
A power they weren't ready to face.

chapters.title: Chapter 172 - 172: 172: Mockery & The Collapse of the Admirals.
chapters.content:
Sengoku watched with a tight jaw, realizing his admirals were stunned by Zenkichi's overwhelming power. Fearing their morale would break, he shouted sarcastically to provoke them back into action.
Luckily, the three Navy Admirals weren't so easily rattled. Despite the monstrous strength Zenkichi displayed, they stood firm. These were men who had fought countless deadly battles, molded through blood and fire. You didn't reach admiral rank in the Navy without extraordinary resolve and monstrous talent.
In the turbulent tides of the world, many so-called "geniuses" were swallowed and forgotten. But those who survived to the top were anything but weak.
There was no room to surrender.
"Still planning to resist?" Zenkichi raised a brow, smiling faintly at the regrouped Admirals and Sengoku.
"Well then… I'll grant your wish."
Sengoku grunted and leapt into the air, golden light surging from his body as he transformed into a massive Buddha.
BOOM!
A thunderous palm strike came crashing down, the shockwave shaking the air itself.
Zenkichi didn't dodge. He responded with a single, clean punch.
The sheer pressure of his blow split the air apart, colliding with Sengoku's shockwave—and shattered it. The impact sent the golden Buddha flying, crashing to the ground with a groan.
"Hellhound!"
Akainu's roar echoed out as he charged in, his magma arm transforming into a snarling, molten hound.
The blazing fist hurtled toward Zenkichi's chest—but the invisible spiritual pressure barrier held firm, stopping it cold.
Even Akainu's ultimate move couldn't break through.
In response, Zenkichi's fist gleamed with Armament Haki. With ruthless precision, he slammed it into Akainu's skull.
CRACK!
Akainu's body smashed into the ground, exploding into splattering magma. The molten puddle twitched and squirmed, slowly reforming into his body—but he looked pale, trembling, blood dripping from his lips.
One punch had done that. A single blow, and a Navy admiral—one known for his monstrous endurance—was nearly done.
Akainu couldn't believe it.
He had always been a war tank, feared for his strength and near-unbreakable body. Even when Whitebeard struck him with a full-powered blow in the original war, he continued fighting and suppressed Whitebeard's captains.
But now?
One punch from Zenkichi nearly ended him.
"Light Kick!"
Kizaru blurred into motion, his body flashing into particles of light. He soared toward Zenkichi, delivering a blinding kick cloaked in shimmering photons.
Zenkichi didn't flinch. A spiritual pressure barrier shimmered into view.
Kizaru's kick connected with a sound like thunder, air rupturing violently—but the barrier didn't even crack.
Zenkichi stared at him with cold indifference.
"No matter how much you struggle, you're still not on my level."
Then, without warning, he moved.
Before Kizaru could react, Zenkichi grabbed his leg mid-air.
"Wha—?"
Zenkichi spun him overhead and slammed him into the ground like a ragdoll.
Again. And again.
One, two, three, four—two, two, three, four!
He smashed Kizaru left and right like a child with a toy. Then with a roar, he hurled him toward a distant warship.
BOOM!
Kizaru crashed into it like a missile, light exploding in all directions. Even though he tried to reduce the damage by turning intangible, the impact still blew a gaping hole into the warship.
Sailors screamed and scrambled as debris rained down.
"Ice Blade!"
Aokiji rushed in, holding a katana-shaped weapon formed from ice, its edge reinforced with jet-black Armament Haki.
He lunged at Zenkichi, aiming straight for his heart.
With a flick of a finger, Zenkichi shattered the blade—then followed up with a punch that sent Aokiji flying.
A golden flash lit up behind him. Sengoku had recovered and charged in again, trying to seize an opening.
But Zenkichi spun and delivered a savage kick enhanced with Flash Step, catching Sengoku off-guard. The force hurled the golden Buddha away, and the marshal tumbled across the ground, groaning in pain.
"The Marshal… and all three Navy Admirals… defeated?"
Zenkichi slowly approached the four battered men, his expression unreadable.
"What do you think the world would say if I killed you here?"
His tone was casual, almost mocking.
"Would it spark panic? Collapse the balance? Or perhaps... usher in something new?"
Sengoku glared at him through labored breaths.
"It's not over… until the final moment."
Zenkichi laughed quietly.
"So you're saying I need to kill all of you to prove I've won?"
From the shattered warship, Kizaru flew out weakly, light flickering from his battered form.
"Sengoku… I think we need to… reevaluate," he said, gasping.
"Continuing to fight now… it's suicide."
Akainu stood shakily, magma dripping from his arm. He scowled at Kizaru.
"Borsalino… are you suggesting we surrender?"
Kizaru shrugged, breath ragged.
"Not surrender. Just… live to fight smarter. Right now, we're not winning this."
Zenkichi glanced at them, amused.
"Relax. I'm not planning to kill you—yet."
"The seas still need balance. And for now, your presence is useful. I have other priorities."

Kaido was a paradoxical figure. While most pirates pursued strength, fame, or power, Kaido seemed to be searching for something far stranger: death.
He had challenged the Navy and other Yonko countless times, and been captured just as often. But never killed. Somehow, he always survived—even after falling from tens of thousands of meters in the sky. His vitality was monstrous, earning him the title of "the world's strongest creature."
And yet, this madman controlled the fearsome Beast Pirates. He also held ties with the shogun of Wano Country, and perhaps even secret dealings with the World Government. His erratic behavior was in stark contrast with his calculated influence, making it unclear whether he was truly insane or simply playing the part.
One thing, however, was certain: his desire for death was real.
He had sensed Zenkichi's overwhelming power from afar, having witnessed his domination of the Navy's top brass through Observation Haki. Yet instead of fleeing, Kaido sought him out—desperate to challenge him, perhaps even hoping he could be killed.
As Kaido's massive dragon form descended, Zenkichi leapt directly onto his head. With firm hands, he grabbed Kaido's horns as if taming a wild stallion.

"Don't get too comfortable. I'll return, and next time, I'll overturn the entire World Government."

"This is serious," Sengoku said gravely, turning to the three battered Admirals. "We need to regroup immediately."
In their current condition, if even one Emperor's second-in-command crossed their path, they'd be doomed.

With a sudden burst of movement, he vanished and reappeared in front of her, his fist colliding with her gut. The impact echoed like thunder.
Blood burst from Linlin's mouth as her steel-like body cracked under the force. She stumbled back, dazed.
Raising his hand, Zenkichi summoned more spiritual pressure. The heavens roared as it surged upward and shattered the Zeus overhead.
"You're weaker than I expected," he said coolly, walking toward her.
Charlotte Linlin's children charged forward in a desperate attempt to protect their mother, but Kaido stepped in.
Wielding his massive kanabo, Kaido crushed them without mercy, knocking them all unconscious in seconds.
Zenkichi approached Linlin, who lay coughing and bloodied on the ground.
"Charlotte Linlin, be my puppet."
His Mangekyō Sharingan activated, the intricate pattern glowing with sinister light. Without even meeting her eyes, his mental force invaded her mind.
Her will shattered like glass.
Just as Danzō had once controlled Mifune with his Sharingan while his eyes were hidden, Zenkichi's power didn't require direct contact. His mental domination was overwhelming.
Charlotte Linlin—Big Mom—was now his.
Over the next few days, Zenkichi consolidated her forces, bringing the entire Big Mom Pirates under his command.
With two Emperors of the Sea already fallen before him, Zenkichi turned his eyes to the next target: the Whitebeard Pirates.
They didn't have a fixed base, sailing the seas on the Moby Dick. But tracking them wasn't difficult—not for someone like Zenkichi.
Soon enough, the shadow of a man descended from the sky, landing heavily on the deck of the great ship.
The Whitebeard Pirates had been mid-celebration, their laughter dying the moment Zenkichi landed.
Whitebeard frowned and looked to the sky, his instincts screaming. He rose slowly, his eyes locked onto the stranger who had silenced the deck with his presence alone.
All eyes turned to Zenkichi.
He had come.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 176 - 176: 176: One Throne to Rule Them All.
chapters.content:
Zenkichi walked through the crowd of pirates aboard the Moby Dick as though he were alone. His calm voice echoed across the deck.
"Whitebeard, I'm here to take you in."
Silence fell, followed by a thunderous uproar.
The members of the Whitebeard Pirates, who regarded Whitebeard as their father, bristled with fury. Unlike the disjointed chaos of the Beasts Pirates, the Whitebeard Pirates were bound by loyalty and love for their captain.
Seeing Zenkichi speak so arrogantly to Whitebeard was an unforgivable insult.
"You dare mock our old man?!"Marco shouted, blue regenerative flames surging around his body as he charged forward without hesitation.
Diamond Jozu followed close behind, his body gleaming like a polished gemstone as he barreled toward Zenkichi like a cannonball.
Behind them came Vista and other Whitebeard commanders, each radiating battle intent, surrounding Zenkichi in moments.
Whitebeard chuckled and took a deep swig from his sake cup, seemingly unfazed. But in the next moment, a crushing force blanketed the entire ship.
The overwhelming pressure of Conqueror's Haki erupted from Zenkichi, rippling through the air.
Without him lifting a finger, most of the pirates collapsed where they stood, the deck beneath them splintering and cracking under the sheer intensity.
Whitebeard's smile faded, replaced by a solemn expression. He gripped his massive naginata tightly and stepped forward.Thɪs NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
"You," he said, his deep voice carrying weight, "Who are you really? What's your goal?"
Zenkichi met his gaze without flinching. "I've already told you. I want you to join me. Become one of my men."
Whitebeard narrowed his eyes. "Making me your subordinate can't be your endgame. What are you really after?"
"This world has been fractured for far too long," Zenkichi replied calmly. "It's time for unity."
"I've heard there's a Void Throne in Mariejois. A throne left empty to symbolize a world without a king… a world where no one rules."
"It's been vacant for 800 years," he continued, "but that ends now. I will be the one to sit upon that throne."
Though he was aware of Imu's existence, Zenkichi had already dismissed him. In his eyes, Imu was a coward, a hidden shadow without the courage to act—a ghost unworthy of his attention.
Whitebeard's frown deepened. "So your target is the World Government. What does that have to do with us?"
Zenkichi's tone sharpened. "All things under heaven belong to the king. Every land, every sea, must bow to the one true ruler."
"You warlords, with your fragmented empires and scattered fleets… you're in my way. Submit to me or be erased. There is no third option."
Whitebeard laughed, gripping his naginata tighter.
"You've got guts, I'll give you that. But words alone don't prove anything."
Zenkichi's voice lowered. "That wasn't bravado. You can feel it, can't you? Charlotte Linlin and Kaido are already mine. Will you be next?"
"If you surrender now, I'll let you remain with your sons. I'll give you autonomy. But defy me, and I'll crush you."
A long silence stretched between them. Whitebeard's gaze remained firm, but there was respect behind it.
"If you want my allegiance, you'll have to earn it," he said.
"I wouldn't have it any other way," Zenkichi replied with a small smile.
Whitebeard moved first. His naginata surged with power as he unleashed a devastating shockwave from his fist. The air itself cracked with the force of the Tremor-Tremor Fruit, a white halo pulsing around his arm.
Zenkichi met it with his own—only his vibration was even stronger.
Their blows collided mid-air, unleashing a titanic shockwave that shook the heavens. But Zenkichi's strength overwhelmed Whitebeard's, and the old pirate was sent flying, crashing into the far end of the deck.
Despite the impact, Whitebeard was not severely wounded. Zenkichi had held back, offering mercy.
Blackbeard Teach, who had once harbored ambitions of his own, shrank into the crowd, lowering his head in silence. The fear in his eyes betrayed him.
With Whitebeard's surrender, the rest of his crew quickly followed. For the sake of his sons, Whitebeard gave up his pride, his title as the world's strongest, and his dreams of dominance.
He had fought long and hard, but in the end, what mattered most to him wasn't power or glory—it was family.
Slowly, he stood up from the wrecked deck and let out a weary sigh.
"You're stronger than me," he admitted. "I'll follow you."
Later, as word of Zenkichi's victory spread, he made his way to a desert island where the Red-Haired Pirates were feasting. He arrived uninvited, but none dared challenge him.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 177 - 177: 177: Conquest of the Red Hair Pirate.
chapters.content:
Zenkichi stood confidently on the deck as the sea breeze whipped around him. His gaze locked onto the man before him—one of the most legendary pirates in the world.
"Zenkichi," Red-Haired Shanks said calmly, gripping the hilt of his sword. "I didn't expect you to show up uninvited. Are you here to challenge me?"
Shanks, one of the Four Emperors of the Sea, had heard the rumors—Zenkichi was quickly rising to prominence, subduing the strongest pirates across the seas.
Zenkichi, however, remained unfazed. "I'm not here to challenge you," he replied, his voice calm and resolute. "I've come to recruit you."
Shanks blinked, uncertain if he had heard correctly.
"From today onward," Zenkichi continued, "you and your crew are mine."
Shanks stared at him, then burst into laughter. "You've got a sense of humor, I'll give you that. But I'm not the kind of man to serve under another."
Zenkichi offered a faint smile. "That's not your decision to make."
A sudden wave of pressure radiated from Zenkichi's body—an immense force of Conqueror's Haki so overwhelming that the very air around them began to tremble. The red-haired pirate's crew froze in place, their bodies immobilized by sheer spiritual force.
Zenkichi stepped forward slowly, unbothered by the resistance. "Are you sure you want to refuse? If you do, I'll have no choice but to end your journey here."
Shanks stood his ground. His own Haki surged outward, clashing violently with Zenkichi's presence. The sheer intensity caused the ship's planks to creak and splinter beneath their feet.
Gritting his teeth, Shanks drew his blade. Coating it in Armament Haki, he lunged at Zenkichi, his swordsmanship honed through decades of battle.
But Zenkichi didn't flinch.
With a single, effortless punch, Zenkichi sent Shanks hurtling backward through the air, crashing into the mast. The red-haired captain coughed, struggling to stand.
"Have you reconsidered?" Zenkichi asked. "Refuse me again, and I'll have no choice but to control you."
Shanks wiped the blood from his lip. "I'll never serve another. I had one captain—Gol D. Roger. That will never change."
Zenkichi sighed. Shanks was strong—stronger than he had expected—but stubborn. Unlike Whitebeard, who was willing to submit for the sake of his sons, Shanks' pride stood unbending.
"I didn't want to do this," Zenkichi muttered, his Mangekyō Sharingan flashing to life.
In an instant, a Genjutsu spread through Shanks' mind, forcing control upon him. One by one, Zenkichi subdued the rest of the Red-Haired Pirates through his overwhelming presence and illusionary might.
With Shanks and Whitebeard under his control, Zenkichi united the Four Emperors completely. His next move: the Holy Land of Mariejois.
---
The New World trembled.
Its second half was ruled by pirate emperors, while the first was controlled by the Marines and the World Government. And Dressrosa, caught in between, had become a delicate balancing point between these powers.
Doflamingo stood atop the King's Plateau, overlooking his kingdom with a grim expression. The cheongsam-wearing woman beside him, Violet, appeared pale and shaken.
"Violet, are you certain of what you saw?" he asked, voice low and dangerous.
She nodded. "I'm not exaggerating. All four pirate emperors are heading for Dressrosa—together."
Doflamingo's face twisted in disbelief. "The Four Emperors… allied? The world must be losing its mind."
His instincts screamed that this was more than just a rumor, so without hesitation, he leapt into the sky, launching himself toward the sea using the threads of his String-String Fruit.
He needed to see it with his own eyes.
Not long after, Doflamingo saw it—a massive fleet, stretching across the ocean horizon. Ships bearing the flags of Kaido, Big Mom, Whitebeard, and the Red-Haired Pirates all advancing in unison.
His jaw clenched.
"The world… is about to change," he muttered. "The old order is crumbling. A new age is being born."
Rather than fear, a wild excitement bloomed within him. He hated the World Government and the Celestial Dragons—his former brethren. The opportunity to see them destroyed was something he would never let pass.
"I've worked with Kaido before," he said, a manic grin spreading across his face. "It's time to place my bet."
Doflamingo changed course and soared toward Kaido's fleet.
Upon arrival, he called out from the sky. "Kaido-sama! I've come to join you. Are you really taking the fight to the World Government?"
Kaido, standing tall at the ship's bow, looked up. "Doflamingo… so even you've come crawling."
But something felt wrong.
Kaido's voice lacked its usual pride and rage. His eyes were vacant, his tone dull and mechanical.
Doflamingo narrowed his eyes. "This… isn't the Kaido I know…"
His instincts flared again.
The world as they knew it was no longer the same.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 178 - 178: 178: War against Marie Jois.
chapters.content:
"You're not Kaido… Who are you?"
Doflamingo's expression shifted sharply as suspicion crept in. He instinctively tried to take off and escape, but an immense invisible force weighed down on him, locking his body in place.
"You actually noticed the difference. I underestimated you," the man wearing Kaido's face said.
The expressionless facade of Kaido clashed strangely with the playful tone of the voice behind it. The eerie mismatch sent a chill through Doflamingo's spine.
"My name is Zenkichi. Surely you've heard of me," the man said, stepping forward. As his true form was revealed, the illusion faded completely, leaving Doflamingo face-to-face with the infamous Arakawa Zenkichi.
"It's really you..." Doflamingo's eyes widened in disbelief. The oppressive aura that had frozen him in place—clearly, it was Haki. And not just any Haki, but an overwhelming display of Conqueror's Haki combined with an indomitable will.
"You've taken control of the Yonko Pirates?"
Zenkichi nodded calmly. "Yes. And now the world will fall under my control."
He paused, then asked in a chillingly casual tone, "Doflamingo, let me ask you—do you choose life… or destruction?"
Doflamingo stood frozen for a moment, sweat beading on his brow. He knew this wasn't an idle threat. With no other option, he lowered his head in acknowledgment.
"I'll follow you."
Zenkichi smiled slightly. "Good choice. We'll be making camp outside Dressrosa for a few days. As the host, I trust you'll entertain us well."
Doflamingo forced a dry laugh. "Of course."
Though he ruled Dressrosa with an iron grip and a network of dark dealings, the country had flourished under his rule. What once was a poor and broken land had become a glittering jewel—filled with flowers, beauty, music, and dance. A place tourists from across the seas visited, unaware of the shadows lurking beneath its surface.
As members of the Donquixote family approached, Zenkichi's eyes drifted over to Violet and Monet.Follow current novels on
"Plenty of beauties in your crew, Doflamingo," he said, eyeing the two women casually.
"They're… loyal subordinates of mine," Doflamingo replied, clearly uneasy.
"The two of them stay. The rest can leave."
Zenkichi didn't wait for a response, dismissing the others with a wave of his hand.
It had been too long since he'd let himself relax. Among the Yonko Pirates, there were few women—and none that fit his tastes. Big Mom's crew was full of monstrous characters, and although he'd once considered making a move on Robin, circumstances had shifted too quickly. Now, as his conquest neared its final stages, he wanted no more distractions—just a brief moment to unwind.
Zenkichi's fleet, now unified under his banner, set sail toward Mariejois, the sacred land of the Celestial Dragons.
At the World Government's headquarters, the Five Elders were already aware of the impending attack—and enraged by the news.
"These damn pirates! We didn't even try to crush them yet, and now they dare make the first move!"
"It's not just the Yonko Pirates anymore… this is Zenkichi's doing."
"He overwhelmed Sengoku and all three Navy Admirals. If the reports are accurate, not even the four Yonko together could stop him."
"That means he's brought the Yonko under his command… and he's leading them straight to us."
"Hmph! The World Government isn't so easily shaken. Let them come. They'll learn the price of defiance."
"We've consolidated our power for this moment. When the battle comes, we'll eliminate Zenkichi and every pirate that follows him."
"And once they're gone, our grip over the seas will be absolute."
Their decision made, the Five Elders set their plan in motion. The showdown would take place at the G-5 Marine Branch in the New World, a vital outpost—much like Marineford—that served as the last bastion before reaching the sacred lands of Mariejois.
If the Yonko Pirates captured it, they'd have a direct route to the World Nobles' doorstep.
Recognizing the risk, the Five Elders committed everything to this battle. Forces were pulled back from across the globe. Suppression efforts in the Four Blues and the Grand Line's first half were paused. Every resource was funneled into the New World.
This unprecedented move shook the Navy Headquarters. Many high-ranking officers voiced concern. Vice Admiral Garp was particularly outspoken.
"You're going to let pirates run free across the rest of the world?" Garp roared. "The people will suffer!"
Despite their objections, the World Government's envoys arrived with clear logic—and persuasive words.
"If we don't crush the Yonko Pirates here, what then? If we fall… the seas will fall with us."
"Without the World Government, who keeps the pirates in check? Who holds the line?"
"If we lose this battle, the chaos that follows will be far worse than anything we've seen—even worse than when Roger died."
"There will be no balance. No order. The world will descend into a storm that none of us can stop."
Their reasoning, while cold, was irrefutable.
In the end, even the most reluctant of naval leaders yielded. Orders were accepted.
A force of 400,000 elite marines was gathered. The Five Elders themselves prepared to command from the front lines. Powerful agents from CP-0 and beyond were summoned, and the G-5 base turned into a fortress bristling with strength.
All eyes now turned toward the New World, where the fate of the entire sea would soon be decided.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 179 - 179: 179: The Warlords.
chapters.content:
Crocodile puffed lazily on his cigar, smirking at the tall swordsman beside him.
"I didn't expect the World Government to care this much. They established the Shichibukai system, but when it's time to use it, only the four of us show up to take orders."
After the World Government confirmed that the Yonko coalition was marching toward Mariejois, they issued a summoning order to all remaining Shichibukai.
But of the group, only Dracule Mihawk, Crocodile, Jinbei, and Boa Hancock actually answered the call.
Donquixote Doflamingo had already submitted to the enemy when the Yonko forces took Dressrosa. Now, he was part of their coalition.
Moria had been eliminated early by Zenkichi, and his position as Shichibukai had never been refilled.
The World Government had been far too overwhelmed by the chaos following Zenkichi's rise to focus on recruiting new members.
As for Bartholomew Kuma, though he initially responded to the summons, he received a covert message from the Revolutionary Army along the way.
Kuma, though publicly a Warlord, was secretly a high-ranking agent of the Revolutionary Army embedded deep within the World Government.
Once the revolutionaries learned of the coming war, they urged him to avoid it at all costs. Both the Yonko alliance and the World Government were threats in their eyes.
Letting those two forces clash and weaken each other was exactly what the revolutionaries wanted.
And so, without hesitation, Kuma withdrew. His Devil Fruit ability made evasion effortless — no one could stop him.
Now, only four Warlords remained.
Of course, none of them had full knowledge of the real situation. If they did, it was likely all four would have made the same choice as Kuma.
Boa Hancock looked particularly displeased. Her disdain was plain for all to see.
When she first received the World Government's letter, she tossed it straight into the trash.
After all, she had once been enslaved by the Celestial Dragons. Her hatred for them was absolute.
It was only when Elder Nyon found the letter and begged her to consider it that Hancock reluctantly agreed to go.
The World Government had been careful in its wording — the letter only mentioned a visit to the G5 branch, not a full-scale war.
But the message was clear: if she did not comply, her Shichibukai title would be revoked.
Hancock needed that title.
Her country, Amazon Lily, was still considered a pirate nation. The Kuja Pirates — an all-female crew — would be branded criminals without their legal status.
The Calm Belt no longer served as a true deterrent either, now that the World Government had developed advanced warships capable of traversing it.
If Hancock had known the full truth, she would've thrown that letter away all over again — no matter the consequences. After all, who even knew if the World Government would survive this?
The other three Shichibukai — Mihawk, Jinbei, and Crocodile — were in a similar position.
They had no idea they were being sent to the front lines of a catastrophic war.
And now that they were here, leaving wouldn't be so simple.
Zenkichi had already shaken the New World. It was impossible for men like Mihawk to not have heard the rumors.
But the World Government had blocked all information before it could reach them — a full news blackout enforced with brutal efficiency.
Imu had already voiced his fury and killing intent toward the Five Elders. Under the threat of death, they had no choice but to act with urgency.
They silenced the press using elite CP agents, ones powerful enough to rival admirals. Even the notorious Morgans had no way to resist.
He was silenced like any other voice.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
"They tricked us into coming," Crocodile said, narrowing his eyes. "What if we decide to flip sides and join the Yonko coalition instead?"
"Our status is complicated," Jinbei muttered. "Caught between admirals and vice admirals, constantly watched, distrusted by all sides."
"They won't trust us unless we fight, and they'll demand proof of our loyalty. It's not an easy position."
Jinbei sighed heavily.
His homeland, Fish-Man Island, had always served as the gateway between the first and second halves of the Grand Line — and as a battlefield for pirates.
The World Government had done little to protect it. Instead, it had relied on Whitebeard's protection.
Jinbei never wanted to fight the Whitebeard Pirates. He respected them.
And he couldn't believe for a second that they had joined the other Yonko to destroy the World Government.
No — he didn't believe they would ever align themselves with Zenkichi either.
As this heavy atmosphere loomed over them, the Yonko coalition fleet finally appeared.
The skies above the G5 branch turned dark. Tension crackled in the air.
From the top of the command tower, the Five Elders watched the sea. Their faces were grim as they surveyed the battlefield.
Each Shichibukai stood divided by their own doubts.
Meanwhile, the entire Navy leadership had been mobilized, ready for the largest battle the seas had seen in decades.
And far across the waves, Shanks stood aboard his flagship.
Red-haired had always walked his own path. With his pride and ideals, he would never join the other Yonko in this campaign.
Hawkeye Mihawk, who had long known Shanks, shared the same doubts as Jinbei.
Something didn't add up.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 180 - 180: 180: Only Victors Become Justice.
chapters.content:
"The pirate alliance composed of the Four Emperors has arrived!"
No one knew who shouted first, but the moment those words echoed, tension swept through the entire Marine G5 base.
One Emperor was enough to strike fear into the hearts of seasoned soldiers. Now, four of them had joined forces.
The Four Emperors were recognized as one of the world's two great powers, alongside the Marines. And today, their combined might had taken shape—opposing the government's strongest military force.
Despite reinforcements gathered by the World Government, the strength difference between both sides was razor-thin.
"Marines!"
"Do not fear! Do not falter!"
"This war was provoked by the Four Emperors! As soldiers of justice, we cannot retreat now!"
"If we don't defeat this coalition here, there will be no safe harbor even at the edge of the sea."
"This is a battle we cannot afford to lose!"
"Our defeat would plunge the world into chaos under the tyranny of pirates!"
"For the sake of innocent lives across the globe—justice must not fail!"
Fleet Admiral Sengoku's voice thundered from atop a platform, amplified through a Den Den Mushi.
His words ignited a spark in the hearts of the 400,000-strong navy present.
"For justice!" they roared in unison, echoing across the coastline.
Watching this from the distance, Zenkichi smirked slightly.
Without hesitation, he leapt into the air, landing firmly between the two forces.
"Marines," Zenkichi began, his tone calm but piercing. "Stop pretending you're on the side of justice."
"If you truly stood for justice, you'd be marching into Mariejois to purge the Celestial Dragons."
"You're not a righteous army—you're the weapon of the World Government. The obedient dogs of the nobles who trample this world."
"The World Government is not justice. The very existence of the Celestial Dragons is proof of that hypocrisy."Thɪs ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
His voice carried through the battlefield, and many Marines visibly tensed. The morale so recently kindled by Sengoku began to waver.
Sensing this, one of the Five Elders quickly stepped forward and barked,
"You brought pirates to attack a Marine base, and now claim you represent justice?"
Zenkichi's reply was cold and direct. "Neither you nor I represent justice. Only the victor has that right. Today, I will be justice."
The Elders scoffed, their expressions dripping with disdain.
"You think this ragtag pirate alliance can overcome the World Government?" one sneered. "Confidence is fine. Arrogance is not."
"You've seen my strength," Zenkichi answered flatly. "Why pretend to be surprised?"
"You may be strong enough to challenge the Marines," another Elder said, "but the World Government's strength is far beyond you."
"You'll see it soon enough. You're not qualified to stand against us."
Then, the blond Elder stepped forward.
"Zenkichi, regardless of your intentions, you've drawn the attention of the entire world."
"You've managed to unite the Four Emperors. That alone proves your capabilities."
"But if you press on with this war, the most you can hope for is mutual destruction."
"Despite our power, we don't want chaos. The world relies on stability, and civilians rely on us for protection."
"If you're willing to join the World Government, we will name you a World Noble."
"Your pirate allies will be legitimized, and together, we can maintain peace across the seas."
Zenkichi laughed, derisively.
"To try recruiting me now—how naïve."
The Elder's expression hardened. "You'll regret refusing this offer. You truly believe you can defeat the World Government?"
"I'm not here to fight the World Government," Zenkichi said. "I'm here to overthrow it."
"You will fall, and I will be crowned king."
Without another word, he raised his hand—signaling the Yonko Pirates to begin the assault.
Whitebeard stepped forward first, no longer hesitant. Zenkichi's power had convinced him of the possibility of victory—and a new world.
Massive tremors surged across the sea as Whitebeard used the Gura Gura no Mi. His fists, glowing with a white shockwave, shattered the air itself and sent ocean water reeling in a towering tsunami.
The navy stood ready, their expressions stern, as the wall of sea water rushed toward them.
"Ice Age!"
Admiral Aokiji stepped forward, freezing the tsunami mid-surge. Glacial structures cracked and creaked beneath the weight of frozen destruction.
But Charlotte Linlin—Big Mom—was already moving. With a loud clap, she slammed her hand onto the ice.
Infusing it with a piece of her soul, the frozen sea transformed into a towering ice monster under her control.
Aokiji raised an eyebrow, unimpressed. "Tch… figures. Every one of you is a walking catastrophe."
Despite his lazy tone, he braced for the oncoming chaos.
This was not a mere battle. It was the beginning of a war that would determine the shape of the world.
---

chapters.title: Chapter 181 - 181: 181: Tides of Rebellion.
chapters.content:
The war had finally begun.
Although Zenkichi was confident in his ability to defeat the World Government, the forces under his command were still vastly inferior. The odds were against him—at least on paper. No matter how he arranged his pieces, the sheer power of the World Government was overwhelming.
But that only applied if he didn't act personally.
If Zenkichi took the battlefield himself, there would be no contest. The World Government wouldn't stand a chance.
Still, he chose not to appear immediately. He wanted to observe. The first wave was meant to test his commanders' combat ability—and weed out the weaklings pretending to be loyal.
More importantly, he needed to show the world that the Yonko under his command were not just symbols of chaos, but legitimate forces capable of going toe-to-toe with the strongest the Navy had to offer.
"Pops… why are you following Zenkichi?" Jinbei asked, puzzled, casting a troubled look toward Whitebeard. The former warlord couldn't understand why the legendary pirate would serve someone else.
"That man will defeat the World Government," Whitebeard replied calmly. "I just want to protect my family."
At the same time, he tried to convince Jinbei to switch sides.
"But I've already used Fish-Man Karate against many of the pirate alliance's forces…"
Jinbei hesitated. That was part of the reason why the Navy had allowed him to charge in alone—he wasn't trusted by either side.
"Don't worry," Whitebeard said. "Zenkichi doesn't concern himself with such trivial matters. The ones you killed are insignificant to him. Even us—the Four Emperors—are replaceable in his eyes."
"Come with us. I'll vouch for your safety."
Whitebeard's respect for Jinbei remained intact. Eventually, he succeeded in convincing the Fish-Man to join their side.
Meanwhile, another fierce battle raged.
"Shanks, what's going on with you?! Answer me! Are you even conscious?!"
Mihawk shouted, wielding his massive black blade as he faced off against the red-haired Yonko. Shanks' eyes were empty, devoid of will—yet his attacks were swift, accurate, and terrifyingly powerful.
His overwhelming Conqueror's Haki, combined with equally potent Armament Haki, forced even Mihawk—the greatest swordsman alive—onto the defensive.
"Don't bother," a calm voice interrupted.
Zenkichi stepped in, appearing beside them without warning.
"Shanks is under my control."
"What?! That's impossible!" Mihawk's eyes widened. "A man with Shanks' Haki… there's no way you could manipulate him!"
"As long as your strength is overwhelming," Zenkichi replied coolly, "nothing is impossible."
His eyes shifted.
They were the Rinnegan.
After further developing the power from Uchiha Madara's template, Zenkichi had awakened the legendary eye technique—the Rinnegan.
"Eyes like mine?" Mihawk murmured, stunned by the pattern.
"Not quite. The design may be similar, but the power is on a different level. You'll see what I mean."
The moment their eyes met, Zenkichi activated a genjutsu through his Rinnegan. Mihawk, the famed eagle-eyed swordsman, froze. His will was seized, just like Shanks.
Now, both stood proudly at Zenkichi's side.
Elsewhere, Pirate Empress Boa Hancock crept along the battlefield, using her Observation Haki to sense her surroundings.
"I'll slip away while they're distracted…"
But before she could move further, Zenkichi appeared in front of her.
"Where are you off to?" he asked with a smile.
"You're Zenkichi?" she asked, slightly flustered. "Let me leave. For the sake of my beauty, won't you honor my request?"
She flipped her hair, playing to her strengths—her overwhelming charm. Attacking Zenkichi was out of the question; she knew better than to provoke him. Instead, she attempted to seduce her way out.
Zenkichi laughed.
"If you're so beautiful, why not stay and serve me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 182 - 182: 182: The Forest of Dominance.
chapters.content:
The power of Six Paths Madara had been revived within Zenkichi, and now Zenkichi wielded nearly 90% of Uchiha Madara's original abilities.
"Wood Release: Advent of a World of Trees!"
Forming hand seals swiftly, Zenkichi released a torrent of dense chakra, and from it, immense Wood Release energy erupted.
A colossal forest emerged from nothingness, stretching across the sky and blotting out the sun as it surged toward the distant battlefield.
"A forest?"
"Unbelievable... Zenkichi has more abilities beyond the Gura Gura no Mi and the Pika Pika no Mi?"
Kizaru raised an eyebrow, surprised. His body shimmered into golden light particles as he shot skyward.
"Yasakani no Magatama!"
A storm of golden energy bullets fired from Kizaru's hands, tearing through the incoming wooden tendrils.
Though the golden projectiles shattered many of the thick vines, the forest was too vast. No matter how fiercely Kizaru attacked, it wasn't enough to stop the relentless surge.
Much like Senju Hashirama's True Several Thousand Hands, the strength of each limb wasn't necessarily overwhelming—but their sheer number gave them overwhelming power.
Even Susanoo would eventually succumb under such relentless attacks, as hundreds of wooden fists pounded it until it broke apart.
"Laser Light!"
Kizaru extended his finger, and with a flick, a golden beam sliced through a massive tree like a blade through paper.
But the trees weren't done.
From the severed trunks, fresh vines sprouted and wrapped around each other mid-air, healing themselves and continuing their charge.
"Wood, huh? Let's see how well it burns."
Akainu glared at the writhing mass of vines. His arms bubbled and morphed into searing red magma.
"Meteor Volcano!"
Lava blasted from his arms like meteor fire, hammering the wooden sea.
The impact ignited large portions of the forest, but even then, the vines refused to die. Their vitality was overwhelming.
Even as they burned, the wood remained under Zenkichi's control. Instead of being destroyed, the vines seemed to absorb the magma, becoming even more ferocious and blazing with demonic fire.
"Ice Age!"
Aokiji raised his hands, releasing a chilling wave of energy that blanketed the area in frost.
A sea of ice surged across the battlefield, freezing both the magma and vines.
Yet the freeze lasted mere seconds—shattered instantly by the relentless strength of the Wood Release.
"Tch... what a hassle," Sengoku muttered with visible frustration as he watched the endless vines swarm across Marineford. He had no answer for this level of power.
Indeed, Zenkichi had inherited Madara's Wood Release, but he had far surpassed Madara's strength. His version of the Advent of a World of Trees was even more terrifying than either Madara's or Hashirama's.
The monstrous forest had already swallowed Marineford whole.
This kind of overwhelming area-of-effect assault wasn't something martial artists or even most Devil Fruit users could achieve. Only select Logia types or certain Paramecia wielders possessed the raw destructive potential to compete.
"The rest of this battle has nothing to do with you," a cold voice echoed in Sengoku's ears.
A clone of Zenkichi appeared behind him and struck him down swiftly with a precise chop to the neck.
The vast forest loomed overhead, blotting out the sun and drowning the navy in darkness.
Even the few who withstood the onslaught of the World of Trees now stood subdued under the control of Zenkichi's clones, showing no resistance.
"Five Elders... will you move yourselves, or should I do it for you?"
Zenkichi calmly approached the highest platform where the Five Elders stood, smiling faintly.
"Zenkichi, don't get cocky," the Elder with the goatee snapped, his voice sharp. "We have Im-sama. You won't defeat her."

"Clones again? Just how many Devil Fruit abilities do you have?"
"But using only clones against us?" the blond Elder scoffed, lifting a massive axe. "You underestimate us."
"We are the Five Elders—the supreme authority of the World Government!"
"If we weren't strong, how could we rule the entire world?"
With a snarl, the blond Elder lunged, axe raised.
But Zenkichi's clone stood calm. A faint white aura coated his fist—a clear display of Advanced Armament Haki.
He struck with brutal force.
The air itself shattered.
The axe stopped mid-swing, trembling violently as the shockwave twisted it out of shape. A second later, it exploded into fragments, and the blond Elder was hurled backward by the blast.
"Strong? Perhaps. But you're still far beneath me."
"Even one clone is enough to crush you."

chapters.title: Chapter 183 - 183: 183: Fall of the Celestial Order.
chapters.content:
Mariejois.
The Holy Land of the world, home to the World Nobles—the so-called Celestial Dragons.
It is also the seat of the World Government's power, where the Five Elders reside, untouched for over 800 years.
The last time chaos ever reached this sanctified land was when Fisher Tiger briefly caused a stir. Since then, the Celestial Dragons have lived in a dreamlike delusion, oblivious to the crumbling world around them.
They believed their rule eternal.
But change has a way of coming when least expected.
Arakawa Zenkichi had arrived—dragging the defeated Five Elders behind him like broken dogs.
Their eyes were full of despair. Whether Zenkichi won or lost against Im mattered little; they knew they wouldn't be forgiven.
"Who are you?!" a pompous Celestial Dragon shouted from afar, pointing at Zenkichi with disdain. "How dare a lowly slave step foot in the Holy Land!"
The man scowled. Zenkichi wore no World Noble attire, nor the distinct uniforms of CP agents. Naturally, he was mistaken for a mere servant.
"Someone drag this rat out of here at once!"
In the Holy Land, slaves had restricted movement. Seeing one walk freely in an area forbidden to them enraged the nobles.
"Shut up."
Zenkichi didn't raise his voice. He simply pointed his finger—and a thin golden laser burst forth.
In an instant, the Celestial Dragon and the guards beside him vanished in an explosion of golden light particles.
Boom!
"Clean out Mariejois," he ordered coldly.
Hundreds of wooden clones materialized behind him. Without hesitation, they began storming through the city, capturing Celestial Dragons.
These so-called gods would be executed publicly—to win over the people.
As for the agents, guards, and slaves? They could be repurposed—like pirates, made into followers. Those who resisted could be brought under control by force.
With five clones still holding the Five Elders, Zenkichi moved deeper into Mariejois.
He entered the central throne room.
At the top, seated on the Empty Throne, was a woman with piercing, ringed eyes. Her cold gaze fell on Zenkichi.
This was Im—the true ruler of the world.
"Interesting," Zenkichi remarked, stepping into the chamber. "So, the ruler of the Celestial Dragons turns out to be a rather elegant woman."
He smirked.
Im's expression didn't change. Her voice came cold and smooth. "Mortal. Do you understand the price of defying a god?"
Zenkichi chuckled. "Did your brain get frozen in the last century?"
"You stand there, call yourself a god, and pull this 'divine judgment' act in front of me?"
He scoffed, raising an eyebrow.
"If you're a god, then what I need isn't reverence. What I need is a goddess who serves tea and fetches water."
He gazed at Im with clear mockery.
"Arrogant insect!"
Im's calm shattered. She raised her hand—an invisible force crashed down on Zenkichi.
His body tensed for a moment, but then his chakra flared.
He gritted his teeth slightly, and the invisible pressure vanished.
"…How?" Im's voice trembled. Her eyes widened in disbelief. "My power… why didn't it work?!"
Zenkichi cracked his knuckles and smirked. "That was your Devil Fruit ability, wasn't it?"
"I could feel my blood boiling for a moment. It was like I was about to burst... but I'm just too strong for that."
He took a step forward.
"Even if you're powerful, you're still just an ant to a disaster."
Im raised her hand again. "I'll show you what true power looks like."
She turned her gaze to the moon. Her body pulsed with strange magnetic energy.
"She's controlling the magnetic field?" Zenkichi muttered. "This ability... it's the Magnetic-Magnetic Fruit."
Outside, the moon shifted irregularly. The tides surged unnaturally, threatening to flood the world.
"Hahaha! You're finished now!" one of the Five Elders yelled from the floor.
"Even if we die, you'll go down with us!"
"You lot talk too much."The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
Zenkichi's eyes turned. The purple-red glow of the Rinnegan surged in his pupils. He locked eyes with Im.
In that instant, her soul was dragged into an illusion.
He reappeared in front of her, placing a hand on her head.
"Human Path: Memory Reading."
He dug deep into her soul and memories.
"So it's true... the Magnetic-Magnetic Fruit, developed to this extent. You've mastered the ability to manipulate the iron in human blood. Your control rivals Magneto himself."
"Using the planetary magnetic field to shift the moon and stir global tides... Even becoming a human-form ancient weapon—'King of Heaven'."
"You were once a great figure... but the centuries have eroded your spirit. Now, you're nothing more than a puppet—an umbrella for the Celestial Dragons."
He sighed.
Zenkichi stepped back and glanced at Im, now dazed and powerless before him.
"I'll spare your life. You'll serve tea and water from now on. Since you enjoy calling yourself a goddess, I'll let you be one—my personal maid goddess."
The irony made his smile widen.
After all, Im had once been the most revered woman in the world.
"No! This is impossible!"
The Five Elders stared in horror.
Their goddess, their secret weapon—the so-called King of Heaven—defeated with such ease?
"You can't be serious...!"
"You don't have to believe it," Zenkichi said casually, turning away. "Truth doesn't require your approval."

He stood atop the ruined plaza and made his announcement:
"The World Government has fallen!"
No one was surprised—not the pirates, not the navy. Everyone had already witnessed his power.
What was shocking was that the world had held on for this long.
"I hereby establish a new world government!"
"Both marines and pirates may join. Together, we'll rebuild the order."
Naturally, many from the navy objected.
But they were swiftly silenced—Zenkichi's Rinnegan crushed their resistance.
"Next, execute the Celestial Dragons publicly."
"Reveal the sins of the old World Government."
"Summon the kings of all nations to Mariejois. The world is about to change—forever."

His vision would reshape everything.

chapters.title: Chapter 184 - 184: 184: A New World Order.
chapters.content:
The World Government had fallen.
Arakawa Zenkichi stood at the summit, having crushed the Navy, absorbed the Yonko Pirates, and forced the ultimate powers of the pirate world to kneel before him.
No force remained that could challenge Zenkichi's dominance.
Not the Revolutionary Army.
Not the Shichibukai, who were nothing more than figureheads by this point.
After establishing the New World Government, Zenkichi began an aggressive restructuring of the world, with centralized authority as the foundation of his vision.
Despite its global reach, the former World Government had operated more like a fragile alliance. The so-called "member nations" paid Heavenly Tribute, and in return, received Navy protection. It was a transactional relationship—not true governance.
Each nation had full sovereignty within its borders. The World Government had no legal right to interfere with their internal affairs.
That era was over.
Zenkichi summoned the kings of every nation. He demanded they relinquish their authority.
In exchange, he offered them ceremonial honors and generous monthly stipends.
"This sort of demand..." many kings murmured, clearly reluctant.
"If we're to give up power," one bejeweled king proposed, "then we demand equal status and rights as the Celestial Dragons!"
Zenkichi chuckled coldly.
He raised a finger. A thin beam of light shot out—a laser—piercing straight through the man's skull.
Boom!
Panic erupted. The kings shrank in their seats, horrified.
"If I give you a little color, you want to open a dye shop?" Zenkichi said flatly, his voice like ice. "Do you even know your worth?"
His eyes narrowed, his tone lethal. "The offer I made was out of mercy. Don't mistake it for negotiation."
"Your consent? It means nothing. Refuse, and I'll conquer your nation myself."
The room fell silent.
The kings realized the truth—Zenkichi's power was absolute. Resistance was meaningless.
"I agree!"
"We've always supported this!"
"Just a misunderstanding—of course, we surrender!"
Each king quickly bowed their head and relinquished their power.
Thus, the New World Government claimed direct control of all territories. The old nations were dismantled and reorganized into centrally managed cities.
---
Baldimore.
"After establishing the New World Government, Zenkichi restructured the Navy and merged the Yonko Pirates into it," a revolutionary soldier reported.
"All territories previously controlled by the Yonko are now under the new government. The former kings have surrendered their authority, and their lands have been transformed into directly governed cities."ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
"The new Navy is rounding up pirates and criminals worldwide. Global order is steadily improving."
Dragon listened in silence, his expression growing increasingly grim.
"Zenkichi's reforms may have benefited the world… but they've made our revolutionary mission far more difficult."
"No doubt, he's a wise and capable ruler," Dragon said solemnly. "But we cannot rely on a single man to steer the future."
"True revolution demands the abolition of monarchies and the birth of genuine democratic freedom."
"The democracy the World Government claimed to uphold for 800 years must now be forged by our own hands."
The room was tense.
But then a voice—calm, yet sharp—cut through the silence.
"Dreams like that… will never come true."
Startled, the revolutionaries turned. A young man stood in their conference room—handsome, composed, emanating power.
"Zenkichi?!"
Gasps filled the room. His face had dominated headlines for months. None could mistake it.
"I'm not here to argue," Zenkichi said flatly. "I'm here to recruit you."
"You have two choices—surrender… or die."
The air itself seemed to bend under the pressure of his presence.
Many of the revolutionaries found themselves trembling, unable to lift their heads. Fear froze their bodies in place.
Dragon hesitated, clenched his fists… then finally exhaled.
This wasn't a battle they could win.
"…I surrender."
The rest of the room followed.
There was no point in fighting a force of nature.
---
East Blue.
Ace's expression twisted in disbelief as he read the latest newspaper headline.
He and his brothers had spent weeks fantasizing about meeting Zenkichi, dreaming of surprising him once they set sail.
But before they could even leave the shore… Zenkichi had reshaped the world.
He crushed the Yonko Pirates.
Overpowered the Navy.
Toppled the World Government.
Ended the age of pirates in one sweeping revolution.
What was left for them to do but look up at him, stunned?
---
Mariejois.
Zenkichi reclined on his throne, the Pirate Empress perched beside him, lovingly feeding him fruit. Behind him, Imu—expressionless—massaged his shoulders like a silent maid.
Zenkichi appeared to be dozing off… but his mind was elsewhere.
His gaze was locked onto the translucent system interface only he could see.
Uchiha Madara's template—fully unlocked.
And now, a new one had appeared.
He stared at the bald-headed figure on the screen with a complicated smile.
Saitama.
The strongest. The unbeatable. The absurd.
"Let's finish unlocking this one…" Zenkichi muttered.
Then he smirked.
"…It's time for the next world."
---

chapters.title: Chapter 185 - 185: 185: Marvel Universe.
chapters.content:
After traveling across the world, Zenkichi found himself standing in the middle of a vast desert.
Using his refined Observation Haki, he scanned the barren terrain until he sensed a concentration of human activity nearby. With measured steps, he walked toward the source.
Eventually, he arrived at a hidden settlement nestled within a deep trench. This wasn't a civilian village—it was a heavily armed militant base. The trench was lined with crude tents, reinforced cave dwellings, and stockpiles of weaponry, including missile launchers.
"Who's there?!"
The armed guards spotted Zenkichi and immediately opened fire. Bullets tore through the air toward him.
"Shinra Tensei."
Zenkichi stood still, eyes calm. A surge of invisible repulsive force erupted from his body. The bullets halted mid-air, frozen in place.
"Return."
With a quiet command, the suspended bullets shot back at blinding speed, piercing through the attackers. Bloody holes appeared in their bodies as they dropped without resistance.
"Enemy sighted! Open fire!"
More militants emerged from their tents, aiming rifles and shouting orders. Zenkichi stepped forward, a faint smirk curling on his lips.
"I know where I am now... so let's end this."
He slowly raised his right fist. A pale white halo shimmered around it.
Air Shock.
With a single punch, the air before him fractured like glass, shattering into a spiderweb of cracks. A massive shockwave blasted forth. The earth trembled as tents were ripped apart, debris flying, and militants were swept off their feet like ragdolls in a storm.
Their gunfire was useless. The shockwaves shattered bullets mid-flight, reducing all resistance to dust.
From a distance, a figure in exoskeleton armor approached the wreckage, surveying the devastation with wary eyes.
"An earthquake?" the man muttered.
Zenkichi turned and smiled. "Tony Stark. I didn't expect to meet you like this."
Tony blinked, then narrowed his eyes. "You did all this?"
Zenkichi nodded lazily. "I did. Consider yourself rescued. Think you owe me one?"
Tony looked around at the wreckage and, without hesitation, shrugged. "No problem. You saved me. Name it—I'm in your debt."
Knowing he was dealing with someone beyond ordinary, Tony wasn't about to test his luck. In fact, he was more interested in teaming up.
"Excellent," Zenkichi replied. "Then let's get out of here."
As he turned to leave, Tony stopped him. "Wait! My friend Yinsen—he's still here. We take him too."
Zenkichi activated his Observation Haki again, easily pinpointing Yinsen's presence.Googlᴇ search NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Unlike in the original story, Yinsen had not sacrificed himself. Zenkichi's timely arrival meant he survived.
Moments later, Zenkichi took both Tony and Yinsen into his arms. Surrounded by an invisible spiritual pressure, he soared into the sky and vanished in a flash of light.
---
Within seconds, they reappeared above New York City.
Tony looked out at the familiar skyline, his voice cracking. "God... I never thought I'd see this place again."
"We came from the Middle East to New York in under a minute?" Yinsen was stunned, his scientific mind in disbelief. "That's—utterly impossible!"
Tony grinned. "He's not normal, that's for sure."
Once they landed, Tony clapped Zenkichi on the back. "Now that you're here, you've got to see my place. Come on!"
Back at Stark Tower, Tony personally hosted Zenkichi and Yinsen. As the world's richest, his hospitality was unparalleled.
---
Meanwhile, the U.S. military and intelligence agencies were in shock.
Tony Stark had vanished without a trace. All their efforts to track him had failed—until now, when he mysteriously reappeared in New York.
Reporters and officials flooded him with questions.
"How did you escape?"
Tony waved them off. "I have my own methods. No comment."
He had no intention of explaining the miracle that was Zenkichi. In his eyes, the government wasn't worth trusting.
---
Inside his private lab, Tony returned to work on a new type of armor.
His traumatic experience in captivity changed him. He now realized that personal power was more important than ever. But lacking the ability to enhance his own body, Tony turned to his true talent—technology.
He began developing the first version of his Iron Man armor.
Zenkichi stepped into the lab. "Your body's being poisoned by palladium. That Arc Reactor in your chest needs an upgrade."
Tony froze. "Palladium poisoning?"
He rushed to grab his scanner, pricked his finger, and let the machine run diagnostics.
Moments later, JARVIS gave the results—Tony's condition was critical.
Tony stared at the results, frustrated. "So I can't use the suit anymore?"
Zenkichi crossed his arms. "Not necessarily. Just take care of yourself. There are better solutions."

After surviving a terrorist attack, Tony had been left with dozens of sharp metal fragments lodged dangerously close to his heart. The Arc Reactor powered the electromagnet embedded in his chest to keep the shrapnel from moving inward.
"This might be a difficult procedure for regular doctors," Zenkichi said, stepping forward casually, his tone relaxed. "But it's not a challenge for me."
With his powerful dōjutsu, Zenkichi peered straight through Tony's body, mapping the precise location of each shard with ease.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet

chapters.title: Chapter 187 - 187: 187: Joining The Chaos.
chapters.content:
Tony Stark had noticed disturbing issues festering within the Stark Group. Someone from inside was clearly colluding with terrorists.
And if one considered it carefully, the internal mole's role likely went beyond supplying arms to them. It wouldn't be surprising if the same person was behind Tony's kidnapping by the terrorist group.
After reflecting for some time, Tony Stark made a bold decision—he shut down the weapons department of Stark Industries entirely.
Despite being the head of the company, Tony had never really involved himself in day-to-day management. As a result, his actual control over the company was limited. Simply banning arms sales to terrorists wouldn't be enough.
After all, the Stark Group had already prohibited that kind of deal on paper long ago. Such orders hadn't stopped people from finding loopholes. Repeating them now wouldn't change the outcome.
So, Tony did what no one expected—he pulled the plug on the entire weapons division.
This move brought pressure from every direction. Even Colonel Rhodes, his longtime friend, and Pepper Potts, the woman closest to him, struggled to fully support his decision.
But Tony remained confident.
He believed that he alone was the true backbone of Stark Industries. As long as he retained his genius intellect, he could rebuild everything with just a few world-changing innovations.
"Don't worry," he said with calm determination, "I'm not about to capsize."
"The company's stock dropping might actually be a blessing in disguise."
"I'll take the opportunity to buy back shares, increase my stake... The government won't let me own too many, but I can register some under your name."
"Think of it as a gift. Not a pricey one, but a valuable gesture."
Tony spoke decisively, as if the shares—worth a fortune—were no big deal at all.
Zenkichi accepted the offer without blinking.
To someone like Arakawa Zenkichi, what Tony offered truly meant little. With his strength and ability, wealth was something he could generate in minutes if he ever cared to.
"I've got my eye on a villa in Queens," Zenkichi said as he prepared to leave. "I'll be moving there soon."

chapters.content:
As soon as Zenkichi returned home, golden sparks shimmered through the room.
The air began to ripple with energy, forming a glowing ring of light. From within it stepped a bald woman in yellow robes, her presence calm yet overwhelming.
Zenkichi narrowed his eyes.
"The Ancient One… the Sorcerer Supreme?"
The woman smiled gently.
"Young man, you're quite the anomaly."
She took a step forward, her gaze locked on Zenkichi.
"The power within you allows me to glimpse another world. You're not from this universe, are you?"
"Your presence disrupts the natural timeline… I can't trace you anywhere within it."
Zenkichi met her gaze, expression unreadable.
"Then, as Sorcerer Supreme, protector of Earth and the Time Stone… what do you plan to do with me?"
"Expel me? Kill me?"
Although he acknowledged her strength, Zenkichi wasn't intimidated. The Time Stone was her most formidable weapon—beyond that, he knew he was stronger.
"There's no need for conflict," she replied calmly.
"I harbor no hostility toward those from other universes. As long as you don't threaten this Earth, I have no reason to act against you."
"I see no evil in you… I believe you're not the kind to destroy worlds."
She gave a light smile, then added,
"If you ever have time, visit Kamar-Taj. I'm curious about other universes… and your presence intrigues me."
With that, the Sorcerer Supreme turned and disappeared into the glowing portal.
"…That's it?"
Zenkichi had braced himself for battle. He hadn't expected her to let the matter slide so easily. But, truthfully, he was glad. He had no desire to clash with the Ancient One—at least not today.
Just as she vanished, another voice echoed in his mind.
"Hello."
Zenkichi paused.
"Professor X?"
The voice had appeared without warning, sharp and subtle. But Zenkichi quickly recognized it—and its source.
"You're entering my mind uninvited. That's not polite," he replied telepathically, his mental voice calm but firm.
"My apologies," came Professor Xavier's voice. "This is the only method I could use to contact you. But rest assured—I didn't attempt to access your memories."
"Not that it would matter. Your mind is… incredibly well-guarded."
Zenkichi didn't reply immediately.
"Speak your reason for contacting me."
"I want to make it clear first—I'm not a mutant," he added firmly. "So if this is part of some recruitment attempt based on that assumption, don't waste your time."
"A shame," Xavier said softly. "But it doesn't change the fact that your abilities, your position… your existence holds great value."
"Mutants and individuals like you are seen as threats, resources, or weapons. But together, we might stand against the powers that wish to control or destroy us."
Zenkichi responded coolly,
"Maybe you're right… but I'll need time to decide that for myself."
Xavier nodded silently through the connection.
"If ever you feel the need—or see the truth in what I've said—you'll know how to find me."
With that, the telepathic link faded.
Back at the X-Mansion, Beast turned to Professor Xavier.
"Did it fail?"
"Not entirely," Xavier replied. "He may not have joined us now, but I have a feeling he'll return."

Just then, a message came through from Tony Stark.
"Zen, just a heads-up. The U.S. military's been poking around. A bunch of high-ranking officials are 'inviting' you to a military base. They're interested in your abilities."
Tony's tone was casual, but the warning was clear.
"I'd tread carefully. They're not looking to give you medals… more like run experiments."

He wasn't threatened. Earth had powerful forces, yes, but the American military wasn't among those who could endanger him.

"Natasha, I've got a mission for you."
